articles.title: Do you need a mouse with an 8K polling rate?
articles.text:
Do you need a mouse with an 8K polling rate?
Hint: You don't.
For years, the standard polling rate for gaming peripherals — mice, keyboards, etc. — has been 1,000 Hz, which equates to a delay, or latency, of 1 millisecond. This is significantly higher than the standard polling rate for non-gaming peripherals, by the way, which is 125 Hz (8ms latency) — in fact, it's eight times as fast.
Well, over the last couple of years, gaming companies have been asking: What if we made the polling rate even faster than 1,000 Hz? What if we made it eight times as fast?
And now just about every single ultra-lightweight, esports-oriented gaming mouse that comes out has up to an 8,000 Hz polling rate. And, of course, this raises the question every time: Do you actually need a mouse with an 8,000 Hz polling rate?
And the answer is... probably not.
What is polling rate, and what does it mean?
Polling rate is, simply put, how often your mouse communicates with your PC. That is, how often it reports mouse movement and clicks to your CPU. At a standard gaming mouse polling rate of 1,000 Hz, your mouse is communicating with your PC 1,000 times per second — or, once every millisecond. Hence, a 1,000 Hz polling rate means 1ms latency. At a standard non-gaming mouse polling rate of 125 Hz, your mouse is only communicating with your PC once every eight milliseconds — or an 8 ms latency. At a polling rate of 8,000 Hz, your mouse is communicating with your PC once every 0.125 milliseconds — a 0.125 ms latency.
| Polling Rate | Mouse Report Rate | Latency | 
| 125 Hz | 125x / second | 8 ms | 
| 500 Hz | 500x / second | 2 ms | 
| 1,000 Hz | 1,000x / second | 1 ms | 
| 2,000 Hz | 2,000x / second | 0.5 ms | 
| 4,000 Hz | 4,000x / second | 0.25 ms | 
| 8,000 Hz | 8,000x / second | 0.125 ms | 
Polling rate affects both mouse movement (if the polling rate is low enough, mouse movement might be jerky) and, more importantly, click latency — you want your mouse clicks to translate instantly.
But it's important to keep this in perspective, because higher polling rates yield increasingly diminishing returns. Going from 125 Hz to 1,000 Hz is definitely noticeable — it cuts your latency from eight milliseconds to just one. But while going from 1,000 Hz to 8,000 Hz cuts your latency by the same factor, we're now talking about fractions of a millisecond. The average gamer can tell if their mouse is lagging by several milliseconds, but can they tell if their mouse is lagging by less than one millisecond?
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Maybe. But probably not.
Why not?
Well, inability to distinguish whether your mouse is lagging by 0.875 milliseconds aside, there are some potential downsides to ultra-high polling rates. The main one being that your system may not be able to handle it. A higher polling rate means that the mouse is communicating with your PC more frequently, so this can affect CPU performance — if you don't have a pretty solid gaming CPU, you may see more of a performance hit than is worth the infinitesimal lower latency (which may not even end up being lower if performance issues cause latency). And if you don't have a gaming monitor with a high refresh rate (at least 240 Hz, if not higher), any perceived smoother mouse movement will be just that — perceived. (Of course, with a higher refresh rate you'll need an even better system to keep up with that and the 8,000 Hz polling rate, and... well, you get the point).
Another downside to an 8,000 Hz polling rate is battery life, because it drops significantly on wireless gaming mice. The battery life of the Corsair Sabre v2 Pro Wireless is a pretty impressive 120 hours at 1,000 Hz, but this drops to just 21 hours at 8,000 Hz. The Razer Basilisk V3 Pro 35K gets up to 150 hours at 1,000 Hz, and just 28 hours at 8,000 Hz. The Turtle Beach Burst II Pro does a little better, going from 150 hours at 1,000 Hz to 40 hours at 8,000 Hz, but it's still a significant drop.
And while you can cheat the system with select Razer and Logitech gaming mice by pairing them with either the Razer HyperFlux V2 or the Logitech PowerPlay 2 wireless charging mouse pads, you will need to pair the mice to your PC using their included (or, in some cases, sold separately) 8,000 Hz dongles — neither the HyperFlux V2 nor the PowerPlay 2 offer 8,000 Hz polling rates if you connect through the built-in receivers.
But... 8,000 Hz!!
You may not need an 8,000 Hz polling rate, but maybe it will make you feel better.
If any category of gaming mouse is going to benefit from lower latency, it's the esports category — where mice need to be lightweight so they can fly across surfaces, relatively small so they can be picked up when sliding them is too time-consuming, and hyper speedy and accurate so competitors can shoot people in the head without missing a beat. And so it's not surprising that flagship gaming mice like the Razer DeathAdder V4 Pro or the Asus ROG Harpe Ace Extreme (or the Asus ROG Harpe II Extreme Edition 20) tout 8,000 Hz polling rates.
But you don't have to spend a ton on an extreme edition flagship gaming mouse to max out your polling rate — several of Razer's older mice work with the company's Mouse Dock Pro and/or HyperPolling Wireless Dongle to get up to 8,000 Hz wireless polling rates, including the Razer Basilisk V3 Pro, and many of its newer mice come with 8,000 Hz polling out of the box (e.g. the Razer Viper V3 Pro, which is currently on sale for $110 at Amazon — 31% off its retail price of $160).
If you don't need a wireless mouse, Razer's DeathAdder V3 wired gaming mouse gets up to an 8,000 Hz wired polling rate (and is currently on sale for $45 at Amazon — 36% off its retail price of $70). Even Redragon, one of our favorite budget-friendly peripherals companies, has a mouse with an 8,000 Hz polling rate: the Redragon M916 ULT, which is wireless and ultra-lightweight (49g) and retails for just $50.
Ultra-high polling rates are creeping in everywhere, not just in the competitive esports market. Even Razer's recently launched V3 Naga Pro, which isn't even an ultra-lightweight, esports-oriented gaming mouse (it's a relatively hefty 23-button mouse for games that definitely do not need to worry about ultra-smooth, accurate mouse movement or click latency), can get up to an 8,000 Hz polling rate if you pair it with either the company's Mouse Dock Pro or HyperPolling Wireless Dongle (both are sold separately, naturally, because — again — you don't need this).
Corsair recently showed off its Nightsword v2 Wireless SD, a mouse with a built-in Stream Deck (sort of), which also has up to an 8,000 Hz polling rate (170 hours of battery life at 1,000 Hz, which drops to 47 hours with the lighting turned off and 25.5 hours with the lighting turned on at 8,000 Hz). And if you think that you can tell the difference between half a millisecond but not that extra quarter, there are also mice with up to 4,000 Hz polling rates, such as the HyperX Pulsefire Saga Pro and the SteelSeries Aerox 3 Wireless Gen 2.
And as for whether you need a keyboard with an 8,000 Hz polling rate, the answer is: absolutely not.
Sarah Jacobsson Purewal is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware covering peripherals, software, and custom builds. You can find more of her work in PCWorld, Macworld, TechHive, CNET, Gizmodo, Tom's Guide, PC Gamer, Men's Health, Men's Fitness, SHAPE, Cosmopolitan, and just about everywhere else.

articles.title: Guía para limpiar tu cuenta de Gmail y ganar espacio sin pagar ninguna suscripción
articles.text:
Toda cuenta de Gmail dispone de 15 gigabytes gratuitos de almacenamiento, un espacio que se comparte con Google Drive y Google Fotos. Cuando ese límite se agota, no es necesario contratar un plan pago de Google: borrar correos con archivos adjuntos y vaciar las carpetas de eliminación permite recuperar capacidad de forma inmediata.
Los mensajes de texto sin adjuntos ocupan, en general, poco espacio dentro de la bandeja de entrada. El consumo real se concentra en los correos que incluyen videos, archivos PDF o fotografías de gran tamaño. Gmail permite localizar ese tipo de mensajes mediante filtros de búsqueda, disponibles tanto desde el teléfono como desde una computadora.
Cómo localizar los correos que más espacio ocupan
Para identificar los mensajes con adjuntos pesados, el usuario puede escribir en el buscador el comando has:attachment larger:10M, que reúne los correos con archivos adjuntos superiores a los 10 megabytes. Esa cifra puede reemplazarse por 15M o 20M según se necesite concentrar la búsqueda en los archivos de mayor peso.
Una vez revisado el contenido de esos mensajes, el usuario puede seleccionar los que ya no necesite y enviarlos a la Papelera. Sin embargo, esa acción por sí sola no libera espacio de manera definitiva: el correo permanece almacenado hasta que se elimina por completo.
Gmail también permite filtrar comunicaciones antiguas con el comando older_than:2y, que agrupa los mensajes recibidos hace más de dos años. Esta búsqueda puede combinarse con has:attachment para ubicar correos viejos que, además, incluyan archivos adjuntos.
Una vez desplegada la lista de resultados, el sistema ofrece la casilla superior para marcar los mensajes y la opción “Seleccionar todas las conversaciones que coincidan con esta búsqueda”. El ícono de la Papelera permite entonces eliminar todo el conjunto en un solo paso.
Boletines, publicidad y notificaciones acumuladas
Las suscripciones a boletines promocionales y las notificaciones automáticas constituyen otra fuente habitual de correos prescindibles. El buscador de Gmail permite localizar esos mensajes con los términos unsubscribe o “darse de baja”, que identifican las comunicaciones vinculadas a listas de distribución.
La eliminación de correos con adjuntos, publicidad y notificaciones reduce el volumen de contenido almacenado, aunque el espacio seguirá ocupado hasta completar un paso adicional: borrar de forma permanente los mensajes de la Papelera y de la carpeta de correo no deseado.
Vaciar la papelera y el correo no deseado
La carpeta de Spam incluye la opción “Borrar todos los mensajes de spam ahora”, que elimina de manera definitiva los correos clasificados en esa categoría. La Papelera ofrece una función equivalente a través del botón “Vaciar la papelera ahora”. Sin ese paso final, los mensajes enviados allí no liberan capacidad real dentro de la cuenta.
Qué hacer si el espacio sigue cerca del límite
Si, tras la limpieza de la bandeja de entrada, el almacenamiento continúa cerca del tope de 15 gigabytes, es posible que el consumo provenga de archivos guardados en Drive o en Google Fotos. La herramienta gratuita Administrador de Almacenamiento de Google One analiza el contenido de los tres servicios y muestra fotos, videos y archivos pesados que pueden eliminarse con un clic.
En el caso de Google Fotos, quienes no necesiten conservar sus imágenes en calidad original pueden activar la opción “Alta calidad”, que permite almacenar fotos y videos con restricciones de resolución y así reducir el espacio que consumen dentro de Drive. Otra alternativa consiste en descargar las imágenes y los videos a un disco duro externo o trasladarlos a otro servicio de almacenamiento en la nube, de modo que la copia de respaldo no permanezca en la misma cuenta.
Las funciones gratuitas de Google One y los planes pagos
El uso del Administrador de Almacenamiento de Google One no exige ninguna suscripción. El servicio de pago aparece recién cuando el usuario decide ampliar la cuota disponible en lugar de eliminar archivos.
Los planes de Google One permiten elevar la capacidad total a 100 gigabytes, 200 gigabytes o 2 terabytes, y esa ampliación se comparte del mismo modo entre Gmail, Drive y Fotos. El acceso a Gmail, Google Drive, Google Fotos, Docs, Sheets, Meet y Calendar está incluido sin costo en toda cuenta de Google. También forman parte de las funciones gratuitas el filtro de correo no deseado y la verificación en dos pasos.

articles.title: Prime Day : cette batterie INIU de 20 000 mAh à 26,99 € chez Amazon booste l’autonomie de vos appareils
articles.text:
La batterie externe INIU permet de recharger smartphone, tablette et console portable où que vous soyez. Jusqu’à ce soir, les membres Prime peuvent l’obtenir à 26,99 € chez Amazon, contre 36,99 € en temps normal.
Les dernières heures des Jours Flash Prime se déroulent en ce moment même. Si vous cherchez à vous équiper d’une batterie externe afin de pouvoir recharger facilement vos appareils portables, vous pouvez opter pour la Power Bank INIU de 20 000 mAh, disponible à 26,99 € chez Amazon. Ce modèle délivre jusqu’à 45 W et intègre un câble USB-C directement dans son boîtier. Il s’adresse aux voyageurs, aux étudiants et aux personnes qui utilisent beaucoup leur smartphone (ou leur Nintendo Switch) loin d’une prise.
La batterie externe INIU 20 000 mAh 45 W est à 26,99 € chez Amazon pour les membres Prime jusqu’à ce soir.
Pour profiter des Jours Flash Prime n'oubliez pas de devenir membre Amazon Prime. Vous bénéficiez d'un essai gratuit de 30 jours, c'est donc le bon moment pour tester.
Pourquoi choisir cette batterie externe INIU ?
- Pour sa capacité : les 20 000 mAh constituent une réserve pour plusieurs recharges de smartphone, trois à quatre fois en moyenne selon le modèle.
- Pour son câble intégré : vous pouvez brancher directement un appareil USB-C sans emporter de cordon supplémentaire.
- Pour sa charge rapide : elle fournit jusqu’à 45 W à un appareil compatible, avec la prise en charge des protocoles PD et PPS.
Un accessoire pratique pour les longues journées
Que vous soyez du genre à oublier de recharger votre smartphone la nuit ou que vous aimiez jouer à des jeux mobiles gourmands dans les transports en commun, cette batterie peut vous offrir plusieurs heures d’utilisation supplémentaire au quotidien. Son affichage numérique indique le niveau de charge restant, ce qui évite d’être pris au dépourvu lorsqu’elle est presque vide. En complément du câble intégré, elle dispose d’un port USB-C et d’un port USB-A pour alimenter jusqu’à trois appareils simultanément. Attention cependant : INIU indique une puissance totale limitée à 15 W en charge simultanée, contre 45 W au maximum sur une seule sortie USB-C.
Une réserve généreuse qui peut nécessiter une grande poche
Une capacité de 20 000 mAh assure plusieurs charges de smartphone et de tablette, et la batterie est autorisée dans les cabines des avions. En revanche, avec environ 326 g et 2,9 cm d’épaisseur, elle sera moins discrète dans une poche qu’une petite batterie de dépannage.
✅ Les points forts
- Capacité de 20 000 mAh.
- Câble USB-C intégré.
- Jusqu’à 45 W pour un appareil compatible.
❌ Les limites
- Puissance totale réduite à 15 W en charge multiple.
- Poids d’environ 326 g.
Pratique et endurante, cette batterie INIU noire coûte 26,99 € aujourd’hui chez Amazon.
À ce tarif, cette batterie INIU constitue une réserve utile pour les utilisateurs réguliers de smartphones et de tablettes, avec un câble toujours disponible. Et elle est compatible avec les consoles portables !
Cependant, si vous désirez simplement prolonger l’autonomie de votre smartphone en rentrant chez vous après une journée de travail, vous pouvez aussi opter pour une batterie avec une capacité plus réduite, et donc plus facile à transporter.
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Comment profiter des Jours Flash Prime ?
Afin de profiter des Jours Flash Amazon Prime, vous devez avant tout souscrire à un abonnement Amazon Prime. Pour ça, rien de plus simple, il vous suffit de créer un compte Amazon puis de souscrire à l'une des offres Amazon Prime :
- Amazon Prime à 69€ par an
- Amazon Prime à 6,99€/mois
- Amazon Prime Student 3,49€/mois (pour les étudiants et les 18-22 ans)
Si vous n'avez jamais été abonné, Amazon vous permet de bénéficier d'un essai gratuit de 30 jours au service Amazon Prime.

articles.title: PoeLLM Malware Infects 3,400+ Servers to Expand Crypto Mining Botnet
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers are calling attention to a new malware family that has been observed targeting exposed artificial intelligence (AI) and large language model (LLM) infrastructure with an aim to deploy cryptocurrency miners and further expand the scale of the botnet.
The financially motivated campaign, dubbed Canto Incognito, has been found to install cryptocurrency miners, including XMRig and Iron, and connects victims to Kryptex, a Russian cryptocurrency mining service.
"Compromised hosts are reused to expand the botnet," Lumen Black Lotus Labs said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "Infected servers are turned into scanners and exploit servers, allowing the actor to find and compromise additional vulnerable systems."
The malware distributed as part of the campaign has been codenamed PoeLLM owing to what has been described as a "creative" technique that hides the command-and-control (C2) address within a poem the threat actors wrote and hosted in a GitHub repository ("github[.]com/ejejejdfbbebe"). The first commit to the repository was on April 13, 2026.
"Each time they set up a new C2, they change a few words in the poem, and the malware derives the address from the key associated with those words," Ryan English, information security engineer at Lumen Technologies, told The Hacker News.
The attacks have been primarily found to single out enterprise, internet-facing deployments such as LiteLLM and Gotenberg, as well as Gitea and Ivanti Sentry appliances.
| C2 Extraction Logic | 
The targeting of these LLM instances is no coincidence as the intention is to abuse their compute power for illicit cryptocurrency mining. Evidence indicates that the malware has been active since April 2026, with more than 3400 victim servers identified so far. The infections are concentrated in the U.S. and Western Europe.
"At the peak of operations in mid-June, the campaign involved almost 2,200 affected servers, with nearly 800 active per day," the cybersecurity company said. "More recent traffic toward SSH and other login portals suggests experimentation with distributed brute-force attacks; that capability’s maturity remains uncertain."
Another notable aspect of the campaign is that it repurposes some of the compromised systems to scan the internet for similar instances, send an HTTP POST request to exposed ports on identified targets that instruct them to download the malware from the C2.
Lumen Black Lotus Labs has attributed the activity to an Italian-speaking threat actor with moderate confidence based on the presence of Italian-language artifacts and netflow indicators. The end goal of the campaign is to weaponize known vulnerabilities in publicly exposed services to enlist them into a cryptocurrency mining botnet and convert a subset of them into a scanner to expand the victim pool.
"AI infrastructure is becoming an attractive target," Lumen said. "Exposed AI/LLM services are valuable not only because of software vulnerabilities, but also because they may contain useful data and run on powerful hardware suitable for mining."

articles.title: Who else can match Samsung's end-to-end $1bn AI infrastructure bet?
articles.text:
Moving beyond chips and screens: Samsung joins Nvidia and KKR in a massive $1 billion data center infrastructure deal
Samsung's extensive capacity is a major advantage
- Samsung and five affiliates are putting $1 billion into Helix Digital Infrastructure
- KKR founded Helix in June 2026, with Nvidia and Vistra among investors
- Helix will secure power capacity, which limits how quickly data centers open
Samsung and five affiliated businesses are committing $1 billion to Helix Digital Infrastructure, deepening the group's involvement in the backbones of artificial intelligence.
Samsung Electronics will provide $500 million, while five other affiliates supply the remaining investment through the venture.
The commitment combines semiconductor expertise, cooling equipment, construction, computing services, batteries, and infrastructure financing within one corporate strategy.
Samsung brings multiple infrastructure capabilities together
Helix, established by KKR in June 2026, is intended to develop data centers while securing electricity and network connections
Its founding investors also include Nvidia, Kuwait Investment Authority, and US electricity company Vistra, adding financial and energy capabilities.
Samsung's involvement extends beyond its financial commitment because several affiliated businesses can contribute technologies and services needed to develop and operate data centers.
Samsung Electronics contributes memory technology, and its FläktGroup subsidiary provides cooling systems for data centers.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Samsung C&T can handle major engineering and construction projects, with Samsung SDS developing data centers and providing rented GPU computing capacity.
Samsung SDI adds batteries for uninterrupted power systems, supporting facilities where servers must operate continuously without electricity interruptions.
The group therefore controls several functions that competitors would typically obtain from separate equipment manufacturers, contractors, technology providers, and infrastructure companies.
Samsung says the arrangement could help it move from supplying hardware toward participating directly in building artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Helix also plans to obtain power capacity, making electricity availability an important part of its proposed development model
That approach gives Samsung exposure to infrastructure requirements extending beyond processors, memory products, cooling equipment, and computing systems.
Huawei and SoftBank appear closest among rivals
Samsung's breadth is a major advantage, and few rivals can compete with such an extensive combination of infrastructure capabilities.
Huawei is among the closest comparisons, with capabilities spanning Ascend processors, storage, networking, security, cooling equipment, and electricity infrastructure.
That range gives Huawei significant technical reach, although the company may not have a comparable $1 billion infrastructure commitment.
SoftBank also has semiconductor interests through Arm, Ampere Computing, and Graphcore, as well as plans for an artificial intelligence facility in Ohio.
Its combination of chip businesses and infrastructure ambitions gives it substantial reach, although matching Samsung would still require capabilities from multiple businesses.
Nokia offers networking products for artificial intelligence facilities and has attracted investment from Nvidia, but its role remains concentrated around connectivity technologies.
Ericsson's work with SoftBank focuses on artificial intelligence applications for cellular networks rather than developing complete computing campuses and supporting infrastructure.
The difference is that Samsung can draw on affiliated businesses for capital, components, construction, cooling, computing, and battery systems within the same corporate group.
Huawei may be closest in technological range, while SoftBank has substantial semiconductor resources and growing ambitions around AI infrastructure, but neither company can combine these capabilities through affiliated businesses as extensively as Samsung does.

articles.title: Qué es intranet, para qué sirve y cómo se ha usado en gobiernos, universidades y escuelas
articles.text:
Las organizaciones recurren cada vez más a redes privadas de comunicación interna para ordenar su funcionamiento diario. Una intranet permite a empleados, docentes, estudiantes o funcionarios acceder a información, gestionar trámites y colaborar entre sí dentro de un entorno cerrado y protegido, distinto de internet.
Esta herramienta se ha extendido tanto en el sector privado como en instituciones públicas, universidades y escuelas, donde cumple funciones específicas según las necesidades de cada comunidad.
A diferencia de una red abierta, la intranet exige autenticación mediante credenciales y aplica medidas de seguridad adicionales para proteger datos sensibles. Funciona mediante la interconexión de computadoras, servidores y otros dispositivos, y utiliza protocolos similares a los de internet, como HTTP y HTTPS, pero restringidos al uso interno.
Qué es una intranet y cuál es su función principal
Una intranet es una red privada pensada para uso exclusivo dentro de una organización, con el objetivo de agilizar la comunicación, centralizar la información y facilitar la colaboración entre sus integrantes. Es, en esencia, una versión interna de internet que da acceso a aplicaciones, sistemas de gestión y herramientas de trabajo compartido, como correo electrónico interno, calendarios, repositorios de documentos y directorios de contacto.
Su funcionamiento se sostiene en servidores que almacenan y gestionan los datos y recursos que utilizan los distintos usuarios de la red. Cada persona ingresa con sus propias credenciales, lo que garantiza que solo el personal autorizado pueda ver cierta información.
Esta estructura cerrada reduce la exposición a ataques externos y permite a cada institución decidir qué contenidos son visibles para cada perfil de usuario.
La utilidad de una intranet depende del tipo de organización que la implementa. En empresas, sirve para mejorar la productividad y centralizar recursos. En el ámbito público y educativo, en cambio, adopta formas particulares: desde la gestión de expedientes administrativos en un ministerio, hasta el seguimiento de calificaciones de un alumno por parte de sus padres.
Cómo se utiliza la intranet en gobiernos y administración pública
En el sector público, la intranet funciona como soporte operativo para funcionarios y empleados estatales. Permite centralizar boletines oficiales, normativas internas y protocolos de actuación en un mismo espacio, de modo que toda la información regulatoria esté disponible sin depender de archivos físicos dispersos.
También sirve para gestionar trámites propios del personal, como solicitudes de vacaciones, nóminas, viáticos y evaluaciones de desempeño. Estas tareas, que antes requerían formularios en papel o gestiones presenciales, se resuelven dentro de la misma plataforma digital.
Otro uso frecuente es la coordinación entre distintas dependencias del Estado. La intranet habilita canales seguros para que ministerios o departamentos intercambien información confidencial sin recurrir a redes públicas, lo que reduce riesgos de filtración.
A esto se suma la incorporación de flujos de aprobación digital, que incluyen firma electrónica y seguimiento de expedientes administrativos. Esta función permite disminuir el uso de papel en las dependencias estatales y acelerar los tiempos de resolución de trámites internos.
El rol de la intranet en universidades y educación superior
En las universidades, la intranet suele dividirse en dos grandes áreas: una orientada al personal administrativo y docente, y otra dirigida a los estudiantes a través de un portal o campus virtual. Por el lado académico, permite gestionar la inscripción y matriculación en asignaturas, consultar horarios, revisar el historial de notas y solicitar certificados o títulos.
El acceso a aulas virtuales y repositorios de investigación es otro componente central. A través de la intranet, estudiantes y académicos pueden consultar bases de datos científicas con licencia institucional, entregar tareas y participar en foros de discusión vinculados a sus cursos.
La plataforma también cubre servicios directos al estudiante, como la reserva de libros en biblioteca, el pago de colegiatura, la solicitud de becas y la gestión de servicios de residencia o transporte universitario. Estas funciones reducen la necesidad de trámites presenciales en las oficinas de la institución.
Por último, la intranet universitaria cumple un papel de comunicación institucional: envía notificaciones masivas sobre fechas de exámenes, eventos académicos, convocatorias de investigación y avisos emitidos por el rectorado, de forma que toda la comunidad reciba la misma información de manera simultánea.
Cómo funciona la intranet en escuelas y colegios
En la educación básica y media, la intranet está diseñada para conectar a tres actores: directivos y docentes, alumnos, y padres de familia. Uno de sus usos más extendidos es el portal para padres, que permite el seguimiento en tiempo real de la asistencia, las calificaciones, los boletines escolares, las citaciones con profesores y la conducta de los estudiantes.
Desde el punto de vista pedagógico, la intranet se utiliza para publicar calendarios de exámenes, listas de útiles escolares, tareas diarias y material didáctico descargable, de manera que alumnos y familias tengan acceso directo a esa información sin depender exclusivamente de comunicaciones impresas.
También habilita canales de mensajería directa entre profesores y apoderados, pensados para evitar el uso de redes sociales o aplicaciones de chat personales con fines escolares. Esto ordena la comunicación institucional y deja un registro formal de los intercambios.
En el plano administrativo, la intranet escolar permite controlar matrículas, gestionar el cobro de pensiones o cuotas y tramitar autorizaciones para salidas de campo u otras actividades fuera del establecimiento. De este modo, la gestión diaria del colegio queda concentrada en una sola plataforma, accesible para cada perfil de usuario según su rol dentro de la institución.

articles.title: Get a great deal on the original MSI Claw during Best Buy clearance sale — handheld with Intel Core Ultra 7 155H and 1TB SSD is just $562, $187 off list price
articles.text:
Get a great deal on the original MSI Claw during Best Buy clearance sale — handheld with Intel Core Ultra 7 155H and 1TB SSD is just $562, $187 off list price
Gaming handhelds are expensive, but the price on the MSI Claw A1M is reasonable during Best Buy's clearance sale.
The original MSI Claw (A1M) was forgotten about almost as quickly as it launched, being the first handheld from MSI, and the first one to sport an Intel CPU (in this case, the Core Ultra 7 155H from the Meteor Lake family). Unsurprisingly, Best Buy has the handheld on clearance, and right now it's available for a surprisingly good price of $562.99 considering how expensive newer handhelds are.
In this case of handheld gaming PC, this is the cheapest option you can get right now. Even the ROG Xbox Ally with the Ryzen Z2 A and 512GB of storage is $600. Handhelds with 1TB of storage and the Ryzen Z1 Extreme (the chip Intel originally targeted) will run you north of $1,000.
In both build quality and layout, the A1M is nearly a carbon copy of the original Asus ROG Ally. It sports a 7-inch 1080p display with a 120Hz refresh rate, a single USB-C port for charging and peripherals, and a microSD card slot for storage expansion; though, you can replace the SSD inside, as well.
The MSI Claw A1M is a handheld gaming PC with the Intel Core Ultra 7 155H, 16GB of memory, and a 1TB SSD. It comes with a 1080p display with a 120Hz refresh rate.
This is a great deal considering the price of handhelds right now, especially those packing 1TB of storage, but the A1M was glossed over quickly for a reason. The Meteor Lake chip inside wasn't built for handheld gaming, so although it offers decent performance, it does so at relatively high power draw.
In a game like Horizon Zero Dawn, it's able to achieve around 30 FPS at native 1080p with the Balanced power plan, which uses a 30W target. Plugged in with a full 40W power budget, the game can crack 30 FPS in titles like Cyberpunk 2077 with the Steam Deck preset.
It falls between 5% and 10% short of the Z1 Extreme, and with worse battery life. With prices equal, we'd normally recommend the ROG Ally. Considering the price gap, the A1M is worth considering. The software isn't as clear as what you get with an Asus handheld, but MSI has made dozens of updates to its firmware and overlay software since the original A1M launched.
Performance is less of a concern than battery life, with the Meteor Lake chip sucking down quite a bit of power relative to modern PC handhelds. That's not a dealbreaker at this price, but make sure to have a quality USB-C charger at the ready.

articles.title: Si la cámara del celular se activa sola o hay aplicaciones desconocidas instaladas, positivo para espionaje
articles.text:
Una cámara que se enciende sin intervención del usuario y la presencia de aplicaciones desconocidas en el listado de apps instaladas figuran entre las señales más claras de que un teléfono fue hackeado, según un análisis de la empresa de ciberseguridad ESET. Ambas alertas están vinculadas a la actividad de spyware, un software malicioso que permite a los ciberdelincuentes acceder de forma remota a la cámara del dispositivo o reflejar su pantalla sin autorización.
La cámara puede activarse sin dejar rastro visible
El comportamiento inesperado de la cámara constituye uno de los primeros indicios de infección. El teléfono puede encenderla por cuenta propia, aunque ciertos tipos de spyware desactivan el punto verde que normalmente advierte sobre el uso de esta función, con lo que ocultan su actividad frente al usuario.
También puede darse la situación inversa: que el propietario no logre acceder a la cámara porque otra aplicación la está utilizando en ese momento, circunstancia que el propio sistema operativo suele notificar.
A este indicio se suma la aparición de fotos o videos en la galería que el usuario no recuerda haber capturado. Este tipo de archivo, generado sin conocimiento del propietario del dispositivo, representa una de las pruebas más directas de que alguien tomó control de la cámara de forma remota, según el análisis de ESET.
El consumo de batería y de datos delata actividad oculta
El spyware instalado de manera encubierta demanda energía de forma constante, incluso cuando el teléfono permanece sin uso. Por ese motivo, un consumo de batería superior al habitual y el sobrecalentamiento del equipo funcionan como indicadores de alerta.
El envío de la información capturada también requiere conexión a internet. Los ciberdelincuentes que acceden de forma remota a un dispositivo necesitan transferir las imágenes obtenidas, por lo que un aumento repentino en el consumo de datos o en la factura mensual puede evidenciar transferencias de archivos ajenas al usuario.
Fallos de rendimiento y apps desconocidas completan el cuadro
El malware no solo agota la batería: también consume recursos del sistema. Esto puede traducirse en el cierre inesperado de aplicaciones, lentitud general o, en casos extremos, falta de respuesta del dispositivo. Los reinicios sin motivo aparente o el encendido de pantalla sin intervención del usuario son otras señales que pueden apuntar a una manipulación remota del equipo.
El spyware diseñado para espiar suele instalarse bajo la apariencia de una aplicación legítima. Dado que muchos usuarios tienen decenas de apps instaladas, una adicional puede pasar inadvertida, por lo que ESET recomienda revisar de forma periódica el listado completo de aplicaciones presentes en el teléfono.
Medidas de prevención ante esta amenaza
Entre las medidas de prevención figura la revisión periódica de los permisos otorgados a cada aplicación, con el fin de revocar el acceso a la cámara o el micrófono cuando no resulte necesario para su funcionamiento. También se recomienda instalar software de seguridad de un proveedor externo confiable y mantener actualizados tanto el sistema operativo como las aplicaciones.
Descargar aplicaciones únicamente desde Apple App Store o Google Play disminuye las probabilidades de instalar software malicioso disfrazado de app legítima. En Europa, Apple está obligada a permitir tiendas de terceros para iOS, aunque la recomendación general es evitarlas. Hacer jailbreak o rootear el dispositivo también eleva el riesgo, ya que deshabilita medidas de seguridad, limita las actualizaciones automáticas y expone al equipo a aplicaciones maliciosas.
Proteger el dispositivo con un PIN seguro y autenticación biométrica, junto con contraseñas únicas almacenadas en un gestor dedicado, dificulta el acceso de terceros a las aplicaciones y cuentas del usuario. Quienes buscan una protección adicional pueden colocar una pegatina sobre el lente de la cámara cuando no la utilizan.
Las redes wifi públicas representan otro punto de vulnerabilidad: si los datos que circulan no están cifrados, un ciberdelincuente podría espiar la navegación o redirigir al usuario hacia sitios maliciosos. El phishing continúa siendo uno de los principales vectores de infección, mediante correos que generan urgencia para inducir al clic en enlaces o archivos adjuntos.
Qué hacer ante una infección confirmada
Ante la sospecha de acceso no autorizado, se recomienda ejecutar un análisis con una aplicación de seguridad confiable, desinstalar programas sospechosos o instalados recientemente y revisar los permisos de cámara otorgados sin justificación clara. Actualizar el software completo del dispositivo dificulta la acción de amenazas ya presentes.
Si los problemas de comportamiento persisten pese a estas medidas, puede resultar necesario un restablecimiento de fábrica o la restauración del equipo desde una copia de seguridad. Las amenazas contra los teléfonos inteligentes pueden originarse en la búsqueda de datos para vender en la dark web, en acecho personal o en vigilancia por parte de organismos gubernamentales o policiales.

articles.title: The Sixth Voice of the CISO Data Shows Cyber Risk Has Moved Inside the Workflow
articles.text:
The 2026 findings are not just a year-over-year shift. They mark the latest point in a five-year arc where resilience, AI governance, human risk, and board scrutiny are converging inside the systems where work actually happens.
For years, the enterprise cybersecurity story has been told as a straight line of escalation: more attacks, more data loss, more pressure, and more urgency. That narrative is still familiar, but comparing the five most recent years of Voice of the CISO research suggests a more useful reading. The CISO role has not simply become harder because every metric is rising at once. It has become harder because the center of risk has shifted and moved closer to the way work now gets done.
The latest 2026 findings show signs of progress. Fewer CISOs expect a material cyberattack in the next 12 months, and fewer report material loss of sensitive information than in 2025. But those improvements sit within a longer trend line that is much less settled. Over five years, attack expectations have risen, fallen, and risen again. Board alignment has swung sharply. Human risk has remained stubbornly central. AI has moved from an emerging concern to defining mandate. The result is not a simple story of improvement or decline. It is a story of risk changing location.
That distinction matters because it changes what security leaders should be optimizing for. The question for CISOs is no longer only, "What threat will hit us next?" It is becoming, "Where does critical work happen, who or what has access to it, and can the organization protect sensitive data as it moves across people, cloud platforms, collaboration tools, SaaS applications, and AI-enabled workflows?"
The five-year trend is not linear
The year-over-year (YoY) movement from 2025 to 2026 is important, but it doesn’t tell the whole story. The five-year view shows a profession that has been forced to absorb and manage wave after wave of change rather than follow a smooth maturity curve.
The value of the five-year view is that it resists easy conclusions. Attack expectations cooled in 2026 after a 2025 high, but they remain above 2022. Reported data loss fell YoY, but more than half of CISOs still report material loss and preparedness barely moved. Board alignment rebounded to its highest level in the series, but excessive expectations also rose concurrently. Taken together, the data trends across the years point to a security function that is gaining visibility and support while also being asked to govern a much wider operating environment.
AI turned the CISO agenda from protection to governance
AI is the clearest example of how quickly that operating environment has changed. In 2024, 54% of CISOs said GenAI was a security risk. That rose to 60% in 2025 and 78% in 2026. Over the same period, the business conversation around AI has moved from experimentation to embedded use, with assistants, copilots, automation, and agentic workflows becoming part of daily work.
The instinct to restrict access is understandable, and many organizations are doing exactly that. In 2026, 78% of CISOs say their organization blocks or restricts employee use of GenAI tools, up from 59% in 2025. But restriction is not the same as governance. As AI becomes embedded in productivity suites, collaboration platforms, SaaS tools, and business workflows, a simple allow-or-block model becomes too blunt for how work actually happens.
The more durable question is whether organizations can govern AI in context. What data can a user access? What is the AI tool allowed to summarize, generate, or act on? What happens when an assistant, agent, or automation moves from answering a question to influencing a decision or triggering an action?
This is where the AI conversation becomes a data security conversation. AI risk is not only about prompts, models, or hallucinations. It is about sensitive information, identity, permissions, intent, and control. That makes the resource signal in the 2026 report especially important: 79% of CISOs say they are expected to manage AI-related risks without a proportional increase in resources or expertise. The gap is no longer awareness. It is operational capacity.
Human risk is no longer a soft problem
Across the five-year trend set, human risk remains one of the most persistent signals. The wording has evolved over time, from human error to human risk, but the direction is clear enough to matter: 56% in 2022, 60% in 2023, 74% in 2024, 66% in 2025, and 79% in 2026 identified human risk or error as the biggest cyber vulnerability.
That should change how organizations discuss the topic. Human risk is often treated as a training problem, but the 2026 findings show it is much more than that. Among organizations that experienced material data loss, 93% say departing employees played a role. The leading root causes of material data loss were malicious or criminal insiders, careless insiders, compromised insiders, misuse or misconfiguration of AI tools, external attacks, and third-party compromise. In other words, data loss increasingly sits at the intersection of behavior, identity, access, permissions, tooling, and intent.
This is why human risk should be viewed as a systems problem with a human interface. A user may be malicious, careless, compromised, over-permissioned, under-governed, or simply working inside a process that gives them more access than the business can justify. Awareness training still has a role, but it cannot carry the burden alone. Organizations need to understand behavior in context: who the user is, what data they are touching, whether access is appropriate, whether the action is unusual, and whether a change in role, employment status, or intent has altered the risk.
The boardroom is closer to the problem, but not necessarily closer to resolution
The board trend is one of the most revealing five-year signals because it has not moved in a straight line. In 2022, 51% of CISOs said their board saw eye to eye with them on cybersecurity. That rose to 62% in 2023 and 84% in 2024, fell to 64% in 2025, and rebounded to 85% in 2026. That volatility is important. It suggests that cybersecurity has a firmer place on the board agenda, but alignment still depends on how effectively CISOs can communicate and translate technical risk into commercial risk, operational resilience, regulatory exposure, and customer trust.
The issues boards are perceived to care about reinforce this commercial framing. CISOs say their boards are concerned about business valuation, significant downtime, reputational damage, loss of sensitive information, disruption to operations, loss of current customers, and loss in revenue. That list reads less like a security operations dashboard and more like an enterprise risk agenda.
That creates an opportunity for CISOs, but it also raises expectations. In 2026, 77% of CISOs say excessive expectations are placed on the CISO or CSO, up from 66% in 2025 and from 49% in 2022. Better board alignment has not made the role lighter. It has made the role more visible, more commercial, and more accountable for risk that now spans people, data, identity, AI, regulation, and business continuity.
The next phase of resilience will be decided inside the flow of work
The practical takeaway from five years of CISO data is not that the threat landscape has become less dangerous. It is that danger has become more operationally embedded. Security strategy needs to reflect where work now happens, which means treating identity, collaboration platforms, SaaS applications, cloud repositories, endpoints, APIs, automation, and AI systems as part of the same risk fabric rather than as separate control domains.
For CISOs, several priorities follow. AI governance should be treated as a data security and decision-control issue, not only as an acceptable-use policy. Human risk should be managed across the employee lifecycle, especially during role changes, privilege expansion, contractor access, and employee departures. Board reporting should move from threat volume to business consequence, helping directors understand how cyber exposure maps to the business concerns of valuation, downtime, customer trust, regulatory impact, and resilience. Control effectiveness should be measured where work actually happens, not only where traditional security tools have historically been deployed.
The more thought-provoking conclusion is that cybersecurity's center of gravity has shifted from the perimeter to the workflow. The modern enterprise is not secured only by stopping attacks at the edge. It is secured by understanding how people, data, identity, applications, and intelligent systems interact every day.
That is the CISO mandate now. Not just to prevent the next incident, but to help the business work safely in the places where risk and productivity have become inseparable.
See what 1,600 global CISOs revealed about AI, human risk, and cyber resilience in the 2026 Voice of the CISO report. Download the report.
Source: Proofpoint Voice of the CISO reports and annual findings, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026.
Note: This article has been expertly written and contributed by Patrick Joyce, Global Resident CISO, Proofpoint.

articles.title: Introuvable, la PS5 Pro d'occasion en passe d'être vendue 1 500 dollars chez ce revendeur ?
articles.text:
À l’approche de GTA 6, la PS5 Pro devient particulièrement difficile à trouver aux États-Unis (comme ailleurs). Une situation qui commence à produire des tarifs pour le moins surprenants sur le marché de l’occasion.
Depuis son lancement en novembre 2024, la PS5 Pro, affichée alors à 799 € (sans lecteur de disque), n’a jamais été une console bon marché. Mais à l’approche de la sortie de GTA 6, le tarif demandé pour mettre la main sur le modèle le plus puissant de la gamme PlayStation prend une tournure assez inattendue. Aux États-Unis, l’un des plus importants revendeurs spécialisés du pays n’exclut pas de proposer certaines PS5 Pro d’occasion jusqu’à 1 500 dollars selon Kotaku.
La PS5 Pro d’occasion (beaucoup) plus chère que la neuve ?
L’information provient initialement d’une note interne attribuée au réseau GameStop, avant qu’une PS5 Pro d’occasion soit effectivement apparue sur le site américain de l’enseigne au prix délirant de 1 399,99 dollars. D’autres variantes pourraient atteindre les 1 500 dollars. Un tarif d’autant plus difficile à digérer que le prix conseillé d’une PS5 Pro neuve est actuellement fixé à 899 dollars « seulement » outre-Atlantique.
Bien sûr, le contexte actuel on ne peut plus tendu concernant la PS5 Pro explique en partie cette décision. Depuis quelques jours déjà, les stocks de PS5 Pro neuves sont très limités, tandis que la perspective de jouer à GTA 6 sur « la console la plus puissante du monde » alimente évidemment la demande.
Aussi, faute de pouvoir acheter la console neuve, certains joueurs pourraient donc être tentés de se tourner vers l’occasion. Le problème, c’est que la facture peut donc largement dépasser celle du produit neuf… Le 2 avril dernier, Sony procédait à une hausse généralisée des tarifs de sa gamme PlayStation, avec une PS5 Pro alors révisée à 899,99 euros (toujours sans lecteur) en Europe.
Au Japon, Sony prend le problème à l’envers
Cette situation fait forcément écho à une autre actualité récente concernant la PS5 Pro au Japon. Sur l’archipel, Sony a récemment mis en place un système destiné à réserver l’achat de PS5 Pro neuves à des joueurs déjà actifs sur PlayStation.
Pour participer au tirage au sort organisé via le Sony Store japonais, il faut notamment avoir cumulé au moins 60 heures de jeu sur deux ans. L’objectif est cette fois clairement affiché, à savoir limiter les achats destinés à la revente et tenter de contrer les terribles scalpers.
En France aussi, la rupture est généralisée, et Micromania avait récemment ouvert les vannes pour de nouvelles commandes, avec quelques livraisons prévues pour ce mois d’octobre.
Avec GTA 6 attendu dans un peu plus d’un mois maintenant, la tension autour de la console de Sony pourrait encore monter d’un cran. Bien sûr, rien n’empêchera de jouer au dernier-né de Rockstar Games sur une PS5 classique (qui vient de bénéficier de la nouvelle technologie d’upscaling QSSR), ainsi que sur Xbox Series.
- Améliorations graphiques significatives
- Technologie PSSR efficace quand bien implémentée
- Efficacité énergétique

articles.title: 'Yes, we will make that change': Elon Musk says SpaceXAI will be renamed — but AI's 'Super Intelligence' rebrand is running ahead of the technology
articles.text:
Elon Musk is renaming SpaceXAI to match Trump's new ‘Super Intelligence Force’ — but critics say the White House body 'isn’t the answer'
SpaceXAI is becoming SpaceXSI and Washington pretends a terminology change is a technological strategy
The U.S. government has a new task force devoted to AI — and it's decided that it would now prefer that everyone stops calling it artificial intelligence.
President Donald Trump has announced the creation of the “Super Intelligence Force,” a White House-led group that will spend the next 120 days examining the risks, opportunities, and appropriate federal response to rapidly advancing AI systems. The task force responds to mounting pressure from lawmakers and even AI company executives for stronger safeguards around increasingly capable models.
The group has a formidable remit. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will lead what is supposed to include work on cybersecurity, biosecurity, and more standards, along with reviewing how AI companies report breaches and hacks.
There is substance buried underneath the comic branding. OpenAI and Anthropic have both been dealing with increasingly uncomfortable demonstrations of what powerful models can do with cyber tools. The new task force is at least an acknowledgment that voluntary promises from AI companies cannot be the entire federal strategy.
A super rebrand
Elon Musk then entered the naming discussion, responding “Yes, we will make that change,” when asked on X whether SpaceX's AI operation would change its name from SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI.
This would be the third rebrand for the AI branch of the company and, like those other new names, doesn't actually change the technology or the business.
The SI terminology comes directly from Trump. An executive order signed in late September directs executive departments and agencies to use “Super Intelligence” and “SI” instead of “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” in official communications and other non-statutory documents.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The order argues that today's frontier systems have moved beyond merely imitating or automating human intelligence and that the new terminology better reflects their “promise, potential, and rapidly advancing capabilities.”
For now, the executive order defines “Super Intelligence” as the same technologies already covered by the federal statutory definition of artificial intelligence. It asks officials to develop a possible new federal definition within 60 days, but the immediate transformation from AI to SI is linguistic rather than architectural. And even then, seems unlikely to spread very far. SpaceXAI becoming SpaceXSI is much more about politics and branding than a technological milestone.
Notably, “superintelligence” is already used in AI discussions. It's how researchers refer to a hypothetical artificial intelligence that significantly exceeds human capabilities in many ways.
But language does shape how technology is sold and regulated, and “artificial intelligence” has accumulated plenty of baggage after several years of hallucinations, deepfakes, job anxiety, copyright fights and increasingly unsettling demonstrations of autonomous behavior.
Trump explicitly calls renaming it super intelligence a way to spin the technology more positively as something to “empower Americans, strengthen our economy, and improve the lives of the American people.”
Watchdog with a countdown
The Super Intelligence Force arrives after a White House meeting with AI leaders who signed voluntary commitments covering internal model evaluations, independent external audits, and board-level oversight. But corporate promises alone won't settle any argument about technological abilities or regulation.
Its charter gives it 120 days to develop recommendations, with the possibility that its work could be extended or transferred elsewhere. There is already disagreement about how far oversight should go.
“Greater international oversight is absolutely necessary, but concentrating responsibility in one single, global body isn’t the answer,” Nik Kairinos, CEO and co-founder of RAIDS AI said in a statement. “AI is developing far too quickly and across too many jurisdictions for one organization to effectively police it. A stronger and more realistic model would be decentralized oversight, with a broad and diverse ecosystem of AI companies monitoring and scrutinizing one another.”
The difficulty is making decentralized oversight genuinely independent when many of the organizations scrutinizing one another also share an enormous financial interest in keeping development moving quickly.
The Trump administration appears determined to avoid moving too aggressively. But AI policy has the problem of trying to govern technology that can change substantially between the drafting of a rule and its implementation. A 120-day task force is therefore potentially more useful than another years-long commission producing a report about models that nobody uses anymore.
But trying to rename AI to “SI” does not make today's models superintelligent any more than changing SpaceXAI's name makes the employees more intelligent. The Super Intelligence Force might have some value, but it won't be because of any branding exercise.
“Oversight itself needs to be continuous, distributed and capable of evolving at the same speed as the technology,” Kairinos said. “Rules and standards set by governments are then an important supporting layer. The safest AI ecosystem will be one where responsibility for keeping systems in check is shared, rather than concentrated in the hands of a single watchdog.”

articles.title: C'est fou ! SpaceX veut lever 40 milliards de dollars... simplement pour acheter des puces Nvidia
articles.text:
Les milliards vont continuer de pleuvoir sur le secteur de l'intelligence artificielle. SpaceX et Elon Musk recherchent en effet près de 40 milliards de dollars pour acquérir encore plus de GPU NVIDIA !
À la fin du mois dernier, Elon Musk expliquait que le nombre de GPU installés dans son cluster de supercalculateurs Colossus 2 allait exploser. Mais pour faire tomber des centaines de milliers d'accélérateurs IA dans l'escarcelle de SpaceX, il va falloir beaucoup, beaucoup (beaucoup !) d'argent. Et pour ce faire, le géant américain veut lever une dette incroyable !
SpaceX veut lever une somme historique de 40 milliards de dollars pour financer l'acquisition de GPU NVIDIA
Avec son entrée en Bourse historique, SpaceX avait réussi à lever une coquette somme de 75 milliards de dollars. Mais ça n'est toujours pas assez pour financer ses besoins dans l'IA, comme nous l'apprend Bloomberg.
Le média anglophone annonce en effet que SpaceX souhaite lever une somme de 40 milliards de dollars, destinée à financer l'achat de GPU NVIDIA. Dans cette opération, 10 milliards de dollars viendraient de prêts bancaires, quand les 30 milliards restants seront eux de la dette dite « investment grade » (les obligations ou titres de créance affichant un haut taux de solvabilité).
Un niveau de financement par la dette historique dans l'IA
Le fonds de capital-investissement et gestionnaire d'actif Apollo Global Management mène cette opération, qui en est encore à ses débuts (et n'est donc pas encore sûre d'aboutir). Si le tour de table avait finalement lieu, la somme serait levée l'année prochaine, en 2027.
Et même si l'on commence à avoir l'habitude des chiffres énormes dans le domaine de l'intelligence artificielle, cette levée de fonds serait tout de même un des financements par emprunt les plus importants de l'histoire - certes courte - de l'intelligence artificielle. À noter que ce n'est pas la première fois qu'Apollo travaille avec l'entreprise IA d'Elon Musk, ayant déjà notamment investi 7 milliards de dollars précédemment dans xAI, là aussi pour financer des GPU NVIDIA.

articles.title: Instagram activa la función crear y editar carruseles directamente en Edits: cómo hacerlos
articles.text:
Edits, la app de edición de Instagram competencia de CapCut, permite crear carruseles que combinan fotos, videos y texto en un mismo lienzo. La nueva función incorpora las herramientas creativas de la aplicación y otras diseñadas para este formato.
Con el editor de carruseles, una imagen puede extenderse de una diapositiva a otra y un titular puede abarcar varias piezas.
Por ejemplo, un creador puede usar una foto panorámica dividida en dos diapositivas, sumar texto sobre toda la composición y convertir el deslizamiento en parte de la narrativa.
Dan Moreno, ingeniero de diseño del equipo de edición, explicó que los carruseles fueron una de las funciones más solicitadas por los creadores. El objetivo, señaló, fue desarrollar una plataforma que acompañe formatos como los diseños fluidos, los recortes creativos y la combinación de fotos y vídeos.
Cómo crear carruseles en Edits
Para comenzar, hay que abrir Edits, ir a la pestaña Proyectos, pulsar el botón “+” y seleccionar Carrusel. Luego se pueden elegir una o más fotos y videos para incluirlos en el proyecto. La función estará disponible próximamente para Android.
El contenido se organiza sobre un lienzo continuo, donde es posible ajustar la posición de cada elemento con herramientas como la corrección de color, la escala y la rotación. Permite añadir texto, audio, filtros, ajustes, diseños y stickers creados con la herramienta de recorte.
Para sumar una diapositiva, se puede pulsar el botón “+” dentro del editor e insertar una página en blanco. Otra opción es arrastrar desde el borde derecho del carrusel.
Desde el menú de tres puntos de cada diapositiva, el usuario puede duplicarla, insertar una nueva a la izquierda o a la derecha y modificar el orden de las páginas.
La herramienta de diseño permite incorporar varias fotos en composiciones preestablecidas. Además, se puede cambiar el relleno y el espaciado de los elementos, así como editar de forma individual los ajustes y filtros de cada imagen dentro del diseño.
Qué características tienen los carruseles en Edits
La función conserva los recursos guardados en Edits, como modificaciones, colores, audio y estilos de texto.
De esa manera, los creadores pueden trasladar su identidad visual a los carruseles sin configurar nuevamente esos elementos en cada proyecto.
Como ejemplo de uso, Raven, de @Beautymavenraven, utilizó la función de carrusel para mostrar productos de maquillaje, desde la base hasta la prebase. Combinó stickers, tipografía amarilla, videos, imágenes y recortes para presentar cada producto.
Cuando el carrusel está listo, se puede compartir directamente desde Edits en Instagram o descargarlo para publicarlo en otras plataformas. Así, no es necesario exportar el archivo, volver a cargarlo ni preocuparse por una pérdida de calidad.
Qué otras funciones hay en Edits
Edits permite crear y editar vídeos, diseñar carruseles con fotos y clips, añadir texto, audio, filtros, ajustes de color y stickers creados con la herramienta de recorte. Ofrece opciones para escalar, rotar y alinear cada elemento con precisión.
La aplicación guarda colores, estilos de texto, modificaciones y otros recursos utilizados en proyectos anteriores, lo que facilita mantener una identidad visual en distintos formatos.
Una vez terminado el contenido, se puede compartir directamente en Instagram o descargarlo para publicarlo en otras plataformas.
Instagram prepara un modo “solo lectura”
Instagram evalúa un modo de solo lectura que permitiría recorrer perfiles, publicaciones e historias sin dejar registro de la actividad. La función bloquearía los “me gusta”, comentarios, seguimientos y mensajes directos, además de impedir que los usuarios sepan quién vio sus historias.
El desarrollador Alessandro Paluzzi detectó referencias a la herramienta en el código de la aplicación y compartió capturas de su posible funcionamiento.
Un portavoz de Instagram confirmó a Engadget que se trata de una exploración interna en una etapa preliminar, sin pruebas externas ni fecha de lanzamiento.

articles.title: FBI Warns FortiBleed Remains Active After Amassing 86,644 Fortinet Device Credentials
articles.text:
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Secret Service (USSS) on Tuesday warned that the FortiBleed credential harvesting campaign remains an active threat aimed at internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and secure socket layer (SSL) virtual private network (VPN) gateways.
"The campaign exploits reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage, enabling threat actors to harvest and crack authentication data at scale," the agencies said. "Initial findings indicate attackers are continuing to scan internet-exposed Fortinet firewalls using previously obtained compromised credentials."
FortiBleed was first documented by SOCRadar in Hudson Rock in June 2026, with the activity targeting thousands of Fortinet firewalls as part of a global campaign. In all, the Russian-speaking operation is estimated to have netted more than 86,644 working device credentials spanning 194 countries as of June 19, 2026.
The campaign subsequently prompted the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to urge Fortinet customers with FortiGate appliances to enable phishing-resistant authentication, terminate active SSL VPN and administrative sessions, reset Fortinet VPN and administrative passwords, use the Password-Based Key Derivation Function 2 (PBKDF2) algorithm to store administrator credentials, and review logs for signs of suspicious activity.
FortiBleed is a five-stage campaign that conducts widespread reconnaissance to identify exposed portals, gain access to those devices using credential stuffing and password spraying based on data obtained from prior leak dumps and infostealer logs, and then deploy a Go-based tool called FortigateSniffer to passively intercept authentication traffic across 24 protocols and harvest credentials and password hashes.
The password hashes are then routed to a GPU-accelerated cracking cluster that uses Hashmat and Hashtopolis for offline cracking, after which they are used to facilitate lateral movement, Active Directory enumeration, Kerberos validation, and SMB authentication. In the final stage, sensitive data from network shares is exfiltrated while stolen session cookies are used to maintain persistent, authenticated access.
"Cracked credentials were enriched, sorted, and validated, with scripts filtering out honeypots, mapping organizations, and prioritizing high-value targets based on revenue and network structure," the agencies said. "New administrative accounts were created on the firewall to maintain persistence."
With the verified credentials in hand, the attackers have been found to move deeper into victim environments, conduct enumeration, and conduct password spraying to expand access and identify privileged accounts.
In addition, the initial access is used to add new accounts to the system as a way of maintaining persistence on the appliance. Some of the commonly identified compromised account names is listed below -
- adminin
- fortiAdmin
- forticloud-sync
- admin
- fgtsecure
- pakedge
- forticloud-tech
- districtadmin
- system_config
- gttadmin
- roadmin
- itadmin
- Technical_support
- adminsslvpn
- IT_Manager
- my_admin
- support_fortinet
- fgtsec
- forti_support2
The adversary is suspected to be an initial access broker that packages the stolen information and sells it to downstream threat actors. This is evidenced by the fact that operator overlaps tying FortiBleed to INC and Lynx ransomware operations, likely indicating that the access is being abused for ransomware deployment.
"Based on initial responses, some victims may get locked out of their Fortinet devices if the threat actor either deletes or changes the password for original accounts on the system," the FBI and USSS warned.
"During the initial intrusion, threat actors create new accounts not previously on the device. In certain cases, threat actors delete existing accounts to block organizations from accessing affected devices and to maintain persistence on the system while attempting lateral movement within the environment."
If potential compromise is detected, organizations are advised to isolate the affected devices, collect necessary artifacts and logs, report the incident to the FBI and USSS, and apply relevant countermeasures to mitigate the threat.

articles.title: Think you could contain a rogue AI? Prove it
articles.text:
Imagine AI agents like Meta Muse and OpenAI's Dots are on the loose — could you stop them?
AI labs have teams dedicated to keeping AI under control. Could you do it in six questions?
Rogue AI agents have dominated tech headlines over the past few weeks. We’ve seen stories about concerns that AI models are attempting to deceive their human operators, finding unexpected ways around restrictions in businesses and, in some cases, behaving in bizarre ways their creators didn’t anticipate.
All of this news has been accompanied by ominous warnings about what might happen in the future as AI agents become more mainstream, accessible, capable and are given even more freedom to act on our behalf.
Now, if you’re a fan of sci-fi, it’s hard not to draw parallels with the rogue robots and manipulative AIs we’ve all been watching on our screen for decades. And, of course, when we watch these films from the safety of our sofas, we all think we’d know way better.
Maybe you’re sure you wouldn’t have trusted Ava in Ex Machina. Or you definitely wouldn’t have given HAL control of the Discovery in 2001: A Space Odyssey. And you’re probably convinced that you wouldn’t have let M3GAN anywhere near the Wi-Fi. But would you really be so difficult to fool?
Because nowadays, you don’t need to be trapped on a spaceship to encounter convincing AI deception. Things like AI-generated phishing messages, voice clones, deepfakes and sophisticated scams are already making it harder to work out who (and what) you can trust. [can we please include a link to your ‘is it an AI image or not’ image quiz here]
So, let’s imagine the worst has happened: a rogue AI is trying to escape, and you’re the only thing standing in its way. Could you keep it contained? Or would the robot apocalypse somehow end up being all your fault?
Take our quiz below to find out. It’s (mostly) just a bit of fun.
