articles.title: Spotify estrena audiolibros en México, Colombia, Perú y Brasil: Gabriel García Márquez es protagonista
articles.text:
Spotify ampliará los audiolibros a más de 180 territorios antes de que termine 2026, incluidos España, Colombia, México, Perú y Brasil. La plataforma incorporará títulos en español, portugués, italiano, polaco y otros idiomas, con modelos de acceso y precios que variarán según cada país.
En Colombia, los suscriptores elegibles de Spotify Premium contarán desde el 7 de octubre con una asignación mensual de 12 horas de escucha incluida en su plan actual.
La expansión también alcanzará a Italia, Portugal, Polonia, Chile, Noruega y decenas de mercados de América, Europa, Asia, África y Oceanía.
El catálogo global reunirá más de 350.000 títulos en más de 120 idiomas. Entre las editoriales disponibles figuran Grupo Planeta, Penguin Random House Grupo Editorial y Laguna Libros, junto con obras de autores colombianos como Gabriel García Márquez, Pilar Quintana y Laura Restrepo.
Cómo acceder a audiolibros en Spotify
Spotify ofrecerá distintas formas de acceder a los audiolibros, según el mercado. Los usuarios podrán encontrarlos incluidos en determinados planes Premium, mediante Audiobooks+ o a través de compras directas dentro de la plataforma.
La modalidad Audiobooks+ permite a los suscriptores Premium adquirir horas adicionales de escucha por encima de las incluidas en su plan. También ofrece a los miembros de los planes Premium Family y Duo la posibilidad de sumar 15 horas mensuales mediante un complemento recurrente.
Los oyentes encontrarán una pestaña específica de Audiolibros en la aplicación. Ese espacio incluirá recomendaciones personalizadas a partir de los hábitos de escucha de cada usuario, junto con un catálogo de títulos en distintos idiomas.
Qué traen los audiolibros
La plataforma incorporará herramientas diseñadas para integrar la escucha en las rutinas diarias. Entre ellas están los marcadores automáticos, que guardan el punto exacto en el que el usuario dejó un libro, y el temporizador de apagado, que permite programar el momento en que se detendrá la reproducción.
Spotify también actualizará Page Match, la función que permite alternar entre un libro físico, una edición electrónica y su versión en audio.
Los usuarios podrán escanear el código ISBN de un ejemplar y utilizar números de página para encontrar el fragmento correspondiente en el audiolibro.
Page Match funciona en más de 30 idiomas. Según Spotify, más de un millón de lectores la utilizaron desde febrero para pasar entre formatos.
La compañía informó además que la cantidad mensual de oyentes de audiolibros creció cerca de 40% durante el último año, mientras que las horas de escucha aumentaron más de 30%.
Spotify agrega cuestionarios para los más fanáticos
Spotify ampliará Music Quiz, una función de cuestionarios para que los usuarios demuestren cuánto saben sobre sus artistas favoritos. La herramienta se implementará de forma gradual en 11 países y estará disponible para mayores de 18 años con una suscripción Premium.
La función llegará inicialmente a Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, Canadá, Irlanda, Australia, Nueva Zelanda, Singapur, India, Nigeria, Sudáfrica e Indonesia.
Spotify prevé ofrecer cuestionarios sobre más de 2.000 artistas, aunque algunos estarán disponibles solo en inglés durante la primera etapa. La compañía anticipó que incorporará nuevos idiomas, mercados y músicos de manera progresiva.
Music Quiz incluirá preguntas de trivia, desafíos para reconocer portadas de álbumes y fragmentos de audio para identificar canciones.
Las consignas abordarán el catálogo de cada intérprete, los principales momentos de su carrera y otros hitos de su trayectoria. Al finalizar, cada usuario podrá conocer su puntuación y compartirla con amigos.
Spotify probó la herramienta con ARMY, el fandom de BTS, durante el lanzamiento de ARIRANG, el quinto álbum de estudio del grupo surcoreano. La experiencia se estrenó el 20 de marzo y permitió que los usuarios Premium de todo el mundo respondieran preguntas vinculadas con la historia de la banda.
El cuestionario de BTS estuvo disponible en inglés, indonesio, coreano, japonés, portugués y español. La iniciativa propuso un recorrido por los lanzamientos y momentos que consolidaron el vínculo entre el grupo y su audiencia global.

articles.title: Avec l'iPhone Duo, Apple veut un lancement parfait, sans reproduire les erreurs des smartphones Android
articles.text:
L'iPhone Duo doit impérativement être un lancement réussi. Pour la marque à la pomme, aucun problème de compatibilité ne sera toléré. Les applications doivent être nativement compatibles avec les deux écrans, et le constructeur met les bouchées doubles auprès des éditeurs d'applications pour une sortie sans accroc.
Apple met en place une stratégie pour assurer que l'iPhone Duo, qui arrive dans deux semaines, ne rencontrera pas les problèmes de compatibilité d'applications que les téléphones pliables Android ont connus à leurs lancements respectifs. Le smartphone doit être pleinement opérationnel dès la sortie de la boite, et les applications optimisées pour ces nouveaux formats d'écrans.
Apple accompagne les développeurs
La firme de Cupertino a publié des directives détaillées destinées aux développeurs sur son blog officiel. Trois étapes permettront de garantir que les applications fonctionnent correctement sur le nouvel appareil.
La première consiste à recompiler les applications existantes à l'aide de Xcode 27.1. Cet outil offre des fonctionnalités de visualisation permettant aux développeurs de vérifier l'apparence et le comportement de leurs applications sur l'iPhone Duo.
La deuxième étape porte sur les éléments nécessaires à la publication sur l'AppStore, notamment les captures d'écran et les caractéristiques des aperçus de l'appli dans l'AppStore. La troisième étape correspond à la soumission de l'application elle-même.
Des délais progressifs pour la conformité
Apple commence dès à présent à accepter les applications optimisées pour l'iPhone Duo. À partir d'avril 2027, toutes les nouvelles applications soumises à l'App Store devront supporter l'iPhone Duo et inclure des captures d'écran montrant leur affichage sur l'appareil.
La société organise également des ateliers spécialisés pour les développeurs. L'idée étant bien évidemment d'apprendre des erreurs des smartphones précédents sous Android, pour ne pas les reproduire.
En effet, le jour du lancement de certains smartphones Android, bon nombre d'applications présentaient des bugs, en raison d'une taille d'affichage non correspondante à l'écran du smartphone en question. Apple veut à tout prix éviter ce scénario catastrophe, qui serait celui de la désillusion pour certains utilisateurs.
Si les applications natives fonctionnent parfaitement, les applications tierces sont plus sujettes à risque, c'est ce risque que la marque à la pomme anticipe.

articles.title: Atlassian Data Center Flaw Draws Exploitation Attempts Within Two Hours of Public Details
articles.text:
Threat actors have begun to exploit a newly disclosed critical security flaw impacting Atlassian Data Center products that could allow access to sensitive files under certain conditions.
The arbitrary file access flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-21589 (CVSS score: 9.3) affects multiple products, including Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center, Crowd Data Center, Crucible, and Fisheye.
"This arbitrary file access vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions," the Australian company said.
"Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path; this vulnerability does not allow attackers to enumerate or list directory contents. In some configurations, there may be sensitive files present that increase your risk."
Atlassian said impacted Atlassian Cloud products have been patched, adding that fixes are available for the following products -
- Bitbucket Data Center - 9.4.26, 10.2.8, and 10.5.1
- Confluence Data Center - 9.2.26 and 10.2.19
- Jira Service Management Data Center - 5.12.40, 10.3.26, and 11.3.12
- Jira Software Data Center - 9.12.40, 10.3.26, and 11.3.12
- Bamboo Data Center - 10.2.24 and 12.1.12
- Crowd Data Center - 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7, and 7.2.4
- Crucible - 4.9.15
- Fisheye - 4.9.15
As temporary mitigation, Atlassian is recommending that customers remove their instance from the public internet, apply a Web Application Firewall (WAF) rule, block requests using Tomcat's RewriteValve (for Confluence, JSM, Jira, Bamboo, and Crowd), and add a new rule to urlrewrite.xml (for Bitbucket).
According to telemetry data from Previdian, a total of 15 exploitation attempts have been detected from three unique IP addresses located in Japan and the U.S. -
- 38.60.157[.]86
- 146.70.187[.]234
- 159.26.119[.]225
The exploitation activity targeting its honeypot network is said to have begun two hours after watchTowr released additional technical details of the vulnerability, stating it allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve sensitive files within the webroot directory through a single request and extract tokens, credentials, keys, or other authentication material.
According to the preemptive exposure management firm, the underlying vulnerability has to do with Atlassian's web-resource handling, which converts a string like "..::..::..::..::WEB-INF::web.xml" to "../../../../WEB-INF/web.xml."
As a result, an unauthenticated attacker with knowledge of the resource-resolution logic can abuse this path resolution logic and combine it with an Atlassian "/includes/jquery/plugins/colorpicker/images/" plugin resource by taking advantage of the trailing "/" to reach other files (e.g., "WEB-INF/web.xml") elsewhere in the application -
GET /download/resources/jira.webresources:color-picker-popup/images/..::..::..::..::..::WEB-INF::web.xml HTTP/1.1
Host: {{Jira-Hostname}}
Importantly, in the case of Atlassian Crowd and Jira, the attacker could exploit the flaw to access "WEB-INF/classes/crowd.properties," which stores Crowd credentials, and then use them to gain administrative access to the application. Armed with this privileged access, it's possible to create new users, modify user privileges, and elevate a newly created rogue user to Jira Administrator.
"Within two hours of public exploit details becoming available, we were already seeing exploitation attempts hit our honeypot network," Previdian Founder and CEO Ryan Dewhurst said in a statement shared with The Hacker News.
"The release of a Nuclei template will make mass automated scanning even easier, so we expect activity around CVE-2026-21589 to increase quickly. Organizations running affected Atlassian products should treat patching as an immediate priority."

articles.title: Elon Musk anuncia que Grok Bot ahora incluirá a Claude para tener mejores respuestas
articles.text:
Grok Bot, el agente de inteligencia artificial desarrollado por SpaceXAI, incorporó Claude Opus 5.5 de Anthropic como parte de su sistema de inteligencia. El cambio llega en un momento de fuerte competencia entre los nuevos agentes de IA, herramientas capaces de ejecutar tareas de manera más autónoma y que buscan convertirse en asistentes digitales para los usuarios.
La actualización permite que Grok Bot utilice uno de los modelos más avanzados de Anthropic para procesar solicitudes y generar respuestas. La incorporación de Claude supone un cambio en la tecnología que se encuentra detrás del agente, que hasta ahora dependía principalmente de modelos propios de SpaceXAI y Cursor.
Grok Bot está disponible actualmente para iPhone, iPad y Mac, después de ampliar su presencia en dispositivos de Apple desde su lanzamiento inicial.
Grok Bot recurre a Claude para procesar las solicitudes
La principal novedad de la actualización está en el modelo de inteligencia artificial que utiliza Grok Bot. A partir de ahora, el agente puede recurrir a Claude Opus 5.5 para proporcionar la capacidad de razonamiento necesaria para responder a las instrucciones de los usuarios.
En términos sencillos, el modelo de IA funciona como el componente que interpreta lo que una persona solicita y determina cómo responder o qué acciones realizar. Al incorporar Claude, Grok Bot suma una tecnología desarrollada por Anthropic a su propia arquitectura.
El cambio resulta llamativo porque no se trata únicamente de una actualización visual o de nuevas funciones para el usuario. La modificación ocurre en la parte interna del servicio, donde se decide qué modelo de inteligencia artificial se utiliza para procesar las solicitudes.
La compañía prevé además una actualización importante de su sistema interno durante octubre, con la que Claude tendrá un papel más relevante dentro del funcionamiento del agente.
La competencia por los agentes de IA aumenta
Grok Bot forma parte de una nueva generación de aplicaciones que buscan ir más allá de los chatbots tradicionales. En lugar de limitarse a responder preguntas, los agentes de IA están diseñados para realizar tareas y actuar como asistentes capaces de intervenir en diferentes procesos.
El mercado comenzó a recibir nuevas propuestas durante los últimos meses. Meta trabaja con Muse, un agente de IA orientado a realizar tareas para los usuarios, mientras que OpenAI desarrolla ChatGPT Dot, una propuesta de asistente proactivo basada en Astra.
La llegada de Claude a Grok Bot se produce precisamente en este contexto de competencia. Cada compañía busca diferenciar sus agentes mediante mejores capacidades de razonamiento, mayor autonomía y acceso a diferentes herramientas.
Para los usuarios, uno de los principales cambios de esta evolución es que la calidad de un asistente ya no depende exclusivamente de la aplicación que se utiliza. También adquiere importancia el modelo de inteligencia artificial que funciona detrás de ella.
La relación entre Anthropic y SpaceXAI
La incorporación de Claude también resulta relevante por la relación entre las compañías. Anthropic se convirtió este año en cliente de SpaceX para obtener capacidad de procesamiento necesaria para atender el crecimiento en el uso de Claude.
Ahora, el movimiento ocurre en sentido contrario: una aplicación de SpaceXAI utiliza tecnología de Anthropic para reforzar su capacidad de inteligencia artificial.
Esto muestra cómo el desarrollo de estos sistemas no necesariamente implica que una empresa utilice exclusivamente sus propios modelos. Las compañías pueden combinar modelos y servicios de diferentes proveedores para construir sus aplicaciones.
Grok Bot compite por convertirse en un asistente cotidiano
Grok Bot fue lanzado en agosto con aplicaciones dedicadas para iPhone y iPad. Durante septiembre amplió su disponibilidad para iPad y recibió opciones de acceso con precios más económicos.
Con la incorporación de Claude Opus 5.5, el servicio busca reforzar su posición en una categoría que está creciendo rápidamente: los agentes de IA diseñados para acompañar al usuario en tareas cotidianas.
La competencia con Meta y OpenAI probablemente llevará a que estas plataformas incorporen nuevas capacidades durante los próximos meses. En este escenario, la diferencia entre un chatbot y un agente estará cada vez más relacionada con su capacidad para comprender instrucciones, utilizar herramientas y completar acciones, además de simplemente generar respuestas.

articles.title: 3D-printed bomb could give US Army squads precision strikes beyond 3 miles
articles.text:
US Army shows off its in-house 'Dragoons' drone with 3D-printed bombs which can fly up to 12 miles
Soldiers loaded 250 grams of C-4 for the live-fire test
- US soldiers in Germany built and flew an armed drone without contractors
- The live strike took less than five minutes from launch to impact
- Officers say the 3D-printed casing can carry almost two pounds of explosives
The US Army has tested an attack drone assembled and operated by soldiers, marking an unusual step toward independently produced battlefield systems.
The 2nd Cavalry Regiment conducted the live-fire exercise on September 30 2026, at the Grafenwoehr Training Area in Germany.
It used an Orqa MRM2-10 aircraft carrying a custom 3D-printed explosive container that soldiers designed and prepared themselves.
Soldiers build and operate the strike system
According to unit company commander Capt. Michael Bapp, the exercise followed more than two years of development.
The soldiers assembled the aircraft from manufacturer-provided components before adding an electronic safety mechanism and their printed explosive housing.
The regiment named the device “Dragoon bomb” after its nickname, with the container capable of carrying nearly two pounds of explosives.
This weapon can reportedly strike from over three miles away under guidance from experts from the military.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
An additional receiver could extend the stated operating distance beyond 12 miles, though battlefield performance remains dependent on conditions.
“If we hit the right spot on the vehicle, we’d be able to get a 100% kill as well,” said 1st Lt. Eugene Lee, reconnaissance platoon leader.
“We can modify the Dragoon bomb, make it into a shape charge, which would be very effective in destroying smaller tanks.”
For the live-fire event, soldiers loaded 250 grams of C-4 alongside M6 low-voltage blasting caps.
The casing can also accommodate different configurations, including ball bearings arrangement for specific battlefield applications.
“This is a conventional Army first, potentially an Army-wide first as far as a live, kinetic drone strike conducted without any contractor support,” said Capt. Bapp.
Staff Sgt. Angel Caliz flew the explosive-carrying aircraft more than one mile before reaching the designated target during the exercise.
The flight from launch to impact required less than five minutes, while another drone transmitted the strike to soldiers watching nearby.
Army drone push builds on Ukraine lessons and in-house assembly
These efforts follow the conflict in Ukraine, where cheap commercial drones, widely available since the start of the war in 2022, have been changing the dynamics of the war.
Drone warfare has since spread to Middle Eastern conflicts, where Iran recorded some devastating wins against the U.S. using cheap drones.
The US Army has begun pursuing in-house production and repair capacity of its own after watching how the war unfolded in Ukraine.
It now operates a three-week course in additive manufacturing and piloting, while the Marine Corps and Navy pursue their own drone fabrication projects.
The Army's experiment therefore combines commercially sourced aircraft components with locally produced additions and soldier-level assembly.
Col. Timothy Price said the exercise showed how existing equipment could be adapted while soldiers develop capabilities without relying entirely on external support.
Army officials said its system could eventually give smaller formations access to precision weapons beyond the reach of conventional equipment.
The US Army even compared the potential of this device with the AT4, which soldiers commonly use against armored threats at relatively short engagement distances.
The unit's account suggests squads could gain precision strike options cheaply, though one success says little about performance against moving or defended threats.

articles.title: What Is Agentic Pentesting? What It Proves, and Where It Stops.
articles.text:
If you’re evaluating an agentic pentesting solution right now, you’ve probably heard the same pitch more than once: point it at a target, and it discovers, validates, and exploits attack paths autonomously, the way a real attacker would.
That promise is worth taking seriously. It’s also worth pressure testing, and three questions do the heavy lifting.
- What can the assessment actually prove?
- When is that proof produced? And,
- How much of your environment does the proof cover?
Most evaluations stop at the first step. However, it’s at the second and third ones where validation programs are won or lost.
One note on where we stand: Picus builds and sells autonomous pentesting. That is exactly why we can be precise about where it ends, because the limits belong to the method, not to any vendor's implementation, and no roadmap can remove them.
The problem in four numbers
Four numbers from this year explain why the second and third questions now carry more weight than the first.
- Volume: 35,364 CVEs found in the first half of 2026, up 49.5% year over year.
- Prioritization: only 95 of roughly 39,600 CVEs published through August saw confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, so severity-led prioritization is effectively chasing the wrong list.
- Speed: mean time from disclosure to exploitation collapsed from 21.5 days in 2025 to 8 hours in 2026.
- Capacity: of the more than 26,000 vulnerabilities surfaced by AI-scale discovery, only 421 were patched upstream.
You can’t patch, schedule, or predict your way out. You validate, on evidence, within hours of the change that demanded it. Yet an annual pentest leaves as much as a 365-day blind window between a change and the next test, and weekly automated runs still leave a gap of up to seven days.
Against an eight-hour exploitation window, both lose.
Gartner has drawn the conclusion formally: its Continuous Offensive Security Testing (COST) model replaces the point-in-time assessment with trigger-driven, risk-tiered testing completed within risk-aligned timeframes, often minutes or hours, with a planning assumption that by 2028 over 60% of enterprise pentest programs will operate as continuous validation. The key question is no longer "have we tested?" It is "how quickly are we validating new exposures?"
Agentic pentesting is the most important answer to that question.
Two proofs agentic pentesting delivers
Every pentest exists to answer one question: are we exploitable? Agentic pentesting answers it with the two proofs that matter. It proves individual exposures are exploitable or not, confirmed by safely executing the exploit rather than inferring from a version banner. And it proves chained reach: where real exploits are chained from initial access through privilege escalation and lateral movement, with the confirmed path to a critical asset reported as evidence.
On the assets it reaches, nothing is more convincing, and because every fix can be revalidated with one more run, remediation becomes defensible rather than hopeful.
The operative phrase here is "on the assets it reaches." Proving exploitability is the first question answered; the phrase quietly concedes the other two: when the proof arrives, and how much of the estate it covers.
The speed gap – the “when”
Run an agentic pentest across a 250,000-endpoint estate and the full cycle takes weeks. That is a dramatic improvement over the quarter a human-led engagement needs, but it's still the wrong unit of time.
Careful agentic pentesting works step by step: foothold, enumerate, pivot, chain, prove. Repeat that across a quarter of a million endpoints, and the sweep stretches out while the environment changes underneath it. By the time it completes, large swaths of the results describe an environment that no longer exists.
Weeks may be fast for a pentest, but against an eight-hour window, it's slow. A deep sweep alone can't bridge that gap.
The coverage gap – the “how much”
The coverage gap matters more. Live exploitation can only be pointed at part of the environment. Business-critical production systems, very large segments, and restricted or air-gapped zones are off-limits to real exploits for safety, stability and access reasons. The thousands of CVEs with no working exploit give the tool nothing to fire. And the window between disclosure and the first exploit, where the speed numbers show the entire race is now taking place, is precisely, and unfortunately, when an exploit-dependent tool has the least to say.
Add it up and autonomous pentesting alone sees perhaps 20 to 30% of real exploitability in a typical enterprise. Stacking a second or third tool doesn’t change the math, because every tool in the category shares the same method, and therefore the same ceiling. And partial coverage doesn’t reduce uncertainty. It simply relocates it, to the assets you skipped, and the attacker only needs the one thing you skipped for things to go pear-shaped.
The change selects the validation method
The coverage gap closes the same way: let the change that triggered the test select the method that answers it fastest and safest.
An emerging vulnerability lands on your assets. The key question is "is it exploitable in our environment?" Exploitability validation answers this within hours, across the whole affected scope, by testing the attacker techniques the vulnerability depends on, no working exploit required. This answers the objection we hear most often, "doesn't pentesting already cover that?" Yes, but only where live execution can go; in contrast, exploitability validation reaches most of the estate and most of the CVE list.
A new campaign is observed, or a security control changes. The question here is "can we stop this?" Security control validation emulates the campaign's techniques against your live defense stack and shows whether each is prevented, detected or missed.
An infrastructure change lands. The million-dollar question is "did this open a new attack path?" Agentic pentesting confirms it with chained, live proof, the thing only it can do.
Three methods, one findings model
One warning from recent history: vulnerability management splintered into islands of duplicate findings and conflicting priorities, and validation will recreate those islands if each method ships with its own console and queue. The three must feed one shared findings model, deduplicated, evidence-backed, and asset-aware, with one backlog and one closure state per exposure.
This is the principle the Picus Platform is built on, with Autonomous Penetration Testing, Exposure Validation and Breach and Attack Simulation all working off shared evidence.
Against a real clock: a critical CVE drops.
- Hour one, it’s enriched with threat intelligence.
- Hour two, affected assets, criticality, and surrounding controls are mapped.
- Hour four, exploitability is assessed on every affected asset, attack paths are confirmed where live testing is safe, and controls have been tested against the relevant techniques.
- Hour six, low-risk mitigations are deployed, the rest have been routed to owners, and every fix has been revalidated before closure.
Every change is validated. Every exposure is proven. Within hours. Request your demo and see one CVE run through all three methods on one shared findings model.
See it run, live
At The Validation Summit 26, hosted by Hacker Valley’s Ron Eddings, October 14 at 1 PM ET and October 15 at 11 AM BST, we’ll run this model live in the product. Our CTO Volkan Erturk will take an emerging CVE from trigger to validated exposure to a confirmed fix in hours, with the right method selected as conditions change. Additionally, Mikko Hyppönen will open with what changed after Mythos. Security leaders from Chanel, Atlassian, and Kraft Heinz will discuss how they’re preparing.
Two hours. Registration is free. See the workflow run live for yourself.

articles.title: Tickets-restaurant : la mauvaise surprise qui pourrait vous attendre à la caisse du supermarché
articles.text:
Des députés ont proposé de limiter les courses payées en titres-restaurant à 10 ou 15 euros par jour, contre 25 euros aujourd’hui. Ces pistes n’ont pas été retenues en commission, mais pourraient revenir lors des débats dans l’hémicycle.
Le passage en caisse pourrait devenir nettement moins confortable pour des millions de salariés. Alors que l’Assemblée nationale examine une réforme des titres-restaurant, plusieurs amendements, notamment portés par des élus MoDem et Renaissance, proposaient de limiter leur utilisation dans les magasins, tout en conservant un plafond de 25 euros au restaurant.
Lors de l’examen en commission ce 7 octobre, l’amendement de Bertrand Sorre évoquant une limite de 10 euros dans les grandes surfaces n’a pas été soutenu. Une proposition MoDem fixant cette limite à 15 euros hors restaurants a été rejetée. Le texte doit être débattu dans l’hémicycle le 12 octobre, où ces pistes pourraient être proposées à nouveau.
À la caisse, 15 euros à sortir autrement ?
Sur un panier de 25 euros composé uniquement de produits éligibles, un salarié peut actuellement tout régler avec ses titres s’il dispose du solde nécessaire. Avec un plafond ramené à 10 euros, il devrait payer les 15 euros restants avec sa carte bancaire ou un autre moyen de paiement.
La valeur des titres ne baisserait pas et le crédit non utilisé ne disparaîtrait pas. Mais ceux qui font leurs courses une ou deux fois par semaine devraient multiplier les passages en magasin pour dépenser la même somme. Une contrainte loin d’être anodine pour les salariés qui utilisent aujourd’hui cet avantage pour préparer leurs repas plutôt que déjeuner au restaurant.
Restaurants et grande distribution s’opposent sur le plafond
Les organisations de restaurateurs poussent depuis plusieurs mois pour différencier les usages. Le GHR (Groupement des hôtelleries et restaurations de France) réclame, par exemple, un plafond de 25 euros dans les restaurants et de 10 euros dans la grande distribution, estimant que l’élargissement des titres à tous les produits alimentaires détourne une partie des dépenses de leur vocation initiale.
La grande distribution défend au contraire la liberté de choix des salariés et présente les titres-restaurant comme un avantage destiné d’abord à leur pouvoir d’achat.
Le rapporteur Christophe Naegelen proposait une 3e voie en conservant les possibilités actuelles pour les courses et instaurant un plafond supérieur d’au moins 20% chez les restaurateurs. Son amendement a lui aussi été rejeté en commission ce 7 octobre. À suivre…

articles.title: Ahorra más de 20 dólares en vacaciones: solo debes desconectar estos electrodomésticos
articles.text:
Salir de casa durante varios días permite reducir el consumo eléctrico, incluso sin contar el ahorro por no utilizar la cocina, la lavadora o el lavavajillas.
La Organización de Consumidores y Usuarios de España (OCU) calcula que desconectar electrodomésticos e instalaciones antes de unas vacaciones puede reducir la factura hasta en 20 dólares.
Además, dejar determinados aparatos apagados y preparar las instalaciones disminuye el riesgo de averías, incendios, pérdidas de agua y problemas de seguridad durante la ausencia.
Cuánto dinero consume un refrigerador
El refrigerador es uno de los aparatos que más energía demanda cuando funciona de forma continua. La OCU estima que mantener un modelo combi encendido durante un mes puede costar cerca de 3,5 dólares, mientras que una nevera grande de tipo americano puede alcanzar los 7 dólares mensuales.
Si la ausencia será prolongada, la pauta de expertos es vaciarlo, desconectarlo, limpiarlo y dejar la puerta entreabierta. Esa última medida ayuda a evitar olores y la aparición de moho.
Cuando queden alimentos que deban conservarse, se puede ajustar el termostato a una temperatura algo menos fría, porque habrá menos productos en el interior.
Por qué se debe apagar el calentador de agua en vacaciones
El calentador mantiene el agua a una temperatura determinada y repone el calor que pierde el depósito. Por ese motivo, puede continuar con su consumo aunque no haya nadie en la vivienda. Dejarlo activo durante un mes puede sumar entre 7 y 10 dólares, según su capacidad y sus características.
La OCU aconseja desconectarlo antes de salir y cerrar las llaves del agua. Se sugiere utilizar el agua almacenada hasta vaciar el termo, una precaución que puede limitar las consecuencias de una fuga o una rotura durante las vacaciones.
Cómo dejar la lavadora, el lavavajillas y la secadora al salir de vacaciones
La lavadora, el lavavajillas y la secadora deben quedar vacíos antes del viaje. Una prenda olvidada o una pieza de vajilla sucia pueden provocar malos olores si permanecen varios días dentro del aparato. Por esta razón, es conveniente secar las gomas y las zonas donde suele acumularse humedad.
Las puertas pueden quedar abiertas o entreabiertas para favorecer el secado interior. En el lavavajillas, un paño puede servir para mantener una pequeña apertura sin dejarlo completamente expuesto.
En la secadora, hay que vaciar el depósito de agua condensada. Al regreso, la limpieza de filtros, tambor y juntas puede formar parte de la puesta a punto antes de volver a utilizarlos.
Qué pequeños aparatos y conexiones no deben quedar conectados
Cafeteras, tostadoras, robots de cocina, licuadoras y otros pequeños electrodomésticos suelen permanecer conectados por comodidad.
Cuando la casa quedará vacía durante semanas, es preferible retirarlos de los enchufes. La misma pauta se aplica a los cargadores de teléfonos, tabletas, aspiradoras y otros dispositivos con batería.
Asimismo, el router debería apagarse antes de salir. Aparte de evitar su consumo eléctrico, esta decisión desconecta la red WiFi y reduce la posibilidad de accesos no autorizados.
Si no es posible desenchufar cada dispositivo, el cuadro eléctrico permite cortar circuitos concretos y limitar los consumos fantasma de microondas, hornos, televisores y otros aparatos que conservan indicadores encendidos.
Por qué se debe evitar tener los aparatos en stand-by
El consumo en espera representa alrededor del 10% de la electricidad que utiliza un hogar, según la OCU. En una casa con un consumo anual medio de 4.500 kWh, ese gasto equivale a 7,5 dólares al mes.
Televisores, sistemas de sonido, consolas, hornos, microondas y otros dispositivos mantienen funciones activas aun cuando parecen apagados. Las pantallas con luces de espera, los relojes de los electrodomésticos y los aparatos con memoria interna son parte de ese consumo.

articles.title: Anthropic Expands Claude Access for Vetted Cyber Teams as Glasswing Finds 129,000 Flaws
articles.text:
Anthropic on Tuesday said it's expanding a program that allows vetted cybersecurity professionals to test its advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models with reduced safeguards and blocking classifiers, as the company claimed its Project Glasswing initiative uncovered at least 129,000 verified software vulnerabilities between April and July 2026.
The company said it also found an additional 5,500 verified software vulnerabilities between April and October 2026 through open-source scanning efforts.
"Of these verified vulnerabilities, more than 33,000 have so far been rated as critical- or high-severity," Anthropic said. "This is likely an undercount, as it is based on survey data from only a subset of Glasswing partners. As such, we expect the true impact to be at least five times higher."
The updated program, called the Cyber Verification Program (CVP), features three access tiers, allowing organizations and security teams to apply for one that best aligns with their work. Each tier comes with access to its models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and new models moving forward.
The three access levels are detailed below -
- Defense Access, which is for defensive work, such as incident response, malware reverse engineering, and vulnerability analysis and validation.
- Red Team Access, which adds authorized penetration testing and red-teaming to the defensive use cases.
- Specialized Access, which has the fewest safeguards and is reserved for a limited set of verified organizations that are authorized to test safety systems.
According to a CyScenarioBench evaluation, its safeguards blocked 46 of 50 tasks on Claude Opus 5.5 in the Defense Access tier, while the Red Team Access tier on the same model did not block any tasks, and completed 34 of 50, which is the same completion rate as when no safeguards are applied. Without CVP access, every task was blocked on the first prompt.
"These evaluations give us confidence that we can make advanced cyber capabilities safely available to a broader set of defenders, expanding the defensive efforts we began with Project Glasswing," Anthropic said.
The AI company said it's making these tools available to defenders given their dual-use nature, and to help them secure systems using the same capabilities that could be weaponized by a bad actor for malicious purposes.
In an analysis published late last month, VulnCheck researcher Patrick Garrity revealed that only 2 of the 300 vulnerabilities discovered by Anthropic or Project Glasswing, or 0.67%, have been exploited in the wild. Of these, 39 have been classified as critical, 141 as high, 81 as medium, and 18 as low in severity.
The two vulnerabilities that have witnessed active exploitation efforts are CVE-2026-26980, an SQL injection flaw in Ghost CMS, and CVE-2026-61500, a session forgery flaw in Rejetto HTTP File Server.
If anything, the findings suggest that while AI is lowering the barrier to vulnerability discovery, not every security flaw it uncovers is necessarily exploitable by threat actors or capable of causing significant impacts. Moreover, as demonstrated by 1Password and Veracode, AI-generated vulnerability patches can themselves introduce new security risks of their own.
"Roughly 44% of AI code generation tasks introduced a risky security vulnerability in tests," Veracode said. "The average security pass rate across models is 56% – barely changed from 55% in the first report. In other words, security performance has stayed flat while the amount of AI-generated code entering pipelines has surged."

I keep buying these Beats USB-C cables, and Prime Day just dropped them to $7.60
At home and on the road
It’s Prime Day yet again, and it’s also the second and final day of Amazon’s second members-only shopping event of the year. And there are still a ton of deals to shop, from Lego sets to TVs, AirPods Pro, coffee machines, and countless other gadgets in between.
But rather than a discount on the brand-new Beats 360 headphones — it’s a bit early for that, after all — I’m here with a discount on what might be my most-used tech accessory, and one that’s an even better deal than before.
Beats makes cables, and they’re really good. They offer USB-C to USB-C, and USB-A to USB-C cables, plus a Lightning edition. They don’t break easily; they’re braided and built to the same quality and durability standards as Apple’s own cables, which cost way more.
And for Prime Day, you can get a 1.5-meter USB-C to USB-C cable for just $7.60. You’ll need to be alright with a sleek black color, but it goes with anything.
At just $7.60, this is the best time to get the Beats 1.5-meter USB-C to USB-C cable, as it's never been cheaper. This Prime Day deal beats previous discounts. It's not the most exciting product, but with a durable woven design and support for up to 60 watts of power, it's an excellent cable to have at home or when traveling.
If you're after more than one, it's actually cheaper to buy the 2-pack of Beats 1.5-meter USB-C to USB-C cables as the bundle is also 60% off at just $14.
Whenever I’m on a flight, I travel with a Beats USB-A to USB-C and USB-C to USB-C cable, depending on which port is built into the seat, in case the standard wall-plug AC socket is too worn out. I also have over a dozen at home, and just bought another one.
To a degree, you can never have too many cables, and the Beats cable supports up to 60 watts of power.
And at 60% off, this is a particularly good time to pick one up. The single cable is down to $7.60 from $18.99, a new all-time low price. But if you’re like me and can never have too many cables, the two-pack is an even better option at $14, down from $34.99 — also a 60% discount. Honestly, that’s cheap enough that I’d grab a couple. articles.title: Cómo funciona la herramienta creada por el MIT para corregir modelos 3D generados por IA antes de su impresión
articles.text:
Investigadores del Instituto de Tecnología de Massachusetts (MIT), Google y la Universidad Northeastern desarrollaron InstructMesh, una herramienta que permite corregir modelos tridimensionales generados con inteligencia artificial antes de fabricarlos, con el objetivo de que objetos como tazas, anteojos o soportes cumplan la función para la que fueron diseñados, informó MIT News, el portal de noticias del instituto.
Los sistemas generativos pueden producir la imagen de una taza, pero no necesariamente un recipiente capaz de contener café. El problema es que reconocen la apariencia de los objetos, aunque no siempre comprenden cómo deben funcionar, lo que deriva en diseños impracticables y difíciles de modificar para quienes no dominan el modelado 3D.
La plataforma, descrita en un artículo presentado en el ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology, combina TRELLIS, un sistema de Microsoft que genera modelos tridimensionales a partir de texto e imágenes, con GPT-4, el modelo de lenguaje que respalda a ChatGPT. Esa integración reúne conocimiento visual y textual para que el usuario pueda señalar partes concretas del diseño y pedir cambios antes de enviarlo a una impresora 3D.
Faraz Faruqi, autor principal del trabajo, graduado del instituto y reciente integrante de su Laboratorio de Ciencias de la Computación e Inteligencia Artificial (CSAIL), precisó: “Queríamos reunir las capacidades de los generadores 3D y el razonamiento de los modelos de lenguaje en un espacio interactivo para crear objetos que la gente realmente quiera”. “Los modelos de lenguaje son excelentes con el texto y las imágenes, mientras que la fortaleza de TRELLIS está en su capacidad para crear modelos 3D, porque ha procesado muchísimos”, agregó.
Diseños: de tazas a dispensadores con tentáculos
El sistema produjo una taza aparentemente envuelta por un dragón, cuya cola funciona como asa; un silbato azul brillante con forma de concha; y unos anteojos con alas de mariposa sobre los lentes. También permitió fabricar un dispensador semejante a un pulpo, con líquido que sale por cada tentáculo para llenar varias tazas a la vez.
Los investigadores de CSAIL probaron la herramienta con objetos de uso cotidiano, accesorios y robots. Entre los resultados hubo una rodillera con aspecto de tela vaquera para combinar con los jeans de una paciente.
El programa también sirvió para construir un robot de cerdas con forma de camarón colorido. El dispositivo contiene un motor oculto y, al encenderse, se desliza sobre las superficies de manera similar a un juguete de cuerda.
La interfaz busca reducir una barrera habitual del diseño tridimensional: las herramientas convencionales exigen conocimientos específicos para corregir geometrías, ampliar partes o adaptar una pieza a una necesidad funcional. InstructMesh permite describir el problema en lenguaje natural y evaluar las modificaciones antes de aprobarlas.
Faruqi señaló que la manipulación ocurre en el espacio latente, la representación interna que utiliza el modelo generativo para organizar sus resultados. “InstructMesh admite una descripción en lenguaje natural de los problemas y crea cambios interpretativos en la geometría para que el usuario los evalúe y apruebe”.
Errores estructurales detectados por usuarios inexpertos
Para medir si personas sin formación previa podían identificar fallas antes de fabricar una pieza, el equipo hizo que TRELLIS recreara modelos populares de Thingiverse, una plataforma que alberga millones de diseños imprimibles en tres dimensiones. Casi el 80 % de los modelos generados presentaba algún defecto estructural.
Los investigadores pidieron entonces a usuarios principiantes que detectaran y corrigieran esas fallas con InstructMesh. Un experto evaluó los resultados y determinó que los participantes pudieron encontrar y resolver los problemas en cerca del 90 % de los casos.
Los participantes crearon modelos parecidos a soportes para teléfonos y jarrones. Describieron el sistema como fácil de usar y destacaron que los controles deslizantes les permitían realizar ajustes precisos, como agrandar o extruir una sección determinada del objeto.
“Los usuarios obtuvieron lo que pidieron y modificaron los diseños con facilidad cuando fue necesario”, afirmó Faruqi. “Lo que veían era lo que obtenían, y los objetos funcionaban como se esperaba”.
El investigador trabaja ahora en Google y prevé la posible incorporación de InstructMesh a una plataforma de realidad aumentada. La idea consiste en que una persona describa lo que necesita a partir del entorno que la rodea y obtenga rápidamente un objeto impreso en tres dimensiones, como una funda para teléfono que combine con una billetera.
El proyecto podría incorporar simulaciones físicas para anticipar cómo reaccionaría un diseño ante usos específicos, por ejemplo, si un cuenco se rompe al caer o qué materiales resultarían más adecuados. También podría integrar TRELLIS 2 para perfeccionar detalles más pequeños en los modelos.

articles.title: 100+ Compromised Websites Use Fake Cloudflare Checks to Deliver LunexStealer
articles.text:
The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) has identified more than 100 compromised websites that have been injected with malicious JavaScript to serve an information-stealing malware called LunexStealer (aka Psychedelic Stealer).
The activity, which was observed by the agency in September 2026, has been attributed to a threat cluster dubbed UAC-0277. It did not disclose who the victims of the campaign were or if any systems were successfully compromised as a result of these attacks.
"When visiting such a site, users were shown a forged Cloudflare verification page that, under the pretext of confirming the visitor is human, prompted them to execute a command," CERT-UA said in an advisory. "Executing the command caused a malicious MSI package to be downloaded and installed from a remote server (the ClickFix technique)."
The attacks also make use of the EtherHiding technique to retrieve the domain name of the resource from which the fake verification page is loaded, as well as the script's operating mode, from a smart contract on the Polygon or Ethereum network.
According to CERT-UA, there are three operating modes: 0 – inactive; 1 – passive tracking of visitors that includes gathering data about the website and the page from which the visitor arrived; and 2 – displaying the fake verification page.
In Mode 2, the bogus verification page is shown only to Windows users who arrive at the site from search engine results and not more than twice in 12 hours. These ClickFix lures lead to the distribution of MSI packages that deliver LunexStealer.
At least three different variants of the MSI packages have been discovered -
- Variant 1, which installs LunexStealer on the system.
- Variant 2, which attempts to bypass Windows account control (UAC), configures Microsoft Defender exclusions, leverages the legitimate-but-vulnerable AMD driver ("PDFWKRNL.sys") to blind security software, and then retrieves and runs LunexStealer from a remote server.
- Variant 3, which launches LunexStealer via DLL sideloading by using the legitimate binary ("FnHotkeyUtility.exe") to load a rogue DLL ("spkvol.dll"), which decrypts and executes the stealer.
As documented by both Arctic Wolf Labs and Ontinue, LunexStealer is also designed to install a malicious browser extension called LUNARAXE. The extension masquerades as "Microsoft Office Word Editor" to steal cookies, browsing history, and credentials entered into web forms. It also allows the operator to remotely control the browser and execute arbitrary JavaScript on web pages.
The stealer also deploys an auxiliary component named NAIVEMESS that's installed based on a configuration received from the command-and-control (C2) server. Its primary responsibility is to provide LUNARAXE with access to the Windows file system through a PowerShell-based Native Messaging Host.
"NAIVEMESS functionality includes retrieving the list of drives, browsing directories, reading, creating and overwriting files, as well as executing them," CERT-UA said. "Files are transferred in chunks encoded in Base64, and directories and file groups are pre‑archived into ZIP."
The component does have its own communication channel with the C2 server. Rather, commands are received via the extension, which houses three other modules -
- LUNARAXE.CORE, which handles C2 communication, receives commands, executes them, and exfiltrates browser data (i.e., cookies, browsing history, bookmarks, details about installed extensions, and intercepted credentials). It can also manage tabs, enable/disable extensions, serve notifications, run JavaScript on web pages, and display bogus overlays. It can also copy files from the computer, write files to it, and execute them if NAIVEMESS is installed.
- LUNARAXE.STEALER, which captures credentials entered into web forms and sends them to LUNARAXE.CORE, along with the page URL.
- LUNARAXE.STRIP, which disables Content Security Policy (CSP) protections on web pages by stripping CSP headers from HTTP responses with an aim to run arbitrary JavaScript code.
CERT-UA is advising organizations to prohibit regular users from using the Windows Run dialog via group policies, restrict the installation of MSI packages by users without administrator rights, monitor for the execution of "msiexec.exe," enable blocking of vulnerable drivers via Microsoft's vulnerable driver blocklist, and limit the installation of browser extensions to allowlisted ones.
Microsoft also recommends turning on the Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rule "Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers" to prevent an application from writing a vulnerable signed driver to disk.

articles.title: Some of the best PC speakers and soundbars we've tested are on sale starting at just $27.99 — save up to 36% off a new pair of PC speakers from Creative, Edifier, and Onkyo
articles.text:
Some of the best PC speakers and soundbars we've tested are on sale starting at just $27.99 — save up to 36% off a new pair of PC speakers from Creative, Edifier, and Onkyo
Upgrade your audio setup with a bit of savings.
One of the simplest upgrades you can make to your desktop setup is a pair of the best PC speakers, many of which are on sale now as part of Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days. We've tracked down six of the best deals on speakers we've tested, some of which are among the best we've tested on the market.
If you want an alternative to headphones or don't want to keep relying on your monitor's junky internal speakers, you need a dedicated pair of PC speakers that you can use for listening to music, watching movies, and of course, playing games. The picks below are all compact, stereo speaker systems that should easily fit on most desktops — though there are larger surround sound systems available, like the SteelSeries Arena 9, if you have the space (and cash) to spare.
The Creative Labs Pebble V2 is a set of stereo speakers that connect to your PC via USB and feature a minimalist design.
Read moreRead less▼
Starting with an old favorite of Tom's Hardware, the Creative Labs Pebble V2 are about as simple and straightforward as PC speakers come. We've seen them for a couple of dollars less before, but at just $28 for a 2.0 stereo set of speakers, it's hard to complain. The speakers connect via USB-C (power) and 3.5mm (audio), and there's a volume dial on the front of the right speaker for quick adjustments.
We've reviewed the Pebble Pro set, which comes with an optional power boost to round out the low-end, as well as modern wireless connectivity with Bluetooth, but they're around $60. For a no-nonsense set of speakers that you plan on exclusively using with a desktop, however, the base Pebble V2s remain our go-to option.
The G2000 speakers from Edifier come with a peak power raing of 32W and a frequency response of 98 Hz up to 22 kHz, along with analog and Bluetooth connections.
Read moreRead less▼
Up a step in quality, you can save a solid 27% off the Edifier G2000 speakers, which currently rank as our best set of PC speakers for 2.0 gaming. With 32W of peak power, the G2000s are substantially more powerful than what you get with the Pebble V2, helping to deliver better low-end performance out of the 2.75-inch drivers.
In addition to USB and 3.5mm connections, the speakers also support Bluetooth, and there's an optional input for a subwoofer if you want to expand to a 2.1 stereo setup in the future. This is the first time this pair of speakers has dropped below $80 this year, with the set mostly selling for around $90 and $100 on sale, so now's a great time to pick them up.
The Edifier M60 speakers feature a 3-inch woofer and 1-inch tweeter, as well as 66W of total output across the four drivers.
Read moreRead less▼
If you're after the illustrious Audioengine A2+ speakers, they unfortunately aren't on sale right now. The Edifier M60 set does a decent impression, however, and they're half the price right now at $149.99. Peak power is more than doubled compared to the G2000, up to 66W peak with the internal Class-D amp; the drivers are enlarged to 3 inches, and Edifier includes a 1-inch tweeter to help separate the high-end frequencies.
For connections, Edifier includes USB-C, 3.5mm, and Bluetooth, and the speakers come with a pair of aluminum stands that angle the drivers up toward your ears at 15 degrees (an extra with Audioengine speakers).
These 6.81 x 4.68 x 5.51-inch speakers have attractive removable cloth fronts, 10-degree angled stands to aim them up at your ears, and they performed well in our testing. They also have ample connectivity, with Bluetooth 5.3 LE, USB-C, RCA (with a built-in Phono stage for vinyl record players), optical, and a subwoofer connector. I've used these for years as the sound system for my projector and have been very happy with their audio output.
Read moreRead less▼
For around the same price, you can pick up a pair of the GX-10DB speakers from the Japanese brand Onkyo. These speakers are similar to the M60 set, featuring a 3-inch driver and 3/4-inch tweeter, though with a lower 30W of total power through the Class D amp. Onkyo also includes 3.5mm, USB-C, and Bluetooth inputs, along with an optical input and an RCA output for a subwoofer.
The main reason to go for the Onkyo's is the enclosure and DSP chip, which is better than what you get with the Edifier's. Both the white and black versions are on sale, and regardless of the color you choose, you get a pair of wood-finished angled stands and speaker grilles with the Edifier logo.
These 4-inch 50-watt speakers look great, come with angled desktop stands, and can connect to your PC and just about everything else. Features include Bluetooth as well as 3.5mm AUX, HDMI ARC, USB-C, line/phono, and optical connections.
Read moreRead less▼
If you have a bit more budget, the larger GX-30ARC speakers from Onkyo are also on sale, and they currently rank as our top multi-use 2.0 PC speakers. They're virtually identical to the smaller GX-10DB set, just with larger 4-inch drivers and a bump up to 50W on the amp. Onkyo also includes an HDMI CEC input with these speakers if you want to us them with a TV or console.
You can read more about both sets of speakers in our Onkyo Creator Series review.
The Fluance Ai41 speakers feature 5-inch drivers with a 1-inch tweeter, and they come with an included remote that controls volume, bass, and treble.
Read moreRead less▼
Stepping up once again to a 5-inch driver, the Fluance Ai41 speakers are on sale for around $255. Similar to the Edifier M60 set, these are modeled after Audioengine's A5 speakers, though they cost half the price right now. Plus, Fluance includes some extra goodies that Audioengine doesn't, such as a remote that controls volume, treble, and bass, in the box.
In our Fluance Ai41 speaker review, we found that the audio quality was excellent for the price, assuming you have space for larger speakers on your desktop. The speaker accepts RCA, Bluetooth, and optical inputs, and the two satellites connect with the included 18-gauge speaker wire.
The OXS Thunder Pro speakers is a 5.1.2 system with Dolby Atmos support that comes with an included neck pillow that function as satellite speakers.
Read moreRead less▼
At the high end, the OXS Thunder Pro soundbar is on sale for a solid $150. It's a 5.1.2 system with Dolby Atmos support, with the soundbar packing dual 3/4-inch tweeters, dual 2.5-inch full-range drivers, and four 1.5-inch full-range drivers. You can optionally purchase a neck pillow with two additional 1.75-inch drivers, though we found the neck pillow to be mostly a gimmick in our OXS Thunder Pro review.
Although the soundbar is angled toward PC, it includes two HDMI inputs (one of which supports eARC), a USB-C and USB-A connection, a microphone and headset input, as well as a separate 3.5mm audio input. OXS also includes a wireless remote, as well as a wired desktop volume rocker.

articles.title: This $549 Core i7 laptop is 2x faster than the $699 Apple MacBook Neo
articles.text:
Save $350 on this Newegg Core i7-13620H laptop with 1TB SSD — $549 Hasee X5 has 16GB RAM, is 2X faster than $699 Apple MacBook Neo
This is no ordinary laptop
Newegg is throwing a massive spanner in Amazon’s well-oiled Prime Day engine in the shape of the best-value laptop you can buy this October.
The Hasee X5 is no ordinary laptop. It is the only one with a Core i7 (not one of these obsolete 10-year old ones), 16GB LPDDR5 RAM and a humongous 1TB PCIe Gen4 SSD. All this for a mere $549.99, a saving of 38% off its SRP of $899.99.
Intel core i7 13620H | 16G LPDDR5 RAM | 1TB SSD
This 15.6in Windows 11 laptop features an i7 processor, 16GB memory for smoother multi-tasking, a built-in privacy shutter, and loads of ports including three USB-A and 1 USB-C port.
Let’s start with the processor. This is an Intel Core i7-13620H with 10 cores and contains an Intel UHD Graphics. It is usually found inside gaming laptops, paired with a discrete GPU. None of this here unfortunately.
That said, this is probably the most powerful CPU in a sub-$649 laptop. I chose that price specifically because it relates to Apple’s iconic MacBook Neo.
The 13620H is about 2X faster than the A18 Pro that powers the Neo (based on figures from CPUBenchmark). This is both a compliment to Apple’s exceptional hardware team and to Hasee for how good of a deal the X5 is.
Next there’s 16GB LPDDR5 (albeit in one slot) with a huge 1TB Foresee PCIe 4.0 SSD. Both rarities on a desktop PC let alone a laptop at this price point.
A quick hop over to Dell shows that a Dell 15 laptop with 16GB of inferior DDR4 and 1TB SSD will set you back a massive $1,050, almost 2X more expensive. Oh and the 13420H is about 50% faster than the Ryzen 7 7730U that powers the Dell laptop. Mic Drop.
The Hasee X5 feels reasonably premium as well thanks to a silver finish and a metal chassis. I like the dedicated keypad, the backlit keyboard, the fact that the 15.6-inch full HD IPS screen can lay flat and the privacy shutter for the 2-megapixel webcam.
I don't know the expected battery life of this laptop but don’t have high hopes. The CPU is a power hungry one and the battery capacity is a mere 62.7Whr. You’d be lucky to get for hours out of it although Hasee claims you can get nine ours out of it.
As for connectivity, there’s WiFi-6 (courtesy of Intel), a microSD card reader, something we don’t see often, three USB 3.2 ports, a HDMI one, a Type-C connector and an audio interface. The power port is a barrel type which is not my preference.

articles.title: Elecom Unveils a USB-C Dock with Built-In Dial Knob and Four Macro Keys
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
Elecom Unveils a USB-C Dock with Built-In Dial Knob and Four Macro Keys
Japanese peripheral maker Elecom has introduced the DST-L080BPBK, an 8-in-1 USB Type-C dock that combines a conventional docking station with a large dial knob and four customizable buttons. The company is known for some unusual PC peripherals, including the M.A.P.P. mouse and IST trackball mouse. The dock measures 74 × 87 × 59 mm and weighs approximately 250 g. The top of the dock houses the dial and four buttons, with their functions configurable through Elecom's Mouse Assistant software. The dial and buttons can be assigned to different functions depending on the user's needs, turning the dock into a small control panel in addition to its connectivity features. The dock features one USB 5 Gbps Type-C and two USB 5 Gbps Type-A ports for data, along with a USB Type-C upstream connection.
The device also has a USB Type-C port with Power Delivery, up to 100 W input / 90 W output and one HDMI port that supports up to 4K at 60 Hz. The features are completed by one SD and one microSD card slot, Gigabit Ethernet, and a 3.5 mm audio jack. It supports Windows 10/11 and macOS Tahoe 26. Elecom plans to launch the DST-L080BPBK in Japan in early October, the dock is currently listed on the company website for ¥13,728 (around $87). The company has not announced availability in other regions.

articles.title: Android tendrá su propia versión de Face ID de iPhone: así sería esa herramienta de seguridad
articles.text:
Google trabaja en una función que busca resolver el principal punto débil del desbloqueo facial en los Pixel: la poca luz. Se trata de Face Active Illumination, detectada en el código de la beta 1 de Android 17 QPR3, según Android Authority.
La función aparece dentro de los ajustes de Face Unlock y, aunque todavía está en una fase temprana de desarrollo, apunta a ser la respuesta definitiva de Android a Face ID, el sistema de reconocimiento facial que Apple lanzó hace casi una década.
Cómo funciona Face Active Illumination de Android
El código de la beta incluye un interruptor general para activar o desactivar la función, además de una escala de brillo con tres niveles ajustables mediante un control deslizante.
También se detectaron permisos específicos para habilitarla en situaciones puntuales: en ambientes oscuros, durante el horario de descanso, al activar el modo No Molestar o mientras se conduce.
Face Active Illumination es una función en desarrollo dentro de Android 17 que busca mejorar el desbloqueo facial de los Pixel en condiciones de poca luz. Según el código detectado en la beta, ajustaría el brillo de la pantalla para iluminar el rostro del usuario y permitir así una autenticación más confiable durante la noche o en espacios oscuros.
El reporte de Android Authority precisó que la interfaz de la función todavía está casi vacía y que la mayoría de los textos dentro de la aplicación se encuentran ofuscados, con excepción de la etiqueta correspondiente a No Molestar. Esto confirma que los desarrolladores apenas consiguieron activarla para pruebas internas.
Ni la filtración ni Google especificaron qué pieza de hardware sería responsable de generar esta iluminación. Sin embargo, la presencia de controles deslizantes para regular la intensidad del brillo sugiere que el sistema recurriría a la propia pantalla del teléfono en lugar de un sensor infrarrojo dedicado.
Un usuario con acceso a tecnología infrarroja real, como ocurre con Face ID en el iPhone, no necesitaría ajustar manualmente niveles de brillo, ya que ese tipo de iluminación resulta invisible para el ojo humano. La existencia de estos controles, entonces, apuntaría a evitar que la pantalla encandile al usuario en situaciones de oscuridad total.
Una función más de un nuevo sistema de seguridad de Google
Face Active Illumination podría formar parte de un desarrollo más amplio conocido como Project Toscana, la iniciativa con la que Google busca resolver de manera definitiva el desbloqueo facial en sus dispositivos.
Project Toscana no es el primer intento de la compañía en este terreno. El Pixel 4 incorporó radar e infrarrojos para lograr un reconocimiento facial tridimensional, mientras que el Pixel 7 regresó a un enfoque más simple basado únicamente en la cámara frontal para desbloquear la pantalla.
Una filtración previa había revelado que Project Toscana ya alcanzaba una velocidad de desbloqueo equiparable a la de Face ID en distintas condiciones de iluminación. Para esas pruebas, Google utilizó un Pixel con una cámara perforada y dos Chromebooks equipados con cámaras externas y placas a la vista.
Esa filtración no detalló qué tecnología emplea Toscana, aunque todo indica que Google seguiría un camino similar al de Apple. Face ID funciona mediante un sistema infrarrojo invisible que no requiere que el usuario decida cuándo activarlo, una experiencia que Google querría replicar sin necesidad de recortar la pantalla para añadir un sensor adicional.
Cómo esta herramienta soluciona el problema de la luz
Los Pixel actuales ya cuentan con desbloqueo facial y certificación biométrica de Clase 3, el nivel que habilita su uso para proteger pagos y aplicaciones bancarias.
El inconveniente es que ese rendimiento depende en gran medida de la iluminación del entorno: en una habitación con poca luz, el sistema se vuelve prácticamente inútil.
Face Active Illumination apuntaría a corregir esa falla puntual sin modificar la certificación de seguridad ya existente, al mejorar las condiciones bajo las cuales la cámara puede captar el rostro del usuario.
Por el momento, Google no ofreció información oficial ni sobre Face Active Illumination ni sobre Project Toscana, y no está confirmado que ambos desarrollos estén directamente conectados. Todo indica que la primera función podría funcionar como un paso intermedio mientras la compañía avanza hacia una tecnología más cercana a las prestaciones de Face ID.

articles.title: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude Ad Portals Capture Credentials and MFA Codes
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a "human-operated phishing platform" that impersonates advertising products for artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots like Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI ChatGPT, Perplexity, Meta Muse, and Manus.
The products, which claim to offer campaign optimization, spend audits, and business-account connections, are designed with one goal in mind: to capture credentials and multi-factor authentication (MFA) codes via spoofed login windows using the browser-in-the-browser (BitB) trick.
"Each product was built around the same action: Connect," Island researchers Oleg Zaytsev and Ofek Ronen said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "Clicking it opened a browser drawn inside the real browser. The fake address bar displayed trusted origins such as accounts.google.com or an Okta tenant, while the real browser remained on the phishing domain."
"Behind the interface, the platform kept every password attempt, fingerprinted the device, and let an operator pick which MFA challenge the victim saw next."
One of the websites in question is "museads.ai," which emerged on September 16, 2026, a little over a week after Meta launched Muse, its AI agent designed for personal workflows. Described as "Your AI ads manager for paid media workflows," the platform claimed to help customers reach buyers, connect their ad accounts, and run sponsored placements.
Prominently placed in the spoofed web page is a Prompt Box with a "Connect" button, clicking which triggers a BitB attack to capture a visitor's account credentials for Google, Meta, TikTok, and Okta workflows. This is accomplished by drawing a fake window displaying a bogus account sign-in form with the address bar pointing to a legitimate domain (e.g., accounts.google[.]com).
In the background, the victim's device is fingerprinted, and the information is transmitted to the attacker at the endpoint "/api/send/ip" over Socket.IO, after which operator commands and victim data are exchanged based on the login workflow. Armed with the account credentials, the attacker attempts to sign in to the account in real-time.
Commands to the phishing page are delivered through two Socket.IO events named operator-command and telegram-command. These commands drive the sign-in process, while the human operator can view what steps the victims are taking and decide the next course of action.
"In the inspected code, both pass the received command text to the same parser, so they don’t represent separate sets of page actions," Zaytsev, Lead Security Researcher at Island, told The Hacker News.
"The commands let the operator steer the victim through authentication in real time: request another password (/password), show an SMS or authenticator challenge (/2fa, /authApp), display Google prompts such as approval, QR, or number matching (/googlePrompt, /googleQrVerify, /verifyTap), or select Okta username, password, SMS, push, authenticator, and number-matching screens (/oktaUsername, /oktaPassword, /oktaSms2fa, /oktaApprove, /oktaAuthApp, /oktaVerifyTap). The operator can also reject a submitted code (/wrong2fa), keep the visitor waiting, or end or suppress the flow (/done, /ban)."
"Every brand gets its own pitch," the researchers explained. "ChatGPT promises a Monday Google Ads brief. Gemini promises MCC (manager account) and linked-client support. Claude gets its own advertising portal, Perplexity offers campaign planning and spend audits, and Manus offers a private Meta integration."
Users are assessed to be directed to these landing pages via fake invitation emails that impersonate these trusted brands to lend the attacks a veneer of legitimacy.
"Each one in this campaign poses as a believable product, with its own brand, pitch, and sign-in flow," the researchers pointed out. "They also move with the news."
Island said the AI ads pages are part of a broader phishing platform that supports a three-pronged operation, the two others being Google Ads-themed refund claims and payment confirmation, as well as recruitment-related sites for Tesla, Louis Vuitton, Nike, and Adecco.
All the identified websites have been found to share the same technology stack comprising Next.js and Socket.IO, and communicate with the same endpoints. What's more, the threat actors behind the operation have exposed source code for earlier versions of the platform through misconfigured public GitHub repositories.
The AI ads-focused campaign is designed to target agency staff, media buyers, and manager-account administrators, likely with the end goal of monetizing the ads accounts to run their own ad campaigns or sell them for profit, especially when they have a clean spend history.
According to a report published by Mimecast in July 2026, malware families like VietCredCare, DuckTail, NodeStealer, and PXA Stealer have engendered ad account theft at scale, leading to a "widespread commodity crime in the advertising ecosystem" where bad actors drain business budgets and sell accounts with good reputation in underground markets.
"For the victim, the card is the easy part: they can remove it within hours. Getting the account back is not," Island said. "Attackers typically add their own administrators and downgrade the legitimate owner, and recovery can take weeks or months while the account keeps serving ads. For a manager account, the damage reaches the agency’s clients."
To mitigate the threat, organizations are recommended to enable phishing-resistant authentication, review advertising control changes, and scrutinize AI integrations before connecting accounts.
The disclosure comes as Island revealed that threat actors are abusing Google-sponsored results to route unsuspecting users to custom GPTs or shared-AI chat content, which then redirect them to a fake Cloudflare verification page serving ClickFix-style lures to deliver NetSupport RAT.
"The campaign did not require a vulnerability in ChatGPT or Google," Island said. "It abused trusted platforms, attacker-authored content, paid search, and social engineering to move people toward malware delivery."
"Across a three-month observation period ending in August 2026, the broader delivery cluster included about 850 paid-ad landings, 26 lookalike ChatGPT destinations, and 71 Google Ads campaign IDs."
(The story was updated after publication to include additional insights from Island.)

articles.title: Microsoft and Nvidia launch Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark starting at $2,599 — RTX Spark preorders live now, coinciding with major Windows 11 changes for agentic AI
articles.text:
Microsoft and Nvidia launch Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark starting at $2,599 — RTX Spark preorders live now, coinciding with major Windows 11 changes for agentic AI
The company also highlighted "hundreds" of games, including Call of Duty.
At an event in San Francisco, Microsoft and Nvidia teamed up to show off the RTX Spark chip, along with the Surface Laptop Ultra and new features in Windows 11 that use the new system-on-a-chip's capabilities. The device, along with the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box and the broader Spark ecosystem is available for pre-order today, with devices shipping on October 16. 
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and Windows and Devices head Pavan Davuluri took turns on stage.
"We've reinvented the personal computer completely," Huang said.
Nadella described the event as one that would be building the "frontier ecosystem," anchoring it in Agent 365, Microsoft IQ, and Copilot. Davuluri describes Windows 11 as being the most secure platform for AI agents, highlighting containment for agents.
Windows 11 and Surface Laptop Ultra
The Surface Laptop Ultra will start at $2,599, while the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box will begin at $5,999. Both are available for pre-order. They, along with PCs from Asus, Dell, Lenovo, HP, and MSI will ship next Friday, Oct. 16.
Davuluri showed the Surface Laptop Ultra running Github Copilot and playing Gears of War: E-Day at 60 frames per second. He said that "hundreds" of AAA titles and indies will be available day one, and that Call of Duty will come to RTX Spark in 2027.
The 4.5-pound system has the brightest peak HDR on a laptop, he said. The system also features a magnetic USB-C charger it calls "magnetic connect." The connector plugs in, similar to Apple's MagSafe or the old Surface Connect ports, except using a standardized port.
An impressive video demo using multiple local and cloud models across Blender, Photoshop, ComfyUI, and Unreal Engine to make a workload that took hours instead of days was impressive, but also highly produced.
Microsoft compared the Spark to the M5 Pro in a MacBook Pro, promising performance up to 2.1 times faster to first token, 4.3 times faster image generation, and 6.2 times faster video generation.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
On Windows 11, there will be new quick actions in the Search menu in the Task Bar, making quick changes to settings, taking screenshots, or arranging windows using natural language. The Taskbar will also launch Copilot if the request calls for it, and you can jump from Search to Copilot.
Davuluri also described local models running from other vendors, including Hermes, OpenClaw, and Perplexity, performing a demo with Perplexity Computer. He also stated that Meta's Muse will come to Windows. There will be a new setup for Windows AI agents to make them easier to configure.
Davaluri also announced DGX Spark and Station for Windows, a "supercomputer" to bring "last quarter's frontier to your desktop." He showed off desktops from HP and Dell that will come "later this year." Up to this point, both have been exclusive for Linux.
Copilot and Local Agents
Microsoft's Jacob Andreou detailed the recent launch of the new Copilot, which is now getting access to local files, local models, and the ability to take actions on account of the user. It will still use cloud models, but will switch to local models when privacy is called for.
In one example, Andreou was grabbing tax data for his accountant. The system used a mix of local and cloud models to search for documents, rename them, and zip them into a folder. Copilot also wrote an email to the accountant to send on his behalf, which he approved. These features, he said, are coming over the next few months.
Containers, Trust, and Hybrid Ingelligence
Daviluri focused on the technical details of agents, including Microsoft Execution Containers, which is moving to general availability. These are sandboxes that are integrated with the OS to decide what data is shared with agents.
Windows will also require agents to attribute their actions to themselves. There will be IT actions for enterprises that want to set agentic rules once and use them across their fleet of devices.
Microsoft's Divya Venkataramu demonstrated this system, showing how she had access to documents even when agents didn't.
Davuluri also described hybrid intelligence, a mix of agents running locally and in the cloud to reduce token budgets. Microsoft's HydraFusion, which balances local and cloud agents, is coming from GitHub to Windows on October 15 for GitHub Copilot, the CLI, and VS Code, and will use new models like MAI Code 1.1 Flash and Nvidia's Nemotron. Using advanced quantization, DeepSeek V4 Flash can be used at 1.6 bits to run locally at 60GB of memory, he said.
Windows ML will serve as the runtime to deploy models across GPU, NPU, and CPU. Llama.cpp will come to Windows ML to give developers chances to experiment with new models at launch.
Microsoft's Kayla Cinnamon demonstrated Hybrid intelligence on a Surface RTX Dev Box by prompting GitHub Copilot to detect unused codes, packages, and feature flags to clean up code. With an Efficiency mode, Copilot selects a model automatically based on how complex a task is. A more complex prompt used GPT-6 Luna, while separate sub-agents ran locally.
