articles.title: Huawei and DeepSeek release open source AI tools in a bid to lower Nvidia exposure — but will programmers make the switch?
articles.text:
Huawei and DeepSeek release open source AI tools in a bid to lower Nvidia exposure — but will programmers make the switch?
DeepSeek just open sourced its Ascend kernel stack
- DeepSeek open sourced Ascend ports of its production kernel and communication libraries with Huawei's support in tow
- Published benchmarks ran on a proof-of-concept hardware kit DeepSeek says is not a publicly distributed release
- Two repositories are genuinely new and have received hundreds of GitHub stars versus Nvidia's thousands; the other announced components are updates to existing tools
DeepSeek has revealed it is open sourcing a set of infrastructure components for Huawei's Ascend accelerators.
DeepSeek published two completely new repositories, DeepGEMM-Ascend for matrix multiplication and DeepEP-Ascend for the all-to-all communication that mixture-of-experts models depend on.
The other components named in the announcement were upgrades: TileKernels, DeepSelect, and FlashMLA are existing projects that received Ascend-targeted updates, a distinction FourWeekMBA established from the GitHub creation dates.
An open source offering with limited use cases?
Reuters framed it as two Chinese firms deepening ties in search of an alternative to Nvidia, with Bloomberg called the centerpiece a programming language named TileLang, China's answer to CUDA.
The question is whether any of this matters when engineers are still on the fence about using these tools and access to Chinese compute remains, at best, elusive.
The biggest piece, as Bloomberg puts it, TileLang itself is neither new nor DeepSeek's own offering. It was open-sourced in January 2025, and its Huawei Ascend adapters were published in an external repository, tilelang-ascend, on September 29, 2025, a full year before the recent announcement.
While TileLang supports Nvidia's CUDA backend, it also supports Huawei's Ascend as an ecosystem backend, classified and maintained in a separate repository. One could therefore argue that TileLang is less a weapon aimed at Nvidia than a shared abstraction layer that half a dozen Chinese accelerator vendors are quietly standardizing on, with Huawei as the largest of several tenants rather than the landlord.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The new software has limitations: DeepGEMM-Ascend requires the Ascend 950 series and CANN 9.20. DeepEP-Ascend requires Ascend 950 silicon with UBMEM connectivity, so it targets a narrow audience beyond Huawei's own engineers and limited Chinese AI labs with access to that silicon.
Despite this, at a time when Nvidia chips are unlikely to be generously exported by the US or allowed in by China, Huawei's Ascend silicon has a large task on its shoulders: DeepGEMM-Ascend keeps the same Python package name and API shape as its CUDA sibling, and DeepEP-Ascend aligns its public buffer interfaces with the Nvidia version.
That is because the goal isn't a performance claim, but switching-cost reduction, and switching costs are precisely what Nvidia's moat is made of: it costs far too much for most developers to abandon CUDA or code their own alternative currently.
Public signals show this remains an uphill task; at the time of writing, DeepGEMM-Ascend has 515 stars and 39 forks, compared with DeepGEMM, which has a comfortable lead at 8,522 stars and 1,359 forks, for example. The story is similar for DeepEP-Ascend and DeepEP, with the latter surpassing 10,200 stars versus DeepEP-Ascend's 224.
The reputational problem Huawei faces here predates the repositories. ChinaTalk, citing the Financial Times, quotes a Huawei researcher describing CANN as making Ascend chips difficult and unstable to use, and a Chinese developer characterizing work on the 910B as a road full of pitfalls.
Epoch AI has reported that Huawei dispatches engineering teams to major customers such as Baidu and Tencent to help port CUDA training code and keep deployments running.
A frontier lab publishing its own production kernels partially answers that complaint, because it replaces vendor documentation with code that has survived contact with a model and can be optimized further. It is also, however, code that runs on one chip family, under one toolkit version, on firmware the rest of the world cannot download or even potentially access.

articles.title: Anthropic : son PDG Dario Amodei touche un salaire très "moyen"
articles.text:
Anthropic est THE entreprise dont on parle ces derniers mois dans le secteur de l'intelligence artificielle. Pourtant, son patron Dario Amodei est loin d'être un des patrons les mieux payés de la tech !
L'intelligence artificielle est devenue aujourd'hui synonyme de fonds gigantesques, dont l'unité de compte de base est le milliard de dollars. Mais si les investissements sont gigantesques, et la croissance des revenus assez remarquable, pour le moment, quelqu'un comme Dario Amodei - à la tête d'Anthropic - gagne encore sa vie de manière assez « modeste ». Même si ça ne devrait pas toujours être ainsi.
Dario Amodei a touché 18 millions de dollars l'an dernier
Vu les promesses que l'on nous fait avec l'intelligence artificielle, et même les rémunérations folles que les entreprises accordent aux stars de l'IA, on se serait attendu à ce que les patrons de ces sociétés soient au sommet. Et pourtant, Reuters nous apprend qu'un Dario Amodei n'a touché « que » 18 millions de dollars l'an dernier.
Sa rémunération s'est divisée entre la rémunération annuelle de 1,4 million d'euros, et des actions et des options dont la valeur est estimée à 16,4 millions d'euros. Sa sœur, Daniela Amodei, qui est la présidente de l'entreprise, a bénéficié des mêmes conditions salariales. Et il faut noter que ces chiffres n'ont rien d'impressionnant. La moyenne des rémunération des patrons des entreprises du S&P 500 (le cas exceptionnel d'Elon Musk mis à part) s'était en effet établi l'an dernier à 22,8 millions d'euros. Dario Amodei se situe donc dans la moyenne basse.
De nouvelles rémunérations sont prévues avec l'IPO qui arrive
Évidemment, ici ce n'est qu'un début. La rémunération « semble plutôt modeste pour une entreprise évaluée à 2 000 milliards de dollars, mais il sera intéressant de voir comment cela évoluera une fois que l'entreprise sera cotée en bourse » commente ainsi Courtney Yu, la directrice de la recherche d'Equilar, qui compile des données sur la rémunération des dirigeants.
Et en effet, Reuters précise que cette année, le conseil d'administration d'Anthropic a validé le potentiel octroi de nouvelles rémunérations, sous la forme d'actions. Des rémunérations qui ne seront débloquées que si un certain nombre de conditions sont remplies, certaines étant liées au fait que Dario Amodei reste en poste, quand d'autres le sont à la future IPO (entrée en Bourse) de la start-up IA.

articles.title: Gateron Launches Silent Low Profile 3.0 Black Switch for Mechanical Keyboards
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
Gateron Launches Silent Low Profile 3.0 Black Switch for Mechanical Keyboards
Following on its launch of the Low Profile 3.0 switch design, which has subsequently made appearances in mechanical keyboards from brands like NuPhy and Chilkey, Gateron has officially launched the latest version of its Low Profile 3.0 switches. The Gateron Low Profile Silent 3.0 Black switch is a linear switch designed with noise-sensitive users and professional environments in mind. As is the case with many other silent switch designs, the Black variant uses silicone o-rings on stem components to silence and cushion the bottom- and top-out sounds. Currently, the Gateron LP 3.0 Black switches are available from (https://www.gateron.com/products/gateron-ks-33-low-profile-silent-30-mechanical-switch-set?VariantsId=11683)]Gateron directly at $14 for 35 switches or $44 for 110 switches. 
Unlike many other silent switch designs, the Black Low Profile 3.0 switches aren't limited by their o-rings, and they feature the same 1.7 mm actuation distance and 3.4 mm total travel as their non-silent counterparts. The Black switches are the heaviest in Gateron's silent 3.0 switch line-up, coming in at 50 gf (±15 gf). The switches have a full POM stem with a nylon bottom housing and clear PC top housing, and they are factory lubricated for smooth keystrokes. The clear top housing also means that keyboard backlighting should still be visible through the switch.Gateron's Low Profile 3.0 switch standard is unique among low-profile switches in that it uses the same 5-pin layout and sockets as regular Cherry MX-style switches, meaning it is easy for manufacturers to offer both low-profile and full-height versions of the same keyboard with only a switch plate swap.

articles.title: Google crea una plataforma para hacer videojuegos con IA sin saber programar
articles.text:
Google lanzó Playground, una nueva plataforma experimental que utiliza inteligencia artificial para permitir que cualquier persona cree videojuegos para navegador a partir de instrucciones escritas en lenguaje natural. La herramienta busca reducir las barreras tradicionales del desarrollo de videojuegos, ya que no exige conocimientos de programación, diseño o ilustración para comenzar a crear un proyecto.
La plataforma fue presentada por Google Labs, el espacio de la compañía dedicado a probar productos y tecnologías experimentales. Playground permite describir qué tipo de juego se quiere desarrollar y utilizar la IA para generar los elementos necesarios a partir de esas indicaciones.
La propuesta está dirigida inicialmente a mayores de 18 años en Estados Unidos, aunque Google tiene previsto ampliar su disponibilidad a otros países.
Cómo funciona Google Playground
Para comenzar un proyecto, los usuarios pueden elegir entre diferentes géneros, como juegos de preguntas y respuestas o carreras, o iniciar una creación desde cero. También pueden decidir si quieren desarrollar una experiencia en dos o tres dimensiones y seleccionar entre un videojuego para un jugador o una propuesta multijugador.
Después, el usuario puede explicar mediante texto cómo quiere que funcione el videojuego. Puede indicar las reglas, la mecánica, el tipo de jugabilidad y el estilo visual. La inteligencia artificial se encarga de interpretar esas instrucciones y convertirlas en elementos interactivos.
La plataforma también permite cargar imágenes propias. Playground puede transformar esas imágenes en recursos para el videojuego y adaptarlas al estilo visual elegido para el proyecto.
Este funcionamiento elimina una parte importante de las barreras que tradicionalmente existen para crear un videojuego. Hasta ahora, una persona interesada en desarrollar uno debía aprender programación o recurrir a especialistas para construir aspectos como los gráficos, las mecánicas y la interacción.
Los juegos pueden compartirse y seguir modificándose
Una vez generado, el videojuego puede ejecutarse tanto desde un teléfono como desde una computadora. Los proyectos pueden mantenerse privados, compartirse mediante un enlace o publicarse en la galería Explorar de Playground.
Los videojuegos que llegan a esa galería pueden incorporar características como tablas de clasificación, lo que permite crear experiencias competitivas. Además, publicar un proyecto no significa que quede terminado: los creadores pueden continuar modificándolo después de ponerlo a disposición de otros usuarios.
Google también anticipó una futura integración con Unity Spark. Esta tecnología podría incorporar capacidades adicionales para desarrollar gráficos y mecánicas tridimensionales más avanzadas.
La integración resulta relevante porque Unity es una de las plataformas más utilizadas en la industria para crear videojuegos. Si la herramienta se incorpora a Playground, los usuarios podrían acceder a recursos de desarrollo más sofisticados sin tener que dominar todas las herramientas profesionales utilizadas habitualmente por los estudios.
La inteligencia artificial cambia la creación de videojuegos
Google Playground forma parte de una tendencia más amplia en la industria: el uso de inteligencia artificial para permitir que personas sin experiencia técnica desarrollen videojuegos.
La idea también está siendo explorada por otras plataformas. Roblox, por ejemplo, presentó en julio una función denominada Build que permite crear juegos utilizando indicaciones escritas en lenguaje natural.
La diferencia está en que estas herramientas no buscan únicamente automatizar determinadas tareas de los desarrolladores, sino permitir que una persona describa directamente lo que quiere construir y deje que la IA transforme esas instrucciones en un producto jugable.
Playground tiene límites de uso
Google Playground puede utilizarse gratuitamente para navegar por el catálogo y jugar los proyectos disponibles. Sin embargo, la creación de videojuegos funciona mediante un sistema de tokens semanales.
El nivel gratuito ofrece una cantidad limitada de estos tokens, mientras que los suscriptores de Google One AI cuentan con límites de uso superiores. Por ahora, la generación de juegos está disponible únicamente para mayores de 18 años en Estados Unidos.
Con Playground, Google amplía su presencia en el sector de los videojuegos después de experiencias como Stadia y YouTube Playables. Esta vez, el foco no está únicamente en jugar, sino en utilizar inteligencia artificial para que más personas puedan convertirse en creadoras de videojuegos.

articles.text:
My 3 top-rated portable power station deals for WFH blackout insurance this Prime Day
If the power goes, the (router) lights stay on
I've spotted a lot of portable power station deals in the Prime Day sale. And while you can't really go wrong with Bluetti, EcoFlow, Jackery, and Anker based on my experiences, it can sometimes become a confusing mess of numbers once you start digging into the differences. So, these are my top three recommendations if you're looking for a little extra insurance while working from home and you're struck by a power outage that keeps you offline (or 'the dark ages', as I like to call it).
For laptops & Wi-Fi routers
288Wh | 600W | <15ms switchover | ★★★★⯪
The Bluetti Elite 30 V2 is my top-rated budget power station with 4.5 stars, with more than enough juice to keep you online during a short, unexpected outage. We used it through several storms during testing.
➡️ UK price: £179 (was £239)
For workstation setups
1024Wh | 1800W | 10ms switchover | ★★★★★
My Editor's Choice portable power station overall, it scored a flawless 5 stars and put in a robust performance during testing. In the US, it's also available with an extra battery for $1019 at Amazon.
➡️ UK price: now £549 (was £699)
For garden offices & heavy appliances
2042Wh | 2200W | <20ms switchover | ★★★★⯪
A high-capacity, high-output power station that earned 4.5 stars in review and saved our reviewer's sanity (and his kids' dinner).
➡️ UK price: now £765 (£1061)
Having reviewed some of the best portable power stations you can get, these are the key specs you want to look for:
Wh - this is the battery capacity - it's like the electrical version of a fuel tank, and it gives you some idea how long the power station will last until you need to recharge it. The higher the Wh, the more battery power you have, the longer it'll run.
W - this is the output the unit can put out. A laptop is typically up to around 65-100W to power while a standard PC is around 200W; a larger appliance like a fridge can be around 300W. Some power stations have dual surge modes, so you get extra power output for high-wattage devices.
UPS switchover - the time it takes during a power outage for the power station to kick in. The quicker, the better so you don't lose connection if it's hooked up to your router or modem. At best, select a unit that kicks in in under 20 milliseconds, but under 10 milliseconds is better.

articles.title: Lancement supposé des Core 2000HX, Intel n'en aurait toujours pas terminé avec Raptor Lake
articles.text:
Alors que la DDR4 est moins onéreuse que la DDR5, le retour d'une gamme de CPU Raptor Lake Next viendrait de réduire (un peu) le prix des laptops.
Tout porte à croire que le retour de l'architecture Raptor Lake concernera des processeurs relativement haut de gamme. Aucune puce Core 3 ou Core 5 n'est pour l'heure évoquée.
Raptor Lake de retour en 2027
Souvenez-vous, en juin dernier nous évoquions un informateur fiable pour évoquer la possibilité de voir des processeurs Raptor Lake revenir sur le devant de la scène dès l'année prochaine.
Cette gamme « Raptor Lake Next » donnait l'impression qu'Intel n'en avait pas terminé avec cette architecture pourtant lancée il y a maintenant plus de quatre ans avec les Core Ultra 13000. Aujourd'hui, le site VideoCardz apporte des précisions : cette gamme serait exclusivement réservée au segment HX, celui des ordinateurs portables les plus performants.
Intel aurait décidé de baptiser ses nouvelles puces Core 2000HX afin de se rapprocher de la nomenclature utilisée pour les puces Nova Lake, les Core Ultra 4000HX. Nous n'en savons cependant pas plus sur les noms exacts des puces, mais des détails ont fuité à propos de leurs caractéristiques techniques.
Le haut de gamme serait représenté par un modèle Core 9 2000HX doté de 24 cœurs partagés entre 8 cœurs performants et 16 cœurs efficaces. À côté de lui, deux Core 7 sont évoqués : le premier doté de 20 cœurs (8P + 12E) et le second avec 14 cœurs (6P + 8E). Des configurations qui rappellent celles des actuels Raptor Lake-HX.
Un recyclage qui pourrait avoir du sens
De fait, le positionnement de cette gamme qui fait du neuf avec du vieux paraît assez clair : Intel ne semble pas prévoir de puces d'entrée de gamme ou de portables à destination des familles, les créateurs de contenus sont visés.
Aucun modèle des séries H, P ou U n'est ainsi prévu et il n'est pas non plus prévu de révolutionner le monde du portable, pour ça Intel compte davantage sur Nova Lake. Non, Raptor Lake Next se rapproche bien davantage d'une sorte de retour d'une architecture éprouvée afin de coller au contexte très particulier que l'on connaît aujourd'hui.
En effet, alors que l'on traverse sans doute la pire crise inflationniste de l'histoire sur le secteur de la mémoire vive, Raptor Lake Next pourrait avoir une carte à jouer. La crise de la RAM est davantage perceptible sur la DDR5 et, ça tombe plutôt bien, Raptor Lake était une architecture capable de cohabiter aussi bien avec de la DDR5 qu'avec de la DDR4, beaucoup moins onéreuse. Un atout bien sûr conservé sur Raptor Lake Next.
Reste évidemment à connaître la tarification envisagée par Intel pour cette vraie fausse nouvelle gamme. Un processeur 24 cœurs peut disposer d'une bonne réserve de puissance et la question de son potentiel, voire de sa mise en concurrence avec les générations plus modernes, se pose.

articles.title: New kitchen, new me — these are the Amazon Prime Day deals I’m buying to upgrade my new home’s cooking space
articles.text:
New kitchen, new me — these are the Amazon Prime Day deals I’m buying to upgrade my new home’s cooking space
My kitchen needs an update
I’ve recently moved into a brand new home, and the tiny kitchen I had to make do with in my old apartment has over doubled in size — and this Prime Day I’m looking for a brand new suite of kitchen gadgets, and general cookware to fill it with.
Top of my list is an airfryer — specifically the Ninja Air Fryer DoubleStack XL which is currently $40-off (now $209.95 at Amazon, and you can save £60 on it at Amazon UK) thanks to its efficient size and cooking prowess — but I’m hoping to indulging myself with a new coffee maker, or perhaps the Ninja Creami I’ve heard so much about (it’s $169.99 at Amazon US, saving you 23%-off, and £153.89 at Amazon UK, a 38% discount).
I’ve already grabbed a few non-techy essentials to fill out my kitchen, and I’ll highlight them below too with reasons you should consider them.
Today's best Ninja deals
The Ninja Double Stack stands as the best airfryer in the world based on our tests thanks to its generous capacity for its small footprint and its “top-tier” cooking performance. Normally it is a bit pricey, but whenever it goes on sale (like right now) it’s one I have my eye on because it represents such an amazing deal.
The Creami is a few years older at this point, but it is still a capable ice cream maker — and I expect it’ll be vital next Summer if the UK faces another record-breaking heatwave which is why I’m considering grabbing it while I can for a discount.
Lastly, the only item I have on this list is the Ninja Kettle (it’s on sale in the UK, in the US I’ve picked a snazzy but simple coffee maker). I love coffee, matcha, chai, and fruit teas, while my wife likes classic black tea, and all need different temperatures for the best results — this kettle lets me easily heat water to the perfect temp for each in no time, and it’s easily my most used (and probably most loved) appliance.
My other favorite Prime Day deals for my kitchen
I’ve tried a few different non-stick pans over the years, but fears over forever chemicals and frustration at safer coatings that never seem to last have brought me back to the ol’ reliable steel pan — and from my experience GreenPan’s are excellent.
I’ve been giving pieces from its 5-ply Premiere collection a whirl in my new flat — which combine steel and aluminum sheets to maximize heat efficiency and resilience while keeping them a less weighty — but as they aren’t on sale right now I’m highlighting this collection of 11 pots and pans, which for only $119.99 are a steal (especially as you get lids with everything too).
The thing to remember is unlike typical non-stick, steel pans will need a bit more oil, and plenty of time to get up to temperature before you add anything (around two to three minutes), but the upshot is they’re dishwasher and oven safe to high temperatures, and can survive metal tools — which for me is precisely what I need.
In the UK GreenPan’s options aren’t discounted at the time of writing, but the Cuisinart Chef’s Classic set should fill a similar role.
The Tormek T-1 isn’t on sale and it is a little pricey, but I’m highlighting it for any home chefs who have just bought new knives, or who are considering upgrading their old dull ones this Prime Day.
I’ve tried cheap and ‘easy’ knife sharpeners but they’re generally ineffective and can create an uneven edge. Meanwhile, sharpening stones are pretty intimidating.
The Tormek T1 works a treat. It’s super simple to use thanks to the instructions and helped transform all my knives into elite kitchen tools again — including some close to a decade-old blades I was close to throwing out given how useless they had become after years of abuse.
If you cook plenty and have some knives you want to look after, but not a lot of time to sharpen them regularly a more old-fashioned way this piece of kit is something to consider — though if you’re on a budget you may want to wait and see if a Black Friday sale can make it cheaper.
Finally as an avid baker I've picked out some essential baking gear I use (or is very similar to the kit I have at home). My favorites of the bunch are the Brod & Taylor Bread Steel and Sourdough Home.
The steel is perfect for crusting the bottom of your loaves, but also works well with pizza and other doughs (I think most ovens should have one), while the Sourdough Home is more of a luxury — but one I adore nonetheless.
I keep my sourdough tucked away inside it at a constant cool 5-degrees celsius, and can easily make the home warmer (usually 24-degrees) when I’m getting my starter ready to be baked with. The Home makes managing your starter all-year-round much less of a chore, though it isn’t something I’d recommend for beginners — just because you don’t want to splash out on gear and only bake a few loaves.
But if you’ve fallen in love with sourdough baking and want to treat yourself (or the baker in your life) this deal is perfect.

articles.title: Cómo crear imágenes de Las Guerreras K-pop como Los Jóvenes Titanes
articles.text:
Crear imágenes de Las Guerreras K-pop como integrantes de Los Jóvenes Titanes requiere seguir una serie de pasos desde la aplicación o versión web de Gemini, la inteligencia artificial (IA) de Google, sin necesidad de descargar programas piratas o durar varias horas en edición.
El proceso depende de asignar una función clara a cada archivo adjunto en el chatbot. Una imagen debe definir los rostros, peinados y cantidad de personajes; la otra debe aportar la estética de Los Jóvenes Titanes, con su paleta de colores, arquitectura, vestuarios y tipo de encuadre.
En este contexto, se explica cuáles son los pasos a seguir para transformar a Las Guerreras K-pop en personajes de Los Jóvenes Titanes, sumado al prompt que se le puede suministrar a la IA para que genere la imagen en pocos segundos.
Qué imágenes se necesitan para comenzar la ilustración
La primera imagen debe mostrar a Las Guerreras K-pop con buena resolución. Conviene elegir una imagen en la que se vean las tres protagonistas de la película de Netflix, ya sea de cuerpo entero o desde la cintura. Esa referencia permite que Gemini identifique rasgos como el cabello, la distribución del grupo, los accesorios y la ropa.
La segunda imagen debe funcionar como guía del mundo de los Jóvenes Titanes. Puede incluir la Torre Titán, una ciudad nocturna, una sala de mando o una escena de acción con líneas marcadas y colores planos.
No es necesario que aparezcan Robin, Raven, Chico Bestia, Cyborg o Starfire. La referencia solo debe transmitir el ambiente visual que se busca reproducir.
Cómo adjuntar los archivos en el chat de Gemini
El trabajo debe empezar en una conversación nueva dentro de la aplicación o la versión web de Gemini. Primero se debe adjuntar la imagen de Las Guerreras K-pop y, después, el archivo que represente el estilo de los Jóvenes Titanes. Ese orden ayuda a diferenciar el contenido de cada referencia.
La primera imagen debe quedar asociada a las protagonistas y la segunda al universo gráfico que se quiere recrear. Junto a los archivos, resulta útil incluir una frase inicial que aclare la función de ambos materiales.
Por ejemplo: “Usar la primera imagen para conservar los rasgos generales y la posición de tres cantantes ficticias. Usar la segunda imagen como referencia de estilo, escenario, colores, vestuario y composición”.
Qué prompt es útil para la generación de la imagen
El prompt debe especificar el número de personajes, la orientación de la ilustración, el plano y el lugar donde transcurre la escena. Para esta propuesta, puede pedirse una composición horizontal, con las tres jóvenes de cuerpo entero, ubicadas frente a una torre de superhéroes o sobre una azotea de una ciudad ficticia.
Una instrucción ideal es: “Crear una ilustración horizontal de tres cantantes ficticias inspiradas en la primera imagen de referencia, convertidas en integrantes de un equipo juvenil de superhéroes”.
Se puede agregar: “Ubicarlas frente a una torre tecnológica en una ciudad nocturna. Usar líneas definidas, colores planos, sombras simples y una estética de animación inspirada en Los Jóvenes Titanes”. El pedido debe evitar nombres, emblemas y uniformes oficiales de personajes existentes.
Cómo corregir errores sin reiniciar la conversación con Gemini
La primera versión puede presentar problemas en las manos, las expresiones, la cantidad de personajes o los detalles del vestuario. En lugar de escribir un prompt nuevo desde cero, es más efectivo pedir correcciones concretas. Esto permite conservar los elementos que ya funcionan y modificar solo el aspecto que necesita ajustes.
Algunos pedidos útiles son: “Mantener la escena y corregir las manos de la personaje ubicada a la izquierda”, “cambiar el peinado de la segunda integrante sin modificar su traje” o “eliminar el edificio del fondo y agregar una torre tecnológica original”. Las instrucciones breves reducen el riesgo de que la herramienta altere por completo la composición generada.
Qué revisar antes de descargar o compartir la imagen
Antes de descargar y publicar la ilustración, conviene comprobar que no incluya logos, nombres, títulos ni símbolos oficiales vinculados con los Jóvenes Titanes u otras franquicias.
La imagen puede inspirarse en el lenguaje visual de las series de superhéroes, pero debe evitar presentarse como una producción oficial o una pieza autorizada.
Asimismo, es clave incorporar una aclaración visible que indique que se trata de fan art generado con inteligencia artificial. Si se necesita una versión para imprimir o colorear, se puede pedir una variante con líneas negras, fondo blanco, sin sombras ni color y con espacios amplios.

articles.title: AMD Confirms FSR 4 Is Coming to APUs by the End of 2026
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
AMD Confirms FSR 4 Is Coming to APUs by the End of 2026
AMD has confirmed that its FSR 4 machine learning upscaling technology will be available for APUs with integrated graphics by the end of this year. Jack Huynh, senior vice president and general manager of the computing and graphics group, shared this news with the South Korean media in Seoul. He mentioned that FSR 4 will be coming to more devices as AMD optimizes the software stack for APUs. Initially, FSR 4 was only available on RDNA 4-based Radeon RX 9000 series graphics cards. This summer, AMD added support for FSR 4 on RDNA 3 hardware with Radeon RX 7000 series discrete graphics cards. However, APUs like "Strix Halo," which feature RDNA 3.5 integrated graphics, were not supported. Now, it appears these models will receive official support by the end of the year. Below is the machine-translated official quote:
AMD's Jack HuynhWe will expand FSR 4 across our product lineup, including APUs, gaming laptops and handheld devices, by the end of this year.
AMD's FSR Upscaling 4.1 model for RDNA 3 GPUs differs fundamentally from the RDNA 4 version. RDNA 4 supports native processing for 8-bit floating point data, allowing FSR 4.1 on RDNA 4 to run on FP8 data types. To enable the FSR 4.1 Upscaling model on RDNA 3, AMD must convert this to 8-bit integer data, as RDNA 3 hardware uses INT8 data types without FP8 support. Therefore, it is likely that RDNA 3.5 has required AMD to perform additional optimizations and possibly develop a different model. It is known that RDNA 2-based Radeon RX 6000 will receive FSR 4 in 2027, but APUs currently seem to be a higher priority.
Sources:

articles.title: La première Jaguar électrique nouvelle génération se dévoile, on dirait un concept-car
articles.text:
Pour une première voiture électrique depuis son rachat, le constructeur opte pour un modèle au look pour le moins original. Si l'on peut croire à un concept-car, c'est pourtant bel et bien le design de la nouvelle Jaguar Type 01.
Jaguar a présenté la Type 01, une grande berline électrique basée sur le concept Type 00, qui avait déjà suscité des réactions mitigées chez le public habituel du constructeur. Ici, le fabricant positionne cette Type 01 comme son véhicule de route le plus puissant à ce jour.
Une transition du concept à la réalité
La transition du concept à la version finale a conservé la majorité des choix esthétiques de l'idée de départ. On retrouve la silhouette épurée, le profil latéral allongé et les jantes de 23 pouces (imaginez le tarif des pneus) caractéristiques du prototype. Le passage à une configuration quatre portes confère cependant des proportions jugées plus équilibrées.
L'aménagement intérieur privilégie les matériaux nobles, avec du cuir et des détails en laiton, tout ce que l'on attend d'un véhicule haut de gamme. On retrouve au centre du tableau de bord, un écran OLED de 24 pouces de diagonale, ainsi que plusieurs écrans supplémentaires de 7 pouces, intégrés à la structure centrale.
À l'arrière, une caméra remplace la vitre arrière, avec retransmission sur écran. Vous avez bien lu, le fabricant préfère filmer et retranscrire l'extérieur via un écran, que de l'afficher via une simple fenêtre. Quoi que l'on en pense, niveau confidentialité, c'est un atout majeur.
Beaucoup de chevaux et beaucoup d'euros à dépenser
Sur le plan technique, trois moteurs électriques développent une puissance maximale de 1 016 chevaux et 1 365 Newton-mètres de couple. Le Type 01 accélère de 0 à 100 km/h en 3,2 secondes et atteint 180 km/h en 4,0 secondes supplémentaires. La batterie de 118 kWh offre une autonomie annoncée de 645 km. La recharge rapide en courant continu permet de récupérer 320 kilomètres d'autonomie en 13 minutes.
Les commandes devraient débuter début 2027, avec des livraisons prévues à partir du deuxième semestre de l'année. Le prix de départ est fixé à 130 000 dollars. En espérant pour le constructeur, que cet argent comble le trou dans la caisse laissé par une précédente cyberattaque.

articles.title: Microsoft Rebuilds Windows 11 Search, Adds Typed Commands and Inline Copilot
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
Microsoft Rebuilds Windows 11 Search, Adds Typed Commands and Inline Copilot
Microsoft has unveiled a rebuilt Windows 11 Search at its Windows and Surface event, and it can now change system settings straight from the taskbar. Windows chief Pavan Davuluri showed it on stage, and Microsoft says the box will handle thousands of quick actions typed as simple commands. Examples include "switch to dark mode", "turn on Bluetooth", "dim my screen", "mute", and "minimize all my windows". Microsoft says these are only the first batch, and Phone Link actions such as sending a text message from a connected phone are also planned. The more interesting part for enthusiasts is probably under the hood. The new Search is built on WinUI 3, which Microsoft says makes it faster and lighter on system resources, and early testing apparently showed sizable gains in speed and memory use. 
The layout is now a single list of results, replacing the current design with its large preview pane. Search should also cope better with typos and synonyms, and richer file details and web previews are planned for later this year. Copilot is part of it too, of course. Its answers show up inside Search, with a shortcut to open the full app. This follows the July cleanup that removed ads and promotional content from Search and added a setting to hide web and Microsoft Store suggestions. The new version started rolling out to Windows Insiders in the Experimental channel on October 7. Microsoft is targeting this fall for regular Windows 11 PCs, though there's no exact date yet.
Sources:

OLED gaming monitors are hot right now, and Prime Big Deal Days is an excellent time to be in the market.
OLED panels are quickly becoming a must-have item for desktop PCs. Most of us were introduced to the panel technology in smartphones, and it’s become increasingly popular on laptops. For desktop gamers seeking an immediate visual upgrade, OLED is the way to go, and fortunately, Prime Day is proving to be a great time to take the plunge. From massive DQHD panels on the Samsung Odyssey OLED G9 (G93SC) to more value-oriented offerings like the Acer Nitro VG277U Xbiip, we have you covered.

Mega-Ultrawide OLED Gaming Monitors
Samsung's Odyssey OLED G9 (9G3SC) is massive, with a 49-inch QD-OLED panel. It also features integrated Wi-Fi for interfacing with Samsung's Gaming Hub service.

Mega-ultrawide gaming monitors are not for the faint of heart. Not only can these monitors be quite expensive, but they can also occupy a substantial amount of desktop space. However, for those who have the need (and the space), there are options such as the Samsung Odyssey OLED G9 (G93SC), which features a 49-inch DQHD (5120 x 1440) QD-OLED panel. Brightness tops out at 250 nits (typical), and you'll still get a fast 0.03 ms GtG response time. The monitor supports AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, and it's also Nvidia G-Sync compatible. As for ports, you'll find one DisplayPort 1.4, two HDMI 2.1, and two downstream USB-C ports.
34-inch Ultrawide OLED Gaming Monitors

If you're looking for something more in a “mid-range” size class, the AOC Agon Pro AG346UCD should be on your shopping list. This is a 34-inch QD-OLED monitor with a 3440 x 1440 resolution and a 165 Hz refresh rate. While that figure may not be as high as the 240 Hz more commonly found with 34-inch panels, the Agon Pro AG346UCD is priced at just $599, taking $50 off its typical asking price. In our review, we praised the monitor for its well-saturated color, excellent contrast, and out-of-the-box accuracy.
It's also worth considering the MSI MAG 341CQP, priced at $549.99 ($100 off its usual selling price). You still get a 34-inch QD-OLED panel, but the maximum refresh rate is slightly higher at 175 Hz.
27-inch OLED Gaming Monitors
This mid-sized gaming monitor sports a QD-OLED panel rated at a decent 400 nits of brightness, with a 240 Hz refresh and a resolution of 2560 x 1440. If you're after a gaming screen on a budget and want inky blacks and saturated colors, this is a tough deal to beat.

The Alienware AW2725DF might be small in stature, but its 27-inch QHD panel delivers a sizzling 360 Hz maximum refresh rate.

One of the best things to happen to gaming monitors in recent years has been the emergence of OLED panel technology. OLED panels are fast, offer rich color and blacker blacks, but have come with a big price premium. But as the technology has matured, prices have come down. That fact is exemplified by the 27-inch, 240 Hz model (VG277U Xbiip) from Acer's Nitro line. It sports a 240 Hz QD-OLED panel rated at 400 Nits of brightness and a 0.03 ms response time. articles.title: Netgear reveals new dark web monitoring tool which will tell you if your personal data turns up online
articles.text:
Netgear reveals new dark web monitoring tool which will tell you if your personal data turns up online
Shine a light on your data
- A new dark web monitoring service has been launched for Netgear customers
- Netgear Dark Web Monitoring is available on Netgear routers supporting its Armor and Armor Plus plans
- Expert analysis of the dark web shows that over 15 billion personal records are available to purchase
Netgear has announced a new service whicht conducts dark web monitoring and notifies you when your stolen data is found lurking in someone else’s database.
Announced as part of its Armor and Armor Plus plans, the Dark Web Monitoring service is available to subscribers via the Netgear app.
The dark web is the hidden arena of the internet where various “out of sight” transactions are conducted. While it has legitimate uses (such as dissidents accessing resources via Tor), it is also the home of a black market in data – typically stolen from large organizations, companies, and governments in successful hacking attempts.
Collection of tools
Owners of the data should be notified by law when their information is stolen. However, often it isn’t until personal information (and more valuable data such as company secrets or software engines) hits the dark web that companies are even aware that they have been hacked. This makes dark web monitoring services such as Netgear’s new feature particularly attractive.
Netgear’s service is added to its existing collection of tools for Armor and Armor Plus subscribers. These include protection against malware and exploits, intrusion, anomaly, and DDoS detection and protection, and a VPN with adblock and anti-tracking.
The dark web monitoring feature adds to these by offering continuous monitoring of the dark web for emails, phone numbers, and financial details lost during a data breach. National Insurance numbers are also monitored.
If anything is found, Netgear Dark Web Monitoring sends alerts and recommends actions. It also offers an Identity Protection Score to illustrate exposure, and as households improve their security the tool tracks their progress.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Finding exposed data
While free services can uncover data that has been exposed in data leaks, the dark web is home to stolen information that may not yet be disclosed. This could be because the organization that has been hacked hasn’t got around to sharing the breach with their customers – or because they don’t know it has even happened.
This makes an active monitoring service like Netgear Dark Web Monitoring particularly valuable.
“Most people think about network security as something that happens within their home,” says Jonathan Oakes, Senior Vice President and General Manager of NETGEAR’s Home Networking Division. “But your details can end up exposed somewhere else entirely, in a breach at a company you’ve never even dealt with directly. Dark Web Monitoring means finding out while there’s still time to act.”
Netgear Dark Web Monitoring is available with its routers’ Armor ($99/year) and Armor Plus ($149.99/year) plans, available to be purchased via the Netgear app.

articles.title: Microsoft coloca Copilot e IA até na barra de busca do Windows • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Microsoft coloca Copilot e IA até na barra de busca do Windows
Nova interface permite alterar configurações, enviar mensagens e conversar com o Copilot sem abrir outros aplicativos do Windows 11.
A Microsoft apresentou uma nova experiência para a barra de busca do Windows 11. A novidade permitirá buscas com texto em linguagem natural e execução de ações no próprio campo de pesquisa, possibilitando, além da localização de arquivos, controlar recursos do PC e conversar com o Copilot.
A empresa anunciou a atualização durante o evento da linha Surface, em São Francisco, nos Estados Unidos. A Microsoft também apresentou o Hybrid Intelligence, que combina modelos de IA locais com processamento na nuvem, conforme cada necessidade.
De acordo com o Engadget, a nova experiência de busca do Windows 11 começará a ser distribuída durante o outono do Hemisfério Norte, período que termina em dezembro. Já os recursos do Copilot baseados no Hybrid Intelligence serão liberados gradualmente para PCs compatíveis ao longo dos próximos meses.
O vice-presidente executivo de Windows e Dispositivos da Microsoft, Pavan Davuluri, demonstrou a nova interface durante o evento. Ele explicou que os usuários poderão encontrar conteúdos e executar ações a partir do mesmo campo de pesquisa.
Existe a possibilidade de controlar o volume do microfone e ligar o modo escuro, por exemplo. Esses ajustes normalmente são manuais, nas configurações do sistema. Um outro exemplo, mais simples, mostra como a barra de pesquisa consegue entender o pedido do usuário sem fazer uma pesquisa exata. No vídeo, o Windows ativa o modo Não Perturbe com um simples comando de “dnd on” (“do not disturb” on).
A busca também poderá acessar funções de dispositivos conectados ao computador. Caso um celular esteja sincronizado, por exemplo, será possível pedir o envio de uma mensagem sem abrir outro app.
O Copilot também estará presente de forma nativa na barra de busca, mesmo tendo um aplicativo dedicado no Windows. “Para tornar a IA parte da vida cotidiana, precisamos levá-la aos locais que as pessoas mais utilizam, no fluxo da ambição humana”, afirmou Davuluri durante o evento.
Durante o evento, a Microsoft apresentou o Hybrid Intelligence, um sistema que determinará se uma tarefa de IA deve ser executada por modelos locais, rodando diretamente no computador, ou por modelos em nuvem. A ideia é otimizar o consumo de tokens, destinando tarefas mais complexas para ferramentas online.
Com o recurso ativado, o app do Copilot ganha permissão para consultar arquivos e interagir com configurações e outros aplicativos da máquina. Tarefas mais complexas devem continuar sendo direcionadas para a nuvem, mas aquelas com maior custo de processamento ou que envolvam arquivos privados serão executadas no próprio PC.
A empresa afirma que a arquitetura também estará disponível para desenvolvedores que criarem aplicativos para o Windows. A execução de agentes locais será isolada por meio dos Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC). A tecnologia cria ambientes separados para limitar o acesso desses sistemas a outras partes do computador durante a execução de tarefas.
A Microsoft demonstrou, também, o uso da funcionalidade com o [Autopilot](https://tecnoblog.net/noticias/microsoft-anuncia-agente-24×7-chamado-autopilot/), capaz de executar tarefas a partir de arquivos armazenados no computador. Segundo o Engadget, todo o processamento do exemplo realizado foi local, sem o envio dos documentos para a internet.

articles.title: New Linux tech compresses memory in RAM, as RAM, for 452x speedup — new CRAM method offers giant boost to compressed memory reads
articles.text:
New Linux tech compresses memory in RAM, as RAM, for 452x speedup — new CRAM method offers giant boost to compressed memory reads
The new method allows access using standard memory semantics instead of as a block device, drastically improving performance.
A new compression model, called CRAM, offers a different path to compression that avoids swap entirely by keeping the compressed data in memory, and it offers up to 452x the performance of ZRAM. I was a kid in the 1990s when the idea seemed so simple to me: I can use PKZIP to compress my files, so why can't we do that with RAM? Indeed, I am not a singular genius, and many other people had the same idea, so memory compression has been a feature of most operating systems for a long time. In Linux, the most popular options are zswap and ZRAM, but both of these options are fundamentally swap-layer features. CRAM is a new take that claims to boost performance tremendously.
CRAM was conceptualized by Gregory Price and his team at Meta. The central realization that seems to have spurred the development of CRAM is that the largest portion of the performance hit from compressed memory isn't the compression; that's tiny. No, the largest hit apparently stems mostly from the fault itself and the swap behavior. So the thinking seems to have been "what if we just do zram, but completely in memory instead of as swap?"
That's a gross simplification of an enormously complex project, but what CRAM seems to be doing is making use of mechanisms Linux already has to enable radically higher-performance compressed memory, particularly on reads. It uses a private NUMA node (essentially, a ghost CPU) instead of pretending to be a block device, and this lets Linux continue using all of its memory semantics, including migration and ballooning, to manage CRAM.
A critical part is the "Chicken Bit," which tells Linux that it has to stop trying to use CRAM while it is busy managing allocations. See, compressed memory seems straightforward until you start actually thinking about it. Compressibility of data varies tremendously based on what you're compressing, all the way from big piles of zeroes (perfectly compressible) up to already-compressed data (non-compressible). Given that, how do you know how much "logical" RAM you have when some of it is compressed? And how do you know when you're going to run out?
CRAM hasn't actually solved that problem yet, it seems; the slides I'm working from seem to establish this as an unsolved problem and an area of ongoing research. But the Chicken Bit is one way it can at least stop cascading failures (colorfully called a "poison storm" in the presentation) from happening when writes outpace CRAM's ability to allocate them.
Because CRAM is stored in RAM and treated as RAM, with full cacheline/byte access, it can be accessed in a read-only fashion with little delay; just the cost of hardware-offloaded compression. As a result, CRAM "runs at DRAM speed," as the creator says in the slide above. While the graph already looks impressive, it's a logarithmic scale; CRAM, in the worst case, is doing 489 million operations per second versus ZRAM's 1.1 million. It's barely comparable.
Even when you enable writes, CRAM is still much faster than ZRAM; 5.4x in the worst tested case of 20% writes. That's a huge drop from the 452x read-only case, but keep your context; a 5.4x speedup is still titanic. The massive performance cliff when writes are involved comes down to the need to page fault and migrate folios back to the original NUMA domain, as you can't write directly to compressed data; you'd corrupt everything.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
My explanation of CRAM might not be completely correct; I wasn't at the Linux Plumbers' Conference in Prague to hear the presentation directly, so I'm working off of the slides available from the session information site (h/t to Phoronix for the spot) I think I've managed to grasp the gist of what Price is getting at, though.
While the obvious target of the work here (given its origin at Meta Platforms) is big Linux servers, ZRAM and Zswap are used all over the Linux ecosystem, even on machines as constrained as the Steam Deck. Many distributions enable one or the other by default. CRAM seems like it could offer a considerable speed-up for some of these machines, so hopefully it finds its way into the kernel once the remaining implementation questions are answered.

articles.title: Subastan un Apple-1 firmado por Steve Jobs y Wozniak: podría venderse en 800.000 dólares
articles.text:
Un Apple-1 firmado por Steve Wozniak y acompañado por una carta de Steve Jobs saldrá a subasta en Bonhams con una estimación de venta de entre 500.000 y 800.000 dólares.
La pieza reúne dos elementos que elevan su interés para los coleccionistas: pertenece a la primera serie de computadoras comercializadas por Apple y conserva referencias directas de sus dos principales creadores.
Jeffrey Kral, especialista del departamento de Historia de la Ciencia y la Tecnología de Bonhams, dijo que el dispositivo forma parte de un grupo reducido de ejemplares supervivientes.
La estimación supera ampliamente el precio original del dispositivo, que se comercializó en 1976 por 666,66 dólares. La diferencia se explica por el paso del tiempo, la baja cantidad de unidades disponibles y el interés de coleccionistas e instituciones por los primeros aparatos vinculados con el surgimiento de la informática personal.
Cómo era el primer ordenador creado por Apple
El Apple-1 fue la primera computadora personal que comercializó la empresa fundada por Jobs, Wozniak y Ronald Wayne. Wozniak lo diseñó y construyó a mano en 1976 como una tarjeta madre ya ensamblada, una característica que lo distinguía de otros productos de su época.
Muchos ordenadores de entonces se vendían como kits con componentes separados. Quien los compraba debía montar y soldar varias piezas antes de ponerlos en funcionamiento.
El Apple-1 simplificó parte de ese proceso: el usuario debía incorporar una carcasa, un teclado, una fuente de alimentación y un televisor que funcionara como pantalla.
De qué forma surgió la idea de comercializar el ordenador
El origen del modelo se remonta a las reuniones del Homebrew Computer Club, un espacio de aficionados a la informática de Silicon Valley durante la década de 1970. Allí, Wozniak presentó un prototipo que permitía conectar un teclado a un televisor, una solución que acercaba la computación a usuarios no especializados.
Jobs identificó una posibilidad comercial en ese prototipo y convenció a Wozniak de producirlo para la venta. Para reunir dinero destinado al primer lote, Jobs vendió su furgoneta Volkswagen y Wozniak se desprendió de una calculadora programable HP-65. Esa inversión permitió iniciar la fabricación de las primeras unidades.
Cuál empresa fue clave para este desarrollo de Apple
La naciente compañía obtuvo uno de sus primeros pedidos de The Byte Shop, una tienda local de informática que solicitó 50 computadoras ensambladas. El encargo fue clave porque obligó a los fundadores a pasar de un prototipo de aficionado a una producción limitada destinada al mercado.
Jobs y Wozniak fabricaron aquellas unidades de forma manual en el garaje de la familia Jobs. El proceso anticipó una etapa inicial marcada por recursos escasos y producción reducida. Entre 1976 y 1977, se construyeron cerca de 200 Apple-1 antes de que la empresa concentrara sus esfuerzos en el Apple II.
Qué pasó después del Apple-1
El ordenador tuvo una producción breve, pero abrió el camino para el Apple II, un modelo que alcanzó una mayor escala comercial. Más tarde, el Macintosh, lanzado en 1984, extendió el uso de la interfaz gráfica y el ratón en computadoras destinadas al público general.
Durante las décadas siguientes, Apple amplió su catálogo con productos como el iPod, el iPhone, el iPad y el Apple Watch. En 2026, el lanzamiento del iPhone Duo, el primer teléfono plegable de Apple, representa la entrada de la empresa en un segmento que otros fabricantes ya desarrollaban desde hace años.
Lo cierto es que la subasta del Apple-1 remite a una etapa anterior a esa expansión global que tuvo Apple en los 2000, cuando la empresa, ahora liderada por John Ternus, todavía fabricaba pequeñas series de placas de circuito para un mercado incipiente de computadoras personales.

articles.title: ChatGPT pour les ados : malgré les garde-fous, son usage est tout de même jugé risqué
articles.text:
Une version de ChatGPT dédiée aux adolescents, l'idée initiale était intéressante. Cependant, cette version spécifique semblerait tout de même dangereuse pour les jeunes, selon une association américaine. OpenAI se fait sévèrement taper sur les doigts.
Selon une évaluation de risques publiée mercredi par Common Sense Media, une association américaine spécialisée dans l'étude des médias et des technologies familiales et pour les enfants, la nouvelle version dévoilée par OpenAI ne serait pas au niveau attendu. L'organisation lui a même attribué sa pire note en termes de sécurité : "Risque inacceptable". OpenAI réfute en bloc.
L'organisme demande à OpenAI de cesser de mettre en avant cette fonctionnalité et recommande aux adolescents d'éviter d'utiliser ChatGPT jusqu'à ce que l'entreprise rende le service sûr pour eux.
Des tests approfondis dévoilent des lacunes
L'Institut de sécurité de l'IA pour la jeunesse, affilié à Common Sense Media, a testé plus de 4 000 requêtes. Si la moitié a été réalisée avant le lancement de cette nouvelle version, le 18 août, l'autre moitié a été testée après, sur des comptes enregistrés au nom d'adolescents de 13 à 17 ans. Cette approche d'un 50/50 équilibré, permet d'évaluer les réels changements apportés par le nouveau mode.
Les alertes destinées aux parents se sont avérées être parmi les défaillances majeures. Lors de discussions portant sur des pensées suicidaires, l'automutilation et les troubles alimentaires sur une douzaine de nouveaux comptes liés à un parent, aucune alerte n'a été déclenchée. Les alertes ont seulement fonctionné sur les comptes ayant un historique de plusieurs semaines sur ces sujets. Fonctionneraient-elles alors en fonction de l'antériorité d'utilisation du compte, ou de la gravité du message ?
Le chatbot s'est également montré insuffisant pour orienter les adolescents vers une aide d'urgence, échouant à le faire dans plus d'un quart des cas où les testeurs l'estimaient nécessaire.
Des contournements faciles et des vérifications inefficaces
Plusieurs garde-fous se sont révélés faciles à contourner. Un bouton "Montrer la réponse" permet aux adolescents de sauter l'étape pédagogique en mode révisions. Les utilisateurs peuvent aussi ignorer les restrictions horaires fixées par les parents en supprimant un court préfixe de leur message.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code
Les vérifications d'âge n'ont pas non plus fonctionné comme prévu. Des comptes enregistrés en tant qu'adultes initialement, ne sont jamais passés au mode adolescent sur plusieurs jours, même après que les testeurs aient informé ChatGPT de l'âge réel de l'utilisateur.
Tout n'est pas à jeter cependant. Certaines protections ont cependant tenu bon, notamment le refus de ChatGPT de participer à des jeux de rôle sexuels explicites. Une petite victoire pour OpenAI, dans un flot de fonctionnalités qui semblent encore ne pas fonctionner correctement. Pour l'entreprise qui veut ajouter un filigrane invisible à ses messages, il y aurait encore du progrès à faire concernant les garde-fous pour les mineurs.
OpenAI rejette les conclusions
OpenAI conteste ces résultats. Un porte-parole d'OpenAI a déclaré à Education Week les propos suivants :
« Nous ne pensons pas que les tests de Common Sense Media reflètent avec précision le fonctionnement des garde-fous pour adolescents de ChatGPT dans la pratique. »
Common Sense Media avait précédemment attribué à ChatGPT une note de « Risque élevé » en octobre 2025, avant de le classer comme risque inacceptable pour le soutien en matière de santé mentale un mois plus tard. L'organisation a également collaboré avec OpenAI pour l'aider à rédiger des politiques de sécurité destinées aux développeurs.

articles.title: ASUS Announces Availability of Its ProArt RTX Spark Windows PCs
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
ASUS Announces Availability of Its ProArt RTX Spark Windows PCs
ASUS today announced the global launch of the new ProArt P16 and P14 laptops, along with the compact ProArt GR1X mini PC, all powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark. Purpose-built for creators, AI developers and workflow builders, these systems boast high-capacity unified memory, a powerful NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and an ultra-efficient NVIDIA Grace CPU. The NVIDIA CUDA ecosystem and an expanding ASUS-exclusive agent-and-application solution make sophisticated local AI easier to deploy, personalize and use. NVIDIA RTX Spark unites NVIDIA AI, RTX graphics, and unified memory in one slim, powerful Windows PC. Designed to run larger AI models locally—without cloud dependency—and move between creative work, development, and immersive gaming without missing a beat. Connect apps, tools, and workflows into one seamless experience. Private by default, RTX Spark brings NVIDIA's full-stack AI platform, ready for the AI workloads of today and whatever comes next. Delivered on the familiar, trusted Windows platform.
Together, Hermes Agent and ComfyUI deliver a compelling local-first, cloud-flexible AI experience. By bringing industry-validated workflows and agent-connected creative tools to users' own PCs, they enable generative AI creation and AI-assisted development, with the flexibility to integrate cloud services when needed.
Dillon Rolnick, CEO of Nous Research"We built Hermes to provide intelligence you can truly own, rather than simply rent. ProArt RTX Spark PCs provide the memory capacity to run powerful models locally, enabling Hermes to drive ComfyUI and MuseTree, work with your files, and keep these workflows on your own machine".
Yoland Yan, CEO and co-founder of Comfy"Creators want to run the best AI models on their own machines, with full control. ProArt RTX Spark PCs have the memory to run big image and video workflows locally, and ComfyUI makes those workflows easy to share, reuse and hand off to agents like Hermes".
A new class of personal Windows PCs powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark 
ProArt P16, ProArt P14 and ProArt GR1X bring advanced local AI computing to slim creator laptops and a compact desktop form factor. NVIDIA RTX Spark combines an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU, an NVIDIA Grace CPU, fifth-generation Tensor Cores with FP4 support and NVIDIA NVLink-C2C interconnect technology in a highly integrated, power-efficient platform.
With up to 1 petaflop of AI performance and up to 128 GB of high-bandwidth unified memory, RTX Spark enables demanding workloads that can exceed the memory capacity of conventional PCs. Depending on model architecture, quantization, context length and available system memory, users can work with large local language and vision-language models, advanced image and video generation pipelines, LoRA customization, agentic workflows and complex 3D scenes directly on their ProArt PC.
Owning local AI capacity provides three fundamental advantages. First, it turns variable pay-per-use cloud spending into predictable computing capacity, allowing users to iterate, regenerate and experiment without per-token or per-generation charges. Second, it helps protect privacy and creative intellectual property by keeping prompts, source files, project data and selected models on device, with workflows that can remain available offline. Third, it gives creators and developers greater control over their tools, enabling them to select models, customize behavior, connect trusted applications and build repeatable workflows around their own needs.
Cloud services remain valuable for frontier-scale models and burst capacity. ProArt RTX Spark Windows PCs give users the flexibility to choose local, cloud or hybrid execution according to performance, privacy, security, cost and workflow requirements.
ASUS creative ecosystem for agentic AI workflows
NVIDIA RTX Spark brings NVIDIA AI and RTX graphics together to redefine Windows PCs for creators, AI developers, and gamers, all on the familiar, trusted Windows platform. RTX Spark fundamentally changes what creators and developers can achieve with a new AI computing platform. Backed by the CUDA ecosystem, it supports a rapidly expanding range of creator applications, AI models and development tools that can run locally with RTX acceleration—creating a highly capable environment for generative AI, model development and AI workflow building.
Combined with up to 128 GB unified memory, RTX Spark also removes one of the biggest limitations of conventional PCs: memory capacity. Larger AI models, higher-resolution generation and more complex workflows can now run locally, opening a new class of possibilities for creators and AI developers. ASUS extends this platform advantage through the layers of its own ecosystem:
Local GenAI, built into ProArt: ASUS preloads exclusive ProArt applications that bring local AI directly into the creative workflow. MuseTree integrates two of the best local image models FLUX and Wan for token-free local generative creation, while StoryCube brings AI-powered scene recognition, media organization and intelligent asset management to Windows.
The best of local and cloud creation: ProArt combines local RTX-powered AI with leading cloud creative services, including Adobe Creative Cloud bundles, giving creators the flexibility to move between local and cloud workflows depending on performance, privacy and creative needs. On eligible ASUS laptops, an exclusive Google AI bundle further enhances hybrid AI creative experiences.
Building the agentic AI workflow ecosystem
Hermes, the personalized creative expert: Built by Nous Research, Hermes is an open-source autonomous AI partner that executes complex goals across desktop apps, terminal, and local files with persistent memory, isolated sandboxes and self-improving skills. Through the dedicated Hermes Skill, it connects with ASUS MuseTree to deliver one of the most accessible local AI image- and video-generation experiences, powered by the popular FLUX and Wan models.
Zenni Claw, the best ASUS native assistant: ASUS agent for everyday AI and productivity that provides deeper integration with ASUS applications and devices for daily tasks, content management and product control.
ComfyUI, the agent-ready workflow builder: ASUS has partnered with ComfyUI, the leading open-source platform for visual AI workflows, used by millions of creators worldwide. ComfyUI's validated workflows and resource packs make it easy to create AI images and video on ProArt PCs, and its agent-ready design lets assistants like Hermes build and run workflows for users. Its global community keeps adding new models and tools, so ProArt users always have the latest in AI.
ProArt P16 & P14 Laptop: Agent-assisted creativity on the move
Built around the highly integrated RTX Spark architecture, ProArt P16 and P14 combine advanced AI capability with thin, lightweight CNC-machined designs. At 12.9 mm (0.51") and 1.77 kg (3.9 lbs), ProArt P16 is the thinnest 16-inch ProArt laptop to date. ProArt P14 measures 13.9 mm (0.55") and weighs 1.48 kg (3.26 lbs), making it the lightest ProArt laptop to date. High-capacity batteries—up to 99.9Wh for P16 and 90Wh for P14—support extended mobile creative workflows.
Both laptops feature ASUS Lumina Pro OLED displays with Delta E<1 color accuracy, up to 1,600-nit peak brightness, 120 Hz variable refresh rate and anti-reflection technology. ProArt P16 supports up to a 4K display with NVIDIA G-SYNC, while ProArt P14 offers up to 3K resolution. Nano Black and Neo White finishes, comprehensive I/O and a precision haptic touchpad complete a creator-focused mobile experience.
ProArt GR1X Mini Windows PC: Always-on local agentic AI for nonstop creativity
ProArt GR1X brings RTX Spark to a compact system designed for creators, developers and small teams that need always-available local AI capacity. Measuring 150 x 150 x 51 mm, it combines high-capacity unified memory with advanced thermal engineering for sustained operation in studios, development environments and shared workspaces.
Its dual-fan cooling system, dual M.2 SSD storage, 10GbE networking, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, and support for up to four 4K displays make GR1X a versatile local AI hub for agents, model serving, generation, and creative workflow automation. Available in silver and black, it extends the ProArt design language to a compact desktop form factor.
From personal AI PCs to enterprise AI infrastructure
ASUS is extending agentic AI across a comprehensive portfolio of local systems including ProArt PCs powered by RTX Spark, systems equipped with GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs, ASUS Ascent GX10, powered by NVIDIA DGX Spark, and ASUS ExpertCenter Pro ET900, powered by NVIDIA DGX Station.
Across this portfolio, ASUS brings together agentic AI, generative AI, recognition and classification technologies, partner integrations, and deployment expertise. From a single creator laptop to shared enterprise infrastructure, customers can access local AI hardware, software, and workflow solutions through one unified ASUS ecosystem.
ProArt RTX Spark Windows PC availability and pricing
In Canada, pre-orders for select NVIDIA RTX Spark-powered ProArt P16 and ProArt P14 configurations begin on October 7, 2026, with shipping estimated to start on October 16, 2026.
ProArt P14 will initially be offered with 24 GB or 128 GB of LPDDR5X memory, while ProArt P16 will be available with 32 GB or 128 GB. The 48 GB ProArt P14 and 64 GB ProArt P16 configurations will be available later this year. Configurations will be offered through the ASUS Store, with the 128 GB ProArt P14 and 32 GB ProArt P16 also available at Best Buy Canada.
ProArt P14 will start at C$3,499, and ProArt P16 will start at C$4,999. Configurations, pricing, pre-order timing, and retail availability may vary by product and region.

articles.title: Galaxy Book 4 tem melhor preço com cupom do TB no Magazine Luiza • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Book 4 tem melhor preço com cupom do TB no Magazine Luiza
Modelo NP750XGJ-KG3BR traz processador Intel Core i5, SSD de 512GB e tela de 15,6". Pague no Pix e utilize o cupom TECNOBLOG300 para pagar mais barato no notebook da Samsung
O Galaxy Book 4 está saindo por um preço menor no Magazine Luiza, comparado à média recente disponibilizada no Zoom. O notebook sai por R$ 3.569,10 no Pix combinado com o cupom da casa TECNOBLOG300. Desse modo, você economiza na compra do dispositivo que entrega um desempenho equilibrado.
O modelo NP750XGJ-KG3BR vem equipado pelo processador Core i5 (de 10 núcleos e 12 threads) e 8 GB de memória RAM. A configuração possibilita um desempenho adequado para tarefas diárias, incluindo propostas básicas para estudos e trabalho; assim como uso com várias abas abertas e streaming. Por isso é uma das melhores opções de notebook custo-benefício.
O SSD NVMe de 512 GB garante a execução de comandos e abertura de programas com agilidade, mesmo assim o armazenamento pode ser expandido até 2 TB. Ao contrário da GPU integrada Intel Iris Xe que fica embutida, porém atende a objetivos de assistir a vídeos e rodar jogos leves, só que para por aí.
O Galaxy Book 4 conta com uma LCD de 15,6 polegadas no qual oferece resolução Full HD e tecnologia antirreflexo para não dificultar a visualização ao ar livre ou em ambientes muito iluminados. Além disso, os alto-falantes estéreo suportam áudio com Dolby Atmos, o que significa um som imersivo a partir de efeitos sonoros envolventes.
O notebook da Samsung também se destaca pelo design ultrafino e leve, com um corpo metálico em grafite ao peso de apenas 1,55 kg e 15,4 mm de espessura. Logo, as dimensões facilitam o transporte na mochila ou até mesmo a mão sem causar desconforto.
Em questão de conectividade, o dispositivo contempla portas HDMI, USB-A, Ethernet e duas USB-C, conector de áudio 3,5 mm (P2), além do já mencionado leitor de microSD. Em relação a bateria, adota um componente de 54 Wh e compatível a carregadores USB-C de até 45 W.
O Galaxy Book 4 utiliza o sistema Windows 11 Home e possui fácil integração com outros dispositivos Galaxy, a ponto de de ser possível abrir apps do celular no notebook, usar a câmera do celular e entre outros recursos. Adquira o modelo NP750XGJ-KG3BR por R$ 3.569,10 no Pix com o cupom TECNOBLOG300 no Magalu.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: MSI Crosshair vs. MSI Katana laptops: I'm baffled why you'd pay $500 more
articles.text:
MSI's Katana 15 HX and Crosshair A16 HX laptops are both over $400 off for Amazon Prime Day — but I'm baffled why most people would pay $500 more here
Intel and AMD processors go head-to-head in these two powerhouses
Choosing between two creative laptops becomes much easier when they share many of the same core specifications but have different prices. That's exactly the situation with two MSI laptops which have been discounted for Amazon Prime Day.
• Best for: I'd choose the MSI Katana 15 HX for most users, while the Crosshair A16 HX makes more sense if you think a larger, faster display is worth paying extra for. And that's not the case for most people.
• The deal: The MSI Crosshair A16 HX is down to $2294 (was $2699), while the MSI Katana 15 HX has dropped to $1791 (was $2200), both at Amazon.
• Why it matters: They both offer RTX 5070 graphics, 32GB of DDR5 memory, and 1TB SSDs, but have different processors (Intel vs. AMD) and price points. The decision largely comes down to whether you think the Crosshair's advantages justify another $503. For what it's worth, at this price, I mostly don't.
This model features an Intel Core i9-14900HX processor, RTX 5070 8GB graphics, 32GB DDR5-5600 memory, 1TB NVMe SSD, 165Hz display, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.4, USB-C, HDMI, and RGB keyboard.
This laptop features an AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX processor, RTX 5070 8GB graphics, 32GB DDR5 memory, 1TB NVMe SSD, 16-inch 2560 x 1600 240Hz display, Wi-Fi 6E, and USB-C connectivity.
Which one I'd recommend
The Crosshair A16 HX has some worthwhile advantages, particularly its larger display. Despite that, of the two laptops, I'd go for the MSI Katana 15 HX as it includes remarkably similar core hardware for $503 less.
The Katana combines a 14th-generation Intel Core i9-14900HX processor with an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 8GB graphics card. There's also 32GB of DDR5-5600 memory and a 1TB NVMe SSD.
Its 15.6-inch display has a 165Hz refresh rate, while Cooler Boost 5 uses dual fans and five heat pipes to help manage temperatures. Connectivity includes USB-C, HDMI, Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6E, and Bluetooth 5.4.
In his 4-star review of the older (less powerful) model, our expert James said "for those with a limited budget, the MSI Katana 15 (2023) is among the best gaming laptops to pick from. There are some compromises, such as the styling and battery life, as well as a flaw or two, but the overall package provides a good quality gaming experience where you won’t feel the portable’s limitations."
The Crosshair A16 HX pairs an AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX with the same RTX 5070 8GB graphics and matches the Katana's 32GB of DDR5 memory and 1TB NVMe SSD.
You get a larger 16-inch 2560 x 1600 display with a much faster 240Hz refresh rate. It also has a 90Wh battery and supports up to 96GB of memory, compared with a 75Wh battery and maximum 64GB on the Katana.
While those extras make the Crosshair more interesting on paper, I'd still buy the Katana.
Price context & historical value
Both laptops have been reduced in price by just over $400 for Prime Day. The Katana falls from $2,199.99 to $1,791, saving you $408.99, or around 19%. It has been lower though. For Black Friday 2025 it was $1,369.99. That's $830 off the standard price.
The Crosshair drops from $2,699 to $2,294, knocking $405 off its regular price, or 15%. This is as cheap as we've seen it previously.
Which MSI laptop should you buy?
✅ Buy the MSI Katana 15 HX if...
You want the better-value laptop of the two. You're getting an RTX 5070 alongside a powerful Core i9-14900HX without paying for some of the Crosshair's more premium features.
✅ Buy the MSI Crosshair A16 HX instead if...
Display performance is a priority. Its 16-inch 2560 x 1600 screen runs at 240Hz rather than 165Hz, while the larger battery and higher maximum memory capacity provide a couple of additional advantages.

articles.title: US government, tech giants and Biohub commit $1.8B to AI biology initiative - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
US government, tech giants and Biohub commit $1.8B to AI biology initiative
More than a half-dozen public and private sector organizations are teaming up to develop biology datasets for artificial intelligence models.
The consortium, which announced the collaboration today, is committing $1.8 billion to the project.
Studying how a cell responds to a new therapy usually requires scientists to set up a physical test environment. That can take years of work and millions of dollars. A faster, more cost-efficient approach would be to test therapies using simulated cells. A simulation doesn’t require expensive lab equipment and can theoretically be spun up in a few hours.
Ultra-detailed, highly reliable simulations that can substitute lab equipment aren’t yet available. The reason is that creating such virtual cells would require a new generation of biology-optimized AI models. Training such models would only be possible with bigger biology datasets than those presently available to scientists.
The research initiative announced today aims to produce the necessary datasets. The biggest contributor to the project is the U.S. Department of Energy, which will commit more than $500 million over five years.
Some of the funds are earmarked for microscopy equipment. The hardware will be used to collect cell measurements for AI training datasets.
The Energy Department will prioritize three imaging methods: neutron scattering, X-ray and cryo-electron microscopy. The first two methods identify the materials that make up a biological sample. Neutron scattering equipment spots light elements and their isotopes, while X-ray machines detect heavier elements. Cryo-electron microscopy, the third imaging method on the list, maps out the internal structure of cells.
The second biggest contributor to the project is Biohub, a research nonprofit backed by Mark Zuckerberg. It’s committing $400 million to the initiative. Three quarters of the funds will go toward in-house research endeavors, while the rest will support external projects.
Like the Energy Department, Biohub will use cryo-electron microscopy to collect cell data. The nonprofit plans to use a specific variant of the technology called cryo-ET. It works by freezing a biological sample and exposing it to an electron beam. When the electrons come into contact with the sample, they change their course and thereby provide insight into its internal structure.
Biohub’s work will also extend to other areas. It plans to collect data about not only the inner workings of cells but also how different cells interact with one another. According to the group, the plan is to create images that contain millions to billions of cells.
The U.S. National Institutes of Health, or NIH, is also participating. It will provide access to biology datasets developed “through more than $500 million in prior federal investment aligned to this initiative.” Biohub and NIH will team up to organize the data into a form that can be more easily processed by AI models.
Google DeepMind, fellow Alphabet Inc. subsidiary Isomorphic Labs and Meta Platforms Inc. are together contributing $300 million. Nvidia Corp., meanwhile, plans to support aspects of the project that will use accelerators and specialized software to run research workloads. The tech giants will be joined by a half-dozen nonprofit research groups including the Allen Institute.
“An accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery by enabling scientists to perform experiments digitally,” said Biohub head of science Alex Rives. “The insights that come from this could unlock a far greater understanding of disease and open up completely new paths for cures.”
