articles.title: Upgrade to Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7 with these stellar savings — TP-Link Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 routers get big discounts
articles.text:
Upgrade to Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7 with these stellar savings — TP-Link Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 routers get big discounts
We've rounded up three TP-Link wireless routers ranging from Wi-Fi 6E to Wi-Fi 7, including mesh offerings.
Amazon Prime Big Deals Day 2026 is here, and we're already seeing some tasty deals on Wi-Fi routers. If you're in the market for a Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7 router, we've scoped out deals on standalone and mesh systems that could give your home (or office) network a much-needed performance boost.
If you have a smaller home that doesn't need the aid of wireless satellites to improve coverage, consider the TP-Link Archer AXE75 Wi-Fi 6E router. While it isn't one of TP-Link's newest Wi-Fi 7 offerings, it still offers a lot of bang for the buck. The Archer AXE75 has a retail price of $119.99, but a $30 instant discount reduces the cost to just $89.99 for Prime subscribers.
That price gets you Gigabit WAN, four Gigabit LAN ports, and even a USB 3.0 port for adding storage to your network. The Gigabit WAN port should be more than adequate if your ISP delivers 1 Gbps or slower speeds. If you're rocking a 2 Gbps or higher internet plan, you might want to invest in a router with at least a 2.5 GbE WAN to fully utilize your plan. Another thing to keep in mind is that if you plan to expand your network in the future, the Archer AXE75 supports TP-Link's OneMesh standard, enabling you to combine multiple compatible routers into a mesh network.
Regarding performance, the Archer AXE75 operates at speeds of up to 574 Mbps on the 2.4 GHz band and up to 2,402 Mbps on the 5 GHz and 6 GHz bands.
The TP-Link Archer AXE75 combines excellent performance and value in a Wi-Fi 6E router. You get four GbE ports, a USB 3.0 port for external storage, and OneMesh compliance for less than $90.
If you need the added coverage of a mesh system, the TP-Link Deco XE75 also uses the Wi-Fi 6E standard. But while the Archer AXE75 covers just 2,000 square feet, the Deco XE75, a three-node system, covers up to 7,200 square feet (over three times the coverage).
Each satellite has three Gigabit Ethernet ports, which are excellent for connecting your wired-only network devices. However, there's another added benefit: the Deco XE75 supports wired backhaul, which can improve overall network performance compared to using the default wireless backhaul between satellites.
When it comes to overall performance, expect a similar experience to the Archer AXE75, as it also offers a maximum of 574 Mbps over the 2.4 GHz band, 2,402 Mbps over the 5 GHz band, and 2,402 Mbps over the 6 GHz band.
The Deco XE75 is typically available for $249.99, but is currently on sale for $229.99. But that's not all; there's also an instant coupon that knocks another $30 off the price of the 3-pack, bringing the price down to $199.99.
TP-Link is offering a complete three-node Wi-Fi 6E mesh router that covers up to 7,200 square feet. Each node has three GbE ports supporting wired backhaul.
Finally, the TP-Link Prime Big Deals Day trifecta is completed with the Deco BE5000. This is an entry-level Wi-Fi 7 mesh router. Because of this alignment, the Deco BE5000 isn't a full-featured tri-band offering; instead, it's a dual-band Wi-Fi 7 solution. Although you miss out on the higher-performance 6 GHz band, you do gain support for Multi-Link Operation (MLO), a key pillar of Wi-Fi 7 (although MLO is one of Wi-Fi 7's most misunderstood features).
Each node features two 2.5 GbE ports, and you also get wired backhaul support. Maximum throughput reaches 688 Mbps for the 2.4 GHz band, while the 5 GHz band achieves 2,882 Mbps.
The Deco BE5000 retails for $299.99 but is currently priced at $198.19, which is a healthy $100 discount.
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Archer AXE75 | Deco XE75 | Deco BE5000 | 
| Wi-Fi Standard | Wi-Fi 6E | Wi-Fi 6E | Wi-Fi 7 | 
| Wireless Bands | 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, 6 GHz | 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, 6 GHz | 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz | 
| Maximum Throughput (Combined) | 5,400 Mbps | 5,400 Mbps | 5,000 Mbps | 
| LAN Ports | 1x GbE WAN, 4x GbE LAN | 3 x GbE LAN/WAN per node | 2x 2.5 GbE WAN/LAN per node | 
| USB Ports | 1x USB 3.0 | None | None | 
| Coverage | 2,000 square feet | 7,200 square feet | 6,600 square feet | 
The TP-Link Deco BE5000 is a dual-band Wi-Fi 7 router that features three nodes and covers up to 6,600 square feet. Each node features 2.5 GbE ports and supports wired backhaul.
There's one other deal perk possible with these router deals if you have an Amazon Prime Rewards VISA credit card. Amazon is offering up to 25% cash back on the purchase of each of these routers when you use the card.

Bon plan – Le casque à conduction osseuse Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 "5 étoiles" à 155,29 € (-21%)
Le casque à conduction osseuse Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 est proposé à 155,29 € chez E. Leclerc - High-Tech soit une baisse d'environ 41 € sur le prix habituellement constaté. C'est actuellement le meilleur produit de notre comparatif.
Avec l’OpenRun Pro 2, Shokz ne tente pas de repousser les limitations sonores de la conduction osseuse, il les contourne. Par le biais d’une architecture hybride, la marque se donne les moyens de ses ambitions dans le bas du spectre. Une formule payante, malgré quelques compromis.

Points faibles

Simple, mais efficace.

articles.title: Orange veut mettre la main sur un nouvel opérateur en Afrique
articles.text:
L'opérateur des télécommunications français historique Orange se développe en Afrique. Et ça va passer par l'acquisition d'un opérateur au Ghana.
Les géants des télécoms français ont tendance à s'exporter à l'étranger ces dernières années. On connait ainsi les opérations d'Iliad (Free), très présent en Pologne, en Italie, et de plus en plus en Amérique latine. Et Orange n'est pas en reste de son côté. L'an dernier, le groupe français annonçait ainsi l'acquisition de l'Espagnol MasOrange, faisant d'Orange le numéro 1 du marché de ce pays. Et cette année, c'est du côté de l'Afrique que la société lorgne.
Orange veut racheter 70% de l'opérateur ghanéen Telecel Ghana
Orange va bien, comme nous le montrent les derniers résultats du groupe. Et cette bonne santé semble permettre des opérations de croissance externe intéressantes. Le média L'Informé nous indique ainsi qu'Orange a entamé des discussions pour s'avancer en Afrique anglophone, au Ghana plus précisément, pour acquérir l'opérateur Telecel Ghana.
L'objectif de la firme française serait d'acquérir au total 70% du capital de cet opérateur, ce qui en ferait l'actionnaire majoritaire. Orange pourrait boucler cette opération d'ici la fin de l'année, et lui permettrait de prendre pied dans un nouveau pays du continent africain, où le groupe n'était jusqu'alors pas présent.
L'Afrique, prochain moteur de croissance d'Orange ?
Aujourd'hui, Orange est installé dans 18 pays d'Afrique et du Moyen-Orient. Un nombre qui devrait augmenter à l'avenir, avec sa stratégie dite « Trust the future » 2026-2030, dont l'ambition est de lui permettre de compter 40 millions de clients supplémentaires à l'horizon 2028.
Et pour ce faire, Orange devrait faire de l'Afrique l'une de ses terres les plus importantes pour se développer. Le Ghana apparaît dans cette idée stratégique, en constituant une implantation à partir de laquelle Orange pourrait renforcer ses marchés sur le terrain de l'Afrique anglophone. Avec d'autres opérations dans les cartons pour l'année 2027 ?

articles.title: Mapa de lluvias en tiempo real en Bogotá: Guía para verlos desde el celular
articles.text:
Las jornadas de lluvia persistente en Bogotá, capital de Colombia, suelen alterar los recorridos, la operación del transporte público y los planes al aire libre, así que antes de salir de casa, una consulta desde el celular aporta una referencia sobre las zonas que registran precipitaciones y sobre el comportamiento reciente del clima en Bogotá.
La ciudad dispone de una herramienta pública para seguir estos cambios. El Sistema de Alerta de Bogotá permite revisar en un mapa las lluvias en tiempo real que se presentan en distintos puntos de la capital, con información de las estaciones de monitoreo y del radar meteorológico del Instituto Distrital de Gestión de Riesgos y Cambio Climático (IDIGER).
Qué plataforma permite ver los mapas de lluvias en tiempo real en Bogotá
El visor de lluvias del Sistema de Alerta de Bogotá, conocido como SAB, está disponible en app.sab.gov.co/sab/lluvias.htm. No requiere descargar una aplicación: solo hay que abrir el enlace desde el navegador del teléfono, ya sea en Android o iPhone.
La plataforma reúne los datos de estaciones distribuidas en varias localidades y los presenta sobre un mapa de la ciudad. De esta forma, una persona que debe desplazarse puede revisar si hay registros de lluvia cerca de su punto de partida, destino o trayecto habitual antes de iniciar el recorrido.
Cómo leer el mapa de lluvias en tiempo real en Bogotá desde el celular
Al abrir la página, el usuario encontrará una vista geográfica de Bogotá con varios símbolos sobre el mapa. Para una mejor visualización, conviene activar la ubicación del teléfono y ampliar la zona de interés con los gestos habituales de la pantalla, como separar dos dedos para hacer zoom.
El visor incluye información del radar meteorológico del IDIGER, que detecta partículas de agua presentes en la atmósfera. Esa lectura permite identificar áreas con precipitaciones y observar su distribución en la ciudad, una opción útil cuando las condiciones cambian entre localidades durante la misma franja horaria.
Qué significan los triángulos que aparecen en el mapa
Los triángulos indican la ubicación de las estaciones pluviométricas que integran la red de monitoreo. Cuando uno de esos símbolos parpadea, la estación respectiva está registrando lluvia en ese momento. Si permanece estático, no hay precipitaciones detectadas en ese punto específico.
Asimismo, el mapa muestra una escala de colores relacionada con el agua acumulada durante el día. Los registros superiores a 50 milímetros corresponden a los niveles más altos de acumulación diaria dentro de la clasificación del visor.
Cómo consultar la evolución de la lluvia en una localidad en Bogotá
Para obtener información de un punto concreto, hay que presionar sobre el triángulo de la estación más cercana a la zona que interesa consultar. El sistema abrirá una ventana con datos de precipitación y una referencia al comportamiento registrado durante las últimas seis horas.
Esa información permite comparar los valores recientes y establecer si la lluvia perdió intensidad o si aumentó en el sector. El historial de seis horas ayuda a tomar decisiones sobre desplazamientos, actividades deportivas o salidas al aire libre, pero no reemplaza las alertas oficiales ni las pautas de las autoridades ante emergencias.
Qué opciones nativas ofrece el teléfono para anticipar lluvias
Los celulares incluyen aplicaciones meteorológicas preinstaladas. En los dispositivos con iOS (iPhone), la app Tiempo muestra pronósticos por hora, probabilidad de lluvia y avisos asociados a la ubicación.
En Android, las herramientas del sistema y los servicios de Google ofrecen funciones similares, según el modelo y la configuración elegida.
Para aprovechar esas opciones, es necesario permitir el acceso a la ubicación y activar las notificaciones meteorológicas. Las alertas de lluvia inminente pueden complementar la consulta del mapa del SAB, sobre todo para quienes necesitan saber si habrá precipitaciones durante las próximas horas en el lugar donde se encuentran.

articles.title: Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra Starts at $2,599, Ships October 16
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra Starts at $2,599, Ships October 16
Microsoft has finally put a price on the Surface Laptop Ultra, and preorders are open as of today. The announcement came at the company's Windows and Surface keynote in San Francisco, with a starting price of $2,599 and shipments set to begin on October 16. Microsoft first showed the laptop at Computex in June without a price or a launch date. The base model gets a 15-inch mini-LED display and the lower of the two NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X configurations, which means an 18-core CPU, a 5,120-core Blackwell GPU, and 24 GB of unified memory. The 20-core version with a 6,144-core GPU starts at $3,699 with 32 GB, and the top model with 128 GB of memory and a 1 TB SSD costs a steep $5,899. The only 2 TB option is a 64 GB model at $4,699. A Surface RTX Spark Dev Box was also announced at a hefty $5,999.
The other reveal is the oversized USB-C port that has had people guessing since June. Microsoft says the Surface Laptop Ultra is the first laptop in the world with a breakaway USB-C port, so a tripped-over cable should pull free without dragging the machine off the desk. The idea is the same as Apple's MagSafe and Microsoft's own Surface Connect, except those are proprietary connectors. This one apparently still works as a regular USB-C port with any USB-C device. As for the price, the $2,599 entry point is a little lower than expected. A TechPowerUp Forums member who spent about a month with a prototype guessed $2,799 for a 24 GB model. That prototype was tested on preview drivers, however, so readers are advised to wait for reviews of retail hardware before preordering.

articles.title: LibreOffice reforça que "ausência de IA" é um diferencial • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
LibreOffice reforça que “ausência de IA” é um diferencial
The Document Foundation não é contra a IA em si, mas diz que a sua adoção tem que ser criteriosa.
Lançado em agosto, o LibreOffice 26.8 trouxe vários novos recursos, mas nenhum tem inteligência artificial integrada. É bom não esperar que seja diferente no curto prazo: a The Document Foundation (TDF), organização por trás da suíte, descreve a ausência de IA como uma qualidade, e não um atraso.
Não surpreende. Já no lançamento do LibreOffice 26.8 a TDF havia destacado que a não inclusão de IA na então nova versão do pacote era um atributo. É como se a organização estivesse protestando contra a onda de ferramentas, assistentes e agentes de inteligência artificial que ganham espaço de modo desenfreado nos mais variados softwares, muitas vezes sem fazer diferença para o usuário.
Em um texto publicado em seu blog oficial, a TDF explica que não é contra a IA em si. A organização é contrária a uma eventual implementação que não siga ou entre em conflito com os princípios que regem o projeto:
O LibreOffice não rejeita a inteligência artificial de imediato, mas um pacote de aplicativos de escritório usado por dezenas de milhões de pessoas — em escolas, hospitais, órgãos públicos, escritórios de advocacia e milhares de outras organizações — não adicionará um recurso à sua configuração padrão até que isso possa ser entregue sob as condições definidas pelo projeto, de acordo com seus princípios.
Italo Vignoli, representante da The Document Foundation
O texto da The Document Foundation dá a entender que o LibreOffice poderá ter recursos de inteligência artificial em algum momento, sim. Mas, para isso, os tais princípios devem ser respeitados. Eles incluem:
A TDF entende que, no atual cenário, esses critérios não podem ser atendidos, o que explica a ausência de recursos nativos de IA no LibreOffice:
Os critérios que listamos não representam uma rejeição definitiva. O setor de IA está evoluindo rapidamente. (…) Caso surja uma abordagem que atenda a todas as condições, nós a avaliaremos com muita atenção.
Italo Vignoli, representante da The Document Foundation
A organização destaca, porém, que usuários que precisam de recursos do tipo na suíte já podem obtê-los por meio de extensões de IA oferecidas por terceiros à suíte.

articles.title: Aracana Unleashed is the D&D 5.5E expansion everyone should buy — especially if you buy it for a discount like this one at Amazon
articles.text:
Arcana Unleashed is an incredible Dungeons & Dragons expansion, but these Prime Day deals make it much easier to recommend
Deals could finally Unleash this expansion's potential
I’ve been playing with Arcana Unleashed for the past month, and the latest Dungeons & Dragons gameplay expansion is exquisite. Easily the best released since the game’s Fifth Edition refresh in 2024, and this week might be the best time to grab this book if you haven’t already.
Arcana Unleashed serves up magic-focused gameplay options for both players and Dungeon Masters. There are brand new and refreshed subclasses for characters to be built around like the Vestige Warlock and Arcane Archer Fighter, spells that friends and foes alike can use to solve dungeons, manipulate social situations and command the battlefield from the front or back lines, and tips for building magical worlds and setting up an arcane adventure.
I’ve read Arcana Unleashed from cover-to-cover and have already started incorporating it into the campaign I’m running (both upcoming sessions, and ones I have planned for the future). Magic is my favorite aspect of this game, and this feels like a love letter to the mystical arts.
However the book is far too short — like a delicious cake you’re only allowed a sliver of, I’m desperate for more and left wishing WoTC had served a more generous helping. But this year's early Amazon’s Big Deals sale has already seen it get a serious discount, and as we head into the holiday sales period proper it could get an even bigger price drop.
The latest D&D book is incredible, and even better thanks if you can score it at a discount like this $10 saving currently at Amazon.
I've loved Arcana Unleashed. My only gripe is it's a little expensive for what you get, but this deal makes it a much easier book to recommend for fans of D&D.
A light touch
A Gameplay Expansion is designed for both players and the DMs who run the games. If you’ve picked up previous D&D 5e expansions it feels like a successor to the popular Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything and Xanathar’s Guide to Everything.
The first chapter of Arcana Unleashed is dedicated to subclasses characters can choose at level three — some new like the Vestiga Warlock, most returning options revised following the 2024 5e game reboot like the Fighter’s Arcane Archer, and the Necromancy, Enchantment, Conjuration, and Transmutation Wizard options that were left out of the 2024 Player’s Handbook (finally letting wannabe mages specialize in whichever of the eight schools of magic they most wish to).
I don’t believe you can judge a subclass by pure numbers — I firmly believe the ‘best’ option depends entirely on the individual campaign setting and the vibes expected by the playgroup — but generally the updates to the older classes seem solid, and the new options feel fun from both a gameplay and thematic point of view. A Warlock getting powers from a dying being of great power has so many story possibilities.
Moving into backgrounds and Arcana Unleashed’s feat options, I love how the new Origin Feats — some special feature your character starts the game with — provide mechanical and flavorful ways to create diversity in builds. Arcane Eloquence making a character better at Persuasion and Deception, without forcing them into a typically Charismatic class like Bard or Sorcerer, or Arcane Infiltrator letting you dodge as a bonus action like a Rogue without committing fully to that class.
There are new spells, items and magical creatures to utilize in games too, though I want to focus on the advice it gives for building magical worlds and creating factions your players could work with (or against) on their adventure.
These chapters go into solid detail about the needs and wants of these groups as well as how their allies might be rewarded, and the sorts of folks the factions would work against. They also offer up plenty of inspiration and things to consider in a magical world — like the development of technology, or the sorts of societies that might spring up.
For a more experienced DM these considerations would be second nature, but for newcomers — especially those new to creating a world from scratch — they provide the perfect level of assistance. You have got something to chew on, but no specific right or wrong answers, and plenty of space to be creative.
Even as a DM with a few years under my belt the book has been a helpful world building tool, and has already helped me conjure up a few new locations for my current on-going campaign.
I’ve loved everything Arcana Unleashed has had to offer up, but it’s not without its faults.
Sharing is caring
My first disappointment is the uneven distribution of new subclasses. I love that Wizards finally get updated rules for the remaining schools of magic not included in the 2024 Player’s Handbook, but this comes at the expense of Bards, Barbarians, Druids, Paladins, Rangers, Rogues, Warlocks and Sorcerers who get nothing.
Of course new subclasses with an intrinsic arcane nature would be perfect — giving players new options for characters from a world where everyone has some kind of magical ability. Though they don’t need to be new. The Barbarian’s Wild Magic subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything could have been updated, as could the Druid’s Circle of Wildfire from the same book, or the Circle of the Shepherd from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything.
I’d maybe understand if this book focused on a hyper-specialized aspect of D&D. If it was say, pirate themed, I wouldn’t expect every class to suddenly be granted a swashbuckling speciality. But for something so intrinsic to this game as magic, and when there are so many still to be updated subclasses which could easily have been included here, it feels like such a let down that most of the games’ classes — including many spellcasters — are excluded.
These more expansive subclass options would also help to solve my other upset: the books feel too short.
At just 160 pages Arcana Unleashed feels kinda thin in my hands as I hold it. Meanwhile 5e expansions I keep comparing them to are longer — Tasha's Cauldron of Everything is 192 pages, as is Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, Strixhaven A Curriculum of Chaos is 224 pages, and Van Richten’s Guide to Ravenloft is 256.
Short doesn’t necessarily mean bad, but 160 pages on an expansion dedicated to something so quintessential to D&D just isn’t enough. It hits especially hard when the cost is $49.99 / £41.99 / AU$69.99.
I do think Arcana Unleashed has more than enough going for it to be something folks should pick up — it feels like a true successor to the ‘of Everything’ books I’ve referenced throughout this piece, which were (and still are) some of the most essential 5e expansions — but I’d recommend you wait for a discount.
Be that a sale form a big retailer, or a discount offered by your local game store if Arcana Unleashed cost closer to $35 / £30 / AU$45 (or better yet, less) it’s an easy snap buy. SO keep an eye on it as we head into this year’s holiday sales.

articles.title: Morbihan : une armurerie piratée, les papiers d'identité et l'adresse de détenteurs d'armes mis en vente
La Bugatti Bolide devait dépasser 500 km/h, encore faudrait-il trouver une piste assez longue et des pneus capables de supporter une telle vitesse
articles.text:
La Bugatti Bolide devait dépasser 500 km/h, encore faudrait-il trouver une piste assez longue et des pneus capables de supporter une telle vitesse
C’est en 2020 que Bugatti a présenté sa Bolide. À l’époque, le constructeur automobile parlait d’une vitesse supérieure à 500 km/h. Sauf qu’il s’agissait de celle en simulation et finalement, la version disponible pour les clients est limitée à 380 km/h. Mais même si la supercar proposait bien les 500 km/h de la simulation, encore faudrait-il trouver une piste assez longue et des pneus capables de supporter une telle vitesse.
Lors de la simulation de sa Bolide, Bugatti a utilisé un moteur W16 de 8,0 litres à quatre turbos avec de l’essence de compétition à 110 octanes pour 1 850 chevaux et un poids sec théorique de 1 240 kilos. Pour les chronomètres, les calculs donnaient 5 minutes 23 secondes et 1 centième sur la boucle Nord du Nürburgring et 3 minutes 07 secondes et 1 centième au Mans. Mais on ne parle pas là d’un essai chronométré sur circuit puisque comme expliqué précédemment, c’est une simulation.
Pourquoi atteindre 500 km/h aurait été compliqué
La version de série est finalement très différente de la simulation, même si sa fiche technique est très solide pour une supercar, disons-le clairement. Le moteur développe 1 600 chevaux avec de l’essence à 98 octanes et son poids atteint 1 450 kilos. La sécurité a aussi été revue, tout comme le refroidissement et l’aérodynamisme pour une utilisation sur circuit.
La vitesse maximale officielle est fixée à 380 km/h dans la configuration qui réduit le plus la résistance de l’air. Mais à 500 km/h, une telle vitesse est difficile à exploiter. Bugatti explique que les lignes droites des circuits homologués par la Fédération internationale de l’automobile dépassent rarement deux kilomètres. Une supercar a besoin de bien plus de distance pour accélérer vers 500 km/h puis freiner sans risque.
La Bugatti Bolide atteint 300 km/h en 11,5 secondes après 604 mètres et le freinage de 300 à 0 km/h demande 228 mètres. Donc passer de 0 à 300 km/h puis s’arrêter demande 832 mètres environ. Forcément, une tentative à 500 km/h demanderait une zone d’accélération et de freinage bien plus longue.
Andy Wallace, pilote d’essai de Bugatti, a atteint 490,484 km/h à Ehra-Lessien avec une Bugatti Chiron modifiée. Pour la tentative, le vainqueur des 24 Heures du Mans a pu compter sur des pneus spéciaux conçus par Michelin. Les roues de la Chiron tournaient jusqu’à 4 100 fois par minute et les pneus furent renforcés pour supporter d’énormes forces.
Vous l’aurez compris, approcher ces 500 km/h a déjà demandé une préparation spécifique sur une autre Bugatti conçue pour la vitesse de pointe.
Une Bugatti Bolide pensée juste pour les pistes
Le manuel de la Bugatti Bolide (disponible ici pour les curieux et curieuses) impose le remplacement des pneus de piste après 60 km et ces mêmes pneus sont aussi remplacés après dix passages à 380 km/h maximum. Les pneus pour 380 km/h ont déjà une durée d’utilisation minuscule et le manuel de la Bugatti Bolide n’indique même pas que ces pneus sont validés pour atteindre 500 km/h.
L’autre obstacle, c’est l’aérodynamisme. À 380 km/h, la Bolide produit près de 3 000 kg d’appui, soit une force qui plaque la voiture au sol. L’appui aide dans les virages mais augmente aussi la résistance à l’air. La Bugatti Bolide est une supercar capable de freiner fort et de garder une forte adhérence en courbe, mais pas forcément pensée pour un record de vitesse.
En tout, il existe 40 exemplaires de la Bugatti Bolide en circulation qui ont été vendus pour 4 millions d’euros hors taxes. Bien évidemment, cette supercar n’est pas homologuée pour la route. Bugatti propose des journées sur circuit pour les propriétaires qui cherchent à profiter de leur supercar et de ses sensations de vitesse.

articles.title: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5 small model and halves Sonnet 5.5 cache read prices - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5 small model and halves Sonnet 5.5 cache read prices
Anthropic PBC today released Claude Haiku 5.5, pricing its newest small model at roughly a quarter of what Haiku 4.5 costs to run.
Claude Sonnet 5.5 is getting cheaper as well, since the company is halving what it charges for cache reads on that model.
Two weeks after Opus 5.5 launched Sept. 22, Haiku 5.5 makes three models in the 5.5 generation. Anthropic is aiming it at repetitive work. High-volume summaries and classification are the main target, and coding teams can also use the model as a subagent that Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 hands smaller tasks to. Because no Anthropic model runs faster at standard speed, the company suggests it for live customer support and browser automation.
Anthropic’s running-cost figure rests on a steep cut to list prices. Haiku 4.5, released last October, costs $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output. For prompts of up to 100,000 tokens, which Anthropic said covered about 90% of the older model’s requests, Haiku 5.5 is 90% cheaper on input and output alike, at 10 cents and 50 cents per million tokens. Longer prompts get a 50% discount. The 75% average saving the company quotes takes in a new tokenizer that uses slightly more tokens per task. Cost can be tuned further, since Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku model with an adjustable effort setting.
The 10-cent and 50-cent rates match what OpenAI Group PBC charges for GPT-6 Luna, the low-cost model it launched last month. Anthropic’s published benchmarks have Haiku 5.5 ahead of Luna on all six tests where both have a score. On OSWorld 2.1, a test of agents operating a real computer through long multistep tasks, the new model scored 72.4% on the offline subset against 48.9% for Luna. Luna scored 16.4% on the Terminal-Bench 4.0 agentic coding test, less than half the new model’s 39.2%. For complex agentic coding, Anthropic still points customers to Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5.
Asana Inc. was among the customers that tested Haiku 5.5 before release, running it through the evaluation suite for its AI Teammates agent. Task completion latency came in more than 30% lower than with the model Asana uses today, and inference on each agent turn ran up to 2.5 times faster. “It’s a noticeably snappier experience,” said Aaron Vinh, a staff software engineer at the company.
On safety, Anthropic said alignment testing turned up far fewer instances of misaligned behavior than Haiku 4.5 showed. Cybersecurity safeguards on the model allow more defensive work than Sonnet 5.5 permits. Penetration testing is still blocked, as are other techniques attackers are more likely to use, and organizations that need wider access can apply to the Cyber Verification Program Anthropic expanded on Tuesday.
The Haiku launch also came with a price cut for Anthropic’s midsize model. Cache reads on Sonnet 5.5, which launched Sept. 28, drop from 20 cents per million tokens to 10 cents. Because cached tokens account for a large share of what models consume, Anthropic expects the cut to take about 20% off the cost of most agentic work on the model.
Claude Max and Team subscribers will also start receiving monthly application programming interface credits for the Claude Platform this week. A Max 5x subscription comes with $100 a month, double that on Max 20x. Team accounts get up to $500 shared across their users, and the credits can go toward any Claude model.
Haiku 5.5 is available now on the Claude Platform as claude-haiku-5-5 and through Amazon Web Services Inc., Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.

articles.title: This $7.99 TP-Link gigabit switch lets you cheaply upgrade your home network, and it's back at its lowest ever price — unmanaged LAN switch that adds five high-speed Ethernet ports to your setup for lag-free gaming or streaming
articles.text:
This $7.99 TP-Link gigabit switch lets you cheaply upgrade your home network, and it's back at its lowest ever price — unmanaged LAN switch that adds five high-speed Ethernet ports to your setup for lag-free gaming or streaming
Expand your local network with gigabit speeds
Wi-Fi is great until you hit lag, network congestion, or interference. If you need to expand your network, you'll want a network switch with gigabit speeds. Luckily, Amazon's big sale means you can pick up this TP-Link Lightwave 5-port unmanaged Ethernet switch for just $7.99 right now, bringing it back down to its lowest-ever price.

You don't need to worry about Wi-Fi lag or interference here, as you'll get a solid, dedicated wired connection instead. Back to a record low price
The TP-Link Litewave 5-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch LS1005G provides four additional Ethernet ports, delivering reliable, high-speed wired internet for your gaming PC, NAS, console, TV, and other connected devices.
As it's unmanaged, you do lose some of the customization features that you'd gain with a more expensive managed switch. That isn't really a downside here. This switch is less than $8. Another brilliantly-priced gigabit Ethernet switch, this Ugreen model has five ports, no fans for silent running, and should work with all of your usual wired networking devices.
There really isn't a better way to expand your wired network than with a network switch like this. For $7.99, both the TP-Link LS1005G and the Ugreen 35492US models will serve you well, delivering gigabit speeds across your LAN without worrying about Wi-Fi lag. It's a good, affordable option but, with Amazon's deal set to end tonight, you've got to be quick if you want to grab one (or two, or three) of these brilliantly-priced switches.

In this AI Infra Summit interview, Synopsys explains why the LLM is not the source of engineering truth. articles.title: Google revela el divertido detrás de cámaras de BTS interactuando con su IA Gemini
articles.text:
Los integrantes de la banda de k-pop, BTS, utilizan Gemini para tareas en su día a día. En el caso de Suga, su utilidad es en el estudio. (Instagram: googleespanol)
Google reveló el detrás de cámaras de su colaboración con BTS. Los integrantes de la banda surcoreana lideraron una campaña que muestra cómo Gemini puede integrarse en la vida cotidiana.
Por ejemplo, Jin, el mayor de los integrantes, utiliza la inteligencia artificial para perfeccionar sus técnicas de tenis, mientras que Jungkook usa Gemini como apoyo en las tareas de mantenimiento de su moto.
En el nuevo material revelado por Google, los integrantes se divierten detrás de cámaras y bromean entre ellos.
Cómo BTS utiliza Gemini, la IA de Google
Los videos, publicados en la cuenta de Instagram de Google en español, presentan a RM, Jin, SUGA, j-hope, Jimin, V y Jung Kook utilizando funciones de la inteligencia artificial para resolver situaciones de su rutina.
En los anuncios difundidos hasta ahora, Gemini responde consultas por voz, analiza imágenes y videos, y accede a información almacenada en aplicaciones como Gmail.
En un garaje, Jung Kook le pregunta a Gemini en coreano: “¿Cuándo fue la última vez que cambié el aceite de mi motor? Búscalo en mi Gmail”. La inteligencia artificial responde: “Tu último cambio de aceite fue el 7 de abril de 2026”.
Con esa información, el cantante revisa el mantenimiento de su motocicleta sin tener que buscar manualmente entre sus correos electrónicos.
V también recurre a Gemini para cuidar una planta cuyas hojas comenzaron a ponerse amarillas. “Gemini, ¿cómo debo cuidar esta planta según el pronóstico de esta semana?”, pregunta.
Tras analizar la imagen de la planta y la previsión meteorológica local, Gemini le indica a V que las hojas amarillas podrían deberse a un exceso de agua. Además, le recomienda reducir el riego ante la alta humedad prevista.
Por su parte, Jin carga un video de su saque de tenis y consulta: “Aquí hay un video de mi saque de tenis. Sigue pegando en la red. ¿Qué estoy haciendo mal? / ¿Por qué no me está saliendo bien mi saque?”.
Gemini le responde: “Según el video de saque que subiste, te estás inclinando demasiado hacia adelante en el video durante el lanzamiento. Solución: Mueve el lugar del lanzamiento aproximadamente a la distancia de media o una bola más arriba y un poco detrás de tu cabeza”. Luego de seguir la indicación, Jin consigue ejecutar un saque exitoso.
Por su parte, j-hope utiliza a Gemini para que lo asistencia en clase de batería. El artista le consulta a la IA por un resumen de los comentarios más recientes que ha recibido en sus clases para practicar según las observaciones.
Suga muestra que utiliza la IA para apoyarse al momento de establecer conversaciones en inglés, ya que el opta por hablar en coreano. Por tanto, Gemini funciona como un traductor en tiempo real.
RM, líder de la banda, le solicita a Gemini un itinerario para recorrer Nueva York. La inteligencia artificial de Google le proporciona un plan adaptado a sus intereses y disponibilidad, además de incluir restaurantes de comida coreana.
Mientras tanto, Jimin usa Gemini para apoyarse en la redacción de sus discursos en inglés. “Gemini, voy a leer la carta, por favor revisa mi pronunciación”, le solicita el cantante a la IA.
Gemini ya puede entender lo que muestra la cámara del celular
Google incorporó Guided Vision a Gemini Live, una función que utiliza la cámara del celular para describir en tiempo real lo que aparece frente al usuario. La herramienta responde por voz, identifica objetos, colores, formas y espacios, y permite realizar preguntas de seguimiento.
Está orientada principalmente a personas ciegas o con baja visión, ya que ayuda a leer etiquetas, interpretar información nutricional y localizar objetos.
Además, Gemini puede indicar cómo corregir el encuadre de la cámara. Google advierte que no debe emplearse para desplazarse ni detectar obstáculos. Guided Vision funciona en Android 9 o posterior y es compatible con TalkBack.

articles.title: Arizona court hack leads to theft of over 1 million American's data
articles.text:
Arizona court system hack leads to theft of personal data belonging to 1.3 million Americans
Someone "clicked on a link in an email"
- A successful phishing attack at the Arizona Supreme Court led to data compromise
- More than a million people are now thought to be affected
- The court's operations were not disrupted
The Arizona Supreme Court has suffered a cyberattack in which it lost sensitive data on more than a million people after an employee allegedly “clicked a malicious link in an email”, which led to the compromise of information on 1.3 million people.
Information is still scarce on the issue, as we don’t know if that malicious link resulted in the victim’s device being infected with an infostealer, or if they were asked to log into a bogus portal, allowing the threat actors to access their account directly.
It was confirmed that the threat actors copied information on 1.3 million people with unpaid court fees, fines and restitution payments for traffic and criminal violations dating back 30 years. They also nabbed almost 30,000 active and inactive orders of protection, as well as 150,000 reports dating back to 2010 from a foster care board making recommendations in cases where parents were allegedly unable or unfit to care for a child.
This kind of data is a gold mine for cybercriminals. Personal and private information can be used to tailor unique, personalized phishing lures which the victims will have a very hard time identifying. These emails can lure the recipients into downloading malware, or navigating to spoofed login portals designed to steal credentials. That malware can then spread to the victims’ employers, possibly resulting in ransomware deployments or data theft and extortion.
Responding to the attack
According to the Associated Press (AP), the court’s IT team shut down the attack on a backup server, roughly two hours after being spotted, on September 24. Since then, they have been notifying the affected individuals about the breach and theft.
So far, the data has not yet made it to the dark web, it seems: “We don’t have any evidence it has been used or shared” after the attack, Supreme Court spokesperson Alberto Rodriguez said.
This would also suggest that this was not the work of any known ransomware groups or data extortionists because by now they would have at least bragged about it on the dark web.

The investigation is still ongoing. The court’s operations have not been disrupted in any way, Rodriguez added. The records were not altered, or deleted, and the attackers apparently did not steal information about jurors, witnesses, or court employees.
Attacking courts
Courts (both in the US and elsewhere) are frequent targets, mostly due to the sensitivity of the information they work with.
In early September 2026, it was reported that Thomson Reuters, the IT company behind the Reuters news agency, suffered a similar incident in March.
The company operates a court case-management system called C-Track, used by different courts to manage things like cases, filings, hearings, and schedules. It is used by courts in several US states, the US Virgin Islands, as well as Ontario, Canada. Unnamed miscreants managed to break in, obtaining “court records and personal information” across 11 US states, the US Virgin Islands, and Ontario, Canada.
Earlier still, on November 21, 2025, the Georgia Superior Court Clerks’ Cooperative Authority (GSCCCA), which manages court and public-record services across Georgia, detected hackers trying to break into the network. The attack was claimed by threat actors called Devman, which claimed to have stolen sensitive files and demanded a ransom payment in exchange. The GSCCCA temporarily shut down its websites and online services, while the FBI warned the authority of an imminent threat.
However, GSCCCA said it stopped the attackers before they were able to extract or encrypt any data and refused to pay the ransom. Devman is not a household name in the cybercriminal underworld, and apparently, it is a financially motivated group, not a state-sponsored one.

articles.title: Surface Laptop Ultra : RTX Spark 18 cœurs et 24 Go de RAM... à qui servira la mouture la plus accessible ?
articles.text:
Microsoft tiendra ce soir une conférence vraisemblablement dédiée à la présentation détaillée de son Surface Laptop Ultra. Annoncé au Computex, le premier modèle RTX Spark du géant américain n’a aujourd’hui plus tellement de secrets pour nous. De nouvelles informations révèlent désormais quelle sera la configuration la moins onéreuse de l’appareil.
Annoncés en juin dernier à l’occasion du Computex, les PC portables RTX Spark attendus chez MSI, Lenovo, Dell, HP, ASUS et Microsoft se destinent en premier lieu à la gestion locale de grands modèles d’intelligence artificielle. C’est en tout cas la raison d’être des configurations dotées de 20 cœurs CPU et 128 Go de mémoire unifiée, tant vantées ces derniers mois par NVIDIA et ses partenaires.
On sait néanmoins que les machines RTX Spark seront aussi proposées dans des configurations moins coûteuses, limitées cette fois à 18 cœurs CPU et 24 Go de mémoire unifiée. Ce sera notamment le cas de certains modèles ASUS ProArt. On découvre aujourd’hui de Windows Central que Microsoft proposera la même chose sur son Surface Laptop Ultra.
18 cœurs CPU et 24 Go de mémoire unifiée pour le Surface Laptop Ultra le moins coûteux ?
Dans le détail, on apprend que la configuration la plus accessible (ou plutôt la moins dispendieuse) du Surface Laptop Ultra intégrera une puce RTX Spark « castrée », combinant donc 18 cœurs CPU à une partie graphique à 5 120 cœurs CUDA, épaulée par 24 ou 32 Go de mémoire unifiée seulement.
Cette configuration permettra sans doute l’installation de petits LLM locaux (moins de 20 milliards de paramètres a priori), mais a surtout vocation à servir un public gamer ou créatif, pour jouer aux derniers triple A sur une machine élégante, ou se livrer à du montage vidéo lourd, de la retouche photo, du graphisme ou de la modélisation 3D, par exemple.
Les grands LLM de 100-120 milliards de paramètres, eux, se destinent principalement à la meilleure configuration du Surface Laptop Ultra… Dont nous avons aussi le détail. Selon toute logique, on y retrouvera cette fois une puce RTX Spark au grand complet (20 cœurs CPU et GPU de 6 144 cœurs CUDA) couplée à 32, 48, 64 ou 128 Go de mémoire unifiée.
Les gamers et les créateurs de contenus principalement ciblés
Pour contexte, et comme le souligne VideoCardz, un modèle local à 120 milliards de paramètres occupe à lui seul environ 60 Go de mémoire vive avec une quantification à 4 bits. De quoi vous donner une idée. Le Surface Laptop Ultra 24 Go ne fera pas le poids pour cette utilisation en particulier, il s’orientera donc bien vers les usages listés plus haut.
Quoi qu’il en soit, l’appareil devrait proposer les mêmes performances sur secteur ou sur batterie (Microsoft a déjà parlé de performances maintenues à 99,6 % en fonctionnement sur batterie), mais aussi intégrer un écran tactile haut de gamme de 15 pouces « PixelSense Ultra », peu importe la configuration choisie. Cet écran affiche 2000 cd/m2 de luminance HDR et une densité de pixels annoncée à 262 ppp.
Le Surface Laptop Ultra s’appuie enfin sur un châssis en aluminium de 18 mm d’épaisseur pour 2,04 kg, comportant trois ports USB-C, un port USB-A, une prise casque, une sortie HDMI et un lecteur de cartes SD.
Pour l’instant aucun prix n’est encore communiqué, mais Microsoft pourrait nous en dire plus dès ce soir. Affaire à suivre.

articles.title: Après des mois de soleil, c'est le retour de la neige en France avec jusqu'à 10 cm dans ces communes avant les vacances de la Toussaint
articles.text:
Après des mois de soleil, c'est le retour de la neige en France avec jusqu'à 10 cm dans ces communes avant les vacances de la Toussaint
Après un été caniculaire, exit le soleil et la chaleur. À dix jours des vacances de la Toussaint, la neige fait son retour en France avec des températures qui chuteront jusqu’à 10 à 15 degrés en très peu de temps. On parle même de jusqu’à 10 centimètres de neige.
Le changement s’annonce brutal dans les Alpes, qui seront les plus touchées par ces chutes de neige. Plusieurs communes de Savoie et de Haute-Savoie sont concernées par ce changement brutal de température.
La neige de retour en France après un été très chaud
Et pour cause, l’été 2026 fut le plus chaud jamais mesuré en France depuis 1900 et aussi le plus ensoleillé. Ce sont 53 jours de vague de chaleur et un excédent de soleil supérieur à 20 % dans tout l’Hexagone qui furent relevés par Météo-France.
Et le mois de septembre n’a pas cassé cette tendance puisqu’il s’agissait du deuxième mois de septembre le plus chaud depuis 1900 avec une température moyenne supérieure de 3,1 degrés à la normale. Ce fut également le deuxième plus ensoleillé.
Bref, cette période de soleil prend un coup d’arrêt avec une masse d’air froide qui descend du nord et du nord-ouest. Les maximales perdront 5 à 10 degrés sur une large partie de la France et jusqu’à 15 degrés par endroits.
Lejeudi 8 octobre, les températures passeront même sous les normales de saison dans plusieurs régions. L’air chaud remonté d’Afrique du Nord en début de semaine laisse place à un flux bien plus froid. a neige accompagnera donc cette chute du thermomètre.
Dans certaines zones de l’Hexagone, les cumuls de neige pourraient atteindre jusqu’à 35 centimètres au-dessus de 2 800 mètres. Parmi les communes touchées, on trouve Bourg-Saint-Maurice et Modane. ien évidemment, le centre sera épargné puisque les dix centimètres annoncés concernent les hauteurs.
Idem, retour de la neige dans les Pyrénées avec leurs premiers flocons vers 1 800 mètres. Au Puy de Sancy, on parle même de températures proches de zéro degré. Si les précipitations persistent, des flocons seront attendus vers 1 500 mètres dans les Alpes.
Mais le temps doux reviendra ce week-end
C’est le vendredi 9 octobre qu’aura lieu la journée la plus fraîche en France puisque les minimales pourraient tomber autour de zéro degré dans les Alpes du Nord. Mais cette première vague de froid ne marque pas l’installation de l’hiver puisque le redoux commencera dès le week-end. On s’attend à une nouvelle perturbation samedi puis un temps plus sec et doux ensuite.
Le samedi 17 octobre, les vacances de la Toussaint débutent pour les zones A, B et C. Soit au moment où commencera à se terminer cet épisode de froid. Le redoux annoncé dès le week-end fera fondre une partie de la neige à moyenne altitude.
Mais après des mois de chaleur, de soleil et de sécheresse, même dix centimètres sur les hauteurs alpines représentent une vraie différence avec l’été des derniers mois. Car si l’on peut se dire qu’il est logique qu’il neige en montagne, le réchauffement climatique raréfie ces épisodes neigeux d'année en année.

articles.title: Saudi AI startup Echelon secures backing from East40, RAED Ventures and Avra
articles.text:
Saudi AI startup Echelon secures backing from East40, RAED Ventures and Avra
- Saudi AI startup Echelon has raised an undisclosed investment round, backed by East40, RAED Ventures and Avra, alongside Ben Horowitz and other investors.
- Founded in 2025 by Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, Echelon works with global technology providers and organisations in Saudi Arabia to deploy and localise AI technologies within enterprises and government entities.
- The company operates across sectors including energy, industrials, government, telecommunications, defence, aviation, financial services and insurance, and healthcare, and has partnerships with technology companies including Applied Intuition, IFS and Rubrik.
- Echelon plans to launch Frontier, an engineering arm that will deploy and develop AI applications within customer organisations, alongside an Institute to train Saudi engineers in applied AI, during Q4 2026. It also plans to launch Echelon Defense Industries in Q1 2027.
- The company will initially focus on Saudi Arabia before expanding across the region, using the investment to support its strategy of deploying AI technologies in enterprise and government operations.
Press release:
Saudi AI startup Echelon has raised an undisclosed investment round from East40, RAED Ventures and Avra, alongside Ben Horowitz and other investors, as it looks to expand the deployment of artificial intelligence technologies across enterprises and government entities in Saudi Arabia.
Founded in Riyadh by Prince Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud, Echelon has spent around 10 months developing a model aimed at bridging the gap between AI technology providers and organisations seeking to deploy their technologies in day-to-day operations.
Rather than developing a single AI product, Echelon works with technology providers across the AI stack and helps enterprises and government entities select, localise and deploy their technologies.
The company is targeting eight sectors, including energy, industrials, government, telecommunications, defence, aviation, financial services and insurance, and healthcare.
Its current technology partnerships include Applied Intuition, IFS and Rubrik. In September, Echelon partnered with IFS to deploy and localise its industrial AI platform, IFS.ai, for Saudi enterprises, particularly across asset-intensive industries.
It has also partnered with US-based Applied Intuition to bring its physical AI platform to Saudi Arabia, targeting industries including logistics, mining and mobility.
Echelon is building its operations around several business units. Its Technologies division, led by former Microsoft executive Omar Saleh, focuses on commercial partnerships and enterprise deployments.
The company plans to launch Frontier in the fourth quarter of 2026, embedding engineers within customer organisations to deploy AI technologies and develop applications and intellectual property locally.
During the same quarter, Echelon plans to launch an Institute to train Saudi engineers in applied AI, beginning with a programme focused on physical AI. A separate Echelon Defense Industries division is scheduled to launch in the first quarter of 2027.
The company plans to work through commercial partnerships, joint ventures and purpose-built businesses, while committing capital, personnel and operational resources to selected projects.
Echelon is initially focusing on the Saudi market, with plans to expand its model across the wider region.

articles.title: OpenAI publishes 722 AI-generated math discoveries in major scientific milestone - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
OpenAI publishes 722 AI-generated math discoveries in major scientific milestone
OpenAI Group PBC has published 722 math papers that it generated using an unreleased artificial intelligence model.
Some of the papers, which were posted to GitHub late Tuesday, prove long-running hypotheses. Others disapprove proposed explanations of mathematical phenomena or narrow down the possible answers to complex, yet-unsolved puzzles. Overall, OpenAI’s papers span about 20 mathematical subfields.
One of the most notable discoveries relates to the Riemann hypothesis. It’s a more than 150-year-old paper about prime numbers, numbers that can only be divided by themselves or one. The Riemann hypothesis argues that prime numbers follow a pattern described by a mathematical object called the Riemann zeta function.
Proving the conjecture is considered to be one of the most important challenges in mathematics. Its significance partly stems from the fact that many later math papers are based on the assumption the Riemann hypothesis is correct. In other words, proving the Riemann hypothesis would verify those papers.
OpenAI’s unreleased AI model didn’t manage to come up with a complete answer. However, it did prove an important piece of the puzzle called the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
Theoretical computer science was another major focus of OpenAI’s research exercise. The company’s unreleased AI model produced more than 80 papers about the topic.
Three of the papers focus on matrix multiplications, the mathematical operations that AI models use to process data. For the past few decades, researchers have been working to develop faster, more hardware-efficient ways to perform such calculations. It’s believed that matrix multiplications can only be sped up so much before a limit is reached.
OpenAI’s model developed a clearer definition of that limit. In a separate paper, it developed a new algorithm for multiplying integers. An integer is a data structure that contains a whole number. Like matrix multiplications, integer multiplications are foundational building blocks of many programs.
The research breakthrough is also relevant for physicists. The company published more than a dozen proofs that relate to partial differential equations, or PDEs. Those are physics equations that are essential to chip design, architecture, quantum mechanics and a range of other fields.
The model proved a version of De Giorgi’s conjecture, a hypothesis that relates to an equation used to study metal alloys. It also clarified a number of questions related to the Navier–Stokes equations, which engineers use to study the flow of liquids.
In September, the AI model that produced the papers solved a different problem related to the Navier–Stokes equations. That puzzle ranked as one of the most difficult open questions in mathematics.
Many of OpenAI’s new papers contain Lean files. Those are code snippets that make it possible to quickly verify a newly published proof using a computer. Going forward, OpenAI plans to release Lean proofs for more of the papers. The company also intends to finance of research events and programs that will focus on reviewing AI-generated math discoveries.

articles.title: Musk rejects rumors of TSMC takeover of Terafab — Intel reaffirms 14A node deal as Musk floats cleanroom 'sublease'
articles.text:
Musk rejects rumors of TSMC takeover of Terafab — Intel reaffirms 14A node deal as Musk floats cleanroom 'sublease'
Musk wants to run Terafab all by himself.
Intel will remain a part of Elon Musk's Terafab project, Lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of Intel, told reporters on Wednesday. Around the same time, Elon Musk, chief executive of SpaceX, Tesla, and xAI, said that Terafab remains committed to building and operating its fab itself, but proposed to lease a part of the fab to TSMC.
Intel will continue its involvement in Terafab, Lip-Bu Tan told Bloomberg prior to the company's event in Japan that commemorates the company's presence in Japan. Back in April, Intel and Terafab, the semiconductor production venture by SpaceX, Tesla, and xAI, announced that the new chipmaker would use Intel's next-generation 14A fabrication process to make chips. Details of the collaboration are still unknown, but there is a general understanding that Intel will license its manufacturing technology to Terafab, though it is unclear whether it will also help ramp up production using the node.
At around the same time, Elon Musk debunked rumors that his companies would invest in Terafab and then partner with TSMC, which will build and operate the fab. Instead, Elon Musk proposes that TSMC sublease a part of Terafab to make chips for its customers.
"No, we will build and run the fab," Elon Musk wrote in an X post. "Let there be ZERO doubt about that. Maybe TSMC subleases part of the Terafab if they want, but nothing more than that."
Offering TSMC, the world's largest foundry that owns and operates dozens of advanced 300-mm fabs around the world, to 'sublease' a part of Terafab is quite an unusual arrangement for many reasons.
First up, TSMC has its own production facilities as well as aggressive plans for about 10 new fab phases in the coming years, and it hardly needs to sublease any capacity or part of the building or site from a third party.
Secondly, semiconductor fabs are not generic facilities: if Terafab is initially equipped and qualified around Intel's 14A process technology, converting part of the facility for TSMC's A14, A13, or A12 processes that the company will use in the back half of the decade would require different process flows, equipment configurations, materials, automation, qualification, and contamination control. Theoretically, TSMC could install a largely independent production line within the same enormous building, but at that point the arrangement would resemble TSMC building and operating its own fab inside a Musk-controlled site rather than simply renting spare manufacturing capacity.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Thirdly, if Intel licenses 14A technology to Terafab, the agreement would almost certainly contain extensive provisions governing access to Intel IP, process information, equipment configurations, and personnel. Putting TSMC engineers and manufacturing operations inside the same facility could create contractual and IP-isolation issues even if TSMC never directly touches the Intel production line. In fact, IP protection would be extraordinary at Terafab, which will complicate its operation.
Fourthly, if indeed two chipmakers end up in the same fab building, or even in the same campus, responsibility for downtime becomes messy. In the case of a Terafab-owned power distribution system, water plant, chemical system, or cooling installation fails and takes someone's production offline, determining operational responsibility and financial liability for potentially hundreds of millions of dollars of affected wafers would be considerably more complicated than at a site controlled by one company.
Finally, if Terafab can equip enough cleanroom space by the end of the decade to satisfy semiconductor requirements of Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI while still leaving substantial capacity available to TSMC, that would raise questions about whether the project had significantly overbuilt capacity in its initial phases.
Since Musk's statements at X are deliberately vague, it is hard to interpret them. In fact, there might be a conceptual problem with Musk's statement. If TSMC installs its own tools, hires its own employees, brings process technology, and production management, while Terafab just provides land, shell, and infrastructure, calling this a 'sublease' undersells what would be a TSMC fab embedded within the Terafab campus. Alternatively, if Terafab provides the tools and infrastructure and TSMC just operates them, that starts to look much closer to precisely the kind of TSMC operational involvement Musk appears to be denying.
Anyhow, while Intel has confirmed its involvement in the project and Musk wants TSMC to be part of it as well, the latest comments raise more questions than they answer.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: El CEO de AWS advierte que EE. UU. perderá la carrera de la IA si frena los centros de datos
articles.text:
Matt Garman, director ejecutivo de Amazon Web Services (AWS), advirtió que frenar la construcción de nuevos centros de datos puede hacer que Estados Unidos pierda la carrera de la inteligencia artificial (IA), con efectos sobre la economía y la seguridad nacional que, según sostuvo, “podrían prolongarse por generaciones”.
La expansión de estas instalaciones ocurre mientras la inteligencia artificial acelera su adopción y aún se encuentra “en una etapa muy temprana”. Garman afirmó que “ya transforma empresas, industrias y la experiencia de los clientes de formas que no podían anticiparse hace apenas unos años”.
Por qué es clave no frenar los centros de datos, según el CEO de AWS
El directivo comparó la infraestructura digital con el sistema de autopistas desarrollado por Estados Unidos en la década de 1950, al considerar que cumple una función similar para impulsar la actividad económica en todo el país. Garman situó el actual despliegue en una secuencia que incluye la expansión de internet en los años 90 y la computación en la nube durante la década de 2000.
Las tareas cotidianas, desde las compras y las operaciones bancarias hasta la compraventa de acciones, los servicios de transporte compartido, las reservas de viajes, la atención médica y el entretenimiento en línea, dependen de sistemas digitales. Garman explicó que esas actividades “requieren la computación, el almacenamiento y el acceso que gestionan los centros de datos”.
Además, el alcance incluye investigaciones para prevenir y curar enfermedades, sumado a iniciativas destinadas a reducir el uso de energía y recursos naturales. Para el ejecutivo, impedir nuevas instalaciones comprometería la prosperidad económica y la seguridad nacional.
La advertencia se produce ante más de cien moratorias decretadas en distintos puntos del país para detener o limitar nuevos proyectos. Las preocupaciones ambientales y el consumo de energía y recursos figuran entre las razones que impulsan esas restricciones.
Sin embargo, la última edición del Libro Beige de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos, destacó que la demanda de estas infraestructuras contribuye al crecimiento económico del país. Garman defendió que la inversión privada financia el desarrollo de los centros sin utilizar dinero de los contribuyentes.
Cuál podría ser el impacto ambiental de los centros de datos en el futuro
Los centros de datos podrían consumir más del 5% de la electricidad mundial en 2035, casi tres veces la demanda actual, de acuerdo con BloombergNEF. La firma de análisis energético prevé que la mayor parte de ese aumento se cubra con centrales de gas nuevas y ya existentes.
Ese cambio en la matriz de generación podría elevar las emisiones del sector eléctrico hasta un 6% en menos de una década. La proyección vincula el crecimiento de la infraestructura digital con una mayor dependencia del gas para responder a la demanda energética.
BloombergNEF revisó al alza su estimación de capacidad de centros de datos en Estados Unidos para 2030 hasta 118 gigavatios, un 52% más que el cálculo elaborado en diciembre de 2025. La consultora aclaró que una parte importante de esa capacidad depende de proyectos que aún podrían no completarse.
Asimismo, el análisis examinó 99 centrales de gas propuestas para abastecer directamente a centros de datos fuera de la red eléctrica general. Si todos esos proyectos se construyeran, las emisiones del sector eléctrico estadounidense podrían aumentar entre 20% y 33%.
Por su parte, Rhodium Group planteó una proyección más moderada. La firma de investigación energética calculó que una expansión acelerada de la demanda dejaría las emisiones de 2035 entre 6% y 13% por encima de sus escenarios de base, aunque todavía por debajo de los niveles registrados en 2024.
Qué dijo el CEO de AWS sobre la contaminación de los centros de datos
Garman rechazó que los generadores diésel de respaldo emitan grandes volúmenes de contaminantes. Según afirmó, permanecen inactivos el 99,9% del tiempo y funcionan unas 10 horas al año, sobre todo para las pruebas de mantenimiento exigidas.
Cuestionó que las subas en las tarifas eléctricas de las comunidades cercanas sean consecuencia directa de los centros de datos. A su juicio, esa acusación busca un “chivo expiatorio”, mientras que el encarecimiento responde principalmente al envejecimiento de redes eléctricas que no están preparadas para una demanda elevada.

articles.title: MSI Unveils Prestige N16 Flip AI+: An NVIDIA RTX Spark-Powered 2-in-1 Built for the Agentic AI Era

MSI Unveils Prestige N16 Flip AI+: An NVIDIA RTX Spark-Powered 2-in-1 Built for the Agentic AI Era
MSI, a global leader in high-performance and AI computing, today announced that the Prestige N16 Flip AI+ is now available for pre-order through MSI-certified partners in select markets.
Prestige N16 Flip AI+ is powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark, uniting NVIDIA AI, RTX graphics, and unified memory in one powerful and efficient thin-and-light Windows PC. Designed to run larger AI models locally—without cloud dependency—and move between creative work, development, and immersive gaming without missing a beat. Connect apps, tools, and workflows into one seamless experience. Private by default. RTX Spark brings NVIDIA's full-stack AI platform, ready for the AI workloads of today and whatever comes next. Delivered on the familiar, trusted, and secure Windows platform.Key Product Highlights
- Powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark with an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU, NVIDIA Grace CPU, up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance and up to 128 GB of unified memory in a premium, mobile 2-in-1.
- Run personal AI agent workloads locally, keeping sensitive data private, reducing recurring cloud costs, and responding faster by avoiding network delays.
- Support for NVIDIA CUDA, providing broad compatibility with today's AI software.
- Accelerates video, 3D, AI creation, and gaming with NVIDIA Studio and RTX technology, including ray tracing, DLSS, and Reflex.
- Delivers instant-on responsiveness and great performance whether on battery or plugged in—one PC for work, creativity and play.
- Combines the power-efficient, instant-on mobility of Windows on Arm with support for Arm-native apps and familiar Windows software through emulation.
- Prestige N16 Flip AI+ stands alone as the 2-in-1 convertible in the first announced wave of RTX Spark Windows laptops, pairing a 16-inch UHD+ Tandem OLED touchscreen with a 360-degree hinge, a bundled MSI Nano Pen, an MSI Action Touchpad with a 53% larger surface, an SD Card Reader, quad-speaker audio, and laptop, tablet, tent, and presentation modes.
Personal AI, Now in a Premium 2-in-1
At the center of the Prestige N16 Flip AI+ is the NVIDIA RTX Spark, a new superchip that combines an NVIDIA Grace CPU, and a Blackwell RTX GPU. It brings the NVIDIA CUDA platform—the global standard for AI development—to a more mobile form factor. With up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance, it gives creators and developers a powerful local environment for AI agents, model prototyping, coding, and content creation.
Built for the agentic future, the system turns the PC from a tool into a teammate. Local AI agents can run tasks, generate assets, and help write code on demand, while users remain focused on the work they care most about.
Keeping supported AI workloads local improves privacy, reduces recurring cloud costs, and speeds up responses by avoiding network delays. RTX Spark also accelerates creation and gaming with technologies like ray tracing, NVIDIA DLSS, and NVIDIA Reflex.
Up to 128 GB of Unified Memory for Bigger Local Workflows
The Prestige N16 Flip AI+ is available with up to 128 GB of unified memory shared by the CPU and GPU. This large memory pool helps users work with bigger AI models, complex 3D projects up to 90 GB in size, and high-resolution media, while keeping multiple demanding applications simultaneously loaded.
Efficient, Responsive, and Ready to Work
NVIDIA RTX Spark is the most power-efficient RTX chip ever made, bringing lasting performance to slim laptops. Paired with the Prestige N16 Flip AI+'s 99.9Wh battery and instant-on responsiveness, this efficiency lets users move quickly from standby into meetings, sketches, development environments, and agentic workflows with great performance on or off the wall.
UA Creator-Grade Canvas That Adapts to Every Workflow
The Prestige N16 Flip AI+ complements its advanced performance with a 16-inch UHD+ Tandem OLED touchscreen engineered for both creative precision and immersive entertainment. With more than 1,000 nits of peak brightness, 100% DCI-P3 color coverage, Calman Verification, Delta E <1 color accuracy, and variable refresh rate support, the display delivers exceptional contrast, lifelike color, and fluid motion for professional content creation, entertainment, and gaming.
RTX Spark is optimized by the applications creators already rely on. DaVinci Resolve leverages 5th generation Tensor Cores to accelerate color grading and AI-powered editing tools. Blender utilizes DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction for real-time path tracings in the CYCLES viewport Adobe Premiere Pro taps the Blackwell architecture's NVENC and NVDEC engines to speed up video exports. And ComfyUI runs local diffusion workflows with NVFP4 acceleration for faster video generation.
Among the first wave of RTX Spark Windows laptops announced, the Prestige N16 Flip AI+ stands out as a 2-in-1 convertible with a touchscreen and dedicated pen support. Its 360-degree hinge transitions seamlessly between laptop, tablet, tent, and presentation modes. Included at no extra cost, the MSI Nano Pen features MSI's patented design and turns the display into a precise canvas for note-taking, annotation, sketching, and creative work. A purpose-built recess beneath the chassis keeps the pen secure and charged, so it stays with the laptop and is ready whenever inspiration strikes.
A spacious MSI Action Touchpad—53% larger than the previous generation—adds customizable gesture zones that streamline navigation and multitasking. A built-in SD Card Reader helps creators move photos and footage directly from cameras and media, while the quad-speaker system completes a premium experience designed for creation, collaboration, productivity, and entertainment wherever work takes you.
Now Available for Pre-Order Through MSI-Certified Partners
The MSI Prestige N16 Flip AI+ is now available through MSI official stores and authorized retail and channel partners, with availability varying by market.
To celebrate the launch, eligible customers who purchase the Prestige N16 Flip AI+ until December 31, 2026, can receive an exclusive Early Bird Bundle valued at US$299, including an MSI Dual Drive 128 GB, one year of MSI Care Plus, and one year of Accidental Damage Protection. For full promotion details, please visit the website of your local MSI authorized retail or channel partner.
For local availability, campaign dates, and full promotional details, please visit the MSI official website or contact an authorized MSI sales partner.

Power, not chips, has become the limiting factor in the artificial intelligence buildout, according to Axiado founder, President, and CEO Gopi Sirineni.
Speaking with EE Times reporter Sally Ward-Foxton at the AI Infra Summit 2026, Sirineni discussed his presentation, “More Tokens Per Dollar: AI-Driven Platform Efficiency Controllers for High-Density AI Racks.” He explained that the solution to data center power constraints lives in the platform management layer rather than better facilities or better silicon.
Axiado addresses this through AI agents running on its Trusted Control Unit (TCU) silicon that sense, decide and act in milliseconds with no human in the loop. Sirineni detailed what Axiado’s dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) and dynamic thermal management agents can accomplish that a modern server cannot do for itself, noting that efficiency gains range from 10% out of the box to 30% with tuning.
Sirineni argued that effectively managing and securing modern AI infrastructure requires moving away from decades-old legacy management paradigms toward truly intelligent, autonomous infrastructure management to drive higher efficiency, better security and greater reliability.

articles.title: Beltone, Amtaar plan $38 million multi-issuance real estate fund
articles.text:
Beltone, Amtaar plan $38 million multi-issuance real estate fund
- Beltone Asset Management, a subsidiary of Beltone Holding and Egypt's fractional real estate investment platform Amtaar Capital have partnered to establish a multi-issuance real estate investment fund targeting total issuances of EGP 2 billion ($38 million).
- The fund, which is currently under establishment, is expected to launch its first issuance at between EGP 500 million and EGP 700 million, with Beltone responsible for establishing and managing the fund and overseeing asset selection.
- Amtaar will provide the digital platform through which investors can access the fund's first issuance, with investments starting at EGP 1,000.
- The fund will invest in income-generating real estate, allowing investors to gain exposure through fund units rather than directly purchasing an entire property, with potential returns from rental income and capital appreciation.
- The partnership combines Beltone's asset management operations with Amtaar's digital real estate investment platform, as the companies seek to broaden access to professionally managed real estate investments in Egypt.
Press release:
Beltone Asset Management, a subsidiary of Beltone Holding, and Amtaar Capital have announced their partnership on a multi-issuance real estate investment fund, which is currently under establishment, with total targeted issuances of EGP 2 billion. The fund’s first issuance is expected to range between EGP 500 million and EGP 700 million. Under the structure, Beltone Asset Management will establish and manage the fund and oversee asset selection in line with its investment strategy, while Amtaar Capital will provide the digital platform through which investors can access the investment opportunity for the fund’s first issuance.
The fund will enable investors to invest in real estate fund units through Amtaar Capital’s digital platform, providing an opportunity to invest in income-generating properties without the need to purchase or directly own an entire property. Investors will be able to participate in the fund starting from EGP 1,000. Investors may benefit from rental income generated by the underlying real estate assets, alongside potential capital appreciation, subject to the fund’s investment strategy, performance, and applicable terms and conditions.
Khaled Darwish, CEO of Beltone Asset Management, said: “Real estate investment is an important component of many investors’ portfolios, but direct ownership typically requires significant capital and can lead to concentration in a single asset. Our partnership with Amtaar provides a different route to professionally managed real estate investment, combining Beltone Asset Management’s investment management expertise with Amtaar’s digital access.”
Amr Afifi, Co-Founder and CEO of Amtaar Capital, added: “Our partnership with Beltone Asset Management brings together Amtaar’s digital real estate ecosystem and Beltone Asset Management’s investment management expertise to make real estate investment more accessible to a broader range of investors, while offering a simpler digital experience.”
The partnership reflects the increasing role of digital platforms in broadening access to alternative investment opportunities, bringing together investment management expertise and a digital real estate ecosystem to provide a more accessible route to real estate investment.

Faster Wi-Fi, wider coverage.
If you're looking to upgrade your home network without spending a fortune, investing in a mesh Wi-Fi 7 system is worth considering. Combining fast wireless speeds with wide-area coverage, it is a practical option for homes with multiple devices, including smartphones, gaming PCs, laptops, smart TVs, and smart home devices. Currently on sale, the TP-Link Deco 7 BE25 BE500 mesh Wi-Fi 7 dual-pack is currently available for $149.99 on Amazon, down from its selling price of $199.99. If you want even wider coverage, the triple pack is also on sale and can be purchased for $198.19, which is over $100 off its listed price of $299.99.
Built around dual-band Wi-Fi 7, the TP-Link Deco 7 BE25 mesh system offers combined speeds of up to 5,012 Mbps. It can reach up to 4,324 Mbps on the 5 GHz band and 688 Mbps on 2.4 GHz, making it suitable for demanding workloads such as 4K streaming, online gaming, and AR/VR applications. Coverage is another major advantage of the mesh system, with the dual-pack offering up to 4,600 square feet, while the triple-pack extends coverage to up to 6,600 square feet. The system can support more than 150 connected devices, and users can expand the network further by adding additional Deco units.
Upgrade to Wi-Fi 7 for $149.99 with TP-Link’s Deco 7 BE5000 dual-pack Wi-Fi 7 mesh system offering coverage of up to 4,600 sq. ft. and up to 5,012 Mbps speeds.
Save over $100 on TP-Link’s Deco 7 BE5000 triple-pack Wi-Fi 7 mesh system offering excellent coverage of up to 6,600 sq. ft. for large homes.
The Deco 7 also supports simultaneous wired and wireless backhaul, allowing Wi-Fi 7 and 2.5 Gbps Ethernet connections to work together to distribute traffic between Deco units. This can provide faster and more stable connections throughout the home, particularly when multiple devices are connected at the same time. For security, the Deco 7 supports TP-Link HomeShield, which provides network and IoT protection along with features such as security scans, IoT device identification, basic parental controls, Quality of Service settings, and network activity reports.
At $149.99 for the dual-pack and $198.19 for the triple-pack, the Deco 7 BE5000 is a great option if you're looking to dramatically extend wireless coverage across a larger home. It is also an excellent choice if you want to upgrade to a faster Wi-Fi 7 system for your home or office setup.

Sennheiser's wired earbuds might be my favorite I've ever tested, and I still use them all the time two years later — here's why I'd recommend them to everyone today
You don't want to miss this
It feels like wired earbuds have been well and truly back in fashion for a little while now, and I can totally see why. A wired connection gives you access to lossless audio, unlike lossy Bluetooth devices, and they can also look pretty fashionable. And if you're looking to grab a pair of wired earbuds on the cheap, you're in luck. That's because the Sennheiser IE 200 are $99.95 (was $159.95) in the US and just £81.69 (was £129.99) in the UK, thanks to the Amazon Prime Day sales.
