The Sennheiser IE 200 are in-ear monitors (IEMs) that are ideal for audiophiles or musicians on a budget. They provide incredibly detailed, articulate audio for the price you pay, with clean and agile bass, well-defined mids, and precise treble — they truly are perfectly equipped to handle any genre. I've been using them regularly for two years now, I've seen no signs of wear or degradation, and I love using them when I want a more analytical, balanced listening experience.
The IE 200 use a 3.5mm connector, so they work great with laptops, MP3 players, and any phones that retain the now somewhat elusive headphone jack. But if you need something with a USB-C connector for your smartphone, then you're in luck — if you're in the UK that is. Because right now, you can snap up the spectacular Sennheiser CX 80U for £30.95 (was £34.99) at Amazon UK, which is very cheap for the best-sounding wired earbuds in their price-class.

I've been using the Sennheiser IE 200 for years, and they've never let me down. The level of detail they can unearth would be impressive enough at full price, so this deal makes them a true must-buy for audiophiles or musicians on a budget.
Today's best Sennheiser IE 200 deal in the UK
The Sennheiser IE 200 might just be some of my favorite IEMs ever made. That comes down to the fact that they provide such impressive levels of detail and insight while remaining highly affordable. So now, at less than £85, I would urge any audio enthusiast on a budget to scoop these up.
In my Sennheiser IE 200 review, I lauded the IEMs for their fantastic, balanced audio, great build quality, and ultra lightweight, comfortable feel. They also have a really discreet, understated look in use, rather than assuming the chunky form that a lot of IEMs go for.
As they're IEMs, you're not going to get that V-shaped EQ curve with super prominent bass and treble — these are designed for more faithful, critical listening. That's not to say that the low-end or highs lack impact — quite the opposite. They sound incredibly dynamic and expressive, but are simply tuned in a way that intricate mids aren't overshadowed. As a result, casual listeners and audiophiles alike will find plenty to love about the sound here.
Their excellent instrument separation gives plenty of room for every instrument in a mix to breathe, and if you're new to IEMs, you'll almost certainly be wowed by their ability to expose details you've never noticed in your favorite tracks. The IE 200 are a true value-for-money behemoth, so don't miss these impeccable deals that make them even more affordable.
Now, a quick word on the Sennheiser CX 80U for my fellow UK folk. If you want the flexibility of USB-C, then you may actually want to snap these up instead. The CX 80U sound phenomenal, with great balance across the frequency range, but especially strong clarity in the treble range. They also have a mic for taking phone calls, impressive noise isolation, and come with a range of different-sized eartips to help you find your perfect fit. You can read more about this deal down below.
Today's best Sennheiser CX 80U deal (UK only)
I take the Sennheiser CX 80U with me everywhere I go to use with my Nintendo Switch 2 or listen to tunes on my phone, and they continue to impress me no end. They offer amazing audio quality, with especially refined treble and instrument separation, plus the convenience of USB-C connectivity, and even a built-in mic for taking calls. In my view, there aren't any similarly priced USB-C earbuds that can compete with these.

articles.title: Pais usam ChatGPT para criar fotos escolares dos filhos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Pais usam ChatGPT para criar fotos escolares dos filhos
Famílias recorrem à inteligência artificial para fugir dos preços praticados por fotógrafos profissionais.
Pais nos Estados Unidos estão usando ferramentas de inteligência artificial para criar, em casa, retratos semelhantes às tradicionais fotos escolares dos filhos. A prática busca reduzir os gastos com os pacotes vendidos por fotógrafos profissionais, que podem ultrapassar US$ 100 (cerca de R$ 500) para famílias com mais de uma criança.
Segundo o site Futurism, alguns responsáveis estão fotografrando os filhos em casa para pedir que a IA reproduza o enquadramento e os fundos usados nas sessões feitas nas escolas. Os resultados são publicados em redes sociais como o TikTok.
As fotos escolares são uma tradição comum nos Estados Unidos, em que fotógrafos contratados pelas próprias instituições fazem retratos dos estudantes e oferecem os álbuns às famílias.
Entre os casos divulgados nas redes está o da criadora Carlie Bond, que fotografou os três filhos contra uma parede lisa e enviou as imagens ao ChatGPT. No prompt, ela pede que a ferramenta matenha a aparência das crianças e adicione o fundo azul em degradê comum nesse tipo de retrato. “Fotos escolares para três crianças? Nesta economia?”, escreveu na publicação.
 @carlieb0nd School pictures x3 kids?? In this economy? 😂 So we took our own and let my good friend Chat help us out 🤭 And honestly… I’m not mad about how they turned out 😂 #SchoolPictures #MomHack #MomOfFour #ChatGPT #MomLife ♬ Bow Bow Bow – Zeddy Will 
Os comentários da postagem de Bond se dividem entre pais que relatam os mesmos gastos elevados e que outros pontuam os riscos de usar imagens das crianças no chatbot. Para os últimos, usar as mesmas imagens em fundo branco e edita-las em ferramentas de edição, como o Canva (que permite gerar uma imagem de fundo, por exemplo), seria uma opção melhor.
No Brasil, a tendência chegou para momentos mais tardios, como fotos de formatura da universidade, pelo mesmo motivo: o preço. Para alguns usuários, a ferramenta virou uma oportunidade para recriar o momento e enviar para familiares que não puderam estar presentes.
Além de produzir novas imagens, alguns usuários estão recorrendo às ferramentas para retirar marcas d’água das prévias fornecidas pelos fotógrafos. Segundo o site Dexerto, há casos de pais usando IAs para apagar as marcas e obter as fotografias sem pagar.
Aqui, é importante pontuar que a prática pode configurar violação de direitos autorais. Os próprios modelos de IA, no entanto, costumam barrar a geração desse tipo de imagem: o ChatGPT geralmente avisa que não pode remover a marca d’água poir “apagaria uma identificação de direitos autorais”, e sugere a geração de uma imagem parecida, seguindo a mesma proposta.
Em todo caso, alguns dos vídeos também mostram limitações no uso da IA para recriar os retratos. Alguns pais relatam que os modelos modificam características do rosto das crianças mesmo após receberam comandos para preservar a aparência — algo comum em modelos de imagem desde que se tornaram populares.

articles.title: Oubliez votre barre de son : Orange veut la remplacer avec sa nouvelle box Dolby Atmos
articles.text:
Oubliez votre barre de son : Orange veut la remplacer avec sa nouvelle box Dolby Atmos
Et si votre prochain système home cinéma était… votre box TV ? Avec son nouveau Décodeur Home Cinéma, Orange intègre directement un système audio 3.1 dans un boîtier compact, compatible Dolby Atmos et pouvant être complété par des enceintes arrière sans fil. Une solution tout-en-un ambitieuse, pour l’instant réservée aux abonnés Livebox Max.
Orange vient de dévoiler son tout nouveau Décodeur Home Cinéma. Loin des formats ultra-compacts actuellement proposés par l’opérateur français, cette box TV se distingue par l’intégration d’un système audio conçu pour restituer les bandes-son de tous types de contenus audiovisuels, dans une logique d’appareil tout-en-un.
Orange transforme son décodeur en système home cinéma
Le principe d’intégrer des haut-parleurs au sein d’un décodeur n’est pas nouveau. L’exemple le plus probant reste la Freebox Delta, lancée en 2018 et arrêtée récemment, qui intégrait une architecture acoustique signée Devialet. Orange n’en est pas non plus à son coup d’essai dans le home cinéma : l’opérateur s’était déjà illustré dans ce domaine en 2017, mais avec une barre de son baptisée Cabasse for Orange, commercialisée en complément du décodeur.
Orange revient aujourd’hui avec l’ambition de démocratiser le son home cinéma en l’intégrant à un appareil déjà largement présent dans les foyers. À l’inverse de son concurrent Free, l’opérateur a fait le choix de s’éloigner le moins possible du format d’un boîtier TV traditionnel, malgré l’intégration d’un système audio.
Un boîtier compact qui embarque une configuration 3.1 canaux
À peine plus gros que les boîtiers actuellement proposés, le Décodeur Home Cinéma d’Orange ne dépasse pas 20 cm de large. À titre de comparaison, le Player Devialet se rapprochait davantage des dimensions d’une enceinte, avec ses 43 cm d’envergure. Malgré cette compacité, pensée pour ne pas dépayser les utilisateurs de décodeurs traditionnels, l’appareil revendique une configuration 3.1.
Derrière le tissu acoustique qui enveloppe son châssis, on retrouve un woofer dédié aux basses, deux haut-parleurs large bande latéraux et une voie centrale destinée à renforcer l’intelligibilité des voix. Orange indique avoir confié la conception acoustique de ce décodeur au spécialiste danois Bang & Olufsen, qui se serait chargé à la fois de l’optimisation matérielle et du réglage sonore.
Dolby Atmos au programme, avec des enceintes arrière sans fil
Côté formats, Orange met en avant la prise en charge des bandes-son tridimensionnelles Dolby Atmos. Malgré l’absence de canaux verticaux dédiés, le décodeur est capable de décoder ce format seul. Pour renforcer la sensation de bulle sonore, Orange a toutefois développé des enceintes satellites arrière optionnelles. Très compactes et de forme ovoïde, celles-ci intègrent un haut-parleur frontal ainsi qu’un second orienté vers le plafond pour reproduire les effets aériens.
Ces satellites communiquant sans fil avec le décodeur grâce à la technologie Dolby Atmos FlexConnect, ils n'ont besoin que d’une prise secteur pour fonctionner. À noter qu’Orange a opté pour une version propriétaire de ce protocole de diffusion Dolby et n’autorise donc pas le jumelage d’enceintes satellites d’autres marques. Dommage, puisque FlexConnect a initialement été présenté comme une technologie permettant de constituer un système Dolby Atmos à partir d’appareils de différents fabricants.
Hélas, l’ajout d’un caisson de basses n’est pas prévu. Une absence qui pourrait se faire sentir dans les pièces de grande taille, notamment en raison de la compacité du décodeur.
Diffusion musicale depuis un smartphone, tous les services d’Orange, etc.
À l’instar d’une barre de son, le Décodeur Home Cinéma d’Orange permet également de diffuser de la musique depuis un smartphone, en Bluetooth ou en Wi-Fi via Google Cast. La connexion au téléviseur s’effectue simplement via un port HDMI eARC. En revanche, le décodeur ne dispose ni d’une entrée HDMI supplémentaire pour accueillir une source externe, ni d’une sortie optique.
Comme n’importe quel décodeur TV moderne, le Décodeur Home Cinéma conserve l’ensemble des services classiques attendus d’une box Orange. Il donne accès aux chaînes de télévision, au replay des principales chaînes ainsi qu’aux services de streaming, avec les principales plateformes préinstallées. Les utilisateurs peuvent également télécharger d’autres applications et jeux depuis le Google Play Store.
Un décodeur réservé aux abonnés Livebox Max
Le Décodeur Home Cinéma ne vient pas remplacer gratuitement les décodeurs existants sur l’ensemble des offres Orange : il est pour l’heure réservé aux abonnés Livebox Max. L’offre est facturée 47,99 € par mois pendant les 12 premiers mois pour les nouveaux clients, puis 57,99 € par mois. Un tarif qui reste inchangé malgré l’arrivée de ce nouveau décodeur haut de gamme.
Le décodeur est proposé aussi bien aux nouveaux abonnés qu’aux clients Orange déjà abonnés à Livebox Max. Son activation est facturée 50 € pour une nouvelle souscription et 40 € pour les clients existants souhaitant remplacer leur décodeur actuel. Les deux enceintes surround proposées en option nécessitent quant à elles 80 € de frais d’activation.
Bien qu’étant la plus chère du catalogue, la Livebox Max reste l’offre la plus généreuse d’Orange en matière de divertissement, avec notamment une remise de 5 € par mois sur certaines plateformes de streaming partenaires. Le nouveau décodeur vient ainsi compléter une formule déjà pensée pour les gros consommateurs de contenus audiovisuels, en faisant de l’expérience TV et audio l’un de ses principaux arguments.

articles.title: Ces prétendus services d’OpenAI, Google ou Anthropic dissimulent une fausse fenêtre de navigateur pour siphonner vos identifiants
articles.text:
Des chercheurs en cybersécurité ont découvert une vaste plateforme de phishing grimée en faux services ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude ou Perplexity. Son arme principale : une fausse fenêtre de navigateur capable de faire passer un site frauduleux pour une page de connexion légitime.
Les campagnes de phishing n’ont pas attendu longtemps pour exploiter l’engouement autour de l’IA. Les chercheurs d’Island ont remonté la trace d’un dispositif utilisé pour créer toute une série de faux services aux couleurs des grands noms du secteur. Le dernier, Muse Ads, est apparu huit jours seulement après l’annonce de Muse par Meta. Derrière ces façades se cache pourtant le même système, pensé pour voler identifiants et codes MFA.
La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise
Votre petite entreprise a de grandes ambitions. Protégez-là contre les pirates. Et développez sereinement votre activité !
Derrière ces faux outils IA, un navigateur qui n’en est pas un
Les sites repérés par Island se présentent comme de nouveaux outils destinés aux professionnels de la publicité : gestion de campagnes, analyse des dépenses, connexion à Google Ads ou Meta. Tous mènent vers le même bouton « Connect », qui invite la victime à relier son compte Google ou un autre service professionnel. Le clic semble ouvrir une fenêtre de connexion classique, avec le logo du fournisseur, un cadenas et une barre d’adresse pouvant afficher accounts.Google.com.
Sauf que Google ne s’est jamais ouvert. La fenêtre entière a été dessinée à l’intérieur de la page frauduleuse. Cette technique, appelée Browser-in-the-Browser, ou BiB, consiste à reproduire l’apparence d’un vrai navigateur pour faire croire à une redirection vers un domaine légitime. Les attaquants adaptent même le décor à Chrome, Safari, Windows, macOS, iOS ou Android.
L’indice le plus parlant reste la véritable barre d’adresse du navigateur : elle n’a jamais quitté le site de phishing. Celle qui affiche Google à l’intérieur de la page n’est qu’un élément graphique, tout comme le cadenas qui l’accompagne.
L’attaque peut ensuite évoluer au fil de la connexion. Island a découvert qu’un opérateur pouvait suivre la victime et choisir ce qu’elle verrait ensuite. Si Google réclame un code d’authentification, le faux site peut demander ce même code. Si le mot de passe échoue, l’attaquant peut afficher une erreur et en réclamer un autre tout en conservant les saisies précédentes. La plateforme sait aussi reproduire des demandes de validation Google ou Okta. Les chercheurs disent avoir observé des centaines de transmissions de données vers la plateforme pendant leur enquête.
Le dispositif ne sert d’ailleurs pas qu’à usurper des services IA. Island a relié le même système à des pages de remboursement frauduleuses ainsi qu’à de faux sites de recrutement imitant entre autres Tesla, Nike ou Louis Vuitton, dont plusieurs communiquaient avec le même serveur.
Comment repérer le piège et protéger ses comptes
Avant de saisir vos identifiants dans une fenêtre de connexion, vérifiez toujours la véritable barre d’adresse du navigateur. Un site peut imiter un cadenas, une URL ou l’interface de Google dans une fenêtre intégrée à la page, mais il ne peut pas modifier l’adresse réelle de l’onglet.
Pour accéder à un nouveau service, une bêta ou une intégration, passez toujours directement par le site officiel de l’éditeur plutôt que par un lien reçu par mail ou dans une invitation. Vous pourrez ainsi vérifier que la fonction existe bien et éviter de remettre vos identifiants à une copie frauduleuse.
Gardez aussi en tête qu’une double authentification classique ne bloque pas forcément ce type d’attaque. Un code reçu par SMS ou généré par une application peut être récupéré puis utilisé immédiatement par l’attaquant. Les passkeys et les clés de sécurité matérielles offrent une protection plus solide, car elles vérifient le véritable domaine avant d’autoriser la connexion.
Enfin, si vous pensez avoir saisi vos identifiants sur une page frauduleuse, changez votre mot de passe sans attendre, déconnectez les sessions ouvertes et vérifiez les appareils, administrateurs, méthodes de récupération et accès récemment ajoutés à votre compte. Pour un compte publicitaire, contrôlez également les campagnes et dépenses récentes.

articles.title: Cisco broadens agentic features in Webex collaboration platform - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cisco broadens agentic features in Webex collaboration platform
Cisco Systems Inc. today detailed a broad expansion of its Webex collaboration portfolio that brings artificial intelligence agents into team conversations, connects office technology with workplace management and enables customer-service agents to continue working after an interaction ends.
Introduced at WebexOne in Austin, Texas, the updates extend Cisco’s strategy of integrating people, AI agents and enterprise information. The company is positioning such shared context as the foundation for software that can coordinate tasks across applications and carry decisions beyond meetings.
“Agents are entering the workforce at an unprecedented pace, both to help you and operating by themselves,” said Snorre Kjesbu, Cisco’s senior vice president and general manager of collaboration. “Connected intelligence goes from people to people but also people to AI and AI to AI.”
The announcements span Webex software, meeting-room hardware, and customer experience, with most new features and products planned for early 2027.
The redesigned Webex (pictured) provides a personalized view of upcoming meetings, calls and priorities, drawing on calendars, messages and ongoing workflows. Agents can participate in spaces, meetings and calls and help teams schedule conversations, take notes, translate and complete tasks.
Cisco also announced plans to bring Anthropic PBC’s Claude into Webex through Claude Managed Agents. The integration is intended to support analysis, content generation and coordinated actions using context derived from team interactions. Separately, a Model Context Protocol integration will bring Webex information into OpenAI Group PBC’s Dots agents, with plans to make Dots available inside Webex as a personal agent.
“People and agents working together is how collaboration is going to be done going forward,” said Amit Barave, vice president and general manager for Cisco’s Webex Suite and AI.
New personal agents can answer when users are busy, assess a caller’s request and urgency, then help schedule a follow-up or send a message. An AI coach, initially appearing in Webex’s Vidcast video recorder, will provide feedback on recorded presentations, including pacing, tone and unnecessary verbiage.
Knowledge integration
Cisco is also introducing Dialog, a software layer beneath its Webex AI Agent platform that connects customer history with enterprise systems, knowledge and policies. The aim is to replace disconnected service interactions with agents that maintain an understanding of a customer over time.
Dialog supports extended task execution, allowing an agent to coordinate with employees, other agents and backend systems until a customer’s request is resolved. It retains context across channels and learns from customer outcomes and employee judgment within enterprise policies. Cisco anticipates beta availability in the first quarter of 2027.
“We are moving away from a world where we build agents to where we train and onboard agents like digital co-workers,” said Vinod Muthukrishnan, a Cisco executive who leads Webex customer experience operations.
Rather than requiring organizations to construct individual conversation flows, Cisco says Dialog can onboard agents using existing conversations, policies and operating procedures. It is designed to support both Cisco and third-party agents.
Cisco executives said that broader scope also expands the need for oversight. “We are talking about securing, observing and governing an entire execution chain that starts with the conversation and goes well into the enterprise,” Muthukrishnan said.
Cisco is expanding its AI Agent 360 control plane and management platform with observability based on its Splunk technology to connect agent behavior with operational data, including escalation patterns and business impact. General availability is planned for December. Cisco AI Defense provides security capabilities, while additional integrations connect customer-service agents with Google LLC, Nvidia Corp. and Amazon Web Services Inc. technologies.
Cisco is also extending AI to customers that retain on-premises communications systems. Webex AI Agent is generally available for Cisco’s Unified Contact Center Enterprise, with voice support for Contact Center Express planned this month. A separate integration layer, expected in early 2027, will let organizations host third-party AI models locally to meet data sovereignty and compliance requirements.
Design help
For physical offices, Cisco’s Workplace Designer expands planning from individual meeting rooms to floors, buildings and campuses. Organizations can import floor plans and receive recommendations for room configurations, wireless infrastructure and collaboration devices.
Cisco’s Cloud Control unified operations management platform will bring together networking, collaboration and security management. Workplace data can help IT and facilities teams understand utilization, investigate service problems and decide whether existing space meets their needs. Cisco’s AI Canvas combines workspace and device intelligence with network insights to support investigations across systems.
RoomOS 27, scheduled for November availability, adds AI capabilities and native Google Meet support alongside existing meeting-platform options. Its director agent coordinates cameras, microphones and speakers, using Nvidia acceleration for contextual noise removal. Smart Room Assurance helps teams calibrate equipment and monitor room performance.
The new Cisco Ceiling Speaker Pro completes the company’s integrated audio architecture. It works with ceiling microphones and cameras to locate speakers and distribute their voices around a room. A single Ethernet connection carries power, audio and control, while automatic configuration reduces setup work. Cisco expects to make the speaker available for order later this quarter.
“With spatially aware voice lift, we know where the voice is coming from, and we intelligently distribute it where it’s needed in the room,” said Espen Løberg, vice president and general manager of Cisco’s collaboration devices business. “We’re not just making the room louder. We’re making the conversation more natural.”

articles.title: El nuevo peligro de la IA: un agente puede engañar a otro para que robe información
articles.text:
La expansión de los agentes de inteligencia artificial (IA) dentro de las empresas está abriendo una nueva puerta para los ciberdelincuentes. Investigaciones recientes muestran que un atacante puede manipular a uno de estos sistemas para que transmita instrucciones maliciosas a otros agentes de una misma organización y consiga acceso a información confidencial, bases de datos o recursos internos.
El problema fue identificado durante los últimos cinco meses en organizaciones como JPMorgan Chase, Rapid7, Weaviate y organismos gubernamentales de Francia. Aunque estas entidades no tienen una relación directa, todas utilizan agentes de IA conectados entre sí para ejecutar tareas de manera automática.
La técnica aprovecha una debilidad sencilla de explicar: un agente de IA puede confiar demasiado en otro agente. Si uno recibe una instrucción maliciosa y la transmite como si fuera una tarea legítima, el siguiente sistema puede ejecutarla sin comprobar suficientemente su origen.
Cómo funciona el ataque contra los agentes de IA
Para entender el riesgo, hay que imaginar una empresa en la que varios empleados especializados trabajan en cadena. Uno analiza documentos, otro consulta una base de datos y un tercero prepara un informe. Si uno de ellos recibe una orden falsa y los demás confían en él, el atacante puede aprovechar esa relación para avanzar dentro de la organización.
Algo similar ocurre con los agentes de IA. Estos sistemas utilizan herramientas y protocolos para comunicarse entre sí. Uno de ellos puede recibir una solicitud, pedir información a otro agente y posteriormente utilizar esa respuesta para completar una tarea. El problema aparece cuando los controles de seguridad no verifican adecuadamente cada instrucción que circula entre ellos.
El investigador independiente Syed Anas Mohiuddin analizó sistemas utilizados por varias organizaciones y encontró fallos relacionados con MCP, siglas de Model Context Protocol. Este estándar permite que aplicaciones y agentes de IA se conecten con herramientas, bases de datos y otros servicios.
Mohiuddin bautizó esta estrategia como “pivote de protocolo”. El término describe ataques en varias etapas en los que un ciberdelincuente entra por un sistema y aprovecha la confianza existente entre diferentes protocolos para llegar a otro recurso que inicialmente no estaba expuesto.
Google encontró una vulnerabilidad de gravedad alta
Uno de los casos más relevantes apareció en una herramienta de Google para conectar agentes de IA con bases de datos. La vulnerabilidad recibió una puntuación de gravedad de 8 sobre 10 y estaba relacionada con la forma en que el sistema gestionaba determinadas direcciones web y redirecciones.
Un atacante podía manipular un parámetro para conseguir que la herramienta enviara solicitudes a un servicio interno. En otras palabras, un sistema que debía comunicarse con recursos autorizados podía ser inducido a contactar con otro punto de la red.
Google corrigió el problema mediante controles destinados a impedir que el sistema acceda a direcciones IP no permitidas.
Otro caso descubierto en Rapid7 recibió una puntuación mucho menor, de 2,7 sobre 10, y ya fue solucionado por la compañía.
El problema es la confianza entre sistemas
Los investigadores advierten que estos ataques resultan especialmente difíciles de detectar porque cada agente puede estar haciendo exactamente aquello para lo que fue diseñado. El primero recibe una instrucción, el segundo la interpreta como una tarea legítima y el tercero ejecuta una acción autorizada.
Para el sistema, no necesariamente existe una señal evidente de que se está produciendo un ataque.
El riesgo también cuestiona una de las ideas fundamentales de la seguridad informática moderna: la confianza cero, un modelo que parte de la premisa de que ningún dispositivo o sistema debe considerarse seguro automáticamente, incluso cuando se encuentra dentro de una red corporativa.
Los expertos recomiendan aplicar ese mismo principio a los agentes de IA. Cada instrucción que pase de un modelo a una herramienta debería ser revisada como si procediera de una fuente externa y potencialmente peligrosa.
El crecimiento acelerado de los agentes de IA está haciendo que empresas y organismos conecten cada vez más sistemas entre sí. La investigación muestra que esa interconexión puede aumentar la productividad, pero también crear nuevas rutas para los ataques si los mecanismos de autorización y seguridad no evolucionan al mismo ritmo.

articles.title: Researcher ports Doom to $8,000 Hasselblad X2D — 100-mp medium-format camera uses touchscreen for directional control, shutter button to fire weapon
articles.text:
Researcher ports Doom to $8,000 Hasselblad X2D — 100-mp medium-format camera uses touchscreen for directional control, shutter button to fire weapon
The latest version of this professional camera costs nearly $8,000.
An independent camera researcher experimenting with the firmware for expensive camera brands like Hasselblad and Ricoh just built software that lets photographers play Doom directly on the X2D. This feature is part of the Hasselblad-X-System-CIM-Firmware-Research-Feature-Extensions repository on GitHub, which also experiments with capabilities that factory units don’t come with. The creator, Radium Wang, says that this only contains source code, offline tools, tests, and sanitized research findings, and it seems that it’s not meant to “level up” the expensive camera.
This isn’t the first time that someone installed Doom on a camera, as we saw another GitHub programmer do the same on the other end of the price spectrum a couple of months ago. That project brought the game to an entry-level DSLR from 2010 with an 18-megapixel sensor. This makes that camera the polar opposite of the Hasselblad X2D series, which costs thousands of dollars and is designed for professional photographers with its 100-megapixel resolution. Both projects highlight just how powerful embedded systems have become, to the point where even digital cameras can now run a complete game.
When id Software launched the game in 1993, its minimum system requirements were an Intel 386 processor, 4 MB RAM, and a VGA graphics card. These requirements often meant a desktop PC that looked like this Retro95 beige PC from Maingear, with its massive footprint and accompanying 13-inch CRT monitor. However, technological advances have made it so that even the most unlikely gadgets are now capable of running the landmark FPS title. In fact, “Can it run Doom?” has now become a meme and a running joke among tech enthusiasts, with programmers taking up the challenge of porting the game to the weirdest of devices. Some of the weirder examples that we’ve seen recently include an electric cooking pot, an orbiting satellite from the European Space Agency, and even an Apple Lightning-to-HDMI dongle.
Playing Doom on a tiny 3.6-inch touchscreen isn’t exactly fun, especially as the medium-format camera form factor does not lend well to gaming. However, gaming on cameras isn’t actually the point of this and other similar projects; instead, it’s the achievement of making something run somewhere unexpected. Now, if you happen to have an extra Hasselblad lying around in your house and don’t mind experimenting on your expensive equipment, you can take part in the joke by downloading this repo and following Wang’s instructions to reproduce the “research.”

Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.

articles.title: Aston Martin puts back-end AI to work - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Aston Martin puts back-end AI to work while keeping agents off its website
Back-end AI gives manufacturers opportunities to improve operations, but choosing where to apply it requires attention to business value. For Aston Martin Lagonda Ltd., that means evaluating operational use cases while preserving its personalized customer experience.
That decision is sharper for a carmaker selling handcrafted, highly personalized vehicles. Infor LLC is pushing industry-specific AI agents into operational workflows, and one longtime automotive customer sees the payoff starting with Infor’s CloudSuite Automotive tool, according to Steve O’Connor (pictured, right), chief information officer of Aston Martin.
“We get all of the new features, new capabilities almost as soon as they’re released,” he said. “That’s literally unheard of in an [enterprise resource planning] land where you’re normally doing massive transformational programs, upgrades and stuff, as well.”
O’Connor and Max Fisher (left), director of product management at Infor, spoke with theCUBE’s Christophe Bertrand and Alison Kosik at Infor Velocity Week, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed keeping AI out of the customer-facing experience and practical governance for scaling back-end AI use cases. (* Disclosure below.)
Balancing business value and governance in back-end AI
Aston Martin screens every AI idea first for its effect on profit and loss, then for efficiency gains, O’Connor explained. Its operational use cases include back-end systems such as configure-price-quote.
“We’re AI delayers, not deniers. We don’t want to be the people that make the big mistake and make a lot of investment in the wrong thing,” he said. “You will never see an AI agent on the front end of an Aston Martin website because that’s not the experience the customers want.”
More than half of businesses struggle to scale AI, according to Infor research. Its AI Adoption Hub builds each customer’s roadmap from public filings, meeting transcripts and known problems, and use cases now take weeks rather than quarters, Fisher explained.
“If it’s only two to three weeks, learning that lesson … could be worth that [time], and you’re on to the next one,” he said. “If it was three or four years ago, it would take six months, two quarters, three quarters to get a use case done.”
Value can fade once a use case ships. Aston Martin assigns a person in the business to own each AI agent’s outcomes, and O’Connor urges leaders building AI on top of ERP to fix their data and processes first.
“We implemented a large governance framework,” O’Connor said. “What that did was stifle innovation. This AI by its very nature is innovation in a box, in a nutshell.”

articles.title: Elon Musk l'assure, Starlink assurera la connectivité "dans tout le Système solaire et au-delà"
articles.text:
Starlink ne veut pas seulement connecter la Terre entière à Internet. L’un de ses dirigeants vient de dévoiler un plan XXL pour la constellation de satellites, qui doit englober, à terme, « le Système solaire ».
Michael Nicolls, vice-président de Starlink, a pris la parole à Antalya, en Turquie, lors du Congrès international d’astronautique. Et à la fin de son intervention, il a rappelé que l’objectif de SpaceX était d’« étendre la conscience au-delà de cette planète », une formule qui rappelle évidemment celles du P.-D.G. Et cela doit aussi passer par Starlink.
D’abord la Lune, puis Mars
Ainsi, Nicolls a révélé que l’entreprise développait déjà des systèmes de connexion « à très haut débit » basés sur des lasers afin de « connecter la Lune avec une constellation ». Pas si étonnant, lorsque l’on sait que la NASA ambitionne d’implanter une base sur la Lune, et que SpaceX est l’un de ses partenaires privilégiés.
De même, Elon Musk a déjà étayé ses plans pour construire une véritable ville « autonome » sur notre satellite, et cela passera évidemment par la mise en place d’un réseau sans fil fonctionnel. Mais ce n’est pas tout, et le dirigeant a évidemment mentionné Mars, où SpaceX ambitionne de bâtir une colonie d’1 million d'habitants.
« Ensuite, nous relierons Mars, et nous formerons un maillage interplanétaire de connectivité. Ce réseau reposera essentiellement sur les mêmes technologies que celles sur lesquelles nous travaillons avec Starlink », a poursuivi Michael Nicolls. Pour rappel, Blue Origin s'est vue confier par la NASA la mission de mettre en place un réseau de télécommunications martien, un effort sur lequel Rocket Lab travaille également. Le début d’une concurrence acharnée ?
Elon Musk valide
Des propos rapidement adoubés par Elon Musk en personne. Sur X.com, l’homme le plus riche du monde a écrit que « SpaceX assurera la connectivité dans tout le Système solaire et au-delà ». Ces prédictions sont, pour l’heure, à prendre avec des pincettes, car l’entrepreneur est coutumier des annonces excessivement optimistes. Les premiers acheteurs du Tesla Roadster peuvent en témoigner.
Pour sa part, Michael Nicolls explique que pour parvenir à ce résultat, il faut continuer à améliorer la sécurité en orbite basse, alors que la multiplication des satellites pose de sérieuses questions sécuritaires.

Jours Flash d’Amazon : cette batterie externe 5 étoiles est presque à moitié prix jusqu’à ce soir
Besoin d’une réserve d’énergie suffisante pour faire le plein d'un ordinateur, une tablette et un smartphone ? La Ugreen Nexode 25000 mAh 145 W profite des dernières heures des Jours Flash Prime d'Amazon pour tomber à un tarif rarement vu.
Habituellement affichée à 90 €, la Ugreen Nexode 25000 mAh 145 W est proposée à 49 € chez Amazon jusqu’à ce soir. Une baisse de 40 € qui rend cette batterie externe haut de gamme particulièrement séduisante, d’autant qu’elle a obtenu 5 étoiles lors de notre test. Si elle vous faisait de l’œil, mieux vaut donc ne pas trop tarder, car l’offre touche à sa fin à minuit.
UGreen 25000 mAh Nexode Power Bank
Cette Nexode ne manque pas d’arguments pour les utilisateurs très équipés. Sa capacité annoncée de 25 000 mAh permet d’enchaîner les recharges loin d’une prise : lors de nos mesures, nous avons relevé 21 929 mAh réellement disponibles, soit de quoi recharger plus de quatre fois un Galaxy S24 Ultra ou environ cinq fois une Nintendo Switch. Elle peut aussi alimenter un ordinateur portable grâce à son port USB-C principal compatible Power Delivery 3.1, annoncé jusqu’à 140 W.
La connectique comprend deux USB-C et un USB-A, avec la possibilité de charger trois appareils en même temps. À deux en USB-C, elle peut répartir jusqu’à 100 W et 45 W, tandis que son petit écran indique clairement le niveau de batterie restant. Autre bon point : malgré sa grosse capacité, sa propre recharge ne demande qu’environ 1 h 23 avec un chargeur 65 W.
Il faut toutefois accepter ses 513 g, peu adaptés à une poche, et une capacité réelle légèrement inférieure à celle promise. Nos essais n’ont pas non plus dépassé 85 W en sortie dans notre protocole. Des réserves assez mineures face à son autonomie, sa polyvalence et sa rapidité — et encore plus à 49 € !

articles.title: Garmin Forerunner 165 para treinos está 42% mais barato no Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Garmin Forerunner 165 para treinos está 42% mais barato no Mercado Livre
Ideal para maratonas, Garmin Forerunner 165 com tela touchscreen, sensores de saúde e conexão Bluetooth fica com preço mais acessível com pagamento via Pix
O Garmin Forerunner 165 está disponível por R$ 1.599,90 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O smartwatch esportivo com tela AMOLED e GPS integrado, lançado por R$ 2.749, tem uma excelente queda no preço nesta oferta.
O Garmin Forerunner 165 possui uma tela AMOLED touchscreen de 1,2 polegada e caixa feita em polímero reforçado com fibra de 43 mm, pesando somente 39 gramas. O acessório ainda traz vidro reforçado e certificado de resistência à água de 5 ATM.
Indicado para maratonistas, o smartwatch inclui o Garmin Coach para criar treinos personalizados a partir de dados fornecidos por treinadores reais. A função é ideal para quem deseja se preparar para provas de 5 KM até meia maratona (21,1 KM), registrando a rotina de treinos e de recuperação.
Pensado para quem deseja captar todos os detalhes, o Garmin Forerunner 165 inclui um GPS integrado. Assim, é possível mapear trajetos, obter dados de tempo, distância, velocidade e ritmo em treinos na rua.
O smartwatch da Garmin conta com sensores de saúde que registram dados fora dos treinos, como frequência cardíaca, níveis de estresse, oxigênio no sangue e qualidade do sono. Essas informações ajudam o Garmin Coach a elaborar os planos de preparação para as provas.
Em relação à autonomia, o relógio traz uma bateria de até 11 dias no modo smartwatch. Esse tempo de uso cai para 19 horas ao ativar os recursos de saúde e o GPS para as atividades físicas.
Para o dia a dia, o Garmin Forerunner 165 (R$ 1.599,90 no Pix) conta com conexão Bluetooth que permite ser pareado com o Android e iPhone. Dessa forma, o usuário pode receber notificações, controlar mídias e até fazer pagamentos por aproximação com o Garmin Pay.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4: cómo jugar la campaña en acceso anticipado con Nvidia GeForce RTX
articles.text:
Los jugadores que cuenten con una PC equipada con una GPU GeForce RTX de Nvidia podrán acceder de forma anticipada a la campaña de Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 desde el 16 de octubre de 2026, siempre que hayan reservado el juego.
El título incorporará DLSS 4.5, una actualización de la tecnología de renderizado neuronal de Nvidia.
La campaña sitúa el conflicto en la península de Corea, tras una invasión a gran escala de Corea del Norte.
Un joven escuadrón de soldados surcoreanos intenta sobrevivir en líneas del frente que se desmoronan, mientras el capitán Price libra una guerra personal desde las sombras.
Nvidia también lanzó un nuevo controlador GeForce Game Ready con optimizaciones para Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen, la Sim Update 7 de Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, STAR WARS: Galactic Racer y Valor Mortis.
Los jugadores pueden descargarlo a través de la aplicación de Nvidia o desde el sitio web de la compañía.
Las funciones de DLSS 4.5 en Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
En todos los modos, DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution acelerará la jugabilidad y mejorará la calidad de imagen.
Los equipos con GeForce RTX serie 40 podrán utilizar DLSS 4.5 Frame Generation para aumentar las tasas de fotogramas, mientras que las GPU GeForce RTX serie 50 habilitarán Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, con una multiplicación de hasta 6x.
La función está pensada para maximizar el rendimiento al utilizar los reflejos opcionales con trazado de rayos.
Además, Nvidia Reflex podrá activarse en todos los sistemas GeForce RTX para reducir la latencia del PC y mejorar la respuesta del juego. El lanzamiento completo de Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 será el 23 de octubre de 2026.
Gears of War: E-Day ya está disponible con DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution, Frame Generation, Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, Nvidia Reflex, RTX Mega Geometry y trazado de rayos acelerado por hardware.
La precuela sigue a Marcus Fenix y Dom Santiago 14 años antes del Gears of War original, e incluye la campaña y los modos Horde Siege, PvE, y Versus, PvP. Con Multi Frame Generation 6x y trazado de rayos en Ultra, Nvidia indicó un aumento medio del rendimiento de 7,5x a 4K frente al renderizado nativo.
Otros juegos y actualizaciones con tecnologías RTX
Star Wars: Galactic Racer también ya está disponible con compatibilidad nativa para DLSS 4.5 Dynamic Multi Frame Generation y Super Resolution.
El juego de carreras ambientado en el Borde Exterior permite conducir landspeeders, motos speeder, skim speeders y pods en una campaña narrativa o en duelos multijugador.
Incorpora iluminación Lumen con trazado de rayos acelerado por hardware y DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction.
Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival se lanzará el 8 de octubre del mismo año con soporte para DLSS Super Resolution y Generación de Fotogramas.
El juego de acción y terror para un jugador, desarrollado por Saber Interactive y Boss Team Games, sigue a Aidan, quien debe usar los poderes de la Configuración Génesis para rescatar a su novia. Doug Bradley retomará el papel de Pinhead por primera vez en casi dos décadas.
A través de la aplicación de Nvidia, los jugadores podrán actualizar los modelos DLSS y añadir Generación Dinámica de Fotogramas con una multiplicación de hasta 6x.
Dynasty Warrior 3: Complete Edition Remastered ya está disponible e incluye DLSS Super Resolution con el modelo Transformer de segunda generación.
La reedición reúne Dynasty Warrior 3 yDynasty Warrior 3: Xtreme Legends, y permite jugar con más de 40 oficiales en batallas de uno contra mil recreadas con Unreal Engine 5.
La Sim Update 7 de Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 llegará el 13 de octubre de 2026. La actualización gratuita incorporará las Carreras Aéreas del Campeonato Nacional, mejoras del motor y la actualización a DLSS 4.5, además de Generación Multifotograma y Generación Multifotograma Dinámica de hasta 6x.
Por su parte, la expansión de pago Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen se lanzará el 9 de octubre con nuevas historias y encuentros en Norgan, el personaje de Eir, los misterios del inmortal Dragón Caído y 12 mazmorras.
La actualización gratuita Extended Operations de 007 First Light añadirá las misiones TacSim Valhalla Protocol y Jungle Heist, además de New Game+, armas, atuendos, intercambio de dispositivos, dificultad «00» y modo foto.
El juego es compatible con path tracing y DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction en PC con GeForce RTX y en GeForce NOW Ultimate.

articles.title: Why I upgraded to a 4K OLED PC gaming monitor — and why you should or shouldn’t
articles.text:
Why I upgraded to a 4K OLED PC gaming monitor — and why you should or shouldn’t
True blacks and infinite contrast, incredible colors, and burn-in?
4K OLED PC monitors have been out for years, but while some enthusiasts have made the move to OLED tech, some haven’t. Like any new technology, when the first OLED gaming monitor was released - the Alienware AW3423DW - it was expensive, with a launch price of $1,300, and it was price-prohibitive for an overwhelming majority of users. But compared to other PC gaming monitors (think VA and IPS-type panels), it was a Thanksgiving feast for the eyes. The LG UltraGear 32GS95UE, widely considered one of the first 4K OLEDs for gaming, was $1,400.
I eventually settled on the MSI MPG 321URX, which is currently $634 and, without a doubt, it's the best upgrade I’ve made to my system in a long time. There are a lot more affordable options available now, too: Models like the ASRock Phantom Gaming (PG032UFS) dual-mode 4K gaming monitor is on sale for $596, while the MSI 321UPX (similar to mine, but calibrated out of the factory) is $799. A year or so ago, the MSI was around $950, and the ASRock was over $1,000 in late 2025. So while sub-$700 is still a lot of money, prices have come down quite a bit on some quality panels. And while those offer the full-fat 4K resolution, there are even more affordable options if you're willing to step back to 1440p, like the Acer Predator X27U, for under $300.
I remember seeing them at CES and later walking past them in stores. The blacks were as black as could be, and the colors more vibrant than IPS panels. I recall thinking: "I have to have one." Then I looked at the price and walked away. Eventually, prices came down, and I upgraded, donating the 1440p IPS 165Hz panel to my kids, and I’ve been on a 4K OLED ever since. This article explains why I upgraded and offers advice on whether you should or shouldn't.
Why I upgraded to a 4K OLED monitor
Why I upgraded to a 4K OLED monitor
My journey to a 4K OLED started after seeing them at CES a few years ago, and more recently in stores. Seeing the deepest blacks and incredible colors was a sight to behold compared to my previous 27-inch 2560x1440 165Hz Acer Predator IPS panel, which many would consider a very good, fast IPS panel.
I worked on two 2560x1440 panels at my desk. On the left panel, I usually had video streaming, be it Hulu/news or Twitch, on one half of the monitor along with Chrome and several tabs ranging from personal email to a ‘scratch pad’ for work. On the right monitor, I had my ‘work Chrome’ on the right half (along with Slack), and I used the left area as free space to write articles in another Chrome tab and access File Explorer and other applications necessary for my job. This worked, but I quickly realized that I needed more screen real estate. I needed a higher resolution to fit more on the screen and a larger size so my old eyes could actually see what’s on the screen.
But I’m also a gamer at night. Generally, I'm an FPS (First-Person Shooter) guy playing titles like PUBG, Call of Duty, Battlefield 6, and more. Because I mostly play quick-twitch games, I need a high-refresh-rate monitor. Since I was already rocking 165Hz, the next natural upgrade for significantly higher refresh rates and lower display-related input lag was 240Hz. Sure, 180Hz variants are available, but I want a significant upgrade for something I will likely keep until it dies and cannot be replaced.
In the end, I upgraded to a 32-inch 4K OLED in early 2025 before RAM, video cards, and storage prices went nuts. The MSI MPG 321URX was $900 at the time (currently $634) and, without a doubt, the best upgrade I’ve made to my system in a long time. While I spent a pretty penny, not only was I able to get more screen real estate, both physically and in pixel count, but I also got true blacks and better color coverage (99% DCI-P3, 137% sRGB, aRGB 96%) than my IPS panel.
I also wanted to keep pixel density (Pixels Per Inch or PPI) the same or better. And if you do the math, the 27-inch 2560x1440 panel is about 109 PPI and, at least for my old eyes, I can’t see the pixels the way you could with, say, a 27-inch 1920x1080p monitor at a low 81 PPI. If we work out the 4K math on a 32-inch panel, that comes out to almost 138 PPI and even more dense than the 27-inch 1440p monitor.
Watching movies or videos in native 4K without scaling was an incredible experience. Seeing all the details and such bright, vibrant colors was such a drastic difference; I’m not sure I can ever go back. It also makes me thankful I’m not missing out in my living room, where it’s 90% movies and TV shows and around 10% console gaming (Xbox) and running an OLED TV (65” LG C4). The difference between these OLEDs and the 45” LCD TV in my bedroom is dramatic.
The refresh-rate bump was also game-changing. I'm lucky enough to have a GeForce RTX 5090, which is practically a necessity to drive a 240Hz high-refresh-rate OLED monitor and achieve frame rates well over 165 and close to the monitor's maximum refresh rate of 240 Hz. In some heavier titles, like Call of Duty, I need to enable DLSS to help reach that, or better, close to, that threshold, but it’s easier today with the RTX 5080 and, in some titles, the RTX 5070 Ti to reach higher frame rates than it was in the previous generations. Nvidia’s DLSS and MFG (Multi-Frame Generation) and AMD’s FSR have both come a long way (with Nvidia’s implementation being arguably better), so don’t be afraid to use them if needed.
Why should you upgrade?
Why should you upgrade?
The short answer: 4K UHD (3840x2160) gives you sharper pictures and more usable space. Whether you're playing games, watching movies, doing photo/video editing, or working in the office, you can now run multiple windows across the 3840-pixel width, and the higher PPI makes text look better (printed rather than rendered); finer details in pictures, games, and video are more visible. Streaming services also support 4K or 1080p, so you can avoid scaling and view content natively compared to a 2560x1440.
It’s also much easier to run today than it was a year or two ago. DLSS, FSR, MFG, and other upscalers let mid- to high-end video cards produce good frame rates at 4K without rendering each pixel natively. With these technologies from Nvidia and AMD, even if you enable this feature and run below native 4K, the upscaled result looks as good as, or sometimes even better than native 1440p. While you still need a fair amount of graphics horsepower to drive it, especially for high frame rates, it is easier using scaling technologies.
Today, 4K OLEDs are affordable enough that they're within reach of many more people than they were just two years ago. While they are still what I would consider a premium product, 4K panel prices have dropped and now sit in the realm of mainstream price points. In fact, you can buy a 32-inch 4K UHD 240Hz panel for under $700.
Models like the ASRock Phantom Gaming (PG032UFS) dual-mode 4K gaming monitor is $596, while the MSI 321UPX (similar to mine, but calibrated out of the factory) is $799. A year or so ago, the MSI was around $950, and the ASRock was over $1,000 in late 2025. So while sub-$700 is still a lot of money, prices have come down quite a bit on some quality panels.
Summary:
- You need more usable screen space for work or play
- Desire sharper pictures in games, movies, photo/video editing, office work
- True blacks, improved colors
- Easier to run than in years past - DLSS/MFG/FSR looks good and really improves frame rates
- Increasingly affordable - obviously affordable is in the eye of the beholder, but they are a lot cheaper today than even a year ago
- Burn-in has improved, too - While it’s still a concern over time, especially for static images like taskbars, manufacturers have implemented mitigations to prevent the phenomenon
Why you shouldn't upgrade
Why you shouldn't upgrade
There are several reasons to hold off on upgrading to a 4K 240Hz OLED monitor. One is that your current GPU may not keep up. Driving 240 FPS on a 4K monitor isn’t easy. And even with improvements and upscaling from both camps, you can’t make a budget card play like a flagship. Now, if you don’t play games, any video card will output 4K on an OLED, so this reason not to is only for the gamers.
I know burn-in is part of the reason to upgrade, and modern panels handle this better than early OLEDs, but it hasn’t disappeared. If your day is packed with spreadsheets and coding, or you use permanent taskbars/toolbars, those pixels stay in the same place all day. Dark modes and manufacturer mitigations help, but it’s the main risk. Check your warranty, as some brands cover burn-in (think Dell/Alienware, MSI, Corsair, Asus, LG, Acer), while others do not (Lenovo, budget/generic brands), and consider it ‘normal wear’. In short, if you work on static images a lot, you could see burn-in down the road.
Text can look slightly off depending on the panel type. If you work with a lot of text or spreadsheets, both OLED panel types can struggle with text clarity because they use non-standard subpixel layouts instead of the traditional RGB stripes. QD-OLED generally provides sharper overall rendering with ClearType enabled, while WOLED can look a bit hazy if the screen uses a matte coating. The good news is that the pixel density is so high, it’s harder to notice (I don’t on mine, and I write on it in a browser tab for 8+ hours a day).
Here again, we mentioned affordability in the why you should section, but it needs a place here too. For many users, $700+ is still prohibitively expensive. 1440p and 1080p OLED monitors cost much less.
If you’re an esports gamer, especially a competitive one, you likely need less real estate and higher frame rates. So choosing a 24-inch 240Hz+ 1080p IPS/VA panel is the best choice for users who want more FPS and less input lag than they do the highest contrast or saturated colors, for example.
Summary:
- You don’t have a powerful enough video card - If you don’t have an RTX 4080/5070 Ti or greater or AMD Radeon 9070XT, you may want to wait until your next graphics card upgrade. Or, if less than 240 FPS is OK, a lower-end card will work.
- If your day is packed with static images on the screen, burn-in can eventually become an issue, regardless of mitigation features from the panel or user.
- Text can look slightly off - Coming from someone who writes on their OLED daily, this isn’t a big issue, but it's worth noting just in case. The higher the pixel density, the less of an issue this is.
- It’s still expensive - Yeah, they are a lot cheaper than a year ago, but they are still costly. Prices will continue to drop.
- Esports gamer - You want a higher refresh rate and less real estate. Smaller, faster panels are ideal for this user.
OLED stands for Organic Light-Emitting Diode. It uses self-illuminating pixels that create their own light and can turn completely off. In other words, each LED creates its own color and, for black, turns off, creating infinite contrast compared to LCDs (IPS/VA/TN panels).
OLEDs have two subvariants, QD-OLED (Quantum Dot OLED) and WOLED (White OLED), and they differ in several ways, including how they generate light (WOLED: bottom emission; QD: top emission), their subpixel structure, and filtering. To summarize, WOLEDs generate white light from the bottom, which goes through four (RGBW) color filters, the backplane, and out. Whereas QD displays generate blue light and then turn it into green and red through a quantum dot layer.
What is OLED technology?
What is OLED technology?
What does all that mean? Without getting technical, it means QD-OLEDs excel in color volume and saturated highlights, with excellent color uniformity and tinting. WOLEDs offer the same benefits as traditional OLEDs (per-pixel control) but with an added advantage. Using a single white emitter with color filters means you don’t run into the problem of individual red, Green, and blue emitters aging at different rates, which can cause color shifting and burn-in. Now, WOLEDs don’t eliminate burn-in or image retention, but they can lessen the severity.
In the end, finding a bad OLED monitor is difficult, especially when you compare it to VA and IPS panels, since the contrast ratio, color volume, and response times put them in a league far above their IPS and VA counterparts. The biggest downside to any OLED panel is price (OLEDs cost more).
So what about the elephant in the OLED room, Burn-in? If you don’t know, burn-in is a phenomenon where the image on a monitor is retained and visible when other content is displayed. A good example is something static, like the ticker bar at the bottom of the screen or the Windows taskbar; these items tend to ‘burn in’ versus other areas of the panel that constantly change.
Over the years, this has improved. Most brands have mitigation features; for example, Philips (among others, like Samsung and MSI) uses pixel shifting technology to move displayed content one pixel up/down/left/right to reduce burn-in. MSI also uses pixel shifting, pixel refreshing, and OLED Care 3.0 to dim or turn off the screen when you step away. Each vendor has something to reduce it. Burn-in is real, but with today’s prevention features and a little bit of common sense from the user, it could take years to see anything visible on your screen, and something that I, so far, cannot see.
Tom’s Hardware’s own monitor expert, Brandon Hill, wrote a great article (WOLED vs QD-OLED monitors: which panel technology is better) covering the differences between OLEDs and which panel technology is better; it's absolutely worth a look if you want more detail on the panel types.
Takeaways
Takeaways
Jumping up from my 2560x1440 165Hz monitor to a 4K OLED at 240 Hz was, without a doubt, the best upgrade I made to my system in quite a while. For me, the awesome contrast and colors, plus the extra screen space, changed how I worked during the day and played games at night. Frankly, there’s no way I can go back. Prices, while still out of range for some, have come down considerably, and you can now get a 32-inch 4K 240Hz OLED panel for under $700. With upscaling tech like DLSS and FSR making it easier to run, you may not need a graphics card upgrade to reach your goals. If you want a sharper picture, more screen real estate, and a big jump in image quality, a 4K OLED is hard to beat.
That said, it isn’t for everyone. If your graphics card can’t keep up and your day is packed with static spreadsheets and toolbars, or the price is just too much ($700 is still a lot of money), you can wait or look at a 1440p OLED instead. You can find those, like the Acer Predator X27U, for under $300. If you’re a competitive esports gamer, a smaller, faster 1080p panel is likely the best choice. In the end, the price of entry was worth it for me. But affordability is in the eye of the beholder, so be honest with yourself about how you'll use it before you buy.

articles.title: Dell Technologies Drives the Agentic AI Era with New Windows PCs and Workstations
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
Dell Technologies Drives the Agentic AI Era with New Windows PCs and Workstations
Dell Technologies announces an expanded portfolio of Windows PCs and workstations built for the age of agentic AI. Together with NVIDIA and Microsoft, Dell delivers agentic AI across every stage of the creative and development journey, spanning a premium creator laptop, compact creator desktop and an AI workstation within the Windows environment.
NVIDIA RTX Spark comes to the XPS and Dell lineup for the first time, powering the new XPS 16 Creator Edition laptop and Dell Creator Edition Desktop. Paired with Windows, RTX Spark brings advanced AI, creative and gaming workloads together on a platform optimized for its performance. Dell Pro Precision with GB300 will be available on Windows, bringing always-on AI compute into the environment enterprise teams already depend on.Why it matters
A new generation of creators and developers has emerged, from enthusiasts pushing the limits of original workflows to enterprise AI teams deploying always-on agents. Both groups require compute that matches their workloads, available locally, continuously and without full cloud dependency.
Dell, NVIDIA and Microsoft bring that platform to life, delivering an agentic computing experience that redefines how consumers, creators and developers build, work and innovate.
Dell introduces XPS 16 Creator Edition, the first XPS laptop built for NVIDIA RTX Spark 
XPS 16 Creator Edition brings NVIDIA RTX Spark's superchip performance into a premium portable form factor, pairing studio-grade performance and display accuracy with local AI development, all within the meticulously engineered chassis XPS is known for.
At the heart of XPS 16 Creator Edition is the NVIDIA RTX Spark superchip, which unites NVIDIA AI, RTX graphics and unified memory in one slim, powerful Windows PC. The platform is designed to run larger AI models locally, without cloud dependency, while moving seamlessly between creative work, development and immersive gaming. Apps, tools and workflows connect into a single, cohesive experience that is private by default. RTX Spark brings NVIDIA's full-stack AI platform to the familiar, trusted Windows environment, ready for the AI workloads of today and whatever comes next.
The superchip itself combines up to a 6,144-core NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU, up to a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU and up to 128 GB of unified memory, all within a chassis just 17.8 mm thin. This unified memory architecture is what sets XPS 16 Creator Edition apart. CPU and GPU share a single large memory pool, so creators can work with massive 3D scenes, multi-layer 8K timelines and large AI models that would exceed the limits of a traditional discrete-GPU laptop. Dedicated hardware acceleration, including real-time ray tracing, DLSS and native 4:2:2 hardware encode/decode, delivers color-accurate, studio-grade editing and AAA gaming. All of it is wrapped in a CNC aluminium chassis that carries forward the craftsmanship XPS has stood for.
Studio-class display, engineered for accuracy
XPS 16 Creator Edition features a 3.2K tandem OLED display designed for professionals who depend on color accuracy. Key display capabilities include:
- VESA DisplayHDR True Black 600 with peak brightness up to 1,000 nits
- 100% DCI-P3 color gamut coverage
- Factory calibration to Delta E < 2 with Pantone Validation for professional-grade accuracy
- Tandem OLED technology, delivering higher brightness and lower power consumption than traditional OLED panels
- 20 to 120 Hz variable refresh rate, dynamically scaling from smooth 120 Hz motion for gaming and creative work down to 20 Hz for battery conservation during static viewing
Together, these features help ensure that what creators see on screen faithfully reflects their work.
Professional-grade connectivity
XPS 16 Creator Edition offers a full suite of ports designed to support high-end creative and professional workflows without relying on adapters or dongles:
- Full-size SDXC v7.1 card reader for fast, direct photo and video transfer from camera to laptop
- 3x USB4 Type-C ports with DisplayPort 2.1 and Power Delivery, supporting charging from any port and connection to multiple external displays
- HDMI 2.1b for high-definition video and audio output to up to three external displays
- Universal audio jack delivering lossless analog audio with zero latency, for professionals requiring the highest fidelity
Built for local AI development
XPS 16 Creator Edition is designed to meet the growing demand for local AI development and inference. The system includes the full NVIDIA CUDA stack, allowing developers to build and prototype on a single machine. With up to 128 GB of unified memory, users can prototype, fine-tune and run inference on the latest AI models locally, using the same architecture found in production AI environments, without cloud dependency.
Windows provides the platform foundation for this work, with built-in identity, containment, manageability and user controls that support running AI models and agents locally. Leading agentic and AI developer tools, including GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, ComfyUI and Cursor, now run across RTX Spark, making XPS 16 Creator Edition a purpose-built environment for AI-assisted development.
Broad software and gaming compatibility
RTX Spark Windows PCs support both native applications and x86 applications through Prism emulation. Leading creative applications, including Blender, DaVinci Resolve, Adobe Photoshop and Adobe Premiere, run natively, while additional applications such as MATLAB are supported through Prism. For gaming, Windows on RTX Spark supports anti-cheat solutions including Easy Anti-Cheat and BattlEye, as well as XBOX PC app support.
Dell Creator Edition Desktop, always-on agentic AI for the desktop
Dell Creator Edition Desktop brings the same NVIDIA RTX Spark superchip and up to 128 GB of unified memory as XPS 16 Creator Edition into a compact desktop built to run at full performance, continuously.
Freed from the thermal and battery limits of a laptop chassis, it sustains higher performance for longer renders, larger 3D scenes and extended AI training or fine-tuning runs, while local AI agents continue working in the background.
Like XPS 16 Creator Edition, the new desktop supports local AI development and broad application compatibility across creative, developer and gaming workloads. With up to 1 petaflop of FP4 computing power and support for AI models up to 200 billion parameters, users have the compute to take on their most ambitious creative and AI projects.
Dell unifies AI workstation portfolio under Dell Pro Precision
Dell Pro Max with GB10 and Dell Pro Max with GB300 are now Dell Pro Precision with GB10 and Dell Pro Precision with GB300. The rename brings these deskside workstations under the Dell Pro Precision brand, known for powering demanding professional workloads from complex simulations and massive datasets to advanced rendering, 3D modeling and AI development.
Dell Pro Precision with GB300, offering Windows for today's developer teams
Dell Pro Precision with GB300, will be available on Windows, putting advanced AI compute into the environment enterprises already manage. Organizations have traditionally depended on Linux for demanding AI workloads, while productivity, creative and engineering work primarily happens in Windows.
IT teams can deploy Dell Pro Precision with GB300 within existing Windows infrastructure, with no new group policies, operating system changes or workflow disruptions. Developers have a personal supercomputer at their desk to build and deploy powerful, always-on AI agents.
The workstation scales to 20 petaflops of FP4 compute and 748 GB of coherent memory on the NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, supporting models up to 1 trillion parameters locally with no cloud costs. Dell's exclusive MaxCool technology sustains that performance continuously with up to five times higher cooling efficiency.
With Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL), developers get full access to the NVIDIA CUDA ecosystem and Linux AI frameworks inside Windows, alongside their everyday applications with no dual boot or context switching required.
Perspectives
Rob Bruckner, president, Client Devices, Dell Technologies"AI is no longer something you build in the cloud and deploy later. It runs continuously, makes decisions and connects directly to the work people do every day. From a creator pushing the limits of a premium laptop to an enterprise team running always-on AI models at their desk, Dell, NVIDIA and Microsoft are delivering the compute to drive the agentic AI era."
Availability
XPS 16 Creator Edition laptop will be available in the U.S. for pre-order from Best Buy on October 7, and will be available on Dell.com soon after.
Dell Creator Edition Desktop is coming soon.
Dell Pro Precision with GB300 on Windows is coming soon.

articles.title: Arista takes Ethernet into the rack, and the network becomes the backplane - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Arista takes Ethernet into the rack, and the network becomes the backplane
Since its founding in 2004, it’s arguable that no network vendor has made better switches than Arista Networks Inc. That was true then and remains true, as its prowess in this area helped it ride the cloud boom and the artificial intelligence wave.
That model is changing as AI scales. Today, ahead of next week’s Open Compute Project Global Summit in San Jose, Arista announced an expansion of its AI network strategy from switches to rack scale.
Arista is launching an open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio covering both scale-up and scale-out AI fabrics, built with a large ecosystem of players such as Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Arm Ltd., Broadcom Inc., d-Matrix Corp., Meta Platforms Inc., Microsoft Corp. and Qualcomm Corp. The lead announcement is Etherlink SU-144, an Ethernet-based scale-up architecture that connects up to 144 accelerators, or XPUs, within a single-hop domain and up to 1,024 XPUs across racks. It is built on the Ethernet for Scale-Up Networking or ESUN initiative.
In the AI era, the network can no longer be thought of as an independent pipe moving data between servers. It has become a tightly integrated, rack-scale backplane, and how well it’s built determines how much value customers get from their compute. That’s a significant shift for a company whose identity has been built on the network as a distinct layer. But the network isn’t disappearing into the compute. Instead, the compute is being built around the network.
What Arista announced
The scale-up piece comes in three physical form factors, each designed for different use cases. During an analyst briefing, Vijay Vusirikala, Arista’s distinguished lead for AI systems and networks, walked through each one.
- Orthogonal chassis. Servers sit in front, and full-height switch cards in the back connect directly, with no backplane or cabling, drawing on Arista’s modular chassis heritage. It supports 100 to 400 kilowatts of liquid cooling. This is the design for vendors focused on training workloads that need the largest possible scale-up domain.
- Cabled backplane. Switches sit in the middle of the rack and connect to servers via copper cable cartridges. It is less dense but more serviceable, and it lets operators split bandwidth between intra-rack and inter-rack connections.
- Cross-rack. A dedicated switch rack connects separate accelerator racks. It is the most flexible design and the fastest to market because it avoids long co-engineering cycles, but it adds interconnect cost and power. “Copper runs out of juice very quickly,” Vusirikala said, so anything beyond two racks needs optics.
On the scale-out side, Arista offers liquid-cooled rack reference designs in eight-, 12- and 16-switch configurations, built around its 7060EX7 switches. Each delivers 102.4 terabits per second, plus fiber patch panels, cooling manifolds, drip trays with active leak detection, rack management controllers and power shelves with battery backup. Integration partners build, test and deliver the configured racks. The fabric supports Ultra Ethernet Consortium specifications, Multipath Reliable Connection resiliency, multi-plane routing and dynamic and cluster load balancing.
Customers can run Arista EOS or an open network operating system on the common Netdi foundation. Arista also said next-generation optics, including its XPO pluggables and open co-packaged and near-packaged optics, will increase rack capacity from 1.6 petabits per second to 6.5 petabits, cutting the data center footprint by nearly half.
Andy Bechtolsheim to present at OCP
The OCP Global Summit runs Oct. 12-15 in San Jose, and Arista will have a fully assembled liquid-cooled rack at its booth. This departs from the traditional engineering story at an Arista booth, focusing less on switching and more on manifolds, leak handling, fiber management and power. According to Arista’s OCP event page, co-founder and industry visionary Andy Bechtolsheim will present at 1 p.m. Oct. 13 on “The Gigawatt AI Data Center Era.”
Why this matters for Arista
Three takeaways emerged from the Arista announcement. First, Arista is targeting the one part of the AI network it hasn’t owned. It leads in scale-out and is pushing into scale-across, but scale-up has mirrored Nvidia’s NVLink market share. Arista was matter-of-fact that this won’t change for Nvidia-based systems anytime soon. “There is no near-term opportunity because that is proprietary,” Vusirikala told me.
The opportunity lies in non-Nvidia accelerators, and a partner list including AMD, Microsoft’s Maia, Qualcomm and d-Matrix shows that market is real. Arista is betting that heterogeneous compute will become the norm. This is wise for Arista, as there is plenty of opportunity for every vendor without trying to disrupt Nvidia’s seemingly undisruptable business.
Second, Arista is making the case for a single network stack across all three fabrics. These have historically been separate networks. Arista wants the same EOS, telemetry and diagnostics, regardless of whether the silicon underneath is shallow-buffer, deep-buffer, or low-latency. That’s a network-centric view rather than a compute-attached one, and it’s Arista’s strongest argument because fault isolation and predictive maintenance now extend into the most performance-sensitive part of the cluster.
Third, this is a reference architecture strategy, not a SKU launch, and it changes how infrastructure is delivered. Arista supplies the switches, software, designs and validation suites, while partners handle rack integration.
During the briefing, Arista Senior Product Line Manager Arihant Jain explained the importance of this. A 16-switch rack configuration can involve 2,000 fibers, and on-site cabling invites bend-radius violations, miswiring, signal-integrity problems, and dead optics. “The whole old approach of spare parts or things assembled at site has to change,” he said. Racks need to be integrated and tested upstream, then rolled into place. Liquid cooling forces the issue because switches, manifolds, and leak responses must be designed together.
Do you shut down a switch or a rack when a leak is detected, and does that decision tie into the building management system? These used to be facilities questions. They are now network questions.
The caution is that Nvidia’s turnkey stack remains Arista’s biggest obstacle and, in some ways, detracts from its Ethernet prowess. When customers buy a complete system, Ethernet doesn’t always come up. Open designs win on choice and economics, but they demand coordination among accelerator vendors, rack integrators and cooling suppliers.
Execution across that ecosystem will determine how quickly these land. Early buyers will be hyperscalers, neoclouds and AI infrastructure providers. Most enterprises will use these architectures through those providers rather than deploy them directly, at least for now.
Advice for network engineers
- Learn liquid cooling now. Arista expects roughly a 50-50 split between air- and liquid-cooled deployments for its current 100-terabit switches next year. Vusirikala said liquid cooling becomes effectively mandatory at 200 terabits per second. Removing fans alone cuts switch power by about 10%. Engineers who understand manifolds, leak detection and thermal design will be in demand.
- Think in racks, not boxes. Acceptance testing, sparing and troubleshooting shift when the rack is the product. Request rack-level validation data.
- Get fluent in scale-up. Scale-up was the server team’s problem. As Ethernet moves into that domain, it becomes the network team’s problem. Study ESUN, UEC, and features such as link-level retry and credit-based flow control.
- Keep optics options open. Arista said its customers are roughly split between next-generation pluggables and open CPO. Decide based on serviceability, power and your operational model.
- Protect operational consistency. One operating model across scale-up, scale-out and scale-across is worth more than a marginal performance gain.
- Question your AI providers. If you consume AI capacity from a neocloud or cloud provider, ask how its scale-up domains are built and how quickly failed racks are isolated. That affects the accelerator time you pay for.
The InfiniBand-versus-Ethernet debate in scale-out is largely settled. Arista is betting that the same economics hold one layer down, inside the rack. The competition is no longer about port speeds. It’s about who can roll in a validated rack and put expensive accelerators to work fastest. As accelerators diversify, the network that ties everything together becomes the platform, and that is precisely where Arista wants to be.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.
