articles.title: These 15 under-$50 gadgets have upgraded my tech life, and they're all on sale — some are even under $25
articles.text:
These 15 under-$50 gadgets have upgraded my tech life, and they're all on sale — some are even under $25
From M.2 cloners to screwdrivers, and travel-friendly tech accessories, these are affordable game-changers.
As much as I love high-priced tech like my potent RTX 4090-equipped custom gaming rig or the 65-inch LG OLED TV I use as my monitor, most of us can't spend several hundred dollars on a tech purchase or gift all the time. But you can still improve your tech life (or the lives of your friends and family) while spending a comparatively small amount of money.
I own all of the affordable devices listed below, and all are on sale for under $50. Some are even under $25! All of these products have made my tech-saturated world a little nicer in their own way. If you're looking for a small tech splurge for yourself during this deals season, or an affordable gift for that tech-savvy friend or family member, one of these $50-or-under options might be a good fit and a great deal.
My favorite sub-$50 deals
- Rosewill M.2 SSD Cloner: was $49, now $36
- Hoto Electric Screwdriver Kit: was $49, now $28
- 8BitDo Retro R8 Mouse with Charging Dock: was $49, now $39
Become an IT hero with Rosewill's M.2 SSD Cloner
Last year, a family member asked me for help with an older PC, which was trying to run Windows 10 and several programs on a cramped 110 GB SSD. At first, I figured I could clone the boot drive onto a more spacious drive so the OS and programs had more space to stretch out.
But the thought of using multiple USB enclosures or shuffling drives in and out of my desktop filled me with dread as I pictured being there for hours getting everything done and the system back up and running. So I looked into getting an M.2 SSD cloner and was surprised to see they can be found for less than $50.
With support for NVMe M.2 SSDs and offline cloning, this handy device makes it simple to move your files or OS from one drive to another. And with a 20 Gbps USB-C interface, it's also speedy in your OS of choice if you want to use software to clone or move your data between drives.
Read moreRead less▼
While I don't love the glossy plastic shell of Rosewill's model, it's one of the more affordable options. And it supports both NVMe M.2 drives and older AHCI models (Sorry, SATA). Using the cloner is pretty straightforward. You plug in the included USB-C power adapter, put your source drive in the left slot, the destination drive in the right slot, press the power button on the back, and a few logos light up, letting you know you're ready to go. Press the clone button on the top, and drive cloning will commence (provided your destination is the same size or larger than your source).
That's assuming you want to do an offline clone. But because I wanted to also resize the partition between the old 110 GB and the newer Team Group 512 GB SSD, I used the second included USB-C cable to connect the Rosewill cloner to my laptop and powered up the device. Within seconds, both drives were recognized in Windows, so I fired up the excellent free DiskGenius software, cloned the old partition to a new Team Group drive with a few clicks, and then used the software to drag the boot partition to the full size of the new drive. The whole process took just a few minutes, since the Rosewill cloner supports 20 Gbps USB, and I wasn't exactly copying a huge partition. 
When the cloning process was finished and the partition inflated, it was hard to believe it was all that easy. I had expected to be at the task for hours, but I was done in less than 30 minutes. Sure, unless you're in IT, a drive cloner might not be something you use regularly, but it's sure handy to have around. You could also use it to save some money by buying a laptop with a cramped SSD and swapping in something much roomier – provided, of course, the laptop's storage isn't soldered to the motherboard. 
The Rosewill cloner is also handy for just checking the contents of old M.2 drives you may have lying around. But if that's all you need, you can buy an NVMe enclosure or a single-drive dock. I also own a version of this model from Suitok, which costs $12.
This tiny, cheap, magnetic, USB-charging flashlight is great for PC building and other everyday tasks
I picked up the OLIGHT IMINI 2 mini flashlight last year on impulse because it looked well-designed and cost around $20, but now it's down to just $12. Its simple design and built-in USB-A plug for charging make it fun to use – just pull the back off, and it turns on. The magnet at the back lets you easily mount it anywhere you need a little extra light. I've used it inside a steel PC case while fiddling with RGB wires.
At just 2.17 inches long, this flashlight is rated to 50 lumens, and it sports a magnetic back with a USB-A plug for charging. Pulling the back off turns on the flashlight, and the magnetic back makes it easy to mount the light on anything mafe of ferrous metal.
Read moreRead less▼
The OLIGHT IMINI 2 is also small enough for your keychain, is designed to live with your keys, and includes two silicone covers for the USB port and a little carabiner clip. But the flashlight portion is only held to the charging port via a magnet, and I feel like (for me, at least) it would fall off and get lost before too long.
I've used the HOTO 3.6V Screwdriver Set to build dozens of PCs
I build a lot of PCs, though not as many lately thanks to the RAMpocalypse, and I also do regular home improvement work around my apartment. So a cordless screwdriver is a nice thing to have. I also own a much slimmer Wowstick, but have found HOTO's NEX O1 Pro to be more useful thanks to its extra (and variable) torque. It's great for loosening those factory-installed screws on PC cases that just don't want to let go, and also good for assembling furniture.
The HOTO won't replace my DeWalt drill for bigger, tougher jobs. But for everyday tasks, it's powerful enough, easy to charge over USB-C, and even looks good on my workbench.
Hoto's wireless screwdriver has three torque settings, charges over USB-C, and looks surprisingly good. It's even proven quite durable, as I've dropped it off of ladders and my workbench at least a dozen times, and it's still working flawlessly.
Read moreRead less▼
Cheap USB media control box puts volume and track control a touch away
For those of us who grew up in the 1900s, few things beat a chunky tactile volume knob and physical buttons for controlling media, and Vaydeer's USB device provides that and then some. I own the previous version of this device and love it for controlling and muting music at my treadmill desk while I work.
I use the buttons on it to play / pause audio and video and move forward to the next track or backward to the previous one. It's totally plug and play, as no drivers are needed.
Just plug this simple USB device into a USB port and you can control the volume and select tracks without reaching for your keyboard or mouse.
Read moreRead less▼
8Bitdo SN30 Pro Wireless Bluetooth Controller
What's not to love about a SNES-inspired wireless gaming controller that's compatible with Windows, Mac, Android, and the Nintendo Switch? Not much, as far as I'm concerned. 
As you might expect given this controller's small size and many more buttons than the SNES controller it was based on, its Rumble motors aren't the strongest, and the layout can feel kind of cramped for some modern games. But for any retro game and especially platformers (I'm looking at you, Super Mario Bros. Wonder), this is my go-to controller. At this price, maybe I should pick up another one. 
With its SNES-inspired design and white shell, this controller will appeal to gamers of a certain age. But its appeal goes beyond its looks., with Hall Effect joysticks, and support for the Switch, PC, macOS, and basically any OS that supports games and Bluetooth.
Read moreRead less▼
Go retro with modern specs with this NES-themed mouse from 8BitDo
There are so many gaming mouse options, most with specs that go well above and beyond my abilities. So I chose something with style that caught my eye, 8BitDo's Retro R8 Mouse with Charging Dock. This NES-inspired mouse is designed for nostalgia, with its black, gray, and red color scheme and round red side buttons. But 8BitDo went the extra mile (or two) by designing a weighted charging dock (with its own NES-like touches), and a spot for the 2.4 GHz dongle. This is the kind of extra feature that's more common in mice that cost twice as much.
The nostalgia of this mouse's design is nice. But it also sports a 26,000 DPI sensor, 4K polling, and a really nice charging dock that also houses the 2.4 GHz dongle. If you're in a pinch or not gaming, Bluetooth is also supported.
Read moreRead less▼
Under the hood, you get a decent 26,000 DPI sensor and 4K polling (plenty for us older, non-esports gamers), and an ambidextrous design with two side buttons on either side, and a clicky, rubberized scroll wheel. The side buttons, which are concave, took a little getting used to for me. But they are also so distinctive that now I miss them while using other mice. 
If the NES theme isn't your thing, the company also sells a translucent-green XBox version, as well as a champagne-hued C64 Edition.
Never run out of USB ports with this powered 11-port hub
If you're like me, you never have access to enough USB ports. I solved this problem by picking up this Ikai hub, with 60W of power for your drives and peripherals and a premium metal shell. It sports three speedy 10 Gbps ports (two USB-C), along with seven 5 GBps USB-A ports. The final USB-C on the end of the hub is for charging your phone or other devices, and delivers 20W.
The other nice feature, is that all the data ports have a button on the side so you can toggle them on and off. Aside from saving a bit of power, I also find this handy for swapping between wireless mice and keyboards, while keeping the tiny dongles plugged in so I don't lose them.
With 11 ports and up to 10 Gbps speed, a solid aluminum shell, and buttons so you can cut the power to individual ports, this USB hub is a great addition to your desk. It has external power for better stability, and even a 20W USB-C PD port on the end for charging phones or peripherals.
Read moreRead less▼
The sole thing to keep in mind about this (and basically any) hub, is that it has a single 10 Gbps input. So don't expect to plug in multiple high-data devices (like SSDs) and have them run simultaneously at full speed. If that's what you need, you'll need to get a Thunderbolt or USB4 hub (and spend significantly more).
Add recessed power and USB ports to your desk for just $16
OK, this one's only for the DIY-inclined, because it involves cutting a rectangle in your desk (or anywhere else you might want some flush-mount power ports, like a nightstand). Jgstkcity's recessed power strip lets you drop a couple of AC outlets and two USB charging ports (one 30W USB-C) anywhere you need them – again, once you've cut a hole for it.
While it's smart to be wary of no-name power strips, I've used two variations of these strips for roughly three years, and nothing has ever felt hot or failed in any way. I have it installed in the narrow stand I built right behind my couch. It's a super-convenient place for power outlets, especially when friends or family stop by. I just warn people not to put drinks there. Thankfully, the coffee table is even more convenient for that, and it's right in front of the couch.
You'll likely need a drill and a saw to install it, but having a couple of power plugs and USB-C PD power right on the surface of your desk or nightstand is super convenient.
Read moreRead less▼
Stay charged and save space while traveling abroad with Anker's slim Nano Travel Adapter
When you're traveling to another country for more than a few days, every small bit of space you can save helps. But you also usually need a travel adapter to plug your devices into the outlets of other countries. Anker's Nano Travel adapter serves both needs well, as it's roughly half the thickness of other adapters and is designed to work in over 200 countries. 
The Nano Travel Adapter also has four USB ports for charging, which I've found super convenient for keeping my phone, ereader, and earbuds juiced up without needing a separate charger. There are two USB-A ports on the bottom and two USB-C on the side, with the latter delivering up to 20W. It also comes in black or white/silver. I opted for the white one, which makes it easier to find after months in a drawer when I'm not traveling.
Anker's slim travel adapter is 43% smaller than many other adapters, while supporting over 200 countries with its fold-down plugs. It also has two USB-C and two USB-A ports for charging, at up to 20W.
Read moreRead less▼
The major downside over other travel chargers is that the Nano Travel Adapter doesn't support plugging in devices with three-prong (grounded) plugs. But I haven't found this an issue since I typically plug things like my Baseus flat laptop charger in while traveling, rather than high-power devices like a desktop PC or hair dryer.
Powerowl's rechargeable batteries are good and surprisingly cheap
When I first started using rechargeable batteries with my Walkman in the early 90s, they were kind of awful (but still better than spending all my money feeding my music addiction). They couldn't hold a charge and didn't last nearly as long as name-brand disposable batteries. But here in the mid-2020s, rechargeables are surprisingly good.
Panasonic's Eneloops arguably ushered in the rechargeable AA and AAA renaissance, but PowerOwl's batteries are a lot more affordable and I haven't had a single one fail in over three years of using them in my various remotes, smart door locks, and other devices.
These PowerOwl Pro AA batteries are rated to 2800mAh (though I wouldn't put stock in that spec) and are rated to keep 60% of their power for two years. The included USB-powered charger isn't the fastest (10 hours rated), but it gets the job done.
Read moreRead less▼
Lithium rechargeables are great for high-drain devices, and this 8-AA set with charger is just $23
After the good experience I've had with the company's NiMH batteries for years, I bought Powerowl's Lithium rechargeable batteries early this year. And boy am I glad I did. These last months longer in my smart door locks than those older batteries, which means I only have to swap the cells on two doors a few times a year now.
Full disclosure: I have had one of these batteries refuse to recharge after its first power cycle. But out of the three sets I now own, that's not a terrible track record. I just wish the company also made AAA lithium cells for my other devices.
These 1.5V lithium batteries are designed for high-drain devices and rated at 3600 mWh. The charger plugs in over USB-C and can also charge older NiMH batteries.
Read moreRead less▼
TP-Link's AX1800 WiFi 6 USB Adapter delivers Wi-Fi 6 to older devices over USB
Have you upgraded your router to Wi-Fi 6 or later, but your desktop or laptop doesn't have the requisite hardware to take advantage of your recent network tech? TP-Link's AX1800 WiFi 6 USB Adapter is here to solve that problem for you. It's quite large by USB Wi-Fi dongle standards, but I've found it works quite well with the Wi-Fi 6 router I bought in 2020.
I have the router running downstairs from my office. And it instantly fixed an issue I was having with very poor reception from the SFF PC I built in the Fractal Terra case.
Sure, it's big and bulky with two antennas, but this Wi-Fi 6 USB adapter can deliver some serious speed to your desktop or laptop when paired with a Wi-Fi 6 or later router.
Read moreRead less▼
Orico USB 3.0 Clamp Hub is easy to mount on many desks
This is a four-port, 5Gbps USB-A hub that's designed to clamp onto your monitor or desk and give you extra convenient connectivity.
It comes in black or silver and has a nice, sturdy metal frame. Just note that its clamp section is pretty shallow and its adjustable screw can only open between 10 and 32 mm, so it won't fit on all monitors or desks.
An otherwise standard four-port USB 3.0 hub, this Orico model stands out for its metal frame and clamp design.
Read moreRead less▼
Clean up the cables under your desk with a tray
If you to get a handle on the PC cables in your home or office, some cheap cable management trays will do the job. This two-pack comes with tape, though heavier loads will ultimately require some screws.
Besides the trays, this kit also comes with cable ties and a few cable clips you can place along the bottom or sides of your desk. One of these has been holding up the PC cable clutter in my living room for the past year. But I had to screw it into my desk because it's holding one of the above Anker power strips, plus the large external power brick from my LG OLED TV / Monitor.
If there's a rat's nest of cables under your desk, attaching some trays can help you clean it up. This set has tape for light loads, but for longer-term cleanliness, you probably want to consider screws.
Read moreRead less▼
Keep a fast charging cable with your keys
You may, like me, be swimming in a world of USB cables. But that doesn't mean you always have one when you need it away from home. This short 240W USB4 charging cable from EndlesShine solves that by being small enough to attach to your keys. It's not always convenient, at just over 5 inches long, but it will do in a pinch, and has come in handy more than once, particularly on trips when I'm traveling light.
It's short in length, at 5.11 inches, but this keychain cable supports 240W charging and USB4 (40Gbps speeds). Clip it onto your keys and you'll always have a fast cable when you need one.
Read moreRead less▼
If you're the type who is rough with your keys, the plastic cap may wear out over time, so you might want to just keep the cable in a pocket or your bag. It even comes in white and yellow if you don't like basic black.

articles.title: Google Home n'arrive plus à changer la couleur de vos ampoules, Philips Hue compris
articles.text:
Google Home n’arrive plus à modifier la couleur d’ampoules connectées de plusieurs marques, dont Philips Hue. L’allumage et la luminosité fonctionnent toujours, et Google n’a pas encore reconnu le problème.
Une ampoule connectée qui se contente de s’allumer reste une simple ampoule. C’est ce qu’ont découvert mardi avec surprise de nombreux utilisateurs de Google Home, d’après Android Authority, dont les lampes ont soudain perdu le goût des couleurs. Le coupable n’est pas la lumière, mais la couche logicielle qui prétend la commander.
Un bug qui touche l’app, la voix et les routines
Le problème a été signalé sur le subreddit de Google Home : l’utilisateur à l’origine du message n’arrive plus à changer la couleur de ses lampes, ni depuis l’application, ni par la voix via un Google Home Speaker via un écran Google Nest Hub. Les routines, ces scénarios automatiques censés modifier la teinte des lumières, seraient elles aussi touchées. Une douzaine d’utilisateurs ont répondu en confirmant la panne.
Le journaliste d’Android Authority a fait le test mardi matin avec ses ampoules Philips Hue, sans succès : ni l’application Google Home ni ses différentes enceintes connectées ne parvenaient à modifier la couleur. Le problème toucherait des fabricants variés.
Seule la couleur est en cause. L’allumage, l’extinction et la luminosité se règlent normalement via Google Home. Le contournement tient en une phrase : l'application du fabricant permet toujours de changer la teinte, ce qui désigne Google Home, et non les ampoules, comme source du souci. Google n’a, pour l’instant, ni reconnu la panne ni annoncé de correctif.
Un nouvel épisode dans une série de couacs sur les couleurs
Le journaliste à l’origine de l’information a fait le test mardi matin avec ses ampoules Philips Hue, sans succès : ni l’application Google Home ni ses différentes enceintes connectées ne parvenaient à modifier la couleur. Le problème toucherait des fabricants variés.
En avril 2026, c’est l’interface qui avait perdu les commandes de couleur sur certaines ampoules, ne laissant que quelques nuances de blanc. Un contournement existait, en passant par l'application du fabricant, et Google avait annoncé début mai avoir corrigé le défaut.
Les signalements actuels ne mentionnent aucune région, et rien ne permet donc de dire que la France est épargnée ou concernée. En attendant un correctif, mieux vaut passer par l'application du fabricant (Hue, WiZ, Tapo ou autre) pour changer les teintes, et vérifier que les scénarios Google Home basés sur une couleur ne sont pas pris en défaut.

articles.title: Infor uses industry-specific AI to address agent hallucinations - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Infor uses industry-specific AI to address agent hallucinations
Industry-specific AI brings business context to agents handling enterprise workflows. Building around industry processes can help companies address reliability concerns as they automate more tasks.
Infor (US) LLC is developing industry-specific AI agents for several key industries, including industrial manufacturing, aerospace and defense, automotive, and food and beverage. It builds those agents around its existing industry applications, according to Suresh Jayaraman (pictured, right), senior vice president of product management and development at Infor.
“Although the generic agents might work, you will always run into the challenge of not getting a deterministic answer every single time,” he said. “And there will be a lot of hallucinations happening.”
Jayaraman and Rick Rider (left), senior vice president of AI innovation at Infor, spoke with theCUBE Research’s Christophe Bertrand and co-host Alison Kosik at Infor Velocity Week, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed industry-specific AI, micro-vertical configuration and where humans stay in the loop. (* Disclosure below.)
Industry-specific AI starts with micro-vertical detail
Infor initially focused its agents on common bottlenecks and repetitive tasks, Rider explained. Its 2026.10 release adds guardrails through security and scopes.
“Every customer is uniquely different, and out-of-the-box AI does not exist in our world,” he said. “We’re working with customers to say, ‘What do you want?'”
Infor uses common cores shared across similar industries, with lightweight configuration for micro-verticals such as chemicals or heating, ventilation and air conditioning, Rider noted. In food and beverage, receiving details change sharply by product, according to Jayaraman.
“For a dairy, it’s a liquid receipt, which means I need to understand what the fat content of the milk is, the thickness of the milk while I’m doing the receiving function,” he said. “If it’s a protein or red meat, I’m bringing an entire animal into my receiving process. I need to know the country of origin and a few other extra specific configurations.”
Agents can create an order and check demand on their own, but moving one customer’s order to another still requires human approval, Jayaraman explained. Infor is also hiring domain experts to work alongside technologists, according to Rider.
“Finding tech people, programmers, it’s a little bit easier compared to finding the industry-focused people with that deep industry knowledge,” Jayaraman said. “When you’re going in front of the customer, you’re not talking to IT people; you’re actually talking to the business people.”

articles.title: Qualcomm will license patents behind Huawei’s LogicFolding chip architecture, report says
articles.text:
Qualcomm will license patents behind Huawei’s LogicFolding chip architecture, report says — the Kirin 9050 Pro already uses it, with a teardown showing its lower die is mostly cache and I/O
How much logic is actually stacked inside Huawei’s Kirin 9050 Pro?
Qualcomm has reached a deal to license Huawei patents behind the LogicFolding chip-stacking method, Bloomberg reports. The technology, which is used in the Kirin 9050 Pro, splits nearly every block across two bonded dies, and a teardown and die shots show the lower die holds mostly cache and I/O.
Qualcomm’s multiyear, cross-license deal with Huawei has a wide scope, covering 5G devices, AI services, near- and co-packaged optics and networks, a Huawei spokesperson told Bloomberg. Qualcomm also intends to purchase specific Huawei U.S. patents in compute, AI, networking, and other technologies, according to a release. Neither company’s announcement named any patents, LogicFolding, or any chip that uses it.
Bloomberg's report frames the deal as a win for Huawei, validating its chipmaking acumen. The deal remains subject to approval, and Qualcomm will reportedly pay Huawei to license its patents for the first time. According to the report, LogicFolding targets faster data transmission as a workaround for China’s lack of access to EUV lithography machines.
The Kirin 9050 Pro is used in the Huawei Mate XT 2 tri-fold smartphone, launched Sept. 7. Geekerwan, a Chinese tech review channel known for in-depth chip testing, had a lab slice the chip for its teardown. Kurnal, a semiconductor researcher who publishes die-shot analysis, also posted annotated shots of both dies on X. Geekerwan’s cross-section shows the two dies bonded face to face, and both show the execution units on top, with the PLLs also on the lower die.
LogicFolding was first unveiled on May 25 by He Tingbo, president of Huawei’s semiconductor business, at IEEE ISCAS 2026 in Shanghai, under the company’s “Tau Scaling Law,” which uses signal delay rather than transistor size as a measure. Huawei describes both layers as active and working as one. Vertical interconnects work to create shorter signal paths, which can reduce energy consumption. Peking University’s “true 3D” design tool for the technology shows a 30% wire-length cut in its own tests.
Huawei’s papers describe a “Kirin 2026” chip whose figures match the Kirin 9050 Pro’s. In a paper last month, relayed by TrendForce, Huawei said the chip uses a 1.5-micrometer hybrid-bonding pitch with about 50 million interconnects. About 10–15% of those carry signals. Core routing is 20% shorter, with critical paths up to 70% shorter. Power is reduced by as much as 66% for NPU, 58% for GPU, and 41% for a CPU performance core at the same performance level. NPU performance holds 29 TOPS at 63% less frequency and at a lower voltage.
Huawei does not name a process node. On its roadmap is Kirin 2027 at a 1-micrometer pitch and more than 100 million interconnects; for around three years out, a 720-nanometer pitch with over 200 million. It is targeting a 1.4nm-class density by 2031, with LogicFolding in the Ascend 990 AI accelerator around 2030. HiSilicon, Huawei’s chip-design unit, designs the Kirin chips, and SMIC is believed to make them, according to Reuters via TrendForce. It isn’t stated who handles the bonding process.
As for the Kirin 9050 Pro, Geekerwan tested it in a Mate 90 Pro Max phone. Analysis shows that the two dies are bonded with copper-to-copper hybrid bonding, metal layer to metal layer. The bonded circuit layers of both dies sit between two thick layers of silicon rather than directly on the package substrate. For the interconnects, about 80,000 through-silicon vias (TSVs) run through the lower die, taking up, with their keep-out zones, about 8% of the lower die’s usable area, Geekerwan says.
The split spans both dies. In the big CPU core, the execution units are on top, with the L1 and L2 caches directly beneath the load/store units, Geekerwan says. Kurnal's die shots put the GPU and NPU logic over their caches too. The lower die also holds a shared L3, a 12MiB system cache, PLLs, and the LPDDR, PCIe, camera, display, UFS, and USB interfaces, while the top die carries the ISP, modem, and memory controllers. Cache, I/O, and PLLs produce less heat and are less sensitive to the process, so they go below, Geekerwan explains; the denser compute goes on top, on a somewhat more advanced process.
Each die is just over 120 mm², which is smaller than the previous chip’s 140-plus mm². The total silicon area for both is therefore over 240 mm², up 70% overall. Density rose from 155 to 238 MTr/mm² at launch, about 53.5% higher, according to Huawei’s launch numbers. Other notable changes include the NPU’s area, up 150% across both dies, with Geekerwan measuring 68 TOPS INT8. The configuration makes sense and the rationale follows the layout, but an independent die analysis is needed for full understanding.
Huawei’s stacking approach has its competitors. TSMC’s SoIC roadmap set a 6-micrometer bond pitch for 2025 and 4.5 micrometers by 2029, with 3nm chip stacking in volume production last year. Intel’s Foveros Direct is said to have “copper bonding at a pitch of 9µm,” which reached high volume with the Clearwater Forest Xeon, and a second generation targets 3 micrometers. AMD’s first-generation 3D V-Cache stacks a 64MB L3 SRAM die on a complete CPU die, using direct copper bonding at a 9-micrometer pitch. Huawei’s 1.5-micrometer claim comes from its own paper and any comparison has to be taken with a grain of salt.
As to why Qualcomm might be interested, John Han, executive vice president and general manager of Qualcomm Technology Licensing, said the agreement reflects Qualcomm’s “recognition of Huawei’s continued innovation and intellectual property in 5G and other technology fields.” Bloomberg’s report says that at least some of the patents underpin LogicFolding, but no source names the patents. Dr. Ian Cutress, chief analyst at More Than Moore, questioned how new Huawei’s Tau Scaling is, writing on X that it is “a repackaging of what the industry has always done.”
Upon “receipt of the necessary regulatory approvals,” the cross-license and patent purchase deal should proceed. The deal is also subject to Federal Trade Commission review under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act, Bloomberg reported. That U.S. premerger law sets a minimum deal size, $133.9 million this year, among other tests, and the deal’s value wasn’t disclosed.
Nikkei Asia reported that Qualcomm will be the net payer under the deal; Qualcomm’s licensing revenue stopped including Huawei royalties in fiscal Q2 2025, after the license expired. This follows a long history of Huawei paying for Qualcomm licenses, an agreement first inked in 2001. Huawei says it has brought in more license-related income than it’s spent since 2021. Patents behind its chip-stacking method reportedly join that business under the deal.
The industry now waits to see what comes of the FTC review. Qualcomm’s fiscal Q4 results should come early next month, as last year’s did, but its fiscal year ended Sept. 27, before the deal was announced. Additional independent analysis of the 9050 Pro’s die may come from TechInsights or SemiAnalysis. Also of interest is the next iteration in Huawei’s Kirin 2027, to see if its claims are met. The deal between the two companies currently lacks details on the extent of patent coverage, but the silicon on record can help reveal the nature of Qualcomm’s interest.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: El Surface más ambicioso de Microsoft sumará su propio "MagSafe". Ahora también sabemos cuánto habrá que pagar
articles.text:
Un portátil puede estar preparado para ejecutar modelos de IA en local y, aun así, seguir teniendo que resolver problemas mucho más cotidianos. Uno de ellos aparece en cuanto conectamos el cargador: un tirón accidental puede acabar desplazando el equipo o, en el peor de los casos, llevándoselo por delante. Microsoft conoce bien la carga magnética porque la utilizó durante años en la familia Surface, pero ahora ha decidido replantearla de una forma diferente. Lo hace, además, en el Surface más ambicioso que ha preparado hasta ahora, con una solución familiar en su concepto y bastante particular en su implementación.
El protagonista es el Surface Laptop Ultra, un equipo que la compañía no acaba de sacar de la chistera. Microsoft ya lo anunció a finales de mayo como su portátil Surface más potente hasta la fecha, desarrollado alrededor de la plataforma RTX Spark de NVIDIA y pensado para cargas exigentes e IA local. Lo que tenemos ahora es una segunda pieza de aquella presentación: además de enseñar Magnetic Connect, la firma de Redmond ha despejado varias de las incógnitas que entonces seguían abiertas.
Microsoft recupera los imanes, pero esta vez alrededor del USB-C
La comparación con MagSafe resulta difícil de evitar, aunque la implementación de Microsoft tiene una particularidad importante. Magnetic Connect se fija mediante imanes alrededor del USB-C derecho y permite que la conexión se libere ante un tirón, pero no obliga a reservar un conector exclusivamente para cargar el ordenador. Al quitarlo, volvemos a tener un USB-C funcional para datos, vídeo y otros accesorios. Es un planteamiento diferente tanto del puerto MagSafe dedicado de los MacBook como del antiguo Surface Connect: recupera la comodidad de los imanes sin renunciar a la versatilidad del USB-C que ya está en el portátil.
La otra gran incógnita ya tiene respuesta, al menos para Estados Unidos. El Surface Laptop Ultra puede reservarse allí desde 2.599,99 dólares y Microsoft prevé comenzar los envíos el 16 de octubre. Esa configuración combina una CPU de 18 núcleos, 24 GB de memoria unificada y 512 GB de almacenamiento, mientras que la gama escala hasta los 5.899,99 dólares en el modelo con CPU de 20 núcleos, 128 GB de memoria y 1 TB.
Para entender esas cifras hay que volver a lo que ya conocíamos desde mayo. El Laptop Ultra está construido alrededor de RTX Spark, la plataforma de NVIDIA que combina una CPU basada en Arm con gráficos Blackwell RTX, soporte completo para CUDA y hasta 128 GB de memoria unificada que pueden repartirse entre CPU y GPU según la carga de trabajo. Microsoft habla además de hasta 1 petaflop de rendimiento de IA FP4 teórico con sparsity.
Toda esa memoria tiene una finalidad bastante concreta: hacer espacio para cargas de IA que normalmente asociaríamos a máquinas mucho menos portátiles. En mayo, NVIDIA hablaba de ejecutar localmente modelos de 120.000 millones de parámetros con contextos de hasta un millón de tokens; ahora Microsoft asegura que el Surface Laptop Ultra puede manejar modelos comprimidos de hasta 280.000 millones de parámetros en el propio equipo. Ejecutar este tipo de cargas en local puede reducir la latencia, mantener determinados datos dentro del dispositivo y limitar la dependencia de servicios en la nube. El planteamiento va más allá del de los primeros Copilot+ PC, definidos precisamente por el requisito de contar con una NPU capaz de superar los 40 TOPS.
La fotografía es ahora bastante más completa que en mayo, pero todavía no definitiva. Microsoft ya ha puesto precio, fecha y configuraciones a una máquina que entonces conocíamos sobre todo por su arquitectura y sus promesas, y ha añadido además detalles como Magnetic Connect. Aun así, siguen faltando piezas importantes para mercados como España, como el precio, y, sobre todo, queda por comprobar lo que ninguna ficha técnica puede resolver. Sobre el papel ya impresiona; ahora toca ver si también convence fuera de él.

O iPhone 16 de 256 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 4.649,10 no Pix aplicando o cupom de R$ 300 OFF exclusivo para assinantes Amazon Prime. A promoção traz o menor preço já registrado pelo celular da Apple, e representa um desconto de 46% frente ao preço de lançamento (R$ 8.599).
Esta é uma excelente oportunidade para quem busca economizar na compra de um iPhone com Apple Intelligence e câmera de 48 MP. O iPhone 16 fica naturalmente atrás do iPhone 17, seu sucessor, mas quem busca um modelo equilibrado pode aproveitar vantagens frente ao iPhone 17e.
Equipado com o processador Apple A18 de 3 nanômetros e 8 GB de RAM, iPhone 16 suporta os recursos de IA do Apple Intelligence, e oferece ótima performance para rodar jogos pesados e tarefas de produtividade. articles.title: MENA startup funding surges to $1.1 billion in September 2026
articles.text:
MENA startup funding surges to $1.1 billion in September 2026
MENA startup funding staged a sharp comeback in September, crossing the $1 billion mark for the first time in months as a string of large Saudi fintech deals pulled the region out of August’s slowdown.
Startups across the Middle East and North Africa raised $1.1 billion through 73 deals during the month, up 193% from August. Yet the recovery looks less dramatic when compared with last year: funding remained 68% below September 2025.
The rebound was also highly concentrated.
Barq’s $329.5 million Series A, Tabby’s $233 million Series F and Lendo’s $200 million debt financing together brought in $762.5 million, accounting for nearly 70% of all capital raised during the month.
That concentration offers a more nuanced picture of September. Capital returned in force, but it flowed disproportionately to a handful of large, predominantly Saudi fintech companies rather than evenly across the ecosystem.
Debt also remained a significant feature of the funding landscape, accounting for 31.7% of September’s total. That is substantially lower than the 76% recorded in September 2025, suggesting equity played a much larger role in this year’s headline figure.
Saudi Arabia takes back the lead
Saudi Arabia returned to the top of the regional funding table in September, with 40 startups raising a combined $947.2 million.
The kingdom alone accounted for roughly 86% of all capital raised in MENA during the month, underlining just how heavily September’s performance rested on the Saudi market.
Fintech was the clear driver. The sector accounted for 86% of Saudi Arabia’s funding, buoyed by the large rounds raised by Barq, Tabby and Lendo.
The UAE, which led the region in August, slipped to second place with $98.4 million raised across 12 deals.
Five of those companies were fintech startups, and together they accounted for 71% of the UAE’s total funding, showing that the sector’s dominance was not confined to Saudi Arabia.
Egypt, meanwhile, returned to the regional top three after recording no funding in August.
Seven Egyptian startups raised $49.2 million, although here too the total was shaped by one standout transaction. Paymob’s $35 million pre-Series C round accounted for about 71% of the country’s funding for the month.
Further down the table, Qatar moved into fourth place with four deals worth a combined $2.4 million, followed by Kuwait, where COFE recorded an estimated $1 million transaction.
Startups in Syria and Palestine raised a combined $580,000 across two deals, while Bahrain recorded five transactions worth $275,000.
Fintech is back in command
After losing some of its momentum in previous months, fintech returned decisively to the top of the sector rankings.
Twenty fintech startups raised $930.6 million in September, equivalent to around 85% of all funding deployed across MENA.
But, as with the regional total, much of that figure came from a small number of companies. Barq, Tabby and Lendo accounted for around 82% of all fintech funding during the month.
That makes September as much a story about deal size as sector strength. Fintech clearly remained the region’s most capital-intensive vertical, but its performance was amplified by three unusually large transactions.
Proptech came a distant second with $50.2 million raised across three deals. Rize’s $50 million round accounted for virtually all of that total.
Traveltech ranked third, attracting $25.2 million across two deals.
Later-stage deals make a comeback
September also brought some relief at the later end of the funding spectrum.
Five later-stage startups raised a combined $288 million during the month, a notable return of larger equity rounds after a period in which investors had largely favoured smaller and earlier-stage bets.
Early-stage companies nevertheless remained the dominant funding category in September, leading both by deal count and capital raised, with $418.2 million secured across 39 transactions.
Another 23 startups did not disclose the stage of their rounds, while six transactions were classified as debt deals.
The split suggests investors have not abandoned early-stage companies, but larger companies are once again finding ways to secure sizeable pools of capital, an encouraging signal after a year marked by tighter funding conditions.
B2B continues to attract the most deals
Business-to-business startups remained the most active segment of the market, raising $457.7 million across 47 transactions.
Consumer-focused companies attracted $406.4 million across 16 deals, while the remaining capital went to startups operating across both B2B and B2C models.
The figures reinforce a trend that has been visible throughout much of the year: investors continue to favour companies selling to businesses, particularly those with clearer paths to recurring revenue and enterprise-scale growth.
Female founders remain severely underfunded
One imbalance showed little sign of improving.
Male-led startups received around $1 billion in September, dwarfing the $2.4 million raised by female-founded companies.
Startups with mixed-gender founding teams attracted another $7.3 million.
The disparity is difficult to overlook. Even in a month when regional funding topped $1 billion, only a fraction of that capital reached companies founded or co-founded by women.
September’s rebound, in other words, did little to narrow one of the ecosystem’s most persistent funding gaps.
A strong headline, but not yet a broad recovery
September gave the MENA ecosystem one of its strongest monthly funding totals of the year and pushed third-quarter investment above $1.7 billion.
But the composition of that funding matters as much as the total.
Three transactions accounted for almost 70% of September’s capital, one country absorbed about 86% of the region’s funding, and one sector captured roughly 85%.
Strip away those mega-deals, and the picture becomes considerably more modest.
That does not make September’s rebound insignificant. The ability of regional startups to close transactions worth hundreds of millions of dollars — across equity and debt — shows that investors are still willing to make large commitments when they see the right companies and opportunities.
What September does not yet show is a broad-based return of capital across the ecosystem.
That will be the more important test in the fourth quarter: whether the momentum created by a few outsized transactions begins to spread across more countries, sectors and funding stages, or whether MENA’s funding recovery remains dependent on a narrow group of heavyweight deals.
Wamda’s upcoming Q3 report will examine how those dynamics shaped the region’s venture funding landscape over the quarter.
These monthly reports are a collaboration between Wamda and Digital Digest.

Le Samsung 990 Pro 4 To combine une grande capacité de stockage à des débits élevés, ce qui le rend adapté à l’installation de jeux et au stockage de lourds fichiers. Jusqu’à la fin des Jours Flash Prime, Amazon le propose à 549,99 € au lieu de 625 €.
Les Jours Flash Prime se déroulent jusqu’à ce soir sur Amazon, et, si vous cherchez à étendre la capacité de stockage de votre PC, vous pouvez notamment vous tourner vers le SSD Samsung 990 Pro 4 To disponible à 549,99 € au lieu de 625 €. Il s’agit d’un SSD interne au format M.2 2280, utilisant une interface PCIe 4.0. Point important, il s’agit d’un modèle sans dissipateur et il ne peut donc pas être utilisé tel quel dans une PS5.
Le SSD Samsung 990 Pro 4 To est à 549,99 € au lieu de 625 € chez Amazon via une offre réservée aux membres Prime.
Pour profiter des Jours Flash Prime n'oubliez pas de devenir membre Amazon Prime. Vous bénéficiez d'un essai gratuit de 30 jours, c'est donc le bon moment pour tester.
Pourquoi choisir le SSD Samsung 990 Pro 4 To ?
- Pour sa capacité : les 4 To permettent de conserver une bibliothèque de jeux conséquente, mais aussi des projets vidéo et d’autres gros fichiers au même endroit.
- Pour ses débits rapides : Samsung annonce jusqu’à 7 450 Mo/s en lecture et 6 900 Mo/s en écriture séquentielles.
- Pour son logiciel : Samsung Magician permet de surveiller l’état du SSD et de mettre à jour son micrologiciel.
De la place pour installer vos jeux Steam, GOG, Epic…
Les jeux PC prennent toujours plus de place, entre leur installation de base, leurs patchs et leurs DLC. Ce SSD Samsung de 4 To peut vous éviter bien des séances d’arbitrage et de désinstallation pour libérer de l’espace. Quant aux débits annoncés par la marque, ils ont surtout un intérêt pour les transferts de gros fichiers. Notre test du SSD Samsung 990 Pro, réalisé sur la version 1 To, a accordé la note de 9 sur 10 à ce modèle. Pour en exploiter tout le potentiel, il faut néanmoins l’installer dans un emplacement M.2 NVMe PCIe 4.0 x4 compatible.
Une configuration réservée aux usages gourmands
Ce Samsung 990 Pro s’avère donc performant, notamment grâce à sa mémoire TLC et son cache DRAM dédié. Cependant, c’est un fait, son coût reste élevé malgré l’offre d’Amazon : les hausses tarifaires mondiales sont passées par là ! Son achat se justifie si vos besoins sont en accord avec ses performances.
✅ Les points forts
- Capacité de 4 To.
- Débits séquentiels annoncés élevés en PCIe 4.0.
- Logiciel Samsung Magician pour le suivi du SSD.
❌ Les limites
- Dissipateur thermique non fourni.
- Budget conséquent malgré la réduction.
Le SSD Samsung 990 Pro 4 To est proposé à 549,99 € sur Amazon, jusqu’à ce soir.
Si vous êtes à la recherche d’un SSD NVMe doté de beaucoup d’espace de stockage et de débits rapides, le Samsung NVMe SSD 990 Pro se présente comme un choix adapté.
En revanche, pour un usage bureautique, un modèle avec des débits moins élevés, une capacité inférieure et, surtout, un tarif plus accessible, peut s’avérer plus en accord avec vos besoins.

articles.title: Amazon elimina una función de Alexa que todavía era usada por sus altavoces Echo: estos son los modelos afectados
articles.text:
Amazon eliminó una función de Alexa que permitía controlar mediante comandos de voz la entrada auxiliar de 3,5 milímetros en algunos altavoces Echo antiguos. El cambio afecta a cuatro modelos lanzados entre 2018 y 2020 y significa que los usuarios ya no podrán pedirle al asistente que inicie o detenga la reproducción de una fuente conectada mediante ese puerto.
La decisión no inutiliza la entrada auxiliar. Los propietarios todavía pueden conectar físicamente otros dispositivos al Echo para reproducir audio, pero tendrán que controlar la reproducción directamente desde el equipo conectado. Amazon también recomienda utilizar Bluetooth como alternativa.
La compañía ya comenzó a enviar correos electrónicos a los usuarios cuyos dispositivos están afectados para informarles sobre la modificación.
Estos son los Echo que pierden la función
El cambio está limitado a cuatro modelos de generaciones anteriores de los altavoces inteligentes de Amazon. Los dispositivos afectados son el Echo Plus de segunda generación, presentado en 2018; el Echo de tercera generación, lanzado en 2019; el Echo Studio de primera generación, también de 2019; y el Echo de cuarta generación, presentado en 2020.
La medida no afecta a las generaciones más recientes, entre otras razones porque Amazon dejó de incluir el puerto auxiliar de 3,5 milímetros en sus nuevos altavoces Echo.
Hasta ahora, quienes tenían uno de estos dispositivos podían conectar una fuente de audio mediante el puerto auxiliar y utilizar comandos como “Alexa, reproduce desde la entrada de línea” o “Alexa, para la entrada Aux”. Esas instrucciones dejarán de funcionar.
El puerto seguirá funcionando de forma manual
Amazon aclara que el cambio afecta al control mediante Alexa y no al funcionamiento físico de la conexión auxiliar.
Por ejemplo, un usuario todavía puede conectar un dispositivo compatible mediante un cable de 3,5 milímetros y reproducir audio a través del Echo. Lo que desaparece es la posibilidad de utilizar comandos de voz para controlar esa fuente.
Esto significa que la reproducción tendrá que pausarse o detenerse desde el dispositivo conectado. Para algunas personas, el cambio puede pasar prácticamente desapercibido, especialmente si nunca utilizaron Alexa para manejar equipos conectados mediante la entrada auxiliar.
El impacto será mayor para quienes incorporaron el Echo a un sistema de audio y dependían de los comandos de voz para controlar diferentes fuentes.
Amazon propone utilizar Bluetooth
Como alternativa, la compañía recomienda transmitir contenido mediante Bluetooth. Para hacerlo, el teléfono, tableta u otro dispositivo compatible debe emparejarse con el altavoz Echo.
Esta opción permite mantener el control inalámbrico del contenido, aunque modifica la forma en que algunos usuarios habían configurado sus equipos durante años.
La decisión también evidencia cómo las funciones de los dispositivos conectados pueden cambiar incluso después de que hayan sido adquiridos. En este caso, el hardware continúa funcionando, pero una característica vinculada al software y al asistente de voz deja de estar disponible.
El Echo de cuarta generación fue el último con puerto auxiliar
El modelo más reciente de la lista, el Echo de cuarta generación, llegó al mercado en 2020. Desde entonces, Amazon no ha vuelto a incorporar un puerto auxiliar de 3,5 milímetros en sus nuevas generaciones de altavoces Echo.
Esto hace que la modificación tenga un alcance limitado dentro del catálogo actual de la compañía, pero puede resultar importante para quienes todavía utilizan alguno de estos modelos antiguos.
Los usuarios afectados no necesitan reemplazar inmediatamente su altavoz. La entrada auxiliar continúa disponible y Bluetooth ofrece una alternativa para reproducir contenido. Sin embargo, quienes utilizaban comandos de voz para controlar dispositivos conectados por cable tendrán que modificar su forma de utilizar Alexa a partir de ahora.

articles.title: Process automation gets industry depth from Infor AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Infor combines industry expertise and embedded engineers for process automation
AI-powered process automation requires software that understands the industry and workflows it serves. Moving from a promising prototype to practical use also requires implementation expertise.
Infor (US) LLC develops software around the specific processes its customers use in their industries. Its approach combines industry-specific agents, deep vertical expertise and an open architecture, according to Kevin Samuelson (pictured, left), chief executive officer of Infor.
“We had to understand the specific processes that define each of these industries and allow folks to create value,” he said. “Having that depth of industry, understanding processes and how these things work together, and then being open from a technology perspective has given us the ingredients that when AI came along, we could put it on top of all of that to really deliver outcomes that drive value.”
Samuelson and Soma Somasundaram (right), president and chief technology officer of Infor, spoke with theCUBE’s Christophe Bertrand and Alison Kosik at Infor Velocity Week, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed process automation, observability for automated decisions and forward-deployed engineers to accelerate return on investment. (* Disclosure below.)
Industry AI brings precision to process automation
Two in three businesses said off-the-shelf AI doesn’t adequately address their industry’s needs, according to Infor’s new global research. Infor Industry AI is not a single product, but an architecture embedded across the company’s applications, built on its Infor OS foundation and open to the customer’s wider data, Somasundaram explained.
“If you are an automotive supplier [or] parts supplier, material shortage is not an option,” Somasundaram said. “You better deliver the material right at the production line at the right time you promised.”
Trust is the other hurdle as agents take on more decisions. Infor’s approach starts with a human reviewing agent recommendations, then adds observability, auditability and access controls that treat each agent like another citizen of the enterprise, according to Somasundaram.
“If something is being automated, you’re delegating the work to the agent,” Somasundaram said. “When the work gets done, you need a complete trace of how the decisions were made and how the work got done.”
Infor pairs customers with forward-deployed engineers, industry experts who stay on to drive each use case until it delivers value, Samuelson explained. That support is shrinking the time it takes for process automation to go from prototype to production.
“Now it’s taking a customer literally one to two, or at worst, three weeks, even for something that isn’t already a use case,” Samuelson said. “We can prototype so quickly for the customer. That speed will just continue to multiply.”

articles.title: The Dyson Airwrap has had a huge price cut for Prime Day, but this underrated alternative might be a better buy — and it's $150 cheaper
articles.text:
The Dyson Airwrap i.d. is down to its lowest price for Amazon Prime Day, but the Supersonic Nural might be a smarter buy
I've tested both — here's my advice
The Dyson Airwrap has gained somewhat iconic status, but it's not the only great hair tool this brand makes. In fact, I've tested most of Dyson's haircare range, and for me, the Supersonic Nural hair dryer is the unsung hero of the lineup.
Both are discounted in the current Prime Day sales: the Airwrap i.d. is down to $499.99 (was $709.99) and the Supersonic Nural is down to $349.99 (was $449.99). You need to be a Prime subscriber to access both deals, but you can use the free trial.
• Browse the full Amazon Prime Day sale
Before you scramble to purchase an Airwrap, it's worth considering if a Supersonic Nural might actually be a better fit for your styling needs — not least because with these deals, it's $150 cheaper. Scroll down for my take on who should buy an Airwrap, and who'd be better off with a Supersonic Nural...
Good Airwrap discounts are rare, and tend to come and go quickly. This $210 price-drop is well worth hopping on — it take the styler back down to the lowest price we've seen lately.
The price of the Supersonic Nural tends to fluctuate, but based on our price tracker tool it's only been this cheap once before: very briefly, in November 2025 (I'd guess that's Black Friday). It's well worth snapping up this deal.
Buy the Dyson Supersonic Nural if...
✅ You want healthier hair drying: In Scalp Protect mode, this dryer will raise or lower its temperature to maintain what feels like a constant heat on your head. That means you can get right up close to your scalp, for precision styling, without frying your head or your roots. The Airwrap does not have this feature. In general, if hair drying is your priority, the Supersonic Nural is more comfortable and efficient than the Airwrap-plus-dryer attachment.
✅ You have naturally curly hair: The Supersonic Nural is arguably a better choice for those with natural curls — amongst the plethora of attachments you'll find a two-part diffuser (one section for drying another for defining), a wide-tooth comb (ideal for coily hair) and a 'soft air' attachment.
✅ You're a big attachment-swapper: The attachments here are magnetic, and swapping them over is much less fiddly than the clip-in, clip out process required on the Airwrap. More impressive though, is the fact the dryer has attachment recognition, so it knows what's snapped on and will remember your preferred settings.
Buy the Dyson Airwrap i.d. if...
✅ You have straight hair and want curls: There are no curling tools on the Supersonic Nural, so if you're creating curls you need the Airwrap. The i.d. feature makes this process dead easy — you flip a switch on the Airwrap handle and it'll launch into a wrap > curl > cool shot sequence, personalized for your hair type, for perfect results with minimal effort required from you.
✅ You want bouncy blowouts: The Airwrap i.d. comes with a round brush attachment, which I use regularly for creating volume and loose curls. There isn't an equivalent on the Supersonic Nural.

articles.title: American Horror Story : quand sortent les épisodes de la saison 13 sur Disney+ ?
articles.text:
American Horror Story : quand sortent les épisodes de la saison 13 sur Disney+ ?
La nouvelle saison du show signé Ryan Murphy est arrivée sur Disney+. Voici le calendrier de diffusion détaillé des épisodes, pour ne rater aucune miette de la série sur la plateforme de streaming.
Créée en 2011, la série American Horror Story de Ryan Murphy (Glee, Pose) et Brad Falchuck n'a pas perdu en force avec le temps et revient chaque année avec de nouveaux épisodes, et avec de quoi ravir les fans d'horreur et d'univers à l'esthétique soignée.
Le millésime 2026 n'échappe pas à la régle, puisque la série d'anthologie est de retour avec une treizième saison, diffusée depuis ce mercredi 7 octobre sur la plateforme de streaming Disney+.
Vous êtes fans et vous ne voulez rien rater de ce nouveau chapitre d'American Horror Story ? Les Numériques vous détaille ici son calendrier de diffusion.
Combien d'épisodes pour la saison 13 d'American Horror Story ?
Et on commence par une bonne nouvelle, puisque cette treizième saison de la série est particulièrement généreuse. Alors que les précédentes tournées autour des 9 ou 10 épisodes, cette nouvelle saison comptera pas moins de 13 épisodes.
De quoi profiter de cette saison toute particulière, qui se distingue des autres en réunissant de nombreux personnages issus des saisons précédentes, de Murder House à Delicate. L'histoire centrale est celle de Ben DeSoto, un infirmier en soins palliatifs atteint de triskaïdékaphobie (la peur phobique du chiffre 13).
- Regardez la bande-annonce d'American Horror Story saison 13 :
Quel est le calendrier de diffusion de la série ?
L'une des raisons de l'existence de cet article est justement la diffusion erratique de cette saison 13. Alors que la série est diffusée depuis le 24 septembre aux États-Unis, elle n'arrive que en ce début octobre dans l'Hexagone.
Ainsi les trois premiers épisodes sont disponibles dès le 7 octobre en version originale sous-titrée en français, puis la série sera diffusée au rythme d’un épisode par semaine jusqu'au final le mercredi 16 décembre.
La version française des premiers épisodes sera quant à elle proposée à partir du 11 novembre, puis un mois après la sortie de l'épisode concerné en VOST.

- Épisode 4 : Is That All There Is? - mercredi 14 octobre

L'intégralité de la série American Horror Story - c'est à dire les 12 saisons précédentes et la 13ème actuellement en cours - est disponible sur la plateforme de streaming Disney+.

articles.title: Amazon está liquidando (y agotando) hoy estos SSD desde 39,99 euros: quedan pocas unidades disponibles en la Fiesta de Ofertas Prime
articles.text:
Históricamente, las Fiestas de Ofertas Prime de Amazon, los Días sin IVA de MediaMarkt, los Días Naranjas de PcComponentes y los Black Fridays de todas las tiendas especializadas en hardware eran unas ocasiones muy buenas para renovar componentes de nuestros equipos ahorrándonos un buen pellizco.
PNY CS900 250GB
Pero la situación ha cambiado enormemente desde finales del pasado año cuando, a causa del auge de la IA, el sector del hardware (con mención especial a la memoria RAM y los SSD) no deja de ver cómo escalan más y más sus precios. De modo que a día de hoy hay que pagar por lo mismo bastante más de lo que habríamos pagado hace no mucho tiempo atrás.
Sin embargo, estas campañas, como la Fiesta de Ofertas Prime que Amazon tiene activa desde ayer y durante lo que queda de hoy, siguen siendo buen momento para ahorrarnos algo en la compra de hardware. No tanto como antes, pero sí lo suficiente como para que merezca la pena el desembolso. Es el caso de este SSD PNY, que protagoniza unas ofertas que parten de los 39,99 euros.
Disponible en diferentes capacidades (casi todas rebajadas)
Hablamos del CS900 de PNY. Un SSD en formato SATA con el que actualizar el PC de sobremesa o el portátil en pleno 2026 sin dejarnos un ojo de la cara. Y aunque lejos de sus precios más bajos hasta la fecha, sus diferentes versiones están rebajadas a unos precios algo más asumibles para el bolsillo:
- PNY CS900 de 250 GB por 39,99 euros
- PNY CS900 de 500 GB por 65,99 euros
- PNY CS900 de 1 TB por 114,99 euros
- PNY CS900 de 2 TB por 257,64 euros (sin rebaja aplicada y prácticamente agotado)
Si necesitamos actualizar ya nuestro equipo y no podemos seguir esperando a que el mercado se estabilice, que a saber si lo hace y cuándo lo hace, estas son unas ofertas bastante buenas viendo lo visto. Porque aunque se trata de unidades SSD SATA que se alejan de las NVMe en rendimiento, tienen una buena relación calidad precio entre gasto y la capacidad que ganamos.
Superan ligeramente los 500 MB/s, velocidad suficiente para muchos usuarios y que suponen un salto enorme frente a HDD convencionales. Tanto para mover datos y archivos como para instalar aplicaciones, juegos y hasta el sistema operativo. Además, son fáciles de instalar en prácticamente cualquier equipo de hace unas décadas a esta parte.
Sólo un aspecto a tener en cuenta: las rebajas aplicadas sólo estarán disponibles lo que resta de hoy, miércoles 7 de octubre. O hasta que se agote su stock, lo que antes suceda. Pero ojo, porque según indica la propia Amazon, tienen un stock limitado y no deja de bajar. De modo que alguno de ellos probablemente se agote antes de medianoche.

Data centers have become essential to almost every part of the global economy with the continuing rise in computing demands. Modern data centers, consisting of rows of equipment racks for storing, processing, and sharing data, require front-end AC/DC converters that are reliable, operate at unity power factor, offer low input current THD, and achieve high efficiency. The Vienna rectifier is a grid-connected, nongenerative three-level PWM boost converter topology that enables reduced semiconductor stress and improved power quality compared to conventional two-level rectifiers. Owing to these advantages, it is widely used in telecommunication power systems, data centers, wind energy systems, and other high-power applications.
This solution presents the design and control implementation of a 3.6kW rectifier aimed at improving input current quality and DC bus voltage regulation. The design employs a uni-directional three-level AC/DC converter based on high-efficiency wide-bandgap Renesas GaN devices. A SPWM control strategy, formulated in the d–q reference frame, ensures simple and effective neutral-point voltage balancing. In addition, the rectifier integrates power-quality enhancement features to maintain stable energy conversion under dynamic operating conditions. This reference design demonstrates an efficiency > 98%, a power factor > 0.99, and total harmonic distortion < 3%.

articles.title: Clientes do Nubank relatam problemas com Pix nesta quarta-feira • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Clientes do Nubank relatam problemas com Pix nesta quarta-feira
Usuários do Nubank se queixavam de que não conseguiam realizar pagamentos ou transferências via Pix. Empresa afirma ter solucionado o problema.
Clientes do Nubank estão enfrentando instabilidades no serviço nas primeiras horas da tarde desta quarta-feira (07/10). Nas redes sociais, muitos deles se queixam de dificuldades para enviar valores via Pix ou fazer pagamentos por meio da modalidade.
Em linhas gerais, os usuários afetados pelo problema até conseguem acessar o aplicativo do Nubank e acessar algumas funcionalidades, como consultar saldo ou verificar a fatura do cartão de crédito. Aparentemente, a falha envolve somente operações por Pix.
Há queixas sobre valores ou pagamentos que são realizados via Pix por meio do app do Nubank, mas não chegam ao destino. Em alguns casos, o cliente se depara com uma mensagem que diz que o Nubank está processando a transferência e que exibe um botão para acesso ao histórico de operações para que o usuário não realize transações duplicadas.
Em testes rápidos realizados pelo Tecnoblog, o Nubank funcionou normalmente, tanto para receber quanto para enviar valores via Pix. Mas as queixas nas redes sociais são numerosas, o que sugere que alguns usuários enfrentam problemas, enquanto outros não notaram dificuldades.
No Downdetector, site que registra queixas nas redes sociais sobre instabilidades em plataformas online, o volume de reclamações sobre o problema no Nubank atingiu o pico por volta das 14:00 (de acordo com o horário de Brasília), com cerca de 250 menções.
Como a instabilidade está na plataforma, não no aplicativo, fazer login novamente ou reinstalar o app não são ações que surtirão efeito. A orientação, então, é a de aguardar a operação via Pix ser processada ou, se ela não tiver sido concluída (verifique o histórico para ter certeza), tentar novamente.
Pelo que o Tecnoblog apurou, as operações via Pix no Nubank já estão sendo normalizadas. É o que informa o posicionamento que o Nubank nos enviou:
O Nubank está ciente de uma instabilidade temporária e trabalha para restabelecer os serviços o quanto antes.
Por volta das 15:30 desta quarta-feira, o Nubank nos enviou a seguinte atualização para formalizar a resolução do problema:
O Nubank informa que a instabilidade está integralmente solucionada.

Formula V Line Air Power G10 Chassis Launches in the US
Formula V Line has entered the U.S. market with the Air Power G10, a mid-tower PC case now available through Newegg. First previewed at Computex 2026, the G10 features three front intake fans on independently adjustable brackets, with each fan configurable at 0° or 10° to direct intake air toward areas such as the GPU or CPU.
The Air Power G10 includes four 120 mm PA2 120 PWM/ARGB fans, supports up to 11 × 120 mm fan positions and 360 mm radiators, and features swappable PSU and lower fan positions. Six finishes are available at Newegg, with prices starting at $89.99.Aim Front Intake Toward the GPU or CPU
Instead of fixing all three front fans flat against the chassis, the Air Power G10 mounts each on its own adjustable bracket. Each fan can be set independently at 0° or 10°, allowing builders to direct intake air toward areas such as the graphics card or CPU.
Each fan assembly can also be removed independently for cleaning or replacement.
Swap the PSU and Lower Fan Positions
In the lower chamber, the PSU and lower fan bracket can swap between front and rear positions, letting builders change the bottom layout to suit their hardware and cooling configuration.

The Air Power G10 ships with three 120 mm PA2 120 front intake fans and one PA2 120 rear exhaust fan, featuring 4-pin PWM control and 3-pin ARGB lighting.
The chassis supports up to 11 × 120 mm fan positions in total.
Built for 420 mm GPUs and 360 mm Radiators
The ATX mid-tower accommodates graphics cards up to 420 mm long and 240 mm or 360 mm top radiators.

Six Finishes from $89.99
The Air Power G10 is available in six finishes. Black, Black Rose Gold and Black Wood are priced at $89.99, while White, Black Titanium Silver and Black Dark Blue are priced at $99.99.

articles.title: Florida sues TP-Link for ‘lying about the safety of its routers’ — state claims that manufacturer misrepresented its security and ties to China
articles.text:
Florida sues TP-Link for ‘lying about the safety of its routers’ — state claims that manufacturer misrepresented its security and ties to China
TP-Link is estimated to have 50% to 65% of the consumer router market in the U.S.
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier just announced that the state is suing TP-Link, claiming that the company has been “lying about the safety of its routers and its ties to the CCP.” Uthmeier posted a minute-and-a-half video clip on X, saying that TP-Link’s claims of having safe routers aren’t true.
“Chinese state-sponsored hackers exploited TP-Link routers sitting in American living rooms. Many of those models cannot even update themselves automatically, and TP-Link has stopped supporting them,” the Florida AG said on the social media platform. “They also told Floridians they have split from China and that they build U.S. products in Vietnam, but that is fiction. Research and manufacturing remain rooted in China, less than 1% of the parts in that Vietnam plant actually come from Vietnam. TP-Link now claims to have separated from a company with Chinese ties — a company the Pentagon has designated as an arm of the Chinese military.”
The federal government first investigated the company back in 2024, with the Department of Commerce, Department of Defense, and Department of Justice opening inquiries into the company, with the DOJ looking at whether the company has engaged in unfair trade practices and poses a threat to national security. The company has tried to fight these allegations, especially as it points out that TP-Link in the U.S. has already separated from its Chinese parent company in 2024, and that it has been making its routers in Vietnam since 2018.
Unlike Huawei, TP-Link has been able to avoid a full ban in the United States. However, it’s currently facing a major challenge as the FCC has banned the import of new consumer routers. This ban would affect all router manufacturers, including American brands such as Cisco and Netgear, but they were able to go around this by applying for a conditional approval. TP-Link itself applied for this exemption, too, but it’s unclear if it has received one so far. But even if TP-Link hasn’t secured a conditional approval yet, it could continue selling its already existing router models in the U.S.
Florida isn’t the only state to file a case against TP-Link because of its alleged connections to Beijing and the safety of its routers. Iowa, Nebraska, and Montana have also sued the company for exactly the same reasons, and their attorneys general say that they’re doing it to protect their citizens from the Chinese Communist Party.

articles.title: Ethereum: cuál es el precio de esta criptomoneda este miércoles
articles.text:
Ether, comúnmente llamada como ethereum, es la moneda digital #2 en cuanto a términos de capitalización de mercado, por lo que se trata de una de las divisas digitales que más despierta el interés entre los mineros (creadores de las criptodivisas).
Ethereum es una plataforma de blockchain de código abierto que se ejecuta con el uso de su moneda nativa, llamada ether o ETH, por lo que a pesar de que la gente usa estos nombres como sinónimos son cosas distintas.
Ether es un token que se utiliza específicamente en la blockchain ethereum para pagar transacciones. Este token es responsable de impulsar casi todo lo que ocurre en la red, misma que puede ser usada por cualquier persona para crear y ejecutar contratos inteligentes, que son programas de software que se ejecutan de manera autónoma y sin la intervención del usuario.
De acuerdo con el portal de Binance, la moneda digital solana actualmente cuenta con 122.1M de unidades creadas.
Mientras el debate se acalora cada día más sobre la conveniencia o no de su uso, ethereum cotiza este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) en 2554.75 dólares, lo que supone un cambio de -5.83 % con respecto a las últimas 24 horas y una variación de 0.0 % con referencia a su valor alcanzado en la última hora.
En cuanto a su popularidad de mercado, ha mantenido el puesto #2 entre las monedas digitales.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: RBI removes Paytm Payments Bank from list of scheduled banks
articles.text:
RBI removes Paytm Payments Bank from list of scheduled banks
In April this year, the Reserve Bank of India had cancelled the banking licence issued to Paytm Payments Bank for non-compliance with norms, saying affairs of the bank were conducted in a manner detrimental to the interest of its depositors.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has officially removed Paytm Payments Bank Ltd (PPBL) from the list of recognised scheduled banks following the cancellation of its banking licence.
In April this year, the RBI had cancelled the banking licence issued to PPBL for non-compliance with norms, saying affairs of the bank were conducted in a manner detrimental to the interest of its depositors.
Later, the Delhi High Court ordered that PPBL be wound up.
"Paytm Payments Bank Limited has been excluded from the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934...," the central bank said in a statement on Wednesday.
A notification in this regard was published on July 31 and published in the Gazette of India in September.
The Second Schedule of the RBI Act is the official list of recognised banks that meet the central bank's financial standards and get special operational privileges. 'Scheduled bank' means a bank included in the Second Schedule.
PPBL, an associate firm of Vijay Shekhar Sharma-promoted fintech firm Paytm, came under the regulatory scanner on multiple occasions earlier, including in March 2022 when the central bank barred it from onboarding new customers.
While cancelling the licence, the RBI had said the affairs of the bank were conducted in a manner detrimental to its own interests as well as its depositors.
Earlier, PPBL was directed to stop onboarding new customers with effect from March 11, 2022 amid "material supervisory concerns" observed in the bank. The bank was also directed to appoint an IT audit firm to conduct a comprehensive system audit of its IT system.
Thereafter, on January 31, 2024 and February 16, 2024, certain business restrictions were also imposed on the bank, including disallowing any further deposits/credits/ top-ups in existing customer accounts, prepaid instruments, and wallets.
