articles.title: Stuut cashes in on agentic order-to-cash automation with $52.5M in funding - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Stuut cashes in on agentic order-to-cash automation with $52.5M in funding
Artificial intelligence companies that can help even bigger companies to get paid are likely to make a fair bit of money themselves, if the example of Stuut Inc. is any indication.
The company today said it has closed on a Series B funding round worth $52.5 million, bringing its total amount raised to $93 million to date. What’s really notable about the round isn’t so much the money, but the investors, which are among the biggest venture capital firms in Silicon Valley. Insight Partners led the round, with participation from Andreessen Horowitz and Microsoft Corp.’s M12.
They’re backing Stuut because they believe it’s going to make a lot of people a lot of money. The startup is targeting one of the biggest challenges in doing business today – actually getting paid by your customers and clients. It says it wants to fix a broken order-to-cash process that typically wipes out up to 5% of the average enterprise’s revenue each year. That’s not an insignificant number, as it amounts to more than $1 trillion annually if you consider the amount of revenue the Fortune 500 pulls in each year, Stuut says.
This money is lost because what should be a fairly simple process breaks down due to trivial administrative errors, such as missing purchase orders, bad data or invoices sent to the wrong people. Because of these errors, finance departments have to chase down missing payments manually across multiple different billing and invoicing systems, payment portals and so on. These mini-investigations eat up thousands of hours annually, and that’s where the money is lost.
Stuut thinks it can fix this, and its solution won’t surprise anyone. It’s using AI agents to automate the entire order-to-cash cycle from end-to-end. Its platform covers everything from order management to invoicing, credit to collections, cash applications to payments and even handles disputes.
Even better, its customers don’t have to abandon the existing software they’re using. Stuut integrates its agents directly into existing enterprise resource planning and customer relationship management systems and payment gateways.
Stuut co-founder and Chief Executive Tarek Alaruri explained that for each customer, its platform builds up a “living memory” of its payment behavior and portal quirks, which provides the context it needs to chase up missing payments automatically. “Most businesses don’t have the bandwidth to segment their base or give customers the level of service they deserve,” he said. “By leveraging AI, we’re able to deliver the only solution with continuous learning loops to improve the customer experience, reduce churn and deliver better financial performance.”
According to Alaruri, it’s harder than ever for enterprises to keep up with manual payment collections because of a severe shortage of qualified financial experts. More than 300,000 accountants have left the profession since 2019, which is one of the main reasons why U.S. businesses are chasing a combined $7.2 trillion worth of unpaid receivables. Existing payments and billing software simply organizes things, but it does little in terms of executing the work needed to ensure invoices are paid on time.
By matching more than 95% of incoming payments with orders automatically and facilitating more than 81% of outbound collections without any human intervention, Stuut says it can cut the average customer’s days sales outstanding by 47%. That’s why it has grown its customer base more than fivefold in the last year, processing more than $3 billion worth of payments during that time.
Its client list now extends to more than 150 large enterprises, including Verifone Inc., Bishop Lifting Products Inc. and ZoomInfo Technologies LLC. With ZoomInfo, Stuut was able to help it reduce time-to-first-touch by more than 90% while reducing its days sales outstanding from 51 to just 40 days.
Julian Marcu of Insight Partners said many businesses have more cash tied up in receivables than they realize. “A single invoice error can trigger weeks of follow-up across teams and systems and at scale that adds up to real revenue left on the table,” he explained. “Stuut has figured out how to use agents to execute that recovery process and match cash to invoices while fitting naturally within the controls, workflows and systems finance teams already use.”
Stuut not only aims to help customers get paid faster, but also expand deeper into enterprise financial infrastructure. With the funds from today’s round, it’s going to invest in credit scoring, lending and automated fund movement services, as part of its overall goal of managing businesses’ entire transaction processes, from initial sales to the final bank deposit.

articles.title: Forza Horizon 6 PS5 Port Tipped for January 2027, Disc Included
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
Forza Horizon 6 PS5 Port Tipped for January 2027, Disc Included
Forza Horizon 6 will apparently reach the PlayStation 5 on January 26, 2027, according to billbil-kun, the generally reliable leaker at Dealabs. That would put the port a little over eight months behind the Xbox Series X|S and PC versions, which launched on May 19, and it would miss the 2026 window that Microsoft and Playground Games have been promising since January. The game is also said to be getting a physical disc release on the same day as the digital version. That is a change from Forza Horizon 5, which arrived on PS5 in April 2025 as a digital-only title. Pricing is reportedly set at €69.99 in Europe and £59.99 in the UK, the same as the Xbox version, and billbil-kun expects the US price to land at $69.99.
An official announcement is expected as early as this week, with pre-orders opening shortly after. Of course, neither Microsoft nor Playground Games has confirmed any of this. In early September, the studio's own blog still said the PS5 version would be out "later this year". The Verge's Tom Warren had been saying otherwise since late August, and he later reported that the port was being pushed to early 2027, apparently to coincide with the game's first expansion. It looks like he had it right. PS5 owners should keep an eye out for the official launch date and pre-order details.

articles.title: Un nouveau géant du streaming pourrait voir le jour et défier Netflix et Disney+
articles.text:
Ce 6 octobre 2026, Paramount a finalisé le rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery pour 110 milliards de dollars. Cet accord a abouti à la création d’un nouveau géant du divertissement : Skydance. Celui-ci détient donc deux plateformes de streaming, à savoir Paramount+ et HBO Max (Warner Bros.). Inévitablement, la question de leur sort se pose : une même entreprise va-t-elle maintenir deux plateformes de streaming ? Nous avons un début de réponse : une nouvelle plateforme de streaming devrait bel et bien arriver dans les années à venir.
Paramount rachète Warner Bros. : une nouvelle plateforme de streaming pourrait arriver
David Ellison, le président et PDG de Skydance (l’entreprise qui détient donc Paramount et Warner Bros. Discovery), a expliqué comment allaient évoluer les deux plateformes de streaming : « Dans l’immédiat, vous les verrez donc fonctionner séparément, avec des regroupements ou d’autres initiatives qui s’accéléreront à court terme ». Il précise ensuite : « Cela prendra du temps », tout en ajoutant qu’« À long terme, l’objectif est de les réunir ». En résumé, rien ne change pour l’instant pour les abonnés de Paramount+ et d’HBO Max, mais les deux plateformes seront bel et bien un jour réunies. Il reste maintenant à voir de quelle façon.
Pour rappel, Warner Bros. Discovery (HBO Max) détient Harry Potter, Le Seigneur des Anneaux, Game of Thrones, The Big Bang Theory, Friends, Les Sopranos, Rick et Morty, The White Lotus ou encore The Wire, pour ne citer que ces exemples. De son côté, Paramount possède South Park (Comedy Central), Mission : Impossible, Transformers, Yellowstone, Star Trek ou encore Bob l’éponge.
Il serait tout de même peu probable qu’HBO Max soit relégué à un simple onglet sur Paramount+, et inversement. Le plus logique serait la création d’une nouvelle plateforme de streaming qui proposerait directement tous les programmes des deux plateformes de streaming, mais il s’agit pour l’instant seulement d’une hypothèse. Par ailleurs, il serait judicieux que les deux entités gardent leurs identités marquées. Autant dire que l’équation n’est pas simple.
Il reste également la question du prix des abonnements. L’offre standard d’HBO Max coûte actuellement 10,99 € par mois, tandis que l’abonnement standard de Paramount+ s’élève à 7,99 € par mois. Avoir un accès aux deux catalogues impliquerait inévitablement des prix supérieurs à ceux-ci. Il faut aussi préciser qu’en rachetant Warner Bros. Discovery, Skydance a récupéré 80 milliards de dollars de dettes. De plus, la nouvelle entreprise doit réaliser pas moins de 6 milliards de dollars d’économies dans les prochaines années. Autrement dit, l’abonnement à une offre regroupant HBO Max et Paramount+ ne devrait pas s’élever à une dizaine d’euros.
Quoi qu’il en soit, les 80 millions d’abonnés de Paramount+ et les 140 millions d’abonnés de HBO Max devraient donc être réunis, et cela a de quoi inquiéter Netflix, Disney+, Apple TV ou encore Prime Video.
Les plateformes de streaming établissent petit à petit des partenariats
Pendant longtemps, les plateformes de streaming ont évolué chacune de leur côté, mais cette stratégie semble maintenant connaître ses limites. Comme le rapporte Variety, Disney+ vient par exemple de signer un accord avec Netflix permettant à ce dernier de diffuser certains de ses programmes. Ainsi, depuis ce 4 octobre, les deux premières saisons de Percy Jackson, ainsi que les cinq films L’Âge de glace, sont disponibles sur Netflix à l’international. Les films d’animation Soul et Elio (Pixar) arriveront sur la plateforme de streaming au N rouge début 2027. D’autres programmes de Disney arriveront sur Netflix au cours de l’année prochaine.
La plateforme de streaming Prime Video intègre quant à elle dorénavant Apple TV, sous la forme d’un abonnement complémentaire au prix de 9,99 € par mois. Autant dire que si une nouvelle plateforme de streaming regroupant HBO Max et Paramount+ arrive, ces types de partenariats risquent de se consolider et de se multiplier.

articles.title: Atlassian lays groundwork for humans and AI agents to work side by side - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Atlassian lays groundwork for humans and AI agents to work side by side
Atlassian Corp. today announced Agentic Multiplayer Protocol, a platform update designed to change how humans and artificial intelligence agents collaborate and get work done using shared context and tasks within the same digital space.
At the unveiling at Team ‘26 Europe, Atlassian said it wants AI agents to function like employees and bring what it calls “multiplayer” into a fully governed system of work so humans and agents can operate side by side in the open.
AMP is designed to give every agent the data context they need to be useful and limitations to stay safe within the confines of the platform – this includes an identity assigned by administration, including authority and scope.
“This is a multiplayer game,” Head of AI Product Jamil Valliani told SiliconANGLE in an interview. “Humans and agents are working together in a very dynamic space, and there are lots of players.”
However, agents cannot run rampant. Valliani added that Atlassian has an internal statement: “Headless software means brainless software.” The company’s role isn’t merely to provide software for autonomous agents to connect to and operate without people; autonomy is useful, but it isn’t useful without teamwork.
Rovo, the company’s AI assistant that became an autonomous powerhouse, can disappear for hours doing work, but the user sets and guides the objective, reviews the proposed plan, course-corrects it and ultimately reviews the result.
To tackle this, Atlassian announced Rovo Work, a new mode for Rovo Chat that handles complex, multi-step tasks that humans review and approve. It is designed for long-horizon tasks.
“When you opt to send a query to Rovo Work, you’re actually giving Rovo permission to go and actually unleash itself fully,” Valliani said.
In fact, Rovo can go a step further than straightforward work completion. For example, when Work is asked to approach a task it is unfamiliar with, and it doesn’t have what it needs in its model training data, it will attempt to train itself.
In one case, a product manager asked Work for an Instagram-ready reel. Instead of using whatever it had associated with its base model, Rovo researched the right instructions, learned what it needed for the output format, and got tooling for video synthesis.
This is materially different from the standard AI model approach of “is this already available in my training?” to “how do I learn to do this?”
Valliani also confirmed that for power users, Rovo could generate custom skills as part of its work. Although this is a separately supported capability, rather than every learned behavior becoming a skill users can export.
“We can’t really imagine the creativity our customers are going to ask it to unleash,” Valliani said. “We want customers to go and challenge it, and tell it what they really want.”
Loom: Replacing prompt engineering with “show me what you mean”
Atlassian is also bringing something to everyday users that developers have been using with agents in coding for a long time: showing instead of telling.
Loom is a product Atlassian produces that allows users to record video of themselves and their computer screen and share with one another to provide instruction. It can also be used to instruct agents. For example, Loom can be used to draw circles around parts of the user interface, show buttons being clicked and information being entered into fields.
The problem with AI agents isn’t always intelligence. Sometimes humans have trouble explaining in words what they want, but if they can visually point out what they need along with words: “Make this larger, move this, turn it green.” That makes the entire process trivial. Two humans looking at the same screen while speaking to one another have the same context and they have a visual “prompt” plus the words.
“With Loom, it’ll actually capture you saying all that, and the actual references on screen that you’re pointing to when you say it, and then format it into the prompt,” Valliani said.
Atlassian broadens the envelope around code and context for developers
For developers, Atlassian’s broader platform changes amount to an expanded context and operating environment for AI agents.
Unveiled today, Rovo Code Search brings the source itself into the Teamwork Graph, a centralized data intelligence and context engine that maps relationships among people, code and documents. Data Context extends that view into structured information stored in platforms such as Databricks Inc., Snowflake Inc. and Google LLC’s BigQuery. Together, they give agents a wider picture of not only how software is built, but the business information surrounding why it is being built.
The company’s expanded Model Context Protocol server also gives external coding and AI agents a common interface into its platform. Valliani said a substantial portion of those interactions now involve agents writing information back, not just retrieving it. MCP turns Atlassian from a data source into part of the shared workspace where agents leave work for humans and other agents to pick up.
Atlassian’s MCP server now exposes 200 tools and handles roughly 15 million tool calls daily.
This calls back to the company’s desire to make agents part of the team and the “multiplayer” wording, giving agents a place in the company, roles and permissions.
Imagine an AI agent working in Confluence, the company’s knowledge management and document collaboration digital workspace similar to an internal centralized wiki, and it sees another agent or human editing the same document. Because all pages are live and structured, it would know it’s collaborating with another teammate in real time, check for any edits and adjust its approach.

articles.title: Fusées : l'infrastructure au sol ne suit plus la cadence du secteur
articles.text:
Réutilisables et de plus en plus nombreuses, les fusées décollent à un rythme qui ne cesse de s’accélérer. Mais pour les accueillir l’industrie occidentale compte encore majoritairement sur des infrastructures héritées d’une tout autre époque.
Les chiffres donnent le tournis. À Cap Canaveral, en Floride, 110 lancements ont été réalisés l’année dernière, contre seulement 36 en 2021. Une hausse que l’on peut évidemment attribuer à la cadence folle de SpaceX et de son Falcon 9, alors que d’autres acteurs arrivent progressivement sur le marché. Dans ce contexte, la Space Force vise pas moins de 3 000 tirs annuels d’ici à 2036. En clair, les calculs ne sont pas bons.
De nombreux facteurs à prendre en compte
D’autant que les capacités de lancement n’incluent pas uniquement le pas de tir, mais aussi la gestion du trafic aérien, le suivi des fusées, la fourniture de carburants et de gaz, l’électricité, les routes, etc. Si un seul élément ne suit pas, c’est tout le système qui est ralenti, alerte l’ancien responsable des partenariats de la NASA, Philip Metzger, dans une tribune publiée dans Space News.
D’ailleurs, l’inspecteur de la NASA s’inquiétait déjà de la situation dans un rapport publié en juin, dans lequel il affirmait que le centre spatial Kennedy, en Floride, et la base de Wallops, en Virginie, approcheront de leur capacité maximale en 2028-2029. Il a ainsi identifié les trois points faibles du réseau actuel : le réseau d’azote et d’hélium incapable de servir plusieurs utilisateurs à la fois, une électricité utilisée au-delà de sa durée de vie prévue, et environ 19 000 trajets de camions supplémentaires par an sur des routes vieillissantes.
En parallèle, les budgets d’infrastructures de lancement de la NASA ont reculé de 11 à 47 % en cinq ans, sans prendre en compte l’inflation. Un véritable goulot d’étranglement.
Rénover ou construire ?
Face à ces limites, l’expert plaide d’abord pour moderniser l’existant, souvent plus rapide et moins coûteux. Par exemple, le pas de tir 39A, loué par la NASA à SpaceX en 2014, accueillait des Falcon 9 moins de trois ans plus tard. Mais bâtir de nouveaux sites s’avère également nécessaire, selon lui. Il n’y a qu’à voir SpaceX, actuellement en train d’agrandir sa base de Starbase, au Texas, tout en construisant un nouveau complexe gigantesque en Louisiane.
Car en parallèle, la Chine n’attend pas et continue de renforcer ses capacités de lancement. Elle a inauguré, fin 2024, le site de Hainan, qui doit faciliter plus de 60 tirs annuels, et a récemment ouvert un port spatial en mer.

articles.title: Amit Kumar named Google Cloud India interim head; Sashikumar Sreedharan steps down
articles.text:
Amit Kumar named Google Cloud India interim head; Sashikumar Sreedharan steps down
Amit Kumar, who was serving as Managing Director for Digital Natives at Google Cloud India, will step in to lead the India operations.
Google Cloud India Managing Director Sashikumar Sreedharan has stepped down from his role to pursue an external opportunity, with Amit Kumar named as the interim head of the company's India operations, a senior company official said on Wednesday.
The leadership transition was announced by Karan Bajwa, President of Google Cloud Asia Pacific, in a post on LinkedIn.
"Our momentum in India has never been stronger, fuelled by accelerating business and AI growth across the market. As we continue to build our next phase of growth, I want to personally thank Sashikumar Sreedharan, who is moving on from Google to an external opportunity," Bajwa wrote.
He noted that Sreedharan has served in multiple roles during his tenure with Google Cloud, initially as the Chief Operating Officer (COO) for the Asia Pacific (APAC) region and later as the Managing Director for India.
Amit Kumar, who was serving as Managing Director for Digital Natives at Google Cloud India, will step in to lead the India operations.
"As Amit Kumar steps in as interim leader for Google Cloud India, our focus remains clear: building on our incredible momentum. The opportunity ahead for our customers and partners in India has never been bigger, and I'm energised for what our team will deliver next," Bajwa said.
Sreedharan is said to have joined AI firm Sarvam AI as its President and Chief Business Officer.
Before leading Google Cloud India, Sreedharan was Chief Operating Officer of Google Cloud APAC, starting in September 2023. Prior to that, he served as managing director at Microsoft India for over five years, leading its enterprise business. He has also held leadership roles at organisations like SAP and IBM.
(With inputs from PTI.)

articles.title: Un dispositivo de Nvidia que llevaba 7 años en el mercado con el mismo precio subió 100 dólares por culpa de la IA
articles.text:
Nvidia aumentó en 100 dólares el precio de la Shield TV Pro, un reproductor multimedia que lleva siete años en el mercado y cuya última generación fue presentada en 2019. El dispositivo pasó de costar 199,99 dólares a 299,99 dólares, en una decisión que la compañía atribuye al incremento en el precio de componentes tecnológicos, especialmente la memoria.
El caso refleja una consecuencia cada vez más visible del auge de la inteligencia artificial: la enorme demanda de memoria, almacenamiento y otros componentes utilizados para construir centros de datos y sistemas de IA también está presionando los costos de productos destinados al consumidor.
La nueva tarifa comenzó a aplicarse el 2 de octubre. Un portavoz de Nvidia confirmó a Ars Technica que el aumento responde al incremento sustancial del costo de los componentes en todo el sector.
Un dispositivo de 2019 que ahora cuesta 100 dólares más
La Shield TV Pro más reciente fue presentada en 2019 con Android TV, un procesador Tegra X1+ y funciones que, para ese momento, destacaban frente a otros reproductores multimedia. Entre ellas se encontraba el escalado de imagen mediante inteligencia artificial, una tecnología capaz de mejorar la apariencia de determinados contenidos al aumentar su resolución.
El equipo también permite reproducir una amplia variedad de formatos de video mediante decodificación por hardware y puede utilizarse como servidor multimedia Plex, características que han mantenido su atractivo entre usuarios más avanzados.
Cuando llegó al mercado, la Shield TV Pro tenía un precio de 199,99 dólares. También existía una versión estándar de 149,99 dólares, aunque ese modelo dejó de comercializarse.
Ahora, el modelo Pro cuesta 299,99 dólares, un incremento cercano al 50 % respecto de su precio original. El cambio resulta llamativo porque no se trata de una nueva generación con mejores componentes, sino del mismo dispositivo que Nvidia comenzó a vender hace siete años.
La inteligencia artificial también encarece productos antiguos
Nvidia explicó que el aumento está relacionado con el costo de los componentes, incluida la memoria. La situación muestra cómo el crecimiento de la infraestructura necesaria para desarrollar inteligencia artificial puede terminar afectando productos que no tienen relación directa con los centros de datos.
La compañía necesita componentes similares a los utilizados por otros fabricantes de dispositivos electrónicos y compite por ellos en un mercado donde la demanda asociada a la IA ha crecido de forma acelerada.
El fenómeno también ha afectado a otros productos tecnológicos. Las consolas de videojuegos, por ejemplo, han experimentado aumentos de precio durante su ciclo comercial. La PlayStation 5 Pro pasó de 699,99 dólares en su lanzamiento en 2024 a 899,99 dólares actualmente.
En el caso de Nvidia, la situación resulta especialmente llamativa porque la empresa es uno de los principales proveedores de procesadores y aceleradores utilizados para inteligencia artificial. Sus GPU se han convertido en piezas fundamentales para los centros de datos que entrenan y ejecutan modelos generativos.
Nvidia todavía fabrica la Shield TV Pro
La compañía había señalado anteriormente que continúa fabricando la Shield TV Pro y que vende prácticamente todas las unidades que produce. Por ello, el dispositivo no depende únicamente de existencias antiguas fabricadas antes del actual aumento de costos.
Las existencias del reproductor han sido escasas durante los últimos meses, una situación que podría estar relacionada con las dificultades para producir nuevas unidades a precios anteriores.
El nuevo precio puede hacer que la Shield TV Pro resulte menos atractiva para quienes buscan únicamente un dispositivo para acceder a Netflix, YouTube u otros servicios de streaming.
Su principal ventaja sigue estando en funciones más específicas, como la compatibilidad con numerosos formatos multimedia, el procesamiento de imagen y la posibilidad de utilizarla como servidor Plex. Para quienes no necesitan esas características, existen reproductores más económicos.

articles.title: Llega a Lidl el viernes 9 de octubre (por 9,99 euros) el reloj radiocontrolado con termómetro ideal para cocinas y baños
articles.text:
Se acerca el último domingo de octubre y, con él, el cambio de horario de verano al de invierno. Lo que se traduce en tener que retrasar a mano una hora (en la madrugada del sábado 24 al domingo 25) todos aquellos relojes que no lo hacen automáticamente.
Pero desde este mismo viernes, 9 de octubre, según indica en su folleto, Lidl pone a la venta varios modelos de relojes radiocontrolados que realizan este ajuste (y otros tantos) de forma automática. Llegan a las tiendas de Lidl a un precio de 9,99 euros y ya podemos conseguirlos en Lidl online. Como alternativa, Amazon también vende algunos modelos similares en prestaciones que rondan los 25 euros.
Reloj de pared
Con ajuste automático de la hora y disponible en varios colores
El aspecto más diferencial de este reloj a la venta en Lidl desde este viernes es que ajusta automáticamente la hora mediante radiofrecuencia. Esto supone que cambia entre los horarios de verano e invierno sin que tengamos que tocar nada, además de realizar constantemente un ajuste automático de la hora. Así, se elimina ese pequeño desfase habitual de los relojes manuales y evita tener que ponerlos en hora cada cierto tiempo.
Este reloj está disponible en tres modelos diferentes y todos ellos ofrecen más información además de la hora: dos son de aguja y añaden una pequeña pantalla con la temperatura, mientras que el otro es totalmente digital y recoge mucha más información ambiental (la hora, la fecha, el día de la semana, la temperatura y también la humedad).
Cuenta con cuatro ventosas en la parte posterior, lo que permite colocarlo con seguridad en azulejos de cocinas y baños, aunque también se puede usar de pie en cualquier superficie que permita usar sus ventosas. Estando especialmente pensado para cocinas y baños por su resistencia a salpicaduras y la humedad que suele derivar de cocinar y ducharnos. Aunque también encaja de maravilla en salones, dormitorios y vestidores.

articles.title: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,600, running Nvidia's RTX Spark chip
articles.text:
Something to look forward to: Microsoft has just revealed the starting price and release date for its new ultra-tier Surface laptop, along with other notebooks powered by Nvidia's RTX Spark SoC. The company's flagship model is expensive, even next to the MacBook Pro it's meant to rival, but it remains to be seen how RTX Spark stacks up against Apple's M5 Pro.
Pre-orders are now open for the Surface Laptop Ultra and other laptops built on the same Arm-based SoC, which marks Nvidia's entry into the PC CPU market. Microsoft's model starts at $2,600 with 24GB of unified memory.
As previously revealed, the base configuration uses a variant of Nvidia's new RTX Spark SoC with 5,120 Blackwell CUDA cores and an 18-core Arm-based CPU. The notebook can be configured with 24GB, 32GB, 48GB, 64GB, or 128GB of unified LPDDR5X memory, potentially offering the most addressable memory ever on an RTX GPU.
Buyers can choose a 512GB PCIe 4.0 SSD or a PCIe 5.0 drive with 1TB or 2TB of storage, both removable.
Nvidia and Microsoft mostly promoted RTX Spark's local AI horsepower, but its gaming capabilities could also have a significant impact on the Arm and integrated GPU markets.
The top-end RTX Spark chip pairs a 20-core CPU with an integrated GPU of 6,144 CUDA cores, which Nvidia claims performs like the laptop version of the RTX 5070. Microsoft confirmed that Gears of War: E-Day will natively support the chip and Windows on Arm, with Call of Duty to follow in 2027, joining other games from EA, Ubisoft, and Sega. RTX Spark is the first laptop SoC to support Nvidia DLSS, G-Sync, Reflex, and RTX ray tracing.
Microsoft's new flagship laptop features a 15-inch 4K touchscreen with Dolby Vision IQ support and refresh rates up to 120Hz. The company rates the battery for up to 15 hours of local video playback and 12 hours of web browsing.
Among the Surface Laptop Ultra's ports is the first-ever built-in magnetic USB-C charging port, which charges at up to 140W. The other two USB-C ports support DisplayPort 2.1 and, together with the HDMI 2.1b port, can drive up to three 4K displays at 60Hz. A USB-A port rounds out the lineup.
Other RTX Spark laptops shipping on October 16 include the Dell XPS 16, HP OmniBook Ultra 16, Lenovo Yoga Pro 9n, MSI Prestige N16 Flip AI+, and Asus ProArt P16.
Pricing is now available for most of them: the Asus and MSI notebooks start at $3,400 and $3,300, respectively, while the Dell, HP, and Lenovo models are listed at $3,800, $3,200, and around $3,000.
Microsoft also opened pre-orders for the RTX Spark Dev Box. Starting at $6,000, it includes the full-fat RTX Spark SoC and up to 1 petaflop of local AI compute.

articles.title: Petit, léger, mais fragile : notre avis sans concession sur le SSD portable Kioxia Exceria Plus G2
articles.text:
| Capacité de stockage | 500 Go, 1 To, 2 To | 
| Type de stockage | SSD | 
| Interface | USB 3.2 Gen2 2x2 | 
| Vitesse lecture | 1050 Mo/s | 
Le Kioxia Exceria Plus G2 Portable est un SSD externe portable compatible avec l'interface USB-C 3.2 Gen2 2x2. Il est disponible en version 500 Go, 1 To et 2 To de stockage.
Après avoir passé la gamme 2025 de SSD internes de Kioxia sur notre banc de test, c'est désormais au tour du module Exceria Plus G2 Portable de recevoir les honneurs d'un test chez Les Numériques. Il s'agit du premier SSD externe portable de la marque japonaise à intégrer le comparatif dédié, et il arrive dans un contexte plus que compliqué pour l'industrie de l'informatique. Comme pour la concurrence, les tarifs de vente des modules de stockage ont vu effectivement leur tarif passer du simple au double au cours de la période. C'est donc sans surprise que le Kioxia Exceria Plus G2 Portable, lancé autour de la centaine d'euros dans sa version 1 To, s'échange désormais à quelque 200 € chez les revendeurs.
Côté specs, le Kioxia Exceria Plus G2 Portable affiche une compatibilité avec l'interface USB-C 3.2 Gen 2x2, comme c'est la norme sur la plupart des SSD externes portables commercialisés aujourd'hui, mais il se limite à la norme 10 Gb/s, ce qui le place d'emblée derrière certains des autres modules plus véloces de notre comparatif. À voir si Kioxia a d'autres tours dans son sac.
Sur le front des performances, il ne faut pas s'attendre à plus que les chiffres annoncés sur le cahier des charges. Et ce n'est pas un mal puisque la norme 10 Gb/s affichée est respectée sur nos benchmarks réalisés via CrystalDiskMark, avec une moyenne de débits séquentiels de 1057 Mo/s en lecture et 1012 Mo/s en écriture. À peine devant le Crucial X9 Pro, donc, et loin derrière les Samsung T9 (20 Gb/s) et le Corsair EX400U (40 Gb/s).
Comme d'habitude, les différences s'aplanissent lors des benchmarks pratiques de copie manuelle, notamment celle de 800 fichiers photos, où le Kioxia fait presque jeu égal avec la concurrence. L'Exceria Plus G2 Portable reste néanmoins derrière les autres modèles du comparatif lors de la copie d'une archive de 27 Go.
À première vue, l'Exceria Plus G2 Portable ne cache rien de particulier, si ce n'est la petitesse de son format. Ses dimensions très réduites (7,2 x 4 x 1,2 cm) s'accompagnent d'un poids plume pour en faire l'un des SSD externes les plus légers et transportables de notre comparatif, aux côtés de (feue) la série Crucial X9 et X10 de Micron. Cette sobriété s'accompagne néanmoins de quelques manques, notamment les certifications IP et la résistance aux chutes. Aucune résistance ni protection particulière n'est à signaler, alors gare aux chutes malencontreuses qui pourraient nuire à l'intégrité des données stockées. On note la présence d'une petite led d'activité située à côté du port USB-C.
Le Kioxia Exceria Plus G2 Portable ne crée pas la surprise. Pour le bon et le mauvais, le cahier des charges du constructeur japonais est respecté avec des débits décents, mais limités par la norme 10 Gb/s. Nous regrettons avant tout l'absence de certification IP ou de toute protection antichocs, ainsi que d'une option de cryptage.
À tarif peu ou prou égal en fonction des fluctuations du marché des puces mémoire, nous préférons recommander le Samsung T9 plus résistant, ou un Crucial X10 Pro plus véloce.

articles.title: Motorola Edge 70 (512 GB) tem oferta histórica em 12x sem juros na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Motorola Edge 70 (512 GB) tem oferta histórica em 12x sem juros na Amazon
Motorola Edge 70 com câmeras de 50 MP e tela POLED de 4.500 nits atinge o menor preço histórico; dispositivo tem desconto de 58% em promoção parcelada e com cupom
O Motorola Edge 70 de 512 GB está saindo por R$ 2.302 em até 12x sem juros com cupom de R$ 656 disponível na página da Amazon. O celular da Motorola com câmeras de 50 MP e tela POLED de 120 Hz atinge o menor preço histórico, com desconto de 58% sobre o original de R$ 5.499.
Um dos lançamentos recentes da Motorola, o Edge 70 possui uma tela POLED de 6,7″ com taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de 4.500 nits, sendo capaz de reproduzir imagens com cores vibrantes e alta fluidez nas transições, além de ter visibilidade em qualquer lugar. O vidro Gorilla Glass 7i protege-a contra quedas e pancadas.
Seu chip Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 e os 12 GB de RAM física sustentam a execução de apps pesados em multitarefa e soluções da suíte Moto AI. Os 512 GB de armazenamento oferecem espaço interno de sobra para guardar fotos e vídeos.

articles.title: PA measles outbreak tops 1,000 cases, largest since disease was eliminated
articles.text:
Pennsylvania’s explosive measles outbreak is now the largest the US has seen since the highly infectious virus was declared eliminated in 2000. With well over 1,000 cases, it’s the largest on record since 1991.
Pennsylvania’s health officials reported 1,078 measles cases in all of 2026 as of this afternoon. That includes 12 cases in January and March, with the remaining 1,066 cases since April, when the current outbreak began. The tally includes 145 cases recorded in the last seven days and 74 identified since the previous update on Monday. Health officials noted that 40 of the 74 cases added today were from more than two weeks ago and are just now being recorded.
Among the cases, there have been 207 hospitalizations and five deaths—a newborn, a 6-week-old, an 18-year-old, a 20-year-old, and a 40-year-old. All of the deaths occurred during the current outbreak in people who were unvaccinated; the two infants were too young to have been vaccinated.
With slipping vaccination rates nationwide, measles outbreaks and cases have come roaring back in the past few years. A large outbreak in Texas that spanned January–August 2025 ended with 762 cases, while an outbreak in South Carolina ended in April with 997 cases, the previous record holder. Pennsylvania exceeds that handily with its 1,066 outbreak-linked cases as of today. With 34 new infections reported since Monday, the outbreak does not appear to be close to ending.
Measles emergency
Measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. Elimination is earned and maintained with vaccination rates that prevent continuous transmission of the virus during a 12-month period. In November, experts at the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO)—which acts as a regional office for the World Health Organization—will review data on whether the US has lost its measles elimination status. Experts widely expect the US has lost the status. Canada lost its elimination status in 2025.

articles.title: Bell, Nova Scotia bring fibre internet to remote island communities
articles.text:
Bell and the Government of Nova Scotia have announced the completion of a “major” broadband infrastructure project to communities located on the Big and Little Tancook Islands.
The project will bring high-speed fibre internet access to approximately 184 homes and businesses on the islands, and will help “connect one of Nova Scotia’s most remote island communities to new opportunities for work, education, healthcare, and economic growth.”
The press release also notes that to connect the communities, Bell deployed about 7 kilometres of submarine fibre cable and built an additional 8 kilometres of fibre infrastructure on the islands.
It was also mentioned that, before the connection, the communities largely relied on a mix of wireless and satellite technologies for internet access. From experience, these options are liveable, but they can struggle under heavier workloads like online gaming, consistent streaming, or video calls.
“Reliable fibre internet can transform opportunities for island communities,” says Mark McDonald, Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer at Bell. “Working closely with the Government of Nova Scotia and Build Nova Scotia, we delivered an innovative subsea fibre project that will help residents and businesses on Big and Little Tancook Islands stay connected and thrive.”
To add some context, Bell has received a lot of coverage for similar connectivity projects. Back in September 2025, Bell announced a major project to expand and enhance its wireless service in 224 communities across the country by early this year.
Source: Bell

articles.title: Microsoft blocks Outlook from sending two more file types over security concerns
articles.text:
Microsoft blocks Outlook from sending two more file types over security concerns
Say goodbye to .msix and .msixbundle files in your email
- Microsoft will block .msix and .msixbundle email attachments in New Outlook and Outlook Web
- Change aims to reduce malware delivery through application package files sent via email
- Organizations relying on these formats must explicitly allow them before rollout begins
Users of New Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the Web in Exchange Online will no longer be able to download email attachments of two file types: .msix, and .msixbundle, Microsoft has confirmed, saying it’s for the users’ own safety.
“To enhance security in Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, we are updating the default list of blocked file types in OwaMailboxPolicy,” a newly released advisory reads.
“As part of this update, the .msix and .msixbundle file types will be added to the BlockedFileTypes list in the default OWA Mailbox policy and any custom policies created in your tenant.”
What are .msix and .msixbundle files?
MSIX is a file format for packaging and installing applications. It is similar to .exe and .msi installer since it contains files and information Windows needs to install an application. Microsoft introduced .msix as a more modern and secure way of distributing software, saying it comes with features that make installing and updating software more reliable.
MSIXBUNDLE is, as the name might suggest, the same but in plural. It can contain several versions of an .msix package in a single file. For example, a developer can bundle versions designed for different processor architectures (x64 and ARM, for example), and Windows will automatically install the correct one. Both formats are commonly used to distribute Windows applications, including apps delivered through the Microsoft Store.
How big of a deal is this?
Apparently, not that big of a deal. Microsoft itself says that “most organizations are not expected to be affected by this update,” given the fact that these file types are “infrequently used.” However, they seem to be used frequently enough to warrant an update.
“This update is part of our ongoing efforts to strengthen security and help protect organizations from potentially unsafe file attachments,” Microsoft added.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Truth be told, sending application packages as email attachments is hardly the primary way businesses distribute software today. Employees usually do that through managed company portals, the Microsoft Store, package management tools, or direct downloads from software vendors. Therefore, we can assume that the majority of .msix and .msixbundle being sent through email could be malicious and weaponized.
General rollout will begin in early November 2026 and is expected to be complete by mid-November, the advisory reads. Exchange Online administrators who manage OWA mailbox policies are generally affected, as well as those who usually send or receive .msix or .msixbundle attachments in Outlook on the web or new Outlook for Windows Platforms and services. Obviously users of Outlook for the web, New Outlook for Windows, and Exchange Online, too.
So, in roughly a month, these two file types will be added to the BlockedFileTypes list in all OWA Mailbox policies across organizations, including the default policy and any custom policies created across tenants, preventing users from downloading them as attachments, or running them that way, at all.
Organizations that don’t rely on these two file types won’t need to do anything, but those that do should add them to the AllowedFileTypes property of their users’ OwaMailboxPolicy objects prior to rollout.
Defending email users from themselves
For years now, Microsoft has been adding different file types to the “blacklist”, in an effort to prevent users from downloading and running malicious attachments sent in phishing emails. As The Register reminds, in December 2023, the company disabled ms-appinstaller protocol handler by default, after it was abused to distribute malware.
Since then, Microsoft has also blocked .py (Python files), .ps1 (PowerShell files), and .cab (cabinet files). Some people found it surprising it took Microsoft this long to remember .msix and .msixbundle types, as well.
Via The Register

This monster RTX 5090 Alienware gaming PC costs less than buying the GPU and CPU alone — take $500 off a powerful 9950X3D rig
Buy a PC once, then never think about it again.
Nvidia's RTX 5090 now costs $7,000. Or so near to it that it makes no difference. So if you were hoping to buy one in the quest to build a PC, you're out of luck. The PC gaming industry has been decimated by AI. This is a great example of a product that has drastically increased in price in just a few short months, but prices continue to rise, and the window to buy a gaming rig is closing fast.

articles.title: Consumer tech brand Lumio raises $12M led by Blume Ventures
articles.text:
Consumer tech brand Lumio raises $12M led by Blume Ventures
Lumio will use this funding towards R&D, product branding and hiring of talent.
Lumio, the consumer tech brand from Circuit House Technologies, has raised $12 million in a Series A round of funding led by Blume Ventures, with participation from existing investors Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital.
Circuit House Technologies said it will use the capital for growing the Lumio brand, for R&D, and hiring of talent.
Launched in 2025, Lumio's range of products include smart TV, projectors, and speakers.
"In about a year and a half, we have shown we can build products Indian households want, across more than one category. This round lets us invest in the two things that compound: a brand people trust in their living room, and R&D that keeps bringing new categories and devices into the home," said Kailash Sankaranarayanan, Co-founder and COO, Circuit House Technologies.
A statement from the company said, it has crossed Rs 100 crore in gross merchandise value (GMV) within 13 months of commercial sales. Lumio now serves more than 35,000 households across 5,000+ pin codes.
Following this funding, Lumio plans to expand into newer categories and devices for the home segment while also going deeper into its existing categories. It also plans to have an offline retail presence.
Also, Lumio plans to increase its headcount which will enable it to provide wider after sales coverage.
“India's 30-35 million affluent households are reimagining their living rooms, and no longer default to legacy brands. Raghu and Kailash have leveraged their deep experience in home entertainment and customer insights to create a compelling home entertainment brand in Lumio, with nearly half of Lumio's customers upgrading from legacy brands,” said Sajith Pai, Partner at Blume Ventures.
"The backing of our existing investors and the addition of Blume Ventures is a powerful endorsement of our mission to transform the living room experience, reflecting their shared belief in our vision and the progress we have made in a short span of time" said Raghu Reddy, Co-founder and CEO, Circuit House Technologies.

articles.title: Nouvelle cyberattaque en France : 1 400 hôtels potentiellement piratés, des arnaques déjà en cours
articles.text:
Les cyberattaques continuent en France. Après la Région Hauts-de-France et l’enseigne LDLC, c’est maintenant au tour de Medialog d’être victime d’une cyberattaque. 1 400 établissements hôtelier sont potentiellement concernés. Environ 135 Go de données auraient été extraites, comprenant des informations relatives à l’identité, aux coordonnées et aux réservations des clients des hôtels touchés. Si Medialog a appelé les établissements concernés à réagir, les campagnes de phishing ont déjà débuté.
Des clients d’hôtels pris pour cible
Comme le rapporte le média spécialisé French Breaches, le logiciel de gestion hôtelière Medialog Hôtel a été victime d’une cyberattaque. Ce logiciel, développé par l’éditeur parisien Medialog, permet notamment aux hôtels de gérer les réservations, les données de leurs clients et leur séjour. Le logiciel est utilisé par 1 400 établissements. Les clients des hôtels qui utilisent le logiciel Medialog Hôtel sont donc directement concernés.
Pour être plus précis, les pirates ont exploité une vulnérabilité d’un service web pour s’introduire dans le système de Medialog. Si des accès non autorisés ont été détectés entre le 27 septembre et le 5 octobre 2026, l’essentiel de l’extraction de données a eu lieu dans la nuit du 4 au 5 octobre. Il n’est par ailleurs pas possible d’exclure des accès antérieurs au 16 septembre.
Quelles données ont été dérobées ?
Environ 135 gigaoctets de données auraient été extraites. Parmi les données volées, nous retrouvons des informations relatives à l’identité (nom, date et lieu de naissance, nationalité), aux coordonnées (adresse postale, e-mail, téléphone), aux réservations (dates de séjour, chambre, voucher, arrhes) et aux préférences et appréciations des clients. À noter que les réservations sont aussi concernées (dates de séjour, chambre, numéro de voucher, montant des acomptes, etc.). Medialog assure que ni les informations bancaires des clients ni leur carte d’identité n’ont été volées durant cette cyberattaque. La société française a recommandé aux établissements qui utilisent son logiciel de notifier la CNIL et d’informer leurs clients concernés.
À l’heure actuelle, nous ne connaissons pas la liste des hôtels touchés ni le nombre de clients concernés. Dans tous les cas, il faut s’attendre à une vague de phishing mobilisant des noms d’hôtel. Les arnaqueurs peuvent par exemple vous faire croire qu’il est obligatoire de payer un acompte avant d’arriver à l’hôtel, tout en affichant vos données personnelles.
En réalité, les campagnes de phishing ont déjà commencé. Comme l’alerte sur X Seblatombe, expert en cybersécurité, des clients d’hôtels reçoivent actuellement sur WhatsApp et par e-mail des messages les incitant à cliquer sur un lien pour soi-disant vérifier une réservation.
 🔴 Fuite Medialog : les arnaques commencent déjà
Des clients d’hôtels sont ciblés sur WhatsApp et par e-mail avec leurs véritables informations de réservation. Les messages les redirigent vers un faux site leur demandant de renseigner leurs coordonnées bancaires. https://t.co/hUdieLxp8E pic.twitter.com/NJomv6adla
— Seb (@seblatombe) October 6, 2026
En réalité, il n’est aucunement question d’une vérification de réservation. Le site frauduleux vers lequel la victime est redirigée est programmé pour enregistrer les données saisies (coordonnées bancaires, nom, adresse, etc.). Prudence donc.

articles.title: Un joven programador lanzó un asistente de IA que no guarda ningún dato en la nube
articles.text:
Una startup de Silicon Valley llamada Conway Research lanzó Underdog, un asistente de inteligencia artificial (IA) que corre enteramente en la computadora del usuario, sin enviar datos a servidores externos. Su fundador es Sigil Wen, un programador autodidacta que convivió de adolescente con referentes de la industria.
Cómo funciona el modelo de inteligencia artificial
Underdog procesa toda la información en el dispositivo del usuario, ya sea una Mac o una PC con Windows, en lugar de depender de servidores en la nube como hacen la mayoría de los asistentes de IA actuales. Se espera que las versiones para Linux, iPhone y Android lleguen más adelante.
El sistema utiliza Husky, un motor de inferencia desarrollado por el propio Wen que, según explicó, mueve menos datos entre el procesador principal y el chip gráfico de la computadora que otros motores similares. Esa eficiencia permite correr el asistente sin depender de centros de datos externos.
El modelo detrás de Underdog tiene 27.000 millones de parámetros y está basado en un ajuste de Qwen3.8 27B, una cifra muy inferior a la de los modelos más grandes que funcionan en la nube. Wen sostuvo que su desempeño se compara favorablemente con Claude Opus 4.6 de Anthropic en algunas pruebas, el nivel considerado de punta seis meses atrás.
“No hace falta sacrificar la privacidad por la capacidad, porque son igual de capaces”, dijo Wen a TechCrunch. El fundador agregó que los modelos pequeños que corren en el propio dispositivo seguirán ganando capacidad con el tiempo.
En qué se diferencia este asistente de IA
La aplicación es gratuita por ahora y, según Wen, nunca tendrá publicidad. Como el procesamiento ocurre en la propia máquina del usuario, Underdog no enfrenta los costos de inferencia que sí pagan otras empresas por alojar sus modelos en servidores.
En lugar de cobrar una suscripción, la empresa tomará un porcentaje mínimo de las transacciones de pago que el asistente gestione a través de la plataforma Stripe, de manera similar a una comisión de intercambio bancario. Entre los inversores ángeles de Conway Research figura justamente Patrick Collison, cofundador de Stripe.
Ese esquema contrasta con el de otros asistentes de IA, cuyas políticas de privacidad les permiten recolectar datos de los usuarios para venderlos a terceros o para entrenar otros modelos, según señaló TechCrunch.
Wen advirtió que ese tipo de recolección puede ser particularmente riesgosa cuando el asistente necesita acceso a información íntima, desde condiciones médicas hasta datos financieros o de los hijos de un usuario.
“¿Por qué usar IA debería implicar entregar tu información privada?”, escribió Wen en lo que llamó su manifiesto de inteligencia artificial, citado por TechCrunch. El fundador agregó que está construyendo un producto del que se sentiría orgulloso si lo usaran sus futuros hijos.
Cuál es la historia del fundador del asistente de IA
Wen llegó a Silicon Valley a los 17 años y vivió en una casa compartida de programadores de IA junto al investigador Andrej Karpathy, según relató a TechCrunch. Allí coincidió con quienes luego serían figuras centrales de la industria, como Aravind Srinivas, fundador de Perplexity, y Noam Brown, investigador de OpenAI.
En esa etapa probó versiones tempranas de herramientas que después se volvieron masivas, entre ellas un chatbot compartido por el cofundador de Anthropic Ben Mann que terminaría convirtiéndose en Claude, y un generador de imágenes de David Holz que daría origen a Midjourney. El inversor Naval Ravikant lo contrató para Airchat, su antigua red social rival de Clubhouse.
Wen es becario del programa Thiel Fellowship, que financia a jóvenes para que desarrollen proyectos propios en lugar de asistir a la universidad. Conway Research, la empresa detrás de Underdog, recibió 13,5 millones de dólares de financiamiento con el respaldo de Andreessen Horowitz, Khosla Ventures, SV Angel y el fondo conjunto entre Menlo Ventures y Anthropic, entre otros inversores.
Por ahora, Underdog funciona en una beta cerrada y por invitación. La compañía no informó una fecha para su lanzamiento público ni para las versiones móviles anunciadas para Linux, iPhone y Android.

articles.title: Seagate and Toshiba are reportedly fighting to acquire TDK's HDD magnetic-head technology
articles.text:
HDD Bubble: After selling its recording media business to Imation, TDK is now mostly focused on sensors, power supplies, and other advanced electronic devices. HDD magnetic heads, one of TDK's remaining business interests, could soon find a new home with a major hard drive manufacturer.
According to sources familiar with the matter, Seagate and Toshiba are currently battling each other to acquire TDK's magnetic-head business. The Japanese company is one of the few independent manufacturers still making this crucial electronic component, but HDD giants are now looking to strengthen their supply chains as the entire magnetic-recording industry goes through a second, AI-fueled renaissance.
The unnamed sources said that Toshiba began talking with TDK earlier this year, while Seagate made a higher offer during the summer. While the exact amount is still up in the air, the acquisition is expected to be worth a few billion dollars. The winning bidder would gain TDK's HDD magnetic-recording head production, strengthening its hard drive business for years to come.
Seagate, Toshiba, and Western Digital are the three major HDD manufacturers still in business today, after market and technological evolution turned the industry upside down over the past few decades. Both Seagate and WD have their own in-house magnetic-head production lines. Toshiba relies on external partners such as TDK to put its HDD units together.
Losing TDK's support would be highly detrimental to Toshiba's business, but Seagate could also lose a key partner as its HDD production becomes increasingly important. Seagate and WD are experiencing a massive surge in sales and pre-orders, as AI hyperscalers look for a "cheap" storage solution to further expand their LLM-based technology offerings.
The potential acquisition could eventually turn into an industry-threatening situation, which is why representatives from all interested parties met in Tokyo last week to discuss the matter further. Executives from Seagate, Toshiba, and TDK are even considering creating a new joint venture, the sources said. In any case, talks are still in the preliminary stages, and everything could eventually fall apart if an agreement is not reached.
Seagate and WD each account for around 45% of the modern HDD market, while Toshiba serves customers in the remaining 10%. TDK is apparently no longer interested in making HDD magnetic heads, as the company is looking for fresh funds to invest further in major business areas such as batteries, passive components, and sensors.

iPhone 15 sai quase pela metade do preço em oferta no Mercado Livre
iPhone 15 (128 GB) traz tela OLED de 2.000 nits e câmera de 48 MP; celular da Apple recebe desconto de 48% sobre o preço original em oferta no Pix
O iPhone 15 de 128 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 3.798 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O celular da Apple com tela OLED de 2.000 nits e câmera principal de 48 MP alcança um dos preços mais baixos dos últimos meses, com desconto de 48% em relação ao original de R$ 8.099.
Embora lançado em 2023, o iPhone 15 é uma opção acessível para quem quer um celular da Apple e não liga para IA. Seu chip Apple A16 Bionic e os 6 GB de RAM sustentam apps pesados e games mais exigentes. Os 128 GB de armazenamento podem ser expandidos com planos do iCloud.
A tela Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,1″ possui brilho de até 2.000 nits e é capaz de reproduzir cores realistas, além de ter garantia de visibilidade em qualquer ambiente. O vidro Ceramic Shield protege o display de acidentes cotidianos, como quedas e arranhões.

O iPhone 15 de 128 GB (apenas R$ 3.798 no Pix) foi atualizado para o iOS 27 e deve receber pelo menos mais três updates do sistema operacional. O celular da Apple conversa com redes 5G, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3 e NFC.

articles.title: TP-Link problems in US grow amid FCC router ban and four state lawsuits
articles.text:
TP-Link is facing more legal troubles in the US as Florida and three other states filed lawsuits alleging that it lied to consumers about its connections to China and the risks of its routers being exploited by Chinese state hackers.
The lawsuits were filed yesterday, about six months after the Federal Communications Commission announced a sweeping ban on consumer-grade routers produced wholly or partly outside of the US. Numerous router makers have obtained exemptions to the ban, but the Trump administration so far has not granted one to TP-Link.
Router makers that received exemptions include Netgear, Asus, Adtran, Amazon and its Eero subsidiary, Calix, Nokia, SpaceX’s Starlink division, and others. For now, TP-Link is unable to sell its latest Wi-Fi 8 routers in the US, though models approved before the ban can still be sold.
The state lawsuits claim that TP-Link misled US consumers by telling them its routers are safe. The suits allege that TP-Link committed unfair and deceptive trade acts in violation of the states’ consumer protection laws.
“Chinese state-sponsored hackers exploited TP-Link routers sitting in American living rooms,” Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier said while announcing his lawsuit filed in a Florida county court. Uthmeier said Florida “will not allow families to be misled into handing their personal data to the Chinese Communist Party. We are seeking an injunction, restitution for Florida consumers, and [financial] penalties under Florida law.”
TP-Link criticizes coordinated lawsuits
TP-Link was founded in China but moved its headquarters to California in October 2024 amid investigations into high-profile attacks linked to the Chinese government, including a botnet composed mostly of TP-Link routers. The Florida lawsuit accuses TP-Link of “lying about the safety of its routers and its ties to the CCP,” Uthmeier said.
Uthmeier was one of four Republican state attorneys general to sue TP-Link yesterday. Lawsuits were also filed against TP-Link by Montana, Iowa, and Nebraska.
“The coordinated lawsuits are built on false premises,” said Steve Kovsky, TP-Link’s corporate affairs officer. “They do nothing to advance national security while unfairly penalizing an industry-leading US company.” TP-Link said that for the past few months it has “provided state regulators with clear, verifiable documentation demonstrating two fundamental facts: TP-Link Systems devices sold in the US are manufactured in Vietnam and TP-Link Systems is an independent, US company that is not owned or controlled by any foreign government.”

articles.title: HPE Announces ProLiant Gen13 Servers Powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
HPE Announces ProLiant Gen13 Servers Powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs
HPE (NYSE: HPE) today announced the first four of its HPE ProLiant Gen13 Servers powered by 6th Generation AMD EPYC Server processors. The new systems expand compute, memory, and I/O capabilities to help enterprises accelerate agentic AI and inference, analytics, virtualization, simulation, and modeling while strengthening security, simplifying operations, and providing reliability across distributed IT environments.
As AI systems evolve from generating insights to taking autonomous action, trust becomes a prerequisite for scale. McKinsey's 2026 AI Trust Maturity Survey found that nearly two-thirds of respondents cited security and risk concerns as the top barrier to fully scaling agentic AI. Within this evolving landscape, HPE ProLiant Gen13 helps customers address security and operational barriers with a trusted infrastructure foundation that combines HPE iLO 8 innovations for automatic protection, infrastructure trust, and post-quantum readiness with enhanced visibility and control from HPE Compute Ops Management.
Krista Satterthwaite, Senior vice president and general manager, Compute at HPE"Organizations need to turn their investments in agentic AI and inference into business value without adding operational complexity or risk. For these workloads, HPE ProLiant Gen13 brings together optimized performance, built-in, automatic security, intelligent operations, and proven reliability. It gives customers a trusted foundation to modernize and innovate today and adapt as their requirements evolve."
Dan McNamara, senior vice president and general manager, Compute and Enterprise AI, AMD"AI is moving into the applications and operations that run the enterprise, fundamentally changing what organizations demand from their infrastructure. Across generations of AMD EPYC CPUs and HPE ProLiant servers, our teams have worked side by side to turn advances in processor and system design into practical value for customers. With 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors and HPE ProLiant Gen13, we are delivering the performance, efficiency and flexibility enterprises need to scale AI while modernizing the critical workloads their businesses depend on."
AI-ready performance across enterprise workloads
HPE is reinforcing its leadership in enterprise compute by introducing new HPE ProLiant Gen13 Servers that simplify the path to innovation and give customers the secure foundation needed for the AI era. Combining HPE engineering with 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server processors enables delivery of higher core density, memory bandwidth, and I/O capacity.
- The HPE ProLiant DL585a Gen13 Server is a future-ready, high-density platform designed to support up to eight double-wide PCIe GPUs, two 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server processors, and PCIe Gen 6 connectivity. The server maximizes GPU utilization, token throughput, and PCIe bandwidth at every layer for the most demanding workloads including AI inference, virtualization, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) model fine-tuning, analytics, and emerging agentic AI.
- The HPE ProLiant DL525 Gen13 Server is a compact, performance-optimized 1U, single-socket system powered by one 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server processor with up to 256 cores. High bandwidth 16-channel memory, with support for high-speed and high performance -DDR5 and MRDIMM - and PCIe Gen 6 connectivity, make the system ideal for workloads with extremely high data throughput, such as: fraud detection, market-data processing, risk and pricing models, electronic design automation (EDA), simulation, and AI inference.
For large-scale, compute-intensive applications, HPE is also introducing HPE ProLiant XD245 Server and HPE ProLiant XD285 Server - two systems designed to maximize compute performance within a smaller footprint. The two OCP-compliant servers combine high-density compute with efficient shared power and cooling to support data-intensive AI and HPC workloads.
- The HPE ProLiant XD245 Server uses a one-Open Rack Unit (1OU), four-node direct liquid-cooled design to deliver high compute density and is powered by up to eight 6th Gen AMD EPYC Server processors.
- The HPE ProLiant XD285 Server uses a two-Open Rack Unit (2OU), two-node air-cooled design, extending the architecture to a broader range of data center environments.
Engineered to process large-scale simulations, complex computational models, and datasets at the rack level, these systems provide the capacity, bandwidth, and infrastructure flexibility - cooling and accelerator options - needed for CPU-intensive workloads including computer-aided engineering (CAE), weather and climate modeling, scientific research, and financial modeling.
HPE ProLiant Gen13 will expand beyond the systems announced today, giving customers additional choices for mainstream enterprise, edge, virtualization, software-defined infrastructure, database, and AI workloads. 
Automatic security and streamlined operations
HPE ProLiant Gen13 combines automatic security from HPE Integrated Lights-Out 8 (iLO 8) with enhanced HPE Compute Ops Management capabilities to protect data and system integrity while simplifying deployment and lifecycle operations.
New industry-first features, available in HPE ProLiant Gen13, include:
- Automatic self-encrypting drive (Auto-SED) server capabilities, first in the industry, protects data at rest from first boot without added configuration, external key managers, or manual activation.
- Industry-first multi-person authorization (MPA) requires two authorized users to approve high-impact actions, including key provisioning and secure erase, reducing the risk of single-user error or misuse.
- Expanded post-quantum cryptography (PQC) readiness, first in the industry, that now extends beyond firmware to help protect server communication paths from emerging threats.
- Enterprise-grade component verification, built upon HPE's Silicon Root of Trust, validates the authenticity and integrity of critical server components as they are added, replaced, or modified throughout the server lifecycle.
New capabilities from HPE Compute Ops Management help customers operate HPE ProLiant Gen13 infrastructure with greater efficiency and resiliency through low-touch onboarding and near real-time power capacity insights. Organizations using HPE Compute Ops Management spent 50% less time managing servers and generated 209% ROI.
Proven reliability for evolving infrastructure needs
Each new generation of HPE ProLiant undergoes more than 1,000 tests and 10,000 hours of validation to help deliver consistent performance, availability, and resilience enterprises depend on, this includes advanced stress and corner-case testing that push the systems beyond published operating limits. Reliability is the leading HPE ProLiant customer purchase driver, for four consecutive years, with 81% citing reliable performance as a key differentiator from other server vendors and twice-fast support resolution. Additionally, HPE Tech Care Service further strengthens resiliency by delivering up to 97% less unplanned downtime, helping customers prevent, identify, and resolve issues as infrastructure needs change.
Availability
- The HPE ProLiant DL525 Gen13 server will be available later in 2026.
- The HPE ProLiant DL585a Gen13 server will be available in early 2027.
- The HPE ProLiant XD245 and XD285 Servers will be available in 2027.
HPE ProLiant Gen13 Servers are available through HPE Financial Services' 90/9 Advantage program. With no payments for 90 days, followed by nine months at 1% per month, the program helps organizations move forward with critical technology investments outside budget cycles.

articles.title: PlayStation Portal successors might be on the way
articles.text:
It looks like the PlayStation Portal might be getting a successor. According to documents seen by The Verge from the Wi-Fi Alliance, a nonprofit organization that can certify devices as capable of using Wi-Fi, new PlayStation hardware is on the way.
Two new devices have been classified as a “Gaming Console/Peripheral,” with the model numbers CFI-Y2000 and CFI-Y2015. The two devices are also certified for 1×1 2.4GHz and 5GHz Wi-Fi, but not 6GHz. These devices also reportedly run Android 15.
While this isn’t a lot of information to go off of, the current PlayStation Portal has a lot of similarities, such as the model number CFI-Y1001 and also runs Android 15.
If this is a successor, hopefully PlayStation changes how the Portal works. The current Portal is a device that streams from your home PlayStation or Sony’s cloud services, but you can’t play games natively. Hopefully, this hardware allows you to download PlayStation games on-device so you won’t need a Wi-Fi connection to play, similar to the Xbox ROG.
Previous rumours indicate that Sony is working on a Portal with an OLED screen, and another leak suggests that the handheld would sport a 120Hz refresh rate. However, this is just speculation at the moment.
Source: The Verge

articles.title: I'm sick of sleeping with my AirPods in when listening to audiobooks — so I'm about to buy these flatter, more comfortable Anker Soundcore Sleep A30 earbuds
articles.text:
AirPods are great, but they're a nightmare for sleeping in while I listen to audiobooks — which is why I'm getting these Soundcore Sleep A30 earbuds on Prime Day
They're perfect for my endless reruns of comfort listens
I'm a habitual audiobook listener, but I get a lot of my listening done at night. I calm my mind with books that I've read before and enjoyed, usually older classics like Sherlock Holmes stories, The Three Musketeers or The Lord of the Rings.
I go to bed with an audiobook, and if I wake up at night, I put an audiobook back on to help me go back to sleep. I try and avoid disturbing my wife, so I use my AirPods, but they stick out of my ears, and are uncomfortable if I roll onto my side.
That's why I'm getting these Soundcore Sleep A30 earbuds, which are down to $159.99 (was $229.99) at Amazon US in the Amazon Prime Day sales. In the UK, they're also heavily discounted, now just £122.55 (was £199.99) at Amazon UK.
• Browse the full Amazon Prime Day sale
I've included full details on the US and UK deals below. I was convinced to buy them after several of our writers tested the Soundcore Sleep A30 earbuds and rated them very highly, with tech reviewer Becca Caddy writing "they’ve become my go-to earbuds over the past few months. And because I review audio gear for a living, that's not something I say lightly".
Check out the deals in full below.
Today's best sleep buds deals
Save 30% on the Soundcore Sleep A30, which offer active noise cancellation technology to eliminate distractions, and a flatter fit to make sure even side sleepers are as comfortable as possible. At just 3g each, they're light and very comfortable, while you can get up to five nights of use with the charging case. Free sleep content from Calm is also available in the app.

The sliding clamshell case is nice, and the buds' tiny size and lightweight build make them ideal for sleep, yes — but also great for many other scenarios, as you use the ANC to tune out the world. In the app, there's a library of sleep-focused soundscapes, from waves to crackling fire, and they're all customizable with extra layers or density.
Sleep earbuds are having a bit of a moment, and you'll find plenty around from companies like Anker and Oslo, along with earplugs from brands such as Loop. However, Loop doesn't solve my audiobook problem, as I need proper earbuds rather than simple silicon ear plugs.
I like the Anker buds due to their discreet size, stylish case and active noice cancellation. Next time I wake up in the middle of the night, I will be able to reach for the Soundcore Sleep rather than my AirPods and not worry about sleeping on my side.
