articles.title: While VCs crowd into San Francisco, Endeavor Catalyst raises $320M for founders 'elsewhere' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Endeavor Catalyst has closed its fifth fund with $320 million in capital commitments, bringing the firm’s total assets under management to more than $850 million. The raise is good news for founders outside the Bay Area who risk getting overlooked as more funds focus squarely on AI companies in Silicon Valley.
Endeavor Catalyst is the venture arm of Endeavor, a New York-based global nonprofit that has spent 30 years supporting founders outside major tech hubs. (It calls all those other places “elsewhere” throughout its marketing materials.)
The fund is run by managing partner Allen Taylor, a 20-year veteran of the organization, and managing director Jackie Carmel, who joined Endeavor Catalyst 12 years ago, along with a 16-person team. The official general partner, though, is Endeavor itself. What that means, says Linda Rottenberg, who co-founded Endeavor and helped start Endeavor Catalyst in 2012, is that “half of the fund’s profits go back to Endeavor, so every investment helps the next generation of founders who are building elsewhere.”
The bar for those founders is pretty high. A person first has to get into Endeavor’s network, where he or she can access Endeavor’s mentoring and extensive network, and that’s hard. Last year, the group says it screened more than 10,000 candidates and picked 88. The network now has more than 3,100 entrepreneurs in over 50 countries.
When one of those founders’ companies raises at least $5 million in a round led by another institutional investor, Endeavor Catalyst can join in on the same terms as that lead. The team tells TechCrunch that checks usually run $1 million to $3 million but can’t exceed 10% of the round.
Over the next few years, they plan to make 40 to 50 investments annually, investing in up to 150 companies altogether with this new fund, they say.
Taylor, via an email exchange, wouldn’t share numbers on cash-on-cash returns tied to its earlier funds, but he did point to some impressive-sounding numbers. Across all five funds, he says, Endeavor Catalyst has backed 437 companies in 44 markets. Eighty-three of those startups are currently valued at $1 billion or more, he says, and the unit has seen 39 exits and 11 IPOs.
Some of the venture arm’s most valuable holdings right now include four-year-old ElevenLabs, the maker of AI voice tools that was recently valued at $22 billion in a secondary sale (it was founded in Poland originally), and Bending Spoons, the 13-year-old Italy-based conglomerate that went public in July and that currently boasts a $26 billion market cap.
Other holdings include New York-based Reflection AI (founded by two former Google DeepMind researchers — one of whom was born in Greece), which is now valued at $25 billion; Checkout.com, whose founder is Swiss and which was valued last year at $12 billion; the African payments infrastructure company Flutterwave, valued this summer at $3.2 billion; and AI coding startup Replit, co-founded by Amjad Masad, who is Palestinian-Jordanian. Replit snagged a $9 billion valuation earlier this year.
Endeavor, the nonprofit, has especially well-connected people associated with it, including board members Reid Hoffman; Nick Beim, a career VC who has spent the last 25 years at Matrix Partners, then Venrock; and Edgar Bronfman Jr., the former head of Warner Music and Seagram, who chairs Endeavor’s board.
Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is a longtime friend of Endeavor, too, having gone to Harvard with Rottenberg. (Late last month in San Francisco, I sat down with him during a rare visit to the Bay Area that was organized by Endeavor and where he met with tech founders and Greek expatriates.)
Altogether, Endeavor Catalyst’s newest fund includes 400 limited partners, including Hoffman; famed hedge fund manager Bill Ackman; and the Dutch investment group Prosus. According to Taylor, roughly 30% of those backers are Endeavor founders themselves, including founders of Nubank, Revolut, and Checkout.com.
While so much attention is paid to what’s happening in San Francisco and its immediate environs right now, the bets of Endeavor Catalyst suggest what other investors may be missing, and Endeavor, with local teams and mentors in dozens of countries, seems particularly well-positioned to see it.
Indeed, about 90% of the venture arm’s investments are outside the U.S., it says. Europe is its fastest-growing region, with 12 new investments in the first half of 2026 compared with 14 in all of last year, though Latin America is still the largest.
Repeat founders are also becoming a bigger part of the mix. Taylor tells TechCrunch that roughly 14% of Endeavor Catalyst’s fourth fund went to second companies started by Endeavor founders at the seed or Series A stage. With this new fund, the team expects that number will reach 20%.
Pictured above: Endeavor co-founder Linda Rottenberg onstage in Turin, Italy, earlier this month.

articles.title: Electric car sales jump nearly two-fold to 36,108 units in Sep: FADA
articles.text:
Electric car sales jump nearly two-fold to 36,108 units in Sep: FADA
Festive demand, maturing running-cost economics, a widening choice of models and sustained policy support through PM E-DRIVE and progressive state schemes are together turning the EV from an alternative into a default consideration for a growing set of buyers, FADA said.
Electric passenger vehicle retail sales nearly doubled in September to 36,108 units from 18,559 units in the corresponding month last year even as the overall EV sales surged a whopping 74% year-on-year to 3,33,364 units in the previous month, Federation of Automobile Dealers' Association (FADA) said in Wednesday.
Festive demand, maturing running-cost economics, a widening choice of models and sustained policy support through PM E-DRIVE and progressive state schemes are together turning the EV from an alternative into a default consideration for a growing set of buyers, FADA said.
The EV industry had reported a total sales of 191 497 units in September 2025.
"September delivered the highest-ever monthly EV retail India has recorded 3,33,634 units across categories, up 74% year-on-year, lifting overall EV penetration to about 13% from 10% a year ago," said FADA President Sai Giridhar.
Unlike the broader market, where September's headline is flattered by a weak year-ago base, the EV number is a clean, absolute record, he said, adding that electric vehicles did not merely grow against last year -- they set a new all-time high.
The record was led by the mass market with electric two-wheelers touched a fresh all-time high of 2,07,314 units, up 88% year-on-year, taking their share to 11.6%, he said.
More than one in nine two-wheelers retailed is now electric, as per FADA.
"Electric passenger vehicles also set an all-time record at 36,108 units, with penetration rising to 8.5%. Three-wheelers remain structurally electric at 64.9%, and while electric commercial vehicles eased month-on-month, they still grew over 150% year-on-year as fleet electrification deepens," Giridhar added.

articles.title: Détecter gratuitement du contenu IA : Google ouvre SynthID à tout le monde
articles.text:
Google ouvre ce mercredi son détecteur de contenus générés par IA au grand public, sur le site synthid.com. Un compte Google, Apple ou OpenAI suffit : on importe le fichier suspect, et l’outil répond s’il porte le filigrane invisible SynthID. La vérification couvre les contenus produits par les services de Google et de ses partenaires, OpenAI, Nvidia et Kakao en tête, Apple devant rejoindre la liste prochainement. Autrement dit, tout texte ou image générés par ChatGPT et Gemini sont désormais détectables.
180 milliards d’images déjà marquées
Depuis 2023, Google glisse ce filigrane imperceptible dans les images, vidéos et sons produits par ses IA. 180 milliards d’images et de vidéos portent déjà la marque, plus l’équivalent de 240 000 ans de contenus audio, détaille Pushmeet Kohli, vice-président de Google DeepMind, qui signe l’annonce. L’empreinte résiste aux manipulations courantes, et le service recommande d’importer le fichier dans la meilleure qualité possible pour fiabiliser le verdict. Réservée l’an dernier aux professionnels des médias, la vérification s’adresse désormais à tout le monde, en anglais uniquement pour commencer.
Lire aussi : Anthropic détaille l’étiquetage des textes générés par Claude et promet un détecteur accessible à tous
L’outil a pourtant un angle mort, que son interface annonce sans détour : « Ceci n’est pas un détecteur d’IA généraliste. » Il ne sait lire que le filigrane SynthID : une image sortie d’un service étranger au dispositif passera entre les mailles, et l’absence de marque ne prouve en rien qu’un contenu est authentique. Ces vérifications complètent celles déjà intégrées à la Recherche, à Gemini et à Chrome, qui dépassent désormais le million de requêtes par jour. Le texte, lui, reste hors de son périmètre.
OpenAI filigrane ses textes, Bruxelles tient le chronomètre
Lundi, OpenAI a dégainé de son côté : les textes produits par ChatGPT et Codex recevront eux aussi un filigrane invisible, déployé sur plusieurs semaines auprès des utilisateurs européens. Le procédé oriente discrètement le choix des mots du modèle à l’aide d’une clé secrète, et la marque survit au copier-coller. Baptisée textGrain, la méthode est maison : OpenAI, qui appose pourtant le filigrane SynthID sur ses images depuis le printemps et sur ses sons depuis l’été, a préféré sa propre recette pour le texte. Son détecteur reste d’ailleurs réservé à des chercheurs et organismes triés sur le volet, loin de l’ouverture générale du jour. « Les filigranes peuvent indiquer qu’un système d’OpenAI a généré ou retravaillé une partie d’un passage », explique l’entreprise. Elle en reconnaît les limites : remplacer un mot sur dix fait chuter la détection de 92 à 66 %.
Ce déploiement répond au règlement européen sur l’IA, ou AI Act : son article 50, en vigueur depuis le 2 août 2026, impose d’étiqueter les contenus générés ou manipulés par une IA. Le marquage lisible par les machines, filigranes et métadonnées en tête, bénéficie d’un sursis jusqu’au 2 décembre pour les systèmes déjà en service. La Commission a d’ailleurs publié en juin un code de bonnes pratiques pour cadrer la méthode. Google, de son côté, présente son ouverture comme une démarche volontaire, menée de longue date avec ses partenaires.

articles.title: Amazon Prime s’offre un petit parfum de Game Pass avec ce nouveau Star Wars disponible dès sa sortie
articles.text:
Amazon franchit une nouvelle étape avec Luna. Star Wars: Galactic Racer est accessible aux abonnés Prime dès sa sortie, sans achat supplémentaire, une première pour le service de cloud gaming.
Disponible sur PC, PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X|S, Star Wars: Galactic Racer a également rejoint Luna Standard dès son lancement. Développé par Fuse Games et édité par Secret Mode, le jeu est ainsi accessible en cloud aux abonnés Amazon Prime.
L’offre comprend la campagne solo complète ainsi que les modes Arcade et Scénarios. Le multijoueur cross-platform doit arriver ultérieurement. Amazon annonce par ailleurs une diffusion jusqu’en 1080p avec un son 5.1, et une compatibilité avec les manettes ainsi que le clavier et la souris.
Le jeu est bien proposé aux abonnés Prime français. Amazon précise que Star Wars: Galactic Racer est disponible dans tous les territoires où Luna est accessible avec Prime, ce qui inclut la France. Aucun abonnement supplémentaire à Luna n’est donc nécessaire pour y accéder.
Pour Amazon Luna, c’est une première
Jeff Gattis, responsable des jeux chez Amazon, présente ce lancement comme une première pour Luna : jamais encore le service n’avait proposé aux membres Prime un jeu dès le jour de sa commercialisation sur les autres plateformes.
L’expérience rapproche, sur le principe, Luna de la logique popularisée par le Xbox Game Pass, où certaines nouveautés intègrent directement l’abonnement. La comparaison s’arrête toutefois rapidement : Amazon n’a pas encore fait du « day one » une mécanique régulière de son service, dont Luna Standard rassemble actuellement plus de 80 jeux. Amazon ne précise pas non plus combien de temps Galactic Racer restera dans le catalogue : rien ne garantit donc que cet accès soit permanent.
Mais si ce premier essai est suivi par d’autres lancements simultanés, Luna pourrait devenir un argument un peu plus sérieux dans la longue liste des avantages inclus avec Amazon Prime.

articles.title: OpenAI publishes 722 AI-generated math papers as researchers challenge its closed model
articles.text:
The big picture: OpenAI has published 722 papers generated by an internal AI model, reporting advances across hundreds of mathematical problems. The papers cover number theory, algebraic geometry, and other fields. The release comes amid objections from mathematicians who argue that using proprietary AI models to solve mathematical problems prioritizes results over understanding and leaves researchers unable to examine the systems behind the proofs.
OpenAI organized the results into 372 groups and said it had given the model about 4,000 problems. The release gives researchers a large collection of proofs to examine, but not access to the proprietary system that produced them.
The company reported advances related to three of the five remaining Millennium Prize Problems, including the Riemann hypothesis. That does not mean it has solved all three. Even so, the reported Riemann result prompted a strong response from Rutgers University distinguished mathematics professor Alex Kontorovich.
"If a human did this, it would be an instant Fields Medal, no questions asked," he wrote on X.
Alongside the papers, OpenAI released summaries of the model's "chain of thought" for 10 results. The summaries describe the model's reasoning on selected problems, though they cover only a small share of the published work.
 – Alex Kontorovich (@AlexKontorovich) October 6, 2026
OpenAI also said the average result required a fraction of the computing power used for its earlier effort to solve the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem. The company spent millions of dollars on computing for that project.
The new release therefore offers a broader test of the model than the Navier-Stokes announcement alone. Researchers can now examine results across hundreds of problems rather than assess its abilities through a single heavily funded effort. However, the sheer volume of papers does not establish their accuracy. Mathematicians have begun reviewing the papers, but some question whether they can build on the findings without access to the AI model that produced them.
The model continued producing proofs behind closed doors while researchers debated OpenAI's earlier announcement. The company then faced a publication problem: how to release that work to a community already questioning its methods.
OpenAI said it followed publication recommendations from an independent advisory group of leading mathematicians that it recently helped assemble. The group issued its guidelines last week after gathering feedback from hundreds of researchers.
The company did not accept every recommendation. The committee had asked AI developers to stop using closed systems to test advanced mathematical problems.
"We ask them to stop testing advanced mathematical problems on proprietary models," the mathematicians wrote.
OpenAI defended its decision to continue: "It is important to continue to evaluate our internal frontier models on mathematics and other sciences, so we can accelerate developing the tools to advance those fields."
That disagreement concerns more than how papers should be published. Researchers are being asked to assess discoveries from a system they cannot access, with reasoning summaries available for only 10 results.
The advisory effort followed an open letter signed by more than two dozen Fields Medal winners. Titled "A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics," it warned that the industry's rush to solve problems threatened the purpose of mathematical research.
OpenAI and Anthropic have both used difficult mathematics to demonstrate the capabilities of their advanced models. Their competition helped set OpenAI's Millennium Prize effort in motion: the company said it began that work after hearing that Anthropic had already solved at least one of the problems.
The Navier-Stokes announcement also raised questions about the model's source. An academic collaborating with an Anthropic researcher suggested that the system might have drawn on his unpublished research. OpenAI denies the allegation.
The latest release also put pressure on researchers working with AI. Earlier in the week, as rumors spread that OpenAI was preparing to publish hundreds of proofs, some mathematicians hurried to release their own work before they could be scooped.
OpenAI has now made the papers public while keeping the model internal. Mathematicians have far more material to review, but the company and its advisers remain divided over whether advanced mathematical research should proceed on systems unavailable to the wider field.

articles.title: Quién es Dario Amodei: cómo fundó Anthropic con su hermana después de dejar OpenAI
articles.text:
Dario Amodei es uno de los cofundadores de Anthropic, la empresa detrás de Claude. En el último año, cobró 18 millones de dólares por ser el director ejecutivo de esta compañía, según Reuters.
Dicha remuneración lo ubica en una posición intermedia entre los máximos responsables de las grandes compañías tecnológicas. Como referencia, en 2025 Elon Musk recibió unos 158.300 millones de dólares por ser el CEO de Tesla.
Recientemente, Amodei ha estado en el centro de atenciónb debido a declaraciones relacionadas con ralentizar el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial y lanzamientos de su empresa.
Quién es Dario Amodei
Dario Amodei dirige Anthropic. Esta es una corporación de beneficio público enfocada en desarrollar sistemas de inteligencia artificial seguros, interpretables y controlables, según el blog empresarial.
Antes de fundar la compañía, fue vicepresidente de investigación en OpenAI, donde encabezó el desarrollo de modelos de lenguaje de gran escala, entre ellos GPT-2 y GPT-3.
Participó en la creación del aprendizaje por refuerzo basado en retroalimentación humana. Previamente, trabajó como científico investigador sénior en Google Brain.
Amodei es doctor en biofísica por la Universidad de Princeton, donde fue becario Hertz, y realizó una estancia posdoctoral en la Facultad de Medicina de la Universidad de Stanford.
Cómo cofundó Anthropic
Dario Amodei fundó Anthropic tras salir de OpenAI a finales de 2020 junto con un grupo de investigadores, entre ellos su hermana Daniela. La decisión fue el resultado de diferencias sobre la velocidad del desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial y la necesidad de imponer límites a sus posibles riesgos.
Antes de crear la empresa, Amodei trabajó en Baidu, donde observó que el aumento de los recursos destinados al entrenamiento mejoraba el desempeño de los modelos de IA. Más tarde se incorporó a Google como científico investigador sénior, con foco en los peligros potenciales de esta tecnología.
Su paso por OpenAI definió buena parte de su visión. Como vicepresidente de Investigación, participó en el desarrollo de GPT-2 y GPT-3, pero sostenía que la empresa debía ser más cautelosa al comunicar sus avances y consultar con el gobierno sobre sus implicaciones.
Las diferencias internas se profundizaron con el tiempo. Amodei mantenía una postura más prudente que otros directivos de OpenAI, incluidos Greg Brockman y Sam Altman, especialmente sobre la forma en que debían desarrollarse y difundirse los sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
A finales de 2020, Amodei y otros investigadores abandonaron la organización. Con menos de dos docenas de empleados y en plena pandemia de COVID-19, fundaron Anthropic, una compañía orientada a crear modelos de IA controlables, interpretables y seguros.
La nueva empresa no comenzó como una startup sin respaldo. Amodei logró atraer inversores de Silicon Valley, entre ellos el exdirector ejecutivo de Google Eric Schmidt.
Recibió una inversión de USD 500 millones gestionada por FTX, aunque Amodei decidió no otorgar a Sam Bankman-Fried un puesto en el consejo de administración.
En sus primeros años, Anthropic se concentró en ofrecer modelos de inteligencia artificial a empresas de sectores como farmacéutica, servicios financieros, viajes y defensa. La compañía también recibió inversiones de grandes firmas, incluida Amazon.
El lanzamiento de Claude llevó la marca al público general. Aunque apareció un año después de ChatGPT, el chatbot fue adoptado con rapidez, en especial entre programadores, y se diferenció por incorporar criterios de seguridad como parte de su diseño.
Amodei se convirtió, además, en una de las voces más visibles sobre los riesgos de la inteligencia artificial. En 2023, afirmó que veía una probabilidad de entre 10% y 25% de que esta tecnología pudiera destruir la civilización humana.
Esa postura volvió a quedar expuesta cuando Anthropic se negó a eliminar restricciones para usos militares de sus productos y cuestionó ante la Justicia una designación del gobierno estadounidense como “riesgo para la cadena de suministro”.
Renuncia de Jacob Caxon
La renuncia del investigador Jacob Coxon a Anthropic abrió un nuevo debate sobre el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial.
Coxon, quien también trabajó en OpenAI, dejó la compañía al considerar que ambas empresas actúan de forma irresponsable frente a una tecnología que, según advirtió, no debe subestimarse por sus posibles riesgos para la humanidad.
Días después, Dario Amodei publicó un ensayo en el que pidió a las empresas del sector moderar el ritmo de desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial.
Más tarde, el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, firmó un documento con ejecutivos de algunas de las principales compañías de IA durante una reunión en la Casa Blanca.
El texto, denominado “White House Accord on Super Intelligence”, plantea un compromiso voluntario de autorregulación para las empresas que desarrollan modelos de inteligencia artificial.

Prime Day – La montre connectée Garmin Forerunner 70 à 189,29 € (-16%)
La montre connectée Garmin Forerunner 70 passe sous les 200 € chez Amazon Prime soit une baisse d'environ 16% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
L’héritière de la Forerunner 55 est arrivée. Cinq ans après cette montre à prix serré pensée pour la course à pied, Garmin lui substitue la Forerunner 70, toujours positionnée en entrée de gamme. La Forerunner 70 de Garmin constitue une belle mise à jour de la Forerunner 55. articles.title: Chemistry Nobel goes to reactions like those that gave life a hand
articles.text:
Life is remarkably selective. Life relies on many molecules with what is termed “handedness”—they’re chemically identical but are mirror images of each other. Most chemical reactions will make a 50-50 mix of the left- and right-handed forms of a chemical, but life uses only one of them. In fact, because of the differences between left- and right-handed chemicals, most of the key enzymes used by organisms will fail to work if they’re presented with chemicals that have the wrong handedness.
That poses a bit of a challenge for origin-of-life research, as we’re forced to explain how a world that may have started with an even mix of left- and right-handed chemicals produced organisms that only used one of them.
Today’s Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to two individuals, Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai, who discovered chemical reactions could be biased, producing large excesses of one of the two forms of a chemical.
Chirality and life
The technical term for molecular handedness is “chirality,” and scientists replace left and right with dextro (D) and levo (L). But the ideas are largely the same. Your hands have all the same components—fingers and thumbs—organized in the same way. Yet if you point your thumb upward, the fingers curl in opposite directions, making one the mirror image of the other. Depending on the arrangements of the chemical bonds, many molecules can form similar mirror-image forms, with all the same parts oriented slightly differently in space.
(For the geekier among the readership: carbon atoms have four potential sites that can form bonds, spread evenly across the surface of the atom’s sphere. If each of those sites is linked to a different chemical, then swapping the chemicals located in any two of them can potentially change the way it’s arranged in 3D space.)
Amino acids come in both D and L forms, but all of life relies on just one of those.
Amino acids come in both D and L forms, but all of life relies on just one of those.
Credit:
Nobel Prize Foundation
This can really matter when it comes to enzymes, which typically latch onto chemicals using binding sites that are sculpted by evolution to fit only that chemical and its close relatives. Try to feed the enzyme the mirror-image version of that same chemical, and it will often fail to fit the binding site. Since life uses nothing but the D form of sugars, all of its enzymes are optimized to latch onto those, and many cannot interact at all with the L form.
There are two ways this could have happened. The first life may not have been as picky about the reactions it catalyzed and only evolved chirality preferences slowly. Or life could have evolved in an environment where one chiral form dominated. Or there was some combination of the two. But either of the latter two cases simply pushes the question back a bit: How could chemistry create an environment where one chiral form dominates?
From theory to practice
Over the years, there have been a number of ideas about how this might occur. Several of those trace back to a physicist, Frederick Charles Frank, who addressed this issue in a data-free, theory-focused paper. (It’s clear from the Nobel Prize Committee’s writing that, were Frank still alive, he might have shared in this award.) One option is that a catalyst with only a slight preference for forming a D or L molecule could, over time, produce a large excess of that form. Another is that a chiral reaction product could itself serve as a catalyst for forming more of the same form. Or the chiral reaction product could inhibit the formation of its mirrored form.
Many chemical reactions reach an equilibrium, finding a point where forward and reverse reactions occur at similar rates. If the reverse reaction is indifferent to chirality, but the forward one is influenced by one of the factors above, then time would allow this to create a large excess of one chiral form.
All of these were hypotheticals, however, until the researchers being honored got to work. Henri Kagan of the University of Paris-Sud also approached his work very theoretically, describing the factors that would be needed to drive reactions that favored a single chirality. But in several cases, he was able to go out and find actual chemical reactions that demonstrated his ideas mattered in the real world.
Kagan worked with a catalyst that was itself chiral. He found that, in a mix of L and D versions of his catalyst, one of the forms was much more active than the other. While the forms might be present at the same level, most of the actual catalysis was performed by just one of them. And, if it was used to catalyze a reaction that produced a chiral product, this difference could lead to much higher levels of a single chirality.
By the mid-1960s, Kagan had found three different reactions that could produce an excess of a single chiral form. Other researchers who followed up on his ideas showed that chiral catalysts could also be selectively activated or inhibited by the addition of non-chiral chemicals, allowing a finer degree of control that found its way into the production of pharmaceuticals.
Self catalysis
About a decade later, Tokyo University’s Kenzo Soai was working on reactions where one of the products of the reaction acted as a catalyst to boost the same reaction. Eventually, he found one that selected for chirality; one form of the reaction product would catalyze the formation of more molecules of the same chirality. He started the reaction with a slight excess of one form of catalyst and found that, after a single round of reactions, the excess in the catalyst had risen to 55 percent. Using that as a catalyst for a new round of reactions would enhance the excess further; after several rounds, 90 percent of the products were a single chirality.
Eventually, Soai found conditions where one product would not only catalyze the formation of more of the same form, but inhibit the formation of the opposite chirality. This allowed him to start with a tiny excess of a single chiral form (0.00005 percent more) and, after a few rounds of reactions, bring the excess to over 99 percent.
Others later found conditions where a similar reaction that reached an equilibrium of forward and back reactions would gradually lead to a single chiral form dominating.
There are three different aspects of this work that are worth celebrating. One is that it’s simply great science; people reasoned through the ways that an excess of one chiral form could emerge, and then others found ways to demonstrate that the behavior took place in the real world. A second is that it has immense practical applications. Many of our drugs work because they interact with proteins, where chirality often matters. And there are many examples of drugs where the wrong chiral form can be inactive or positively harmful. So finding new ways to catalyze the production of specific chiral forms has a lot of utility.
But the final thing comes back to the origin of life. None of these reactions were demonstrated with anything closely related to a biomolecule, so it’s not obvious that this particular work is directly relevant to the origin of life. But it does show that small excesses of some chiral forms—smaller than the 90 percent seen in this work, but still significant—may be common in the natural world.
The current thinking is that those small differences weren’t decisive, but did help push the emergence of life along a pathway that ultimately led to the exclusive chemistry we see now.
John is Ars Technica's science editor. He has a Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry from Columbia University, and a Ph.D. in Molecular and Cell Biology from the University of California, Berkeley. When physically separated from his keyboard, he tends to seek out a bicycle, or a scenic location for communing with his hiking boots.

articles.title: Microsoft unveils Surface Laptop Ultra, new Windows AI features
articles.text:
Microsoft held a Surface event on Oct. 7 where it detailed new hardware and several Windows updates.
As expected, Microsoft finally unveiled its “builder tier” Surface Laptop Ultra sporting Nvidia’s RTX Spark chipset. Microsoft positions the Surface Laptop Ultra and RTX Spark as the best choice for running local AI models, claiming the laptop outperforms the MacBook Pro with M5 Pro chip in several AI workloads.
While Microsoft characterized the Surface Laptop Ultra as a device aimed at professionals, the first thing the company talked about was gaming, noting that the new Gears of War: E-Day can run at 60fps on the device (though it didn’t share other performance details). Microsoft also said in 2027, Call of Duty would come to RTX Spark.
Other highlights on the Surface Laptop Ultra include a bright, HDR PixelSense display and the most ports on a Surface Laptop. Speaking of ports, Microsoft also showed off a new magnetic USB-C charger, giving customers the best of magnetic charging with USB-C compatibility.
Alongside the Surface Laptop Ultra, Microsoft showed off several other RTX Spark laptops from other manufacturers like Dell, HP, MSI, Asus, and others.
Update Oct. 7, 2026, at 3 p.m. ET: We now have Canadian pricing! The Surface Laptop Ultra starts at an eye-watering $3,899.99 in Canada. Pre-orders are open now with an Oct. 16 release.
We’re also slowly getting pricing for some of the other RTX Spark laptops, and will add those details below as they come in:
- Asus ProArt P14 and P16 – starting at C$3,499 and C$4,999 respectively. Shipping starts Oct. 16.
Hybrid intelligence and Windows updates
Microsoft showed a new capability in GitHub Copilot that can automatically route AI prompts to local, on-device models if those models can tackle the task. If there aren’t any local models that can do it, then Copilot can fall back to cloud models.
Beyond GitHub, Copilot on Windows can also use Hybrid Intelligence to use local models and complete local actions. That means local file access (though thankfully, making changes requires permission). Microsoft says this enables Copilot to see and interact with what’s on your PC, and the local models mean data isn’t leaving your device.
One demo Microsoft showed involved having Copilot help with tax season. With a prompt, Copilot started gathering various tax-related documents stored across the PC, organized the files, stored them in a zip file, and even crafted an email in Outlook to send to the accountant with the zipped folder. It paused at the end for the user to review the email and files before hitting send.
Windows Search is getting some handy upgrades, including quick actions that users can trigger just from search. Some actions Microsoft showed off include launching apps, changing PC settings, and sending texts.
Copilot also lives in Search now, allowing users to quickly ask it questions right from the taskbar.
Another Copilot change Microsoft shared is the ability to create native apps “from a single prompt.” The company claims Copilot can build apps for users that can then run right on their machine.
Elsewhere, Microsoft announced that Meta’s Muse app is coming to Windows. Thought, given the severe security issues with Muse, I’m not sure I’d recommend anyone install it.
Prompt injection protection
A new Windows feature Microsoft unveiled should make agentic AI tasks more secure than before. For one, Microsoft says Windows can now separate AI agent activity from user activity, and thus apply different levels of security and access to those activities.
In a similar vein, Microsoft says its Defender security platform can now detect malicious activity, such as a prompt injection attack — which is when someone includes instructions that only AI models can detect that trick AI into doing tasks other than what the user specified.
However, there are a lot of details Microsoft left out of its demo, so I’m not sure how effective the tool will be. Still, if it works as well as Microsoft claims, it could help address the prompt injection problem.

articles.title: AMD Shares Its Progress with Agentic PCs
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
AMD Shares Its Progress with Agentic PCs
AMD held a press briefing to share how its "Agentic PC" push is going, and it brought a fair number of figures along. Apparently, the company has shipped over half a million Agentic PCs across more than 50 designs, alongside tens of millions of AI PCs across more than 250 designs. Of course, the term "Agentic PC" is AMD's own. It covers any PC whose CPU, GPU, and NPU can run AI agents locally, and AMD says Ryzen AI Max+ systems with 64 GB of memory or more give the best experience. The Ryzen AI Max 400 series is pitched as the "next-gen Agentic PC" for 2026, and most of the briefing focused on its flagship, the Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 "Gorgon Halo" with 192 GB of memory.MemoryThe Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 "Gorgon Halo" supports up to 192 GB of "unified" LPDDR5X memory, and how much of it goes to the GPU can be configured manually. AMD assigned 160 GB for its LLM runs and 128 GB for the ComfyUI comparison. That capacity is what lets the chip load GLM 5.3 Flash, which took roughly 160 GB at 4-bit (UD_IQ4_XS) quantization. The slides headline "300 billion parameter support," though one endnote dated May 10 still mentions "up to 200B-parameter models" for the 128 GB Ryzen AI Max+. That seems to be a leftover from the older configuration.
Local LLM PerformanceApparently, the chip runs Z.ai's GLM 5.3 Flash, a gigantic 320-billion-parameter model, at up to 20 tokens per second, and Qwen 3.8 Flash Next at up to 42 tokens per second. That is a strong result for an integrated GPU. Qwen is listed at 125 billion plus 51 billion parameters, well below GLM, and it ran with MTP enabled, which probably explains the higher speed. Both results seem to come from one short physics prompt, so longer agentic tasks may look different. AMD also calls this the only Windows PC that can run "Opus 4.8 class" agents, and says it can run several "Opus 4.7 class" agents at once using Qwen.
Intel ComparisonIn ComfyUI, AMD showed the chip ahead of Intel's Core Ultra X9 388H in all 18 generative AI workloads. Seventeen of those leads sit between 1.1x and 3.1x, while Yuve is an outlier with a 32.2x lead. Capacity likely explains part of the gap. The Intel system had 64 GB memory, while AMD's had 192 GB of "unified" memory with 128 GB assigned to the GPU. Some Panther Lake chips support up to 128 GB of DDR5, but the Core Ultra X9 388H is limited to LPDDR5X and tops out at 96 GB. We checked, and no Panther Lake laptop currently on sale seems to ship with more than 64 GB, so AMD likely tested the best-equipped Intel system it could get. For the smaller models in the chart, that difference shouldn't matter, since they fit comfortably on both systems. Capacity likely only comes into play in the heaviest workloads, which probably explains the 32.2x lead in the Yuve benchmark.
It's unexpected that AMD got several model names wrong in this chart: "Klien" near Flux 2 should be "Klein," "Yuve"—AMD's biggest win against Intel is actually "YuE," and "Pixal 3D" is called "Pixel 3D".
Software and PartnersAMD leaned on x86 compatibility as well, saying that Windows and Linux run on the chip with no emulation layer, as opposed to Arm-based Snapdragon PCs that lean on Microsoft's Prism emulation for x86 apps. That's important for professional apps such as Solidworks, Autodesk 3ds Max, and Mastercam, which only run natively on Windows, according to AMD. FSR also got a mention, with support for over 700 games. The company pointed to Microsoft picking Ryzen AI Halo as the first Project Zenith platform, Perplexity bringing Portable Computer to Ryzen AI Max systems, and a Cisco partnership aimed at enterprise deployments. No roadmap has been outlined past the 400 series, though the deck does mention a non-PRO lineup alongside the PRO chips.
Light Sail VRAMD also shared a case study from Light Sail VR, an Emmy-winning immersive production studio that runs an AI "production coordinator" locally. Founder and CEO Matthew Celia says the agent started on a Framework Desktop with a Ryzen AI Max chip and 128 GB of memory, and later moved to a system with Radeon AI PRO R9700 graphics cards. Staff talk to it through Slack, and it updates schedules, documents, and emails. Celia says he went from managing one or two jobs at a time to six to nine. He picked local AI for privacy, since the studio works under NDAs, and to avoid "thousands and thousands of dollars in token usage."
These claims haven't been independently verified by AMD. As for the rest of the briefing, all of the numbers come from AMD's own testing, so readers are advised to wait for independent results.
Source:
				AMD			
	
	
	
		
	
		
3 Comments on AMD Shares Its Progress with Agentic PCs
On the other hand, we're getting a pretty fast APU with tons of somewhat fast memory. This can be useful for other things besides AI.
I do wonder how much memory can actually be allocated in total to the GPU, especially outside Linux. This has been a gripe on AMD systems, as dynamically you could only assign up to 50% system memory to the gpu itself. Which for inference, is far from ideal. You want basically all memory allocated to the GPU and only leave a few GBs to the system.

articles.title: The remarkable $12 flashlight every PC builder wishes they bought sooner is now 40% off — Olight lights up the dark corners of any DIY project
articles.text:
The remarkable $12 flashlight every PC builder wishes they bought sooner is now 40% off — Olight lights up the dark corners of any DIY project
Even the smallest, and sometimes the cheapest, tools can change your life, especially if you build a lot of PCs or often work in dark places. The Olight imini 2, a keychain-sized rechargeable flashlight that you can charge by plugging its built-in USB-A into any compatible port, could be the companion you did not know you needed. Right now, at 40% off, the Olight imini 2 is selling for $11.99, just $2 above its all-time low.
The imini 2 has a footprint of just 2.17 x 0.59 inches, so it is right up the alley of a typical USB pendrive or a tube of chapstick. It weighs only 0.69 ounces, which makes the imini 2 a great addition to your keychain. Its compact size fits comfortably in even the smallest hands. The aluminum alloy body lets the imini 2 withstand drops from up to five feet, and the IPX6 rating means you will not have to worry about the flashlight getting wet from water splashes or rain.
While some may argue you can always use your smartphone's flashlight, it is not always practical to hold a bulky device while installing a CPU cooler or screwing the motherboard into the case. The imini 2 is so small that it fits in the tightest spaces, even in SFF cases, and provides adequate illumination. Additionally, the magnetic base lets it attach to metal surfaces for hands-free lighting, such as a computer case, a car hood, a fuse box, or other metal objects.
The imini 2 is a handy little flashlight that easily attaches to your keychain. Built to last and bright enough to be reliable, you will never want to leave the house without it.
The imini 2 may be minuscule, but it packs a powerful punch. With 50 lumens, 115 candela of output, and a wide 80-degree beam angle to about 23 yards, it is more of a floodlight than a flashlight. Nonetheless, it easily lights your workspace, whether you are building a PC, searching a dark closet, or walking down a dimly lit hallway. The iMini 2 has no buttons, preventing accidental turn-ons. Instead, detach the flashlight from the magnetic cap, and it is ready to go.
Powered by a 10180 lithium battery with an 80 mAh capacity, the imini 2 delivers up to 60 hours of continuous use on a single charge. Charging is effortless, too, thanks to the built-in USB plug that connects directly to your laptop, power bank, or wall charger. This design is convenient because you do not have to carry a cable, and you can top up the battery anywhere, anytime. Plus, the USB plug is rated for 10,000 cycles, so it will not die on you.
For the price of a burrito at Chipotle, the imini 2 is one of those gadgets that you will not regret. If you have an extra $11.99 to spend on Amazon's Big Deals, it will be a good choice.

articles.title: Mut zur Lücke: Google öffnet SynthID Detector für alle
articles.text:
Google rollt SynthID Detector für alle aus: Was die KI-Erkennung kann – und was nicht
Im Mai 2025 hatte Google den SynthID Detector präsentiert, ein Tool, das per Google-KI erstellte Inhalte erkennen soll. Basis ist SynthID, das hauseigene Wasserzeichen-Tool des Konzerns. Mittlerweile sind weitere KI-Anbieter eingestiegen, etwa OpenAI, Nvidia und Kakao.
Bald auch für Apple Intelligence
Eine Unterstützung für Apple Intelligence soll „bald“ folgen, wie Google mitteilt. Damit wäre der KI-Detektor eines der ersten Erkennungstools, das Bilder von Apples KI-Features wie Image Playground identifizieren kann, wie Engadget schreibt.
Google hat den SynthID Detector jetzt für alle Nutzer:innen freigeschaltet, nachdem bisher nur ausgewählte Journalist:innen und Forscher:innen Zugriff erhalten hatten. Auf der entsprechenden Website können Nutzer:innen Bilder, Videos und Audiodateien hochladen, um sie auf das Vorhandensein einer SynthID hin untersuchen zu lassen.
Nur eigene Wasserzeichen erkannt
Ist der Inhalt von einem KI-Tool der oben genannten Anbieter erstellt worden – und ein Wasserzeichen vorhanden –, weist Google entsprechend daraufhin. Findet der SynthID Detector nichts, heißt das derweil nicht, dass es sich nicht um einen KI-generierten Inhalt handeln kann. Es bedeutet lediglich, dass kein Google-Wasserzeichen integriert ist.
Wer etwa von Anthropics Claude erstellte Inhalte überprüfen lässt, kann sich sicher sein, dass der KI-Detektor nicht anschlägt. Zudem zeigt SynthID Detector nicht an, ob ein erkannter Inhalt vollständig per KI erstellt worden ist oder nur per KI nachbearbeitet wurde. Zudem lassen sich in manchen Fällen die SynthID-Wasserzeichen durch Bearbeitung aus den Inhalten entfernen.
SynthID Detector ignoriert Texte
Und es gibt noch weitere Lücken. Text erkennt der SynthID Detector gleich gar nicht. Nutzer:innen müssen hier auf andere KI-Detektoren wie Pangram zurückgreifen. Zudem nutzen Microsoft oder Meta eigene Wasserzeichen. Open-Source-Modelle kennzeichnen die von ihnen erstellten Inhalte oft nicht.
Adobe, Microsoft und Google haben außerdem den gemeinsamen Standard C2PA für die Erkennung von KI-Inhalten entwickelt. Einen Detektor, der alle Standards erkennt, gibt es bisher nicht, wie es bei trendingtopics.eu heißt.
180 Milliarden Bilder und Videos markiert
Geht es nur um SynthID, hat Google seit 2023 mehr als 180 Milliarden Bilder und Videos mit dem unsichtbaren Wasserzeichen versehen. Dazu kommen Audioinhalte mit einer Länge von insgesamt 240.000 Jahren.

Nous Research, the startup developing the open source Hermes Agent, has raised a $90 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, confirming TechCrunch’s earlier reporting.

articles.title: From Electrification to Architecture: The Next Automotive Era - EE Times
articles.text:
How software-defined vehicles are reshaping system integration and semiconductor requirements
Perspective: As vehicle architectures become more centralized and software-driven, packaging, test, qualification and manufacturing execution become increasingly important to system performance and reliability.
The automotive industry is undergoing a fundamental transformation. Electrification has already reshaped the vehicle, but a second shift is now underway. It is less visible, yet just as significant: vehicle architecture is changing.
Electric vehicles have significantly increased the role of semiconductors across power electronics, charging systems, sensing and protection. These components now sit at the core of how vehicles operate.
The next phase goes beyond electrification. Automakers are moving toward software-defined vehicles, where software plays a central role in coordinating functions and enabling updates throughout the vehicle lifecycle.
From Many ECUs to Centralized Systems
Traditionally, vehicles relied on distributed architectures with numerous electronic control units, each handling a specific function. Over time, this created more components, more wiring and greater integration complexity.
The industry is now shifting toward more centralized or zonal architectures, where fewer, more powerful computing platforms manage multiple functions.
This does not eliminate complexity. It changes where complexity sits:
- Fewer control units, with each unit becoming more powerful and functionally dense
- Higher integration at chip, package and system level
- Stronger interdependence between hardware capability and software performance
In short, hardware becomes more integrated while the overall system becomes more software-driven.
What Remains Constant
Despite these architectural changes, several fundamentals remain unchanged:
- Power devices continue to underpin battery systems, inverters and energy conversion
- Advanced driver-assistance and sensing systems continue to expand, driven by safety and automation requirements
- Protection components, including e-fuses, remain critical for circuit protection and fault management in high-voltage systems
These functions continue to support semiconductor demand as vehicle electrification advances.
What Is Changing
While the core building blocks remain, the requirements around them are increasing:
- Higher integration and system-level complexity. Fewer hardware elements are handling more functions, increasing the importance of system-level design and validation.
- Greater power density and thermal demands. Centralized compute platforms, combined with high-power electric-vehicle systems, create higher thermal loads and tighter performance margins.
- Stricter reliability expectations. Automotive semiconductors must operate reliably under demanding conditions, including temperature extremes, vibration and long product lifecycles.
Why Assembly and Test Matter More
As vehicle architectures evolve, chip performance alone is not enough. Success increasingly depends on how semiconductor devices are packaged, tested, qualified and manufactured at scale.
Automotive-grade devices must meet stringent reliability requirements. Qualification involves extensive stress testing to help ensure dependable performance under real-world operating conditions.
This increases the importance of:
- Assembly and packaging, to manage thermal, electrical and mechanical performance
- Test and qualification, to verify device performance and long-term reliability
- Manufacturing consistency and yield, to support increasingly complex devices at production scale
For semiconductor companies and automotive system providers, this evolution increases the value of working with assembly and test partners that can address integration, thermal performance, qualification and manufacturing consistency from development through volume production.
Looking Ahead
Electrification increased semiconductor content across the vehicle. Software-defined and centralized architectures are now changing how that content is integrated, managed and scaled.

articles.title: Rupee undervalued; RBI will ensure stability in INR, helping it find its correct value
articles.text:
Rupee undervalued; RBI will ensure stability in INR, helping it find its correct value
The domestic currency has been under pressure for much of this year, especially since the beginning of the West Asia conflict in late February, resulting in a spike in crude oil prices, which poses a direct challenge to an oil-importing country like India.
Stating that the rupee may be "undervalued" as per many estimates, Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Wednesday assured that the Reserve Bank of India will ensure that the currency "stabilises" and will support it in reaching its "correct value".
Speaking to reporters on a day that saw the local currency inching towards all-time low against the dollar, Malhotra noted that while markets can be "irrational" in the short term, they reflect their right value in the long run.
"We will ensure that the rupee stabilises, that the rupee finds its correct value, and we will support an orderly movement of the rupee in finding its correct value and at the same time in ensuring that there is no excessive volatility," the Governor told reporters at the central bank headquarters here.
He was replying to a specific question about the rupee inching towards its all-time low of 96.96 against the dollar, during intraday trading on Wednesday.
It can be noted that the domestic currency has been under pressure for much of this year, especially since the beginning of the West Asia conflict in late February, resulting in a spike in crude oil prices, which poses a direct challenge to an oil-importing country like India.
To counter the fall the RBI introduced a concessional swap facility for diaspora deposits and bond issuances. Banks have mobilised nearly $133 billion under the FCNR(B) deposits facility alone, which lifted the pressure on the currency in the markets for a few days. However, the currency is back under pressure and has depreciated in the last few sessions.
"By a number of estimates, including the REER (Real Effective Exchange Rate), the rupee is not overvalued; it may be undervalued," Malhotra said on Wednesday.
The remarks follow similar comments from Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta on September 24, who opined that there is a case for the rupee to stabilise and appreciate from here on.

articles.title: 5 errores al cocinar en una freidora de aire que provocan humo y daños en la comida
articles.text:
Una freidora de aire puede botar humo y arruinar la textura de las comidas cuando se usa sin atender algunos aspectos básicos de la cocción. La circulación de aire caliente, que permite reducir el uso de aceite, depende de que la cesta tenga espacio, de que no haya exceso de humedad y de que el aparato esté limpio.
Errores como sobrecargar el recipiente, introducir preparaciones con rebozados líquidos o ignorar el precalentamiento pueden derivar en comida blanda, cocción despareja, residuos quemados y humo dentro de la cocina.
Por esta razón, se explican varias prácticas que se deben evitar al manejar una freidora de aire, según el fabricante Philips, sumado a trucos para aprovechar el funcionamiento del electrodoméstico.
Qué pasa si se llena mucho la cesta de la freidora de aire
Una cesta repleta impide que el aire caliente circule de forma uniforme entre los alimentos. Como resultado, algunas piezas pueden quedar doradas en exceso, mientras otras conservan zonas frías, húmedas o poco cocidas.
El problema se acentúa con productos que liberan grasa o agua durante la preparación, porque los líquidos se acumulan con mayor facilidad en la base.
La capacidad del aparato debe determinar la cantidad de comida que se coloca en cada tanda. Preparar porciones más pequeñas permite distribuir los ingredientes en una sola capa o con espacio suficiente entre ellos.
Por qué los alimentos húmedos pueden producir humo dentro de la freidora de aire
Los adobos líquidos, las masas poco espesas y los alimentos mojados pueden gotear hacia la bandeja inferior. Cuando esos restos entran en contacto con las altas temperaturas, pueden quemarse y generar humo.
Además, la humedad en la superficie dificulta el dorado, así que el resultado suele ser una comida con una cobertura blanda o desprendida.
Antes de cocinar, conviene secar carnes, pescados, verduras y otros ingredientes con papel de cocina. Si la receta requiere una cobertura, es preferible usar alternativas secas, como pan rallado, harina o copos triturados.
Los rebozados líquidos no son adecuados para la freidora de aire, salvo que se adapten previamente para evitar que se desprendan durante la cocción.
Qué sucede si no se precalienta la freidora de aire
El precalentamiento permite que la cámara alcance la temperatura prevista antes de incorporar los alimentos. Ese paso favorece una cocción más estable desde el inicio y evita que productos como papas, vegetales, empanados o aperitivos congelados absorban humedad mientras el aparato toma calor.
Cuando se omite esta etapa, la superficie de la comida puede quedar menos crocante y el interior puede requerir más tiempo de preparación.
Asimismo, precalentar la freidora de aire ayuda a respetar los tiempos indicados en recetas y envases, aunque siempre conviene controlar el estado de los alimentos antes de servirlos, porque el tamaño de las porciones puede modificar el resultado.
Cuál es el problema de utilizar la freidora de aire sin limpiarla
La grasa y los restos de comida que quedan en la cesta, la bandeja o el interior del aparato pueden recalentarse en los usos posteriores. Si esos residuos se queman, producen humo, malos olores y manchas que luego son más difíciles de retirar. Otro riesgo es que pueden adherirse a los alimentos y alterar su sabor.
La sugerencia del fabricante es limpiar las piezas extraíbles después de cada uso con agua tibia y jabón, una vez que se hayan enfriado. El interior debe repasarse con un paño húmedo, sin sumergir la unidad principal ni usar elementos abrasivos.
La limpieza frecuente de la freidora de aire limita la acumulación de grasa y contribuye a mantener el funcionamiento del electrodoméstico.
Por qué es peligroso cocinar sin nada de aceite en la freidora de aire
El aparato reduce de gran forma la cantidad de aceite frente a la fritura tradicional, pero eso no significa que todas las preparaciones deban cocinarse completamente secas.
Una pequeña cantidad ayuda a evitar que algunos ingredientes se adhieran a la cesta y puede favorecer el dorado de papas, vegetales, carnes o rebozados. El aceite puede aplicarse con una brocha o mediante un rociador, sin excederse.
La clave está en usar una capa fina y distribuirla sobre la superficie de los alimentos, no llenar la bandeja. Un uso moderado de aceite permite mejorar la textura sin convertir la preparación en una fritura convencional ni generar acumulaciones que luego puedan quemarse.

articles.title: Sony cache deux produits PlayStation inédits, une fuite vend la mèche
articles.text:
La Wi-Fi Alliance, l’organisme qui certifie la compatibilité Wi-Fi des appareils, a enregistré le 21 septembre deux produits Sony sous les codes CFI-Y2000 et CFI-Y2105. Ces références ne correspondent à rien de connu, mais le préfixe CFI-Y ne désigne qu’une seule gamme au catalogue PlayStation : le Portal, dont les déclinaisons actuelles s’échelonnent de CFI-Y1000 à CFI-Y1016. Le dépôt, exhumé par un observateur sur X, redonne corps à une rumeur née fin janvier, celle d’une version OLED de l’accessoire.
Une numérotation qui ne doit rien au hasard
Chez Sony, le passage au millier supérieur accompagne d’ordinaire une révision du matériel, comme l’ont illustré les différentes itérations de la PS5 au fil de ses évolutions internes. La logique voudrait donc que CFI-Y2000 cache un Portal remanié, la seconde référence désignant une déclinaison régionale du même appareil. La fiche ne dit rien de l’écran ni du reste de la configuration : ce type de certification ne couvre que les composants sans fil. Sony, fidèle à ses habitudes, n’a rien commenté.
Fin janvier déjà, l’informateur Kepler_L2, dont les antécédents sur le matériel AMD plaident pour lui, affirmait sur un forum spécialisé que le Portal « semble être un succès » et qu’une « version OLED » sortirait dans l’année. La dalle est le talon d’Achille de l’appareil : un écran LCD de 8 pouces en 1080p, honnête, mais incapable des noirs profonds et des contrastes qui font la réputation de l’OLED tandis que la technologie d’écran supplante peu à peu du côté des consoles portables (Steam Deck en tête).
Du gadget moqué à la meilleure vente d’accessoires
Lancé en novembre 2023 à 219,99 euros, le Portal avait été accueilli avec scepticisme : un écran pour jouer à distance, dépendant de la PS5 du salon et de la qualité du Wi-Fi domestique. L’accessoire a pourtant dominé les ventes de sa catégorie aux États-Unis en 2024, où plus de deux millions d’exemplaires se seraient écoulés, soit environ 7 % du parc de PS5 local. Une dirigeante de Sony a d’ailleurs reconnu une demande supérieure aux attentes de l’entreprise.
Cantonné au départ à la lecture à distance des jeux installés sur la console, l’appareil a aussi grandi en cours de route. Il a gagné l’an dernier le streaming direct d’une sélection de titres PS5 via le cloud, réservé aux abonnés PS Plus Premium.
Pour qui comptait s’offrir un Portal dans les prochaines semaines, le dépôt mérite d’entrer dans l’équation. Une certification de ce type précède le plus souvent une commercialisation de quelques mois, et la fenêtre avancée par la rumeur, la fin 2026, approche. La prudence reste de mise tant que Sony se tait, l’entreprise n’ayant confirmé ni l’existence d’un nouveau modèle ni son calendrier. Sans oublier l’autre chantier prêté au constructeur, une PS6 portable capable de faire tourner ses jeux en local, mais qui piétine à cause de la pénurie de composants. Entre une référence inédite, une rumeur qui refuse de mourir et un succès commercial qui prend de l’âge, le faisceau d’indices n’a jamais été aussi fourni.

articles.title: Pediatricians renew call to ban raw milk as anti-science rhetoric reigns
articles.text:
As many doctors are moving ahead with the latest advances of modern medicine—from powerful obesity drugs to breakthrough cancer treatments—pediatricians are being forced to turn back, fighting to maintain advances in children’s health that were hard-won decades ago.
With anti-vaccine advocate Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as health secretary, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) has spent a considerable amount of time and resources in the past year fiercely defending lifesaving vaccinations—safe, routine shots that have saved the lives of millions of children over decades and thwarted untold suffering and disability.
But just this week, The New York Times reported that Ken Paxton, the attorney general of Texas, has opened aggressive investigations against pediatricians simply because they vaccinated their patients. Paxton falsely claims vaccines are part of a “multi-level, multi-industry scheme.” But critics say his anti-vaccine campaign appears more aimed at currying favor with Kennedy, President Trump, and their supporters as Paxton runs for the US Senate.
Meanwhile, the AAP this week had to renew another decades-old stance for children’s health—one against unpasteurized dairy, aka raw milk. Since the early 20th century, dairy producers in the US have briefly heated milk to kill the array of dangerous pathogens that naturally dwell in and around cattle and can easily migrate into milk. The simple intervention of pasteurization contributed to a sharp, “remarkable” drop in infant deaths and illnesses.
But, much like vaccines, a flood of misinformation has eroded trust and understanding of this public health triumph. And again, Kennedy has been among the advocates working to reverse this health victory.
Regressive health
In recent years, state laws have been loosening on raw milk, despite a federal ban on interstate commerce. At least 27 states now allow raw milk sales. In turn, outbreaks from raw milk have increased over the past two decades, the AAP highlights. Nearly half the illnesses in these outbreaks are in children—who are particularly vulnerable to foodborne pathogens.

articles.title: Denuvo DRM removed from Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, and everyone is wondering why
articles.text:
In context: Denuvo is one of the most hated copy-protection solutions in PC gaming. The company behind the DRM is struggling to keep resourceful pirates at bay, while some studios are already backtracking on their earlier decision to implement the technology.
Earlier this month, the studios working on the Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis remake updated the game's entry in Steam's database. The update appears to remove Denuvo's anti-tamper technology, potentially marking a major change coming four months before the game's scheduled release on February 12, 2027.
While gamers are celebrating yet another major production getting rid of Denuvo, many are wondering why the studios made the decision in the first place. The Irdeto-owned technology is one of the most universally hated copy-protection solutions PC users have to deal with right now, yet many high-profile publishers are still quite willing to implement it in their latest games.
Some users suggested that the developers could re-add Denuvo closer to the game's launch, or even add something "even worse" to the game's executable. Some are even speculating that Tomb Raider pre-orders are doing so poorly that publisher Amazon Game Studios decided to strip the much-maligned DRM from the game to score a small PR win among Lara Croft fans.
Either way, things could change considerably before the game's actual release. Some studios remove Denuvo from their games a few months after launch, while others confirm the DRM's presence when a game is just about to arrive in stores. Denuvo is often blamed for poor performance on otherwise capable PC hardware, but other DRM solutions can perform even worse in this regard.
Over the past few years, Denuvo has made quite a splash among DRM-friendly studios. The anti-tamper technology proved to be a very capable solution for protecting early sales, until hypervisor-based "tricks" and Voices38 started targeting Denuvo-enabled games.
Every Denuvo-protected game released before April 2026 has been cracked, and Irdeto is now resorting to lawyers in an attempt to fight back against pirates. Irdeto recently targeted Voices38, the mysterious developer who has released many successful Denuvo cracks after "Empress" left the piracy scene.
After being targeted by Irdeto and Denuvo, Voices38 said that everything was "fine" and that cracks would continue as usual. Voices38 did not release any cracked games after that message, while Denuvo continues hunting for the coder in an attempt to uncover their real identity and location.

articles.title: Google Playground permite criar jogos sem saber programar • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Google Playground permite criar jogos sem saber programar
Google Playground funciona como um chatbot de IA, só que direcionado à criação de games.
Se você sempre quis desenvolver jogos, mas não tem conhecimento para isso, pode se aventurar no Google Playground, se estiver nos Estados Unidos. Estamos falando de uma recém-lançada plataforma de IA que cria games de acordo com as instruções (prompts) dadas pelo usuário.
Sim, funciona como um ChatGPT ou um Gemini, mas focado em jogos. Tudo o que o usuário precisa fazer é acessar o site do Google Playground e descrever como quer que o jogo seja criado. Pode-se gerar games totalmente do zero, usar prompts pré-prontos como ponto de partida ou recorrer ao suporte guiado de criação.
O usuário pode testar o jogo assim que o Playground apresentar o resultado. Se algo tiver que ser removido, ajustado ou acrescentado, basta dar novas instruções.
A qualquer momento, é possível reescrever regras, ajustar parâmetros de física, modificar o cenário, alterar características de personagens e assim por diante. Não é preciso ter conhecimentos de programação para realizar essas tarefas.
Pode-se criar jogos 2D ou 3D. Sobre esta última categoria, chama a atenção a integração do Playground ao também recém-anunciado Unity Spark, outra plataforma para criação de jogos via IA, mas mais avançada.
Nesse sentido, o Google afirma que o Spark permite “mecânicas robustas de nível profissional, recursos 3D de alta fidelidade e a flexibilidade do ambiente de execução do Unity”.
O Unity Spark não é obrigatório. O Playground conta com outros recursos para a geração de jogos, que incluem os modelos de inteligência artificial do Gemini, o Nano Banana, o Lyria (para efeitos sonoros) e uma camada de software desenvolvida pelo Google especialmente para games.
Os jogos gerados via Playground são direcionados a navegadores, podendo ser executados tanto em dispositivos móveis quanto no desktop. Depois de criados, eles podem ser mantidos pelo usuário como privados em sua conta na plataforma ou serem publicados na galeria Playground Explore, onde podem ser compartilhados.
O Google Playground tem um site oficial. Mas agora vem o balde de água fria: por enquanto, a novidade só está disponível para usuários baseados nos Estados Unidos, até porque a plataforma está em fase experimental. Por lá, é preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para usar o serviço.
Leve em conta também que o Playground libera recursos seguindo níveis de distribuição, que variam conforme a assinatura que o usuário mantém no Google One. Quem não assina o Google One tem acesso somente a recursos básicos.
Quem está fora dos Estados Unidos não consegue criar jogos, mas pode acessar os já existentes. Eu, pelo menos, consegui acessar o Playground Explore estando no Brasil.

articles.title: SK hynix Reportedly Faces Difficulties in HBM Hybrid Bonding, Trailing Samsung
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 7th 2026
SK hynix Reportedly Faces Difficulties in HBM Hybrid Bonding, Trailing Samsung
According to a process development engineer at SK hynix's future technology research institute, who spoke with Damnang, SK hynix is reportedly facing challenges in developing hybrid bonding technology for its HBM memory. These issues are significant enough that SK hynix has not yet begun production of samples, while Samsung has reportedly already sent out samples of HBM manufactured using hybrid bonding to customers. If true, this represents a major setback for SK hynix, whose HBM has held the top spot in global market share by revenue. This could potentially lead to a loss of market share among customers who require higher capacities, better performance, and more advanced technology from their HBM suppliers.
For those unfamiliar, hybrid bonding creates a permanent bond between two silicon chips using embedded metal bumps that are fused together to form a single chip. Multiple dies or entire silicon wafers can be connected by stacking the back ends of two chips together. This technology eliminates traditional chip bumps and directly bonds copper interconnections between the two chips. Essentially, hybrid bonding can create shorter distances, reducing latency and improving performance, lowering signal distortion, and offering many other benefits.Whether any of this will impact SK hynix's market share depends on customer needs and their respective opinions. For example, among HBM shipments, which are now dominated by HBM3E and HBM4, SK hynix is the leading manufacturer with a 50% share, while Samsung holds 33%. SK hynix has experienced a slight decline, as the company previously captured 64% of the global spending on HBM memory but is now down to 50% as Samsung gains momentum.

articles.title: I bought this cheap $65 mechanical keyboard blind, and it ruined me for every other board I own
articles.text:
I bought this cheap $65 mechanical keyboard blind, and it ruined me for every other board I own
Sometimes the hardware matters more than the brand on the box
Sometimes you need a keyboard, and you need it now. That was where I found myself a couple months ago during local AI testing with one of the Nvidia GB10 boxes on my bench. Those systems are incredibly picky about which wired keyboards they'll work with for some reason, and moving the one known-good board I have on hand between systems under test was becoming a massive headache.
After one too many inconvenient keyboard swaps, I had had enough. I wanted a compact Bluetooth board that I could dedicate to my workbench, and I wanted it now. Testing on that GB10 system couldn’t wait, and I didn't want to get stuck in analysis paralysis. So I hopped on Amazon, filtered my choices down to items with same-day delivery, and found the Epomaker x Aula F75 Pro for just $65.
I was suspicious of this board at first, given the lack of in-depth independent reviews online and its unfamiliar switches. It uses Epomaker’s Leobog Reaper switches, which didn't map directly to any of the standard Cherry MX switches or their knockoffs that I'm used to.
But according to the spec sheet, they were linear and didn't have an incredibly heavy actuation force, which is the most important spec I look for in a keyboard when protecting my RSI-ravaged wrists. And they claimed to come pre-lubed, which is an upgrade I’ve never performed myself on any of my prior boards. So we were off to a good start.
The rest of the F75 Pro's feature list suggested custom keyboard DNA in its lineage. Spiffy dual-tone PBT keycaps with side legends? Check. A stack of noise-shaping and noise-reducing materials inside, including a cotton layer and a hefty silicone foundation? Check. A dedicated volume knob that doubles as a mute button? You got it.
Throw in wired, 2.4GHz wireless, and Bluetooth connectivity (with multiple Bluetooth pairing profiles), along with customizable RGB LED backlighting, and I was sold. And for such a low price, plus a few bucks extra for same-day delivery, I was willing to risk it if some aspect of this board wasn’t quite up to snuff.
A couple hours later, my Amazon delivery driver dutifully dropped the F75 Pro at my doorstep. And after a few minutes with the printed shortcut guide so I could pair it over Bluetooth, I had it connected to my GB10 box and was typing away in a terminal.
Despite this board’s low price, the Leobog Reaper switches underneath its keys are honestly the nicest I’ve ever felt. They’ve ruined me for every other board with MX-style switches I have. Whether it’s down to their pre-lubed treatment or inherent construction quality, they don’t have the tiniest bit of wobble or grit in their strokes like the red switch clones in many of my other mechanical keyboards.
The Reapers have a light 36gf initial force, a 45g actuation force and a 55gf bottom-out force, so they don’t place undue stress on my hands and wrists, and they have a nice, high-pitched audible “thock” at the bottom of their range that serves as pleasant reassurance for a successful keypress without rising to the level of a deafening click like blue-type switches might. The five-layer acoustic dampening stack within this board makes it the nicest-sounding one I own, too. And if I ever get tired of these particular switches, the Aula F75 has hot-swap support for easy modding.
I feel like I’m more accurate with these switches than I am with other boards in my office, and at 107 wpm with 99% accuracy on the MonkeyType test, I’m slightly faster than average on this board, too.
For all the thoughtful stuff that might be happening inside the F75 Pro's chassis, the outer plastic shell does feel a bit cut-rate. If you want the pleasure of knowing your board is clad in milled aluminum, carved stone, or some other exotic solid, this board doesn’t offer that satisfaction. But you're not touching the shell as you type. You're touching (and listening to) the keys. And I can attest that the tactile and auditory experience of typing on this board is far, far better than you would expect given its low price.
I also appreciate that most of the Aula F75’s functionality is available without installing any extra software. Although a utility is available, I’ve never felt the need to install it. I do have to refer to the included cheat card to figure out certain Fn combos, though, so don’t throw yours away if you get an F75 Pro of your own.
I do wish this board’s 75% layout dropped the volume knob for a dedicated Home key, but I can live with its existence on a Fn layer given the rest of this board’s virtues. And again, this board sells for $65 (and possibly even less during the current Prime Big Deal Days event). Given the hundreds of bucks that boards from big brands usually go for, I’ll enjoy what I hope is a long-lived and premium typing experience and keep the extra cash in my pocket.

articles.title: Canada is making it easier to build cell towers through new regulations
articles.text:
Canada is considering changes to the rules governing wireless infrastructure, with today being the deadline for final reply comments.
According to PlanHub, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) wants to streamline approval of new cell towers. Under this new proposal, local authorities would have 45 days to approve or formally challenge a project. If no action is taken within that window, the tower can be considered approved.
Telecom companies could also be allowed to build cell towers under 15 metres without the standard municipal and public consultation process. ISED is also looking at ways to make small-cell deployment easier, which PlanHub said could matter as carriers densify 5G networks.
Shifting to roaming and tower sharing, ISED has removed the wording requiring carriers to provide roaming only “where technically feasible,” and now requires roaming to be offered upon request when the customer’s device can access the host network.
A similar change will now be applied to tower sharing, as carriers will be required to share antenna sites when requested. Alongside this, technical disputes will move to arbitration instead of being decided directly by the ISED.
The Government of Canada also noted that both tower sharing and mandatory roaming are important, as it can “empower smaller or regional licensees to provide increased choice for Canadians through services and coverage competitive with those offered by the national wireless operators.”
Source: PlanHub

articles.title: Spiegelbild-Bakterien: Das steckt hinter dem zweiseitigen Projekt der Synthetischen Biologie
articles.text:
Spiegelbild-Bakterien: Das steckt hinter dem zweiseitigen Projekt der Synthetischen Biologie
Im Februar 2019 versammelten sich rund 30 Forschende aus Synthetischer Biologie und Ethik in Nord-Virginia. Sie berieten vier Tage lang über risikoreiche, aber womöglich bahnbrechende Vorhaben, die die National Science Foundation (NSF) fördern sollte. Schließlich einigten sie sich auf eine Idee: das Entwickeln von „Spiegelbild“-Bakterien.
Diese künstlich hergestellten Spiegel-Mikroben sollten so aufgebaut und organisiert sein wie gewöhnliche Bakterien – mit einer Ausnahme: Proteine, Zucker und Lipide wären Spiegelbilder der in der Natur vorkommenden. DNA, RNA und viele andere Bausteine lebender Zellen sind chiral. Das heißt, es gibt sie grundsätzlich in zwei Versionen. Diese Molekülversionen sind auf den ersten Blick völlig identisch, aber nicht deckungsgleich. Sie sind Spiegelbilder voneinander – wie unsere rechte und linke Hand. Für ihre Grundlagenforschung zu dieser Chiralität sind am 7.10.2026 die zwei Forscher Henri B. Kagan und Kenso Soai mit dem Nobelpreis für Chemie ausgezeichnet worden.
Dieser Text erscheint in der Ausgabe 6/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns mit der Schnittstelle, die immer mehr Macht in unserem Leben bekommen zu scheint: das Chatfenster. Wie uns das prägt, erfahrt ihr im neuen Heft, das es ab sofort im Zeitschriftenhandel und im Online-Shop gibt.
Spiegel-Bakterien: Zunächst großes Potenzial für die Biologie und die Medizin
„Jeder – wirklich jeder – fand das cool“, sagt John Glass in Bezug auf die zwei Versionen von Molekülen. Er gilt als Pionier bei der Entwicklung synthetischer Zellen am J. Craig Venter Institute im kalifornischen La Jolla. Es war „ein unglaublich schwieriges Projekt, das uns möglicherweise neue Erkenntnisse darüber liefern würde, wie man Zellen entwirft und baut, oder über den Ursprung des Lebens auf der Erde“. Die Gruppe sah auch großes Potenzial für die Medizin: Spiegelmikroben als biologische Fabriken, die Spiegelmoleküle als Grundlage für neue Medikamente produzieren.
Nach dem Treffen empfahl das Gremium der NSF, einige Forschungsgruppen finanziell zu unterstützen, damit sie Werkzeuge entwickeln und Vorversuche durchführen könnten. Die Begeisterung war groß. Auch die Nationale Naturwissenschaftliche Stiftung Chinas finanzierte Großprojekte in der Spiegelbiologie, ebenso wie das deutsche Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt.
Fünf Jahre später, 2024, sehen viele Teilnehmende des NSF-Treffens Spiegelorganismen eher als massive Bedrohung denn als Chance: Im schlimmsten Fall könnten diese Mikroben ein Ereignis auslösen, das jede Lebensform auf der Erde bedroht. Sie hätten keine Fressfeinde und könnten der Immunabwehr von Menschen, Pflanzen und Tieren entgehen.
