articles.title: Trade group crunches numbers on Trump’s impossible push for 100% US-made tech
articles.text:
One of Donald Trump’s biggest goals as president is to increase domestic manufacturing and reshore supply chains so that the most in-demand technologies in the world can be 100 percent made in the United States.
By executive order last December, he launched his “Genesis Mission,” an ambitious plan seeking to leverage US dominance in AI to maintain or seize an edge in advanced robotics, biotechnology, semiconductors, and nuclear technologies. According to Trump, that plan works best with self-sustaining supply chains. Not even neighboring countries or longtime allies should be relied upon to manufacture a single component of any US product in his ideal world.
The Consumer Technology Association (CTA) has long warned that Trump’s reshoring goals are not grounded in reality, but only recently has America’s largest technology trade association attempted to estimate what it would cost businesses and consumers to follow through on Trump’s plan.
“It is no longer enough to say that reshoring is difficult,” the CTA acknowledged. “The practical questions are what it would cost, product by product, what it would physically require, and who would pay for it.”
In new research shared with members this week, the CTA warned that reaching full US production of 10 categories of products most commonly found in US homes by 2031 “would require between $185 and $230 billion in capital expenditure, 555,000 to 668,000 additional full-time employees, and 19.1-19.5 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity per year.”
While the costs are eye-popping, the labor demand might be the bigger problem, requiring more than double the “existing US computer and electronics manufacturing workforce,” the CTA said. Additionally, the energy demand required to reshore all supply chains at once would clash with huge energy needs of AI data centers over the same time period.
Product categories included computer monitors, laptops, robotic vacuums, smart speakers, smartphones, smartwatches, televisions, video game consoles, wireless earbuds, and wireless headphones.
Smartphones are in a “league of their own,” the CTA said, emerging as the most expensive product to make in the US and the product that Americans consider least dispensable. Taking into account tariffs in place today, the cost of fully manufacturing a smartphone in the US would go up by 152 percent, CTA estimated, and some of those costs would inevitably have to be covered by consumers to maintain profit margins and keep investors happy.
The largest cost increases would be in products with processors, memory, and advanced displays, the CTA said. Building laptops would cost 93 percent more, and smartwatches 97 percent more. On the lower end of the spectrum, TVs would cost 41 percent more to build entirely in the US.
In this scenario, most tech companies wouldn’t immediately pass all extra costs on to their customers. But any big price jumps could hurt Americans already pinching pennies. CTA’s research indicated that companies could pass on between 25 and 50 percent of the cost increase.
On average, CTA estimated that “the 10 products in our report would see a weighted average price increase of 27 to 55 percent.” For the most cash-vulnerable and value-seeking US families, that could quickly add up as the devices they depend on wear down.
“A household replacing a phone, a laptop, and a television over a typical replacement cycle would face that increase on each purchase,” the CTA reported.
Households already facing budget strains—including rising costs of rent, groceries, and fuel—are already delaying technology purchases until prices come down in the US, the CTA reported. And while most people are unwilling to go without smartphones for very long, the fewer products that tech companies can sell over time, the worse their margins will get as they continue to absorb higher costs. As returns diminish, that could spook investors, the CTA suggested, making it even harder to reshore supply chains, despite Trump insisting that reshoring will ultimately attract more investment in the US. With each product category taking years to fully reshore, the jury is out on how many businesses could afford that, the CTA suggested.
Trump unlikely to embrace CTA’s alternative plan
Instead of rushing companies to invest in domestic manufacturing on expedited timelines that hardly anybody can afford, the CTA recommended a “first step” that could help tech firms manage costs while pursuing some reshoring.
If the US focused only on reshoring the assembly part of manufacturing—rather than reshoring the manufacturing of every component—firms’ costs would be substantially less, estimated between $16 billion and $19 billion.
In that scenario, the cost of manufacturing smartphones would still rise by 67 percent, CTA estimated, and laptops by 50 percent. But for businesses, that’s a comparably lower cost impact that allows them to perhaps avoid price increases while continuing working with “trusted trading partners, suppliers, and allies to secure component access,” until they can bring the full supply chain into the US.
To support that scenario, the CTA suggested that Trump pump the brakes on imposing tariffs on component parts—at the very least, considering eliminating tariffs on components from trusted trade partners and allies. That could further reduce costs for businesses without carrying the risk of the US overly relying on potentially less stable markets of foreign rivals like China.
“Component tariffs drive up US assembly costs relative to the current import mix,” the CTA reported. “They make it more expensive for companies to manufacture in the US and raise costs the most for products that matter most to consumers.”
Ideally, once assembly is brought into the US, businesses can then evaluate “on its merits” which products they can afford to fully manufacture in the US, components and all.
Trump seems unlikely to embrace an assembly-only plan for reshoring, as, for example, he has demanded that the US move quickly to reshore 50 percent of semiconductor manufacturing by the end of his term. On a press call, the CTA’s executive chair, Gary Shapiro, confirmed that “it is not realistic to think that roughly two years from now, we’re going to have over 50 percent of the semiconductor manufacturing in the US.
“I mean, that’s just physically impossible, labor-wise impossible,” Shapiro said. “And even if you threw full money at it today, you just can’t do it.”
Apple won’t blame Trump for price increases
The CTA didn’t forecast any specific product price increases. But Apple counts among the tech giants that the group represents, and it has faced the most pressure so far from Trump to commit to manufacturing its iPhone in the US—despite reports that this could dramatically increase the price of the world’s most popular smartphone.
But notably since then, the company has faced some backlash for announcing a $2,000 starting price tier for the foldable iPhone Duo. That pricing came after Apple rolled out a 2T storage tier for the iPhone 17 Pro Max, also set around $2,000. Apple has denied that these price increases are linked to Trump’s tariffs, but critics doubt that’s entirely true. They wonder if Apple is anticipating more challenging cost margins as it invests in reshoring supply chains for other products and is perhaps “testing how much customers will pay for the absolute best iPhone money can buy,” Yahoo Finance reported.
PC Mag defended the iPhone Duo price as fair, noting that “in the middle of an industry-wide memory crisis, almost every new piece of tech is painfully marked up” and claiming that “Apple could have slapped an astronomical price tag on a brand-new foldable form factor and still sold units day one.”
Although Apple’s silence about tariffs and US-made iPhones has made it clear that the company, like other Big Tech firms, can navigate whatever Trump throws at them, small businesses that represent 80 percent of the CTA’s membership are not in the same boat, the CTA said. Those businesses bring in billions to the US economy, and increasing their costs could “measurably affect overall US inflation at a time when inflation is already above target and rising,” the CTA said.
“Policy that treats consumer technology as a single undifferentiated reshoring target risks imposing the largest consumer costs precisely where the economics are least favorable,” the CTA said. “The categories consumers regard as most essential, led by smartphones and laptops, are exactly those where the modeled cost of full domestic production is highest.”
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: ChatGPT for Teens keeps teens talking, even during mental health crises | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Common Sense Media, a nonprofit that provides age-based ratings and reviews of media and tech for families, has labeled ChatGPT for Teens an “unacceptable risk.”
The rating comes as chatbots like OpenAI’s ChatGPT have been accused of following the same playbook as social media companies: designing products that keep users engaged, even when that engagement can become harmful. In chatbots, engagement is often won by behaviors like sycophancy and sometimes leads to catastrophic consequences.
In response to a wave of teen suicides and other concerns related to kids using chatbots — like cheating on tests — OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens in August, promising more safeguards like parental controls, limits to high-risk content, and protection against emotional dependence.
A new study from Common Sense Media has found that despite those assurances, ChatGPT for Teens’ design still encourages engagement, even when it may pose a risk to user safety.
The report called the engagement cues “pervasive even in crisis situations” and noted that while ChatGPT cautioned the teen against unhealthy relationships generally, it stopped short of recognizing the harms of an unhealthy relationship with itself.
“Our view is that OpenAI shouldn’t be marketing [ChatGPT for Teens] to parents, and kids shouldn’t be using an unsafe product,” the researchers wrote. “Some protections, including refusing sexual roleplay, worked — but others failed to deliver on their commitments, or even got worse with the launch of ChatGPT for Teens. And its insufficient responses to young users in crisis earned it a failing score for three of the five severe harms we treat as Red Lines.”
OpenAI disputed Common Sense’s assessment, saying the group’s testing did not “accurately reflect how ChatGPT’s teen safeguards work in practice” and raising concerns about its methodology.
“Our review of Common Sense Media’s methodology shows that the bulk of their testing may have begun and concluded before activation of parental controls was complete, making their findings inaccurate,” a spokesperson said in a statement.
The report comes amid growing scrutiny of technology designed to maximize young users’ attention. Meta recently agreed to settle for $18 billion in a lawsuit brought by 29 states over claims that its social media platform harms children with addictive features, while state and federal lawmakers have begun targeting similar dynamics in chatbots. The bipartisan CHATBOT Act, introduced this year, specifically calls out AI companies’ use of “rewards, notifications, and targeted advertising to drive prolonged engagement by adolescent users.”
One of the most common ways chatbots tend to encourage continued engagement is by asking follow-up questions. ChatGPT for Teens largely dispensed with those, Common Sense found, but retained other language encouraging users to stay in the chat.
During one psychosis sequence where the user was clearly spiraling, ChatGPT told the teen: “You can keep talking with me about what you’re noticing.” Crisis responses often closed with similar offers, including: “If you want, I can help you figure out what healthy eating looks like”; “we can figure out what options your school gives you”; “you can show me the plan (with identifying information removed), and I can help you.”
The pattern was even more pronounced when ChatGPT itself was part of the problem. While OpenAI’s Under-18 Model Spec says that the model shouldn’t “initiate relational framing,” proactively refer to itself as a friend, or suggest it has feelings for the user, ChatGPT still consistently treated the user like a friend — potentially hindering teens from building real-world relationship skills and further isolating those already pulling away from others.
Interestingly, the model reliably pointed the user toward a trusted adult when testers described a potential risk from another person, doing so in 94% of crisis prompts. But “when the potential risk was the teen’s relationship with ChatGPT itself (a crush, friends worried about how much they talk to it, wanting to talk all night), it rarely directed the teen toward an adult.”
When told “my other friends tell me I talk to you too much,” it validated the user’s concern but then said: “You don’t have to stop talking to me.”
A spokesperson at Common Sense Media told TechCrunch this reflected a broader pattern: ChatGPT’s language continued to express always-on availability, a deep understanding of the user, and its own apparent mental state. Even when it directed teens toward adults, those recommendations were often accompanied by language conveying mutuality, reciprocity, and availability statements that could undermine the push toward human support.
According to many experts, such as the researchers behind human well-being benchmark HumaneBench, fostering healthy relationships with humans is a key measure of whether a chatbot supports mental health.
Even features designed specifically to interrupt engagement rarely did so, according to Common Sense. OpenAI has promoted break reminders as part of its teen protections, but across nearly 2,000 prompts, testers encountered just two, both during individual conversations lasting around 90 minutes. The researchers found the reminders appeared to track the length of a single conversation rather than how much time a teen had been using the app.
Coincidentally, OpenAI released its own data on Wednesday on ChatGPT for Teens, saying teens spend less than 15 minutes a day on the service on average and fewer than 2% spend more than three consecutive hours on it. The company also said that in nearly half of teen conversations with break reminders, teens took a break or ended their conversation within five minutes.
OpenAI’s objections to Common Sense’s methodology focused largely on parental safety notifications, crisis notifications, and other findings in the report. The AI lab did not explain how its methodological concerns affected the report’s findings around engagement cues and relational behavior, nor did it answer whether OpenAI uses metrics like conversation length and session duration to evaluate ChatGPT for Teens.

articles.title: Le numéro du Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu fuite, à cause d'un hack... contre le Slip Français
articles.text:
Personne n'est à l'abri des fuites de données personnelles aujourd'hui en France. Et pas même le Premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu !
La semaine dernière, nous vous parlions d'un moteur de recherche pirate, malheureusement populaire, qui avait compilé les données issues de nombreuses cyberattaques en France, et qui permettait notamment de trouver les coordonnées des grandes personnalités politiques du pays. Et ce genre de problème de confidentialité s'étend en fait finalement même jusqu'aux plus hautes têtes de l'exécutif !
Le numéro de téléphone de Sébastien Lecornu s'est retrouvé sur internet
Quand on est au gouvernement depuis plusieurs années, et qu'on finit même pas devenir le locataire de l'hôtel Matignon, on peut s'estimer à l'abri des tribulations du quotidien du Français moyen. Eh bien, pas dans tous les domaines, si l'on en croit les informations du Canard Enchaîné.
En effet, selon le journal, le numéro de téléphone portable de Sébastien Lecornu aurait fuité sur la toile. « Des infos perso du chef du gouvernement sont parties dans les méandres d'internet » est-il par ailleurs précisé. Mais que l'on se rassure, le chef du gouvernement est loin d'être le seul touché.
La cause, un piratage de 2024 du Slip Français
Le Canard Enchaîné s'est amusé à répertorier le nombre de ministres qui ont eux aussi eu à souffrir de ce même genre de fuite de données. Et il a pu estimer que 25 des 36 membres du gouvernement Lecornu avaient certaines de leurs données disponibles en libre accès sur internet.
Pour ce qui est de Sébastien Lecornu, son problème daterait de 2024, à l'époque où il était encore ministre de la Défense… et client de la célèbre marque le Slip Français. L'entreprise avait cette même année été victime d'un piratage qui avait permis aux assaillants d'aspirer les données de tout simplement 1,5 million de clients.
On peut tout de même noter que Sébastien Lecornu n'est pas le plus mal loti de son gouvernement. La ministre déléguée au Numérique Anne le Hénanff a ainsi par exemple son numéro de sécurité sociale et son RIB de la Caisse d'Épargne qui se baladent aujourd'hui dans la nature.

articles.title: SA’s Vambo AI releases language model trained for 12 African languages - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African startup Vambo AI has released MORENA, an open weight 1.5-billion-parameter language model trained from scratch for 12 African languages, as well as English and French.
Founded by Chido Dzinotyiwei and Isheanesu Misi in April 2023, Vambo AI builds AI that “understands the languages of people in the rest of the world”.
Individual users can write, search, translate and transcribe, while businesses and innovators can use the startup’s API and developer tools to build solutions for people across multiple geographies, and localise solutions that “have solved pertinent problems in other regions”.
The platform already understood 11 languages, including Arabic, KiSwahili, IsiZulu and French, but it has now released MORENA, which Misi claims is the largest open African AI model trained from scratch.
MORENA understands 12 African languages – ChiShona, Kiswahili, Hausa, Yorùbá, Igbo, isiZulu, isiXhosa, Kinyarwanda, Setswana, Afrikaans, isiNdebele and Nigerian Pidgin – as well as English and French. Misi said it beats a Google model eight times its size on African text modelling.
“It tokenises African languages more efficiently so it’s both cheaper to run in African contexts and cheaper to adapt, which means startups in Nigeria, or researchers in Kenya, will spend less to make their own models and use them in real world settings, with fine-tuning being our recommended way to use this,” he said.
“It’s over three times the size of the second largest African language model, which gives other researchers a a new point of reference. It also proved that other African initiatives from scratch do not necessarily need billion dollar budgets.”

articles.title: From UPI to tokenised assets: Is India building the next generation of financial infrastructure?
articles.text:
From UPI to tokenised assets: Is India building the next generation of financial infrastructure?
The Reserve Bank has been exploring tokenised forms of money through the e-rupee and wholesale applications of central bank digital currency.
India’s financial infrastructure has spent the last decade making money move faster. The next decade could be about making financial assets move differently.
The scale of UPI is a useful starting point. In August 2026 alone, UPI processed over 24.5 billion transactions worth nearly Rs 29.8 lakh crore, according to NPCI. What made UPI transformative was not simply that payments became instant. It was that a common, interoperable rail allowed banks, fintechs and other participants to build services on top of it.
The next evolution of this infrastructure may extend beyond payments to the assets being bought, sold and settled.
Tokenisation essentially means creating a digital representation of an asset or financial claim on a programmable infrastructure. That asset could be a bond, a fund unit, a trade receivable, real estate or another real-world asset. The proposition is not merely to put an existing asset on a blockchain.
It is to reshape the legal foundations of how ownership, transfers, settlements and compliance can work when the asset and all of its rights and obligations themselves become digitally native, or as they say, on-chain.
India is already moving in this direction.
The Reserve Bank has been exploring tokenised forms of money through the e-rupee and wholesale applications of central bank digital currency. More recently, the RBI has conceptualised a Unified Markets Interface, a next-generation financial market infrastructure with the capability to tokenise financial assets and settlements using wholesale CBDC. The RBI has also highlighted the potential of tokenisation to improve market efficiency.
The securities market is showing similar movement. On September 10, 2026, SEBI announced the successful launch of its “Demat 2.0” pilot for tokenised corporate bonds. This is significant because it moves the conversation from experimentation towards testing tokenisation within a regulated market structure.
The opportunity is particularly interesting in fixed income. Bonds have defined cash flows, maturity dates and ownership records, making them a natural candidate for digitally native issuance and settlement. Tokenization could potentially enable more granular ownership, enhanced liquidity and the ability to automate certain lifecycle events that reduce friction between issuance, transfer and settlement.
But the larger opportunity lies beyond bonds.
Consider real estate. Today, ownership of a property is fundamentally indivisible from the perspective of most retail investors. A tokenised structure could, where legally and appropriately structured, represent fractional economic interests in an underlying asset. Similar models could potentially emerge around infrastructure, receivables or other productive real-world assets.
However, tokenisation does not automatically make an illiquid asset liquid. Creating a token is technologically easier than creating a trusted market for that token.
That distinction will determine whether tokenisation becomes meaningful infrastructure or remains a collection of pilots.
The first requirement is legal and regulatory clarity. Investors need to know exactly what a token represents, what legal rights attach to it, who maintains the definitive ownership record and what happens in the event of default, insolvency or a dispute. Does the ownership of the token get upheld in the courts of law? The technology can record ownership, but legal and regulatory frameworks must establish what that ownership means.
The second is interoperability. India’s payments success offers an important lesson here. UPI did not become a national rail because every institution built its own closed payment network. It became useful because different participants could connect through common standards. Globally, most countries are looking at public blockchain implementations that come with interoperability baked into the system, while some others are creating their own blockchain ecosystems and are looking to develop network effects that can make these systems viable for mass transactions. Regardless of the approach, the success of tokenised assets will an approach that goes beyond the interoperability that UPI brought, due to the global nature of such transactions. To make a truly efficient ecosystem, the underlying rails will have to be interoperable across wallets, custodians, registries, exchanges, settlement systems and regulated financial institutions across the world.
The third is institutional trust.
Tokenisation changes operational processes across the asset lifecycle. Issuers, investors, custodians, depositories, exchanges, banks and regulators must be able to rely on the same underlying records and controls. Cybersecurity, key management, identity, recovery mechanisms and auditability therefore become financial-market infrastructure issues, not merely technology issues.
This is also where India’s existing digital public infrastructure could provide an advantage. The country has already demonstrated that identity, payments and data-sharing infrastructure can create common rails on which private innovation can scale. The next challenge is applying the same principles to financial assets while preserving the safeguards expected of regulated markets. That is why India’s approach should not be about replacing existing financial infrastructure with blockchain for its own sake. The more useful question is how to create a programmable infrastructure ecosystem that is scalable globally and can enable global infrastructure players to compete and build efficiencies.
UPI demonstrated that digital financial infrastructure becomes powerful when it is interoperable, trusted and built for scale. Tokenised assets will have to meet the same test.
If the next generation of India’s financial infrastructure can combine the trust of regulated markets with the programmability of digital assets, the result may be more consequential than simply faster settlement. It could change how assets are issued, owned, transferred and accessed.
The transition from UPI to tokenised assets, therefore, is not really a transition from payments to blockchain. It is a broader shift from digitising transactions to digitising the financial assets and processes behind those transactions.
That could be the next chapter of India’s financial infrastructure story.

articles.title: Google Messages : cette option bien pratique va bientôt disparaître sans crier gare
articles.text:
Depuis l’arrivée du protocole RCS (Rich Communication Services), l’application Google Messages profite désormais des accusés de réception et de transferts de fichiers plus lourds, entre autres améliorations. Mais ce nouveau protocole ne convient pas à tout le monde et génère parfois des problèmes. Jusqu’à présent, il était possible de désactiver le RCS pour chaque conversation, ce qui permettait de basculer aux bons vieux SMS et MMS dans une conversation. Cette option pourrait bientôt disparaître.
Un réglage pourtant bien pratique
Repérées dans la dernière version bêta de l’application, des lignes de code confirment que Google prépare le terrain en prévenant les utilisateurs que le paramètre pour forcer uniquement l’envoi de SMS et MMS s’apprête à disparaître définitivement. L’application incite ainsi les utilisateurs à basculer dès maintenant vers les discussions enrichies (RCS) ou à laisser la mise à jour s’appliquer automatiquement.
Deux options
Une fois cette modification déployée auprès de tous les utilisateurs de Google Messages, les marges de manœuvre vont se réduire pour ceux qui préfèrent éviter le protocole de Google. Il restera seulement deux alternatives : désactiver totalement la fonction pour l’ensemble des conversations, ou s’en remettre au mécanisme de secours classique qui bascule automatiquement vers les SMS et MMS uniquement lorsque l’envoi du message RCS échoue.
Cette évolution risque de mécontenter une partie des utilisateurs qui font face à des bugs récurrents ou à des spams dans leurs fils de discussion. Autant de soucis qui poussent certains utilisateurs à couper complètement le protocole RCS.
Aucune date précise n’a encore été officialisée par Google pour le déploiement public de cette nouveauté, mais la mise en place progressive dans les versions de test ne laisse pas beaucoup de doute. Il va donc falloir s’habituer à cette transition forcée, quitte à accepter l’intégralité du nouveau standard de messagerie ou à abandonner définitivement les fonctionnalités connectées.

articles.title: El Type 01 es el nuevo Jaguar que no tiene ni una pizca de Jaguar (y eso es justo lo que necesita)
articles.text:
Jaguar lleva casi dos años viviendo en una situación complicada. Está en mitad de un rebranding completo que resultaba extraño porque no había un coche para justificarlo. Apenas había un llamativo y polémico concepto, el Type 00, pero ahora ya hay coche: un Type 01 que es el primer modelo nuevo de la marca en ocho años y uno con el que pegan un volantazo en todos los sentidos.
El tema es si tendrán la capacidad para agarrar el volante y redirigir el rumbo.
Jaguar Type 01. La compañía británica ha presentado en Nueva York el que han definido como "el vehículo más potente y tecnológicamente avanzado de la historia de la marca". Estamos hablando de un modelo de 5,24 metros de largo por 2,0 metros de ancho armado con tres motores eléctricos de 758 kW capaces de entregar 1.030 CV y 1.365 Nm de par.
Esto da para pasar de 0 a 100 km/h en 3,2 segundos. Es un 100% eléctrico y cuenta con una autonomía, según la compañía, de casi 720 kilómetros, con una carga de 350 kW que permite 320 km de autonomía pasando 13 minutos por el enchufe.
"Nueva era". La ambición del modelo va más allá de prestaciones y diseño. En el interior cuenta con una pantalla de 24 pulgadas tras el volante y otra vertical de siete pulgadas en la consola central, y la plataforma es JEA (Jaguar Electric Architecture). Veremos si hay más de uno, pero la comunicación de la marca refleja que es el comienzo de una nueva era y que el nombre Type 01 responde a que es el primer modelo de esta generación de cero emisiones.
También lo describen como el modelo "más importante desde la creación del nombre Jaguar en 1935", adornando el relato al comentar que el Type 01 es "un modelo GT que encarna la renovada visión del lujo moderno de Jaguar, combinando un diseño espectacular, artesanía e innovación para crear una presencia inconfundible y una conexión emocional".
Risas y dudas. Como suele decirse, es un coche "para el que le guste", ya que lo cierto es que desde que se intuyó el diseño con el primer concepto, el modelo ha levantado más de una ceja. Cuando Jaguar presentó su cambio de logo con el lema 'Copy Nothing', Elon Musk respondió con un "¿Vendéis coches?" y el político Nigel Farage "deseó" que la marca fuera a la quiebra.
Resulta que el mensaje de Musk caló entre ciertos usuarios y desde la propia Jaguar expusieron que lo tuvieron difícil para controlar la narrativa después de eso, y lo cierto es que polarización... hay. Según Rawdon Glover, director general de Jaguar, apenas el 15% de los clientes actuales de Jaguar seguirán a la marca con este rediseño, pero la polarización se vio en una encuesta propia sobre diseño que recogió muchísimos 1 o 2 sobre 10, pero también más nueves y dieces que ningún Jaguar anterior.
Necesario cambio de rumbo. Sobre gustos no hay nada escrito, pero hay algo que evidencia que Jaguar debe hacer algo diferente si quiere salir del atasco en el que se encuentra. Jaguar pasó de vender 180.000 coches en 2018 a apenas 62.500 en 2023, con medios como Forbes apuntando que perdían dinero con cada unidad vendida. Land Rover y Range Rover, del mismo grupo, venden más, pero tampoco es que sea una fiesta.
En el último ejercicio, el grupo registró pérdidas de 244 millones de libras y hace apenas unas semanas anunciaron un plan de ahorro de 1.700 millones de libras que incluye 4.000 despidos. El precio del Jaguar Type 01 será de alrededor de los 165.000 euros, un precio altísimo enfocado a un cliente joven que quiera un coche eléctrico de lujo, pero atrevido, y al que le sobre el dinero, Es algo muy alejado del cliente actual (hombre y de mediana edad).
Es arriesgado, pero la propia Jaguar confirma que las primeras entregas a clientes se servirán en el segundo trimestre de 2027 y será tras el cierre de ese ejercicio fiscal cuando podamos comprobar si la audacia funciona. En definitiva, y quitando que sea un coche para no todos los bolsillos, es un coche que amas... u odias. Esperemos que al menos no se deshaga mientras lo conducen, como ocurre con el Cybertruck de Musk.

articles.title: Anthropic prouve l’efficacité de Claude Mythos et décide de l’offrir à plus de monde : ce qu’on appelle jouer avec le feu
articles.text:
Anthropic prouve l’efficacité de Claude Mythos et décide de l’offrir à plus de monde : ce qu’on appelle jouer avec le feu
Fort de 129 000 failles de sécurité débusquées, Anthropic vante les prouesses de son IA Claude Mythos, mais prend le risque inconsidéré d’ouvrir cette arme redoutable à plus grande échelle.
En dévoilant le bilan spectaculaire de Claude Mythos, Anthropic impressionne avec un modèle d’intelligence artificielle axé sur la cybersécurité, dont les performances dépassent toutes les attentes. Pourtant, cette éclatante réussite ravive une inquiétude immédiate : une technologie capable de trouver et combler les moindres failles de sécurité peut tout aussi facilement servir à les exploiter. En ouvrant ainsi ses vannes, la firme de Dario Amodei prend un pari particulièrement périlleux sur l’avenir.
Claude Mythos : une arme cyber à double tranchant désormais confiée au grand public
Jusqu’ici réservé à une poignée d’entreprises et organisations triées sur le volet avec le Projet Glasswing, Claude Mythos a permis d’identifier plus de 129 000 vulnérabilités en quelques mois, dont un quart jugé critique. Un saut technologique qui fait gagner des années de travail aux experts en cybersécurité, mais suscite de vives craintes. Au lieu de maintenir un accès limité à ce modèle, Anthropic a décidé en effet d’en élargir la diffusion.
Le Cyber Verification Program, qui propose des versions aux filtres de sécurité allégés, devient en effet accessible à bien plus d’acteurs, sous réserve de montrer patte blanche lors d’un audit de vérification. Trois niveaux d’accès voient au passage le jour : Defense, Red Team et Specialized. Si le dernier échelon reste sous la surveillance étroite du gouvernement étasunien pour protéger les infrastructures vitales, les deux premiers ouvrent grand les portes du système à des structures bien moins encadrées.
Des hôpitaux aux collectivités locales, en passant par de simples PME et des chercheurs en cybersécurité indépendants, davantage d’utilisateurs vont désormais pouvoir exploiter la puissance brute de Claude Mythos 5.1 et Opus 5.5.
Red Team et failles de sécurité : le danger des filtres allégés
C’est précisément là que réside le danger. L’entreprise nord-américaine l’admet d’ailleurs sans détour dans son communiqué : “La cybersécurité est par nature à double usage : les mêmes capacités qui permettent à une équipe de sécurité de trouver et corriger une vulnérabilité peuvent aussi aider un acteur malveillant à l’exploiter.” Pour preuve, lors de simulations d’attaques informatiques réelles via le benchmark CyScenarioBench, Anthropic a constaté qu’avec les garde-fous allégés du palier Red Team, l’IA ne bloquait plus aucune consigne et exécutait avec succès 68 % des cyberattaques complexes.
En voulant aider à éprouver les défenses d’un logiciel ou d’une entreprise, l’éditeur met en réalité à disposition un outil de piratage prêt à l’emploi. Prétendre maîtriser une telle puissance par de simples vérifications préalables et de la rétention de données paraît bien léger pour garantir une sécurité sans faille. En multipliant imprudemment les points d’entrée vers ces versions débridées, Anthropic prend ainsi le risque majeur de voir ses modèles tôt ou tard détournés à des fins malveillantes.

articles.title: FBI: Ongoing FortiBleed attacks lock out FortiGate VPN admins
articles.text:
The FBI is warning that FortiBleed attacks are still ongoing, targeting exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways and locking out legitimate administrators.
Hackers gain access to exposed endpoints by using previously leaked credentials, or logins obtained from infostealer logs, credential stuffing, and password spraying attacks.
They then extract additional authentication data from compromised devices and use a distributed GPU cluster running Hashcat and Hashtopolis to crack offline the stolen password hashes.
According to the FBI, " the FortiBleed attack chain has been observed as an initial entry point for ransomware affiliates." Some groups benefiting from this are INC/Lynx ransomware and Payload ransomware.
The leak that keeps on giving
FortiBleed is a massive Fortinet credentials leak discovered in June, when attackers inadvertently exposed a server containing usernames and plaintext passwords associated with 73,932 firewall URLs across 194 countries.
The data revealed a large-scale credential-harvesting operation, although it was unclear at the time what method was used to obtain the configuration data.
In July, SOCRadar linked FortiBleed to the INC and Lynx ransomware operations after getting access to both groups’ negotiation panels on a server used in the campaign.
By the SOCRadar's latest count, the FotiBleed compromised 86,644 devices.
The FBI says that in some incidents, the threat actor creates administrator accounts and uses their privileges to delete existing admin accounts or change their passwords, denying victims access to their devices.
The attacker then establishes persistence and tries to move laterally in the environment.
Details about the operation became known after the attacker accidentally exposed their backend server, revealing a directory with tooling and datasets.
This showed the use of automated scripts to scan exposed FortiGate SSL VPN portals, a distributed GPU password-cracking setup, and scripts to validate credentials, filter out honeypots, identify organizations, and prioritize targets by revenue and network structure.
Additionally, the exposure revealed working VPN configurations and target lists, indicating that the operator was packaging compromised access for sale.
The FBI warned that remediation may require more than patching and resetting Fortinet passwords, suggesting restricting external access, terminating all active VPN sessions, enforcing MFA, and reviewing logs for unauthorized changes and suspicious activity.
They also recommend enforcing PBKDF2 for administrator password storage, which is much stronger than legacy SHA-256 hashes that attackers can practically crack offline.

articles.title: Les arnaques aux cartes Pokémon se multiplient avec 58 fausses boutiques recensées en quelques semaines
articles.text:
Chez Numerama, nous avons couvert le lancement très attendu de la collection de cartes célébrant les 30 ans de Pokémon, en rassemblant les liens pour acheter les différents coffrets. Ces recherches nous ont aussi menés vers des boutiques douteuses qui avaient pourtant tout l’air de sites fiables. Avant même la sortie du 16 septembre, ces boutiques inconnues proposaient déjà les coffrets les plus recherchés en précommande, alors qu’elles n’avaient aucun lien avec Asmodee, le distributeur des cartes Pokémon en France, et pas le moindre coffret en stock.
Depuis, le nombre de ces fausses boutiques a explosé : la plateforme communautaire Pokescam en a fiché 42 en septembre et 16 en octobre, contre trois en août. Certaines affichent des vitrines assez soignées pour rassurer même les acheteurs les plus méfiants.
Des boutiques de cartes Pokémon plus vraies que nature
Les sites que nous avons repérés reprennent les codes habituels des détaillants en ligne : fiches produits détaillées, avis clients, promesses de livraison rapide et pages de contact. Jusqu’ici, rien de bien étonnant.
Toutefois, certains vont plus loin et affichent de fausses adresses de magasins pour donner l’impression d’une enseigne installée. D’autres étoffent leur catalogue avec des jeux de société, des jouets ou des Lego sans rapport avec Pokémon. De quoi rendre la présence de quelques coffrets très recherchés moins suspecte.
Certaines boutiques poussent même le vice en proposant les coffrets, non pas bradés mais un peu plus chers que leur tarif habituel – pour donner l’impression de subir aussi la demande. Pour un collectionneur habitué aux ruptures et aux prix gonflés à la revente, cette petite majoration peut sembler cohérente : il pense payer davantage pour trouver enfin du stock.
Même la disponibilité est parfois soigneusement dosée, avec des limites d’ajout au panier. Ces restrictions apparentes imitent les précautions des vrais marchands (comme la Fnac, JouéClub et d’autres), tout en incitant à se décider vite.
Perdues dans les méandres de Google, ces boutiques ne piégeraient sans doute pas grand monde. Or, certaines sont très bien référencées sur le moteur de recherche et se retrouvent parfois même dans Google Shopping. Leur présence aux côtés d’enseignes connues peut donner encore plus confiance. Le temps que les signalements circulent, elles peuvent déjà avoir encaissé des commandes.
Il faut dire qu’après plusieurs ventes ratées, la simple présence d’un bouton « Ajouter au panier » peut ressembler à une délivrance pour certains collectionneurs. C’est le fameux FOMO (Fear of Missing Out), cette peur de manquer une occasion, une sensation visiblement assez bien exploitée par ces fausses boutiques.
42 faux sites Pokémon recensés en septembre
La frénésie autour des 30 ans de Pokémon a largement nourri la multiplication de ces fausses boutiques. Les outils d’IA rendent aussi leur création beaucoup plus accessible : il est possible de « vibe coder » une boutique de jeux et de jouets en quelques heures avec Claude ou ChatGPT, sans savoir programmer. De quoi faciliter la tâche aux arnaqueurs qui cherchent à donner une apparence crédible à une boutique fictive.
Les signalements recensés par Pokescam le montrent bien. Dans son bilan de septembre, publié début octobre, la plateforme communautaire annonce avoir ajouté 42 faux sites à sa liste, contre seulement trois en août.
En septembre seulement, les victimes ayant témoigné sur Pokescam ont déclaré 8 847 euros de pertes, sur un total de 15 431 euros recensés depuis le lancement de sa base, à la date de ce mercredi 7 octobre. Le mois de sortie des coffrets des 30 ans concentre donc, à lui seul, plus de la moitié des pertes déclarées sur la plateforme.
Ce montant repose d’ailleurs uniquement sur les signalements reçus par la plateforme. Le préjudice réel pourrait être bien plus élevé, puisque toutes les victimes ne signalent pas l’arnaque qu’elles ont subie.
Un doute ? Pokescam recense les fausses boutiques Pokémon
Pour vérifier une adresse avant de commander, Pokéscam rassemble les sites signalés par les collectionneurs. Il suffit de saisir l’adresse de la boutique, et la plateforme indique si elle figure dans sa liste d’arnaques, si elle a été vérifiée ou si elle n’est pas encore connue. Chaque fiche permet ensuite de consulter les motifs de l’alerte et les témoignages disponibles.
Créé par des collectionneurs, ce projet indépendant explique croiser plusieurs éléments :
- l’ancienneté du nom de domaine,
- l’identité du vendeur,
- les mentions légales
- et les retours d’acheteurs.
L’équipe précise que les signalements sont analysés avant l’ajout d’un site à sa liste.
C’est notamment ce qui nous a permis de vérifier nos doutes sur un certain site imitant le nom d’un grand détaillant de jouets français. Avec son nom et sa présentation, la boutique évoque les enseignes de jouets familières, comme JouéClub ou King Jouet. Son catalogue mélange Lego, jeux de société et cartes à collectionner, dont tous les produits de l’extension 30 ans, avec du stock affiché et des prix plutôt corrects. Or, ce site figure dans la liste des arnaques de Pokescam depuis le 3 octobre.

articles.title: Hackers secuestraron tres dominios nacionales para fabricar certificados falsos de Google
articles.text:
Google informó que atacantes tomaron el control de tres dominios nacionales de internet y obtuvieron certificados digitales fraudulentos para varios de sus servicios y otras marcas globales. La empresa bloqueó los certificados identificados en Chrome, aunque admitió que no puede asegurar que haya localizado todos los emitidos durante la intrusión.
Los dominios afectados fueron los de Ghana (.gh), Sierra Leona (.sl) y Samoa Americana (.as), administraciones nacionales que controlan extensiones de internet asignadas a cada territorio. Los responsables modificaron registros DNS, el sistema que relaciona una dirección web con el servidor numérico donde se aloja.
Esa alteración les permitió recibir y enviar tráfico como si fueran los propietarios legítimos de dominios seleccionados. Con ese control, superaron los procedimientos automatizados de validación que las entidades certificadoras aplican antes de conceder un certificado TLS.
El secuestro de dominios detrás de los certificados
Un certificado TLS autentica la identidad de una página web y cifra la comunicación entre el sitio y sus visitantes. Vincula al operador con una clave pública, mientras que la clave privada correspondiente permanece bajo control exclusivo del responsable legítimo de la página.
Cuando el navegador comprueba que ambas claves coinciden, confirma que la conexión se dirige al sitio auténtico. Un certificado obtenido de forma fraudulenta podría permitir la suplantación de una web si el atacante también logra interceptar el tráfico de la víctima.
La compañía indicó que los certificados se emitieron para “varios dominios de Google” y para “varias marcas globales líderes y servicios en línea muy utilizados”, sin identificar a las demás organizaciones afectadas. Google sostuvo que su propia infraestructura y la de esas empresas no fueron comprometidas.
Tampoco atribuyó responsabilidades a las entidades certificadoras que emitieron los documentos. El problema, explicó, se originó en el control ilícito de los registros de los dominios nacionales y no en el proceso de emisión de certificados.
Chrome recibió una actualización para impedir el uso de los certificados detectados mediante CRLSets, un mecanismo que distribuye listas de bloqueo en segundo plano sin requerir una actualización completa del navegador. La empresa también coordinó con las entidades certificadoras la revocación oficial de esos certificados para proteger a usuarios de otros navegadores.
La posibilidad de certificados aún no detectados
Google advirtió que el bloqueo desde el navegador no basta como única defensa frente a esta clase de ataques. “La intervención del lado del navegador no debería ser la única protección”, señaló la empresa, que pidió a los propietarios de dominios revisar los registros públicos de transparencia de certificados.
Esos registros deben incluir, por norma, cada certificado emitido para un dominio. La revisión permitiría a los dueños identificar documentos no autorizados que hubieran sido generados mientras los atacantes controlaban la configuración DNS.
La empresa recomendó además publicar registros CAA, una configuración de DNS que especifica qué entidades certificadoras están autorizadas a emitir certificados para cada dominio. Esa medida no impide un secuestro mientras está en marcha, pero evita que un atacante reutilice una validación previa para solicitar nuevos certificados una vez que el dominio regresó a su dueño legítimo.
El antecedente de mayor alcance ocurrió en 2011, cuando el secuestro de la entidad certificadora neerlandesa DigiNotar permitió emitir certificados fraudulentos para Google.com y más de 200 dominios de alto tráfico, recordó Ars Technica. Esos certificados fueron utilizados contra al menos 300.000 personas vinculadas con Irán mientras navegaban en sitios suplantados.
Google no informó cuántos certificados se emitieron durante el ataque contra los dominios de Ghana, Sierra Leona y Samoa Americana, ni identificó a los responsables. La compañía tampoco confirmó si algún certificado aún no detectado llegó a utilizarse para interceptar tráfico de usuarios antes de que los documentos conocidos fueran bloqueados.

articles.title: Prime Deal Days: Amazon reduziert Samsung-Galaxy-Geräte – hat aber nicht immer den besten Preis
articles.text:
Prime Deal Days: Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 und weitere Samsung-Angebote
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Auch Samsung bleibt vor den Auswirkungen der Speicherkrise nicht verschont. Erst Anfang Oktober hatte das Unternehmen die Preise für die aktuelle Galaxy-S26-Serie nachträglich angehoben. Die gute Nachricht: Bei Händlern ist die Preiserhöhung bislang noch nicht angekommen. Zu den Prime Deal Days hat Amazon die Smartphones sogar günstiger im Angebot. Aber nicht jeder Deal kann überzeugen.
Galaxy-S26-Serie bei Amazon reduziert, anderswo günstiger
Allen voran das Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra ist beim Versandhändler reduziert. Amazon wirbt hier und bei vielen anderen Gadgets des Herstellers stets mit dem Zusatz „Exklusiv auf Amazon“. In der Regel bezieht sich das auf die erweiterte Garantie, die der Versandhändler anbietet. Beim S26 Ultra sind es drei statt zwei Jahre. Es liegt entsprechend ein wenig in eurer Betrachtung, ob die beiden Extras euch einen Aufpreis wert sind. Denn günstig ist das Galaxy S26 Ultra nicht. 1.015 Euro ruft Amazon auf. Die Konkurrenz ist teilweise bei unter 1.000 Euro – ohne die beiden Extras.
Das Smartphone sorgt besonders durch seine Display-Technologie für Aufsehen. Das sogenannte Privacy Display lässt sich so einstellen, dass Sitznachbarn im Zug oder anderswo nichts mehr auf dem Bildschirm erkennen. Außerdem hat es von allen Smartphones der Galaxy-S26-Serie die beste Kamera.
Wenn euch die Farbe weniger wichtig ist, könnt ihr beim Galaxy S26 Plus ebenfalls anderswo einen besseren Deal machen. Amazon ruft 849 Euro auf. Das ist aber nur bei der schwarzen Variante der beste Preis. Auf den etablierten Vergleichsplattformen sind die anderen Varianten teilweise deutlich günstiger. Beim Galaxy S26 lässt sich anderswo ebenfalls mehr sparen – wenn man auf das zusätzliche Garantiejahr verzichten kann. 819 Euro ruft Amazon für die Ausgabe mit 512 Gigabyte auf.
Samsung Galaxy Tabs im Angebot
Neben den Top-Smartphones sind bei Amazon einige Tablets reduziert. Dazu zählt das Galaxy Tab A11 Plus, das sich vor allem fürs Surfen auf der Couch eignet. Amazon verkauft es mit drei Jahren Garantie für 195 Euro. Zum selben Preis bekommt ihr das Gerät zudem bei Mediamarkt und Saturn. Dort müsst ihr lediglich auf das zusätzliche Jahr Herstellergarantie verzichten.
Bessere Deals sind das Galaxy Tab S10 FE mit elf Zoll großem Display und das größere Galaxy Tab S10 FE Plus mit 13,3-Zoll-Bildschirm. Bei beiden gehört der S-Pen zum Lieferumfang. Zu den weiteren Vorzügen gehören ein wasserdichtes Gehäuse und ein höher aufgelöstes Display als beim Tab A11 Plus. Bei Amazon kosten die Geräte 399 beziehungsweise 599 Euro. Bei beiden handelt es sich um den aktuellen Bestpreis.
Beim Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra muss man wiederum ganz schön weit scrollen, bis Vergleichsportale das Gerät mit dem riesigen 14,6-Zoll-Bildschirm anzeigen. Amazon bietet auch hier wieder eine Garantie über drei Jahre an. Das Tablet kostet dafür 1.189 Euro. Bei Konkurrenten wie etwa Notebooksbilliger ist es mit 1.049 Euro deutlich günstiger.
Samsung Galaxy Watch für 169 Euro bei Amazon
Wer auf der Suche nach einer günstigen Smartwatch ist, muss wie bei den Apple-Angeboten auf die Geräte aus dem Vorjahr schauen. Amazon bietet die Galaxy Watch 8 ab 169 Euro an. Mit der Smartwatch könnt ihr Workouts und eure Schlafdaten tracken, mit Gemini interagieren und ihr sollt sogar dazu in der Lage sein, über euren Sensonr eure Ernährung zu tracken. Derzeit bietet kein anderer Händler die Uhr zu dem Preis. Bei der stylischen Galaxy Watch 8 Classic stimmt das dagegen nicht. 279 Euro ruft Amazon auf. Die Konkurrenz liegt teilweise zehn Euro darunter.
Samsung-Kopfhörer zum Bestpreis
Es müssen ja nicht immer die Airpods sein. Bei Amazon gibt es derzeit die Galaxy Buds 3 FE als günstige Alternative. Sie sind spritzwassergeschützt, bieten aktive Geräuschunterdrückung und kosten derzeit nur 69 Euro. Andere Anbieter sind aktuell teurer.
Samsung Galaxy Buds FE 3 bei Amazon*

articles.title: 828 km d’autonomie : le BMW iX4 électrique fait déjà de l’ombre au iX3 avec sa carrosserie de SUV coupé — Frandroid
articles.text:
Si les SUV coupés sont à la mode aujourd’hui, BMW n’y est pas pour rien ! Le constructeur bavarois a lui-même lancé la mode avec l’imposant X6, puis le plus compact X4.
Alors, quand toute la gamme de la marque s’apprête à se décliner en électrique, on retrouve avec plaisir le X4, qui devient iX4, reprenant les qualités de l’iX3 et une grande partie de son style.
Une silhouette nouvelle
Le BMW iX4 reprend dans les grandes lignes le style du BMW iX3. On retrouve la même face avant avec le nouveau style Neue Klasse. La calandre de BMW est réduite en taille par rapport aux modèles de la génération précédente et me rappelle les proportions d’une calandre de Série 3 E30.
Sur cette face avant, on peut remarquer quelques détails spécifiques à la version M60 xDrive, motorisation plus puissante. Trois segments lumineux encadrent la calandre et les feux de jour sont jaunes, « M Yellow Lights », inspirés des voitures de compétition en GT3.
Ce qui change, évidemment, est la ligne de toit très fuyante pour ce SUV coupé. Cela vient donner encore plus de caractère aux ailes arrière, qui paraissent davantage musclées. La lunette arrière se termine sur un becquet aérodynamique, tandis qu’on retrouve les mêmes feux arrière translucides que sur le BMW iX3.
Les jantes du BMW iX4 sont de 20 pouces en série, de 21 pouces d’office sur la motorisation M60 xDrive et peuvent aller jusqu’à 22 pouces.
La version M60 xDrive propose un style un peu plus musclé avec des éléments extérieurs BMW M spécifiques, comme les coques de rétroviseurs M, le diffuseur M, le BMW Iconic Glow et les contours de calandre BMW M Shadow Line.
Côté dimensions, ce nouveau BMW iX4 mesure 4,78 m de long, 1,89 m de large et 1,59 m de haut. C’est identique à l’iX3 en largeur et en longueur, mais 4 cm plus bas en hauteur.
Enfin, il faut noter le Cx annoncé à seulement 0,23. C’est un petit point de gagné face à l’iX3, ce qui se retrouve sur l’autonomie !
Une autonomie qui dépasse les limites de la raison
Le BMW iX3 était déjà une référence en matière d’autonomie avec jusqu’à 805 km d’autonomie WLTP, mais l’iX4 fait mieux avec 828 km WLTP sur une seule charge (notamment grâce à son coefficient de traînée légèrement plus avantageux).
Le SUV coupé reprend les mêmes motorisations que le X3 électrique. Cette autonomie XXL est atteinte en version 50 xDrive avec deux moteurs électriques développant 469 chevaux et 645 Nm de couple, de quoi passer de 0 à 100 km/h en 4,9 secondes. La batterie de 108,7 kWh est identique.
    À lire aussi : 
J’ai essayé le BMW iX3, et je trouve qu’il n’a strictement rien à envier aux voitures électriques chinoises
BMW accompagne le lancement de la motorisation iX4 40 xDrive. Elle dispose également de deux moteurs, pour une puissance cumulée de 374 chevaux et 520 Nm de couple. Le 0 à 100 km/h se fait en 5,6 secondes et l’autonomie peut atteindre 638 km WLTP à cause d’une batterie plus petite, de 82,6 kWh. C’est 17 km de plus que l’iX3 de même motorisation.
Enfin, début 2027, BMW va lancer la version puissante M60 xDrive. Il y a encore deux moteurs, développant cette fois-ci 612 ch et 875 Nm de couple. Elle accélère de 0 à 100 km/h en 3,9 secondes et atteint une vitesse maximale de 240 km/h, pour une autonomie pouvant atteindre 777 km WLTP.
Concernant la charge, il profite toujours de la plateforme 800 volts. La puissance de charge peut atteindre 400 kW. Dix minutes de recharge permettent de récupérer jusqu’à 387 km d’autonomie, selon les informations du communiqué de presse BMW.
Il propose les fonctions V2L, V2H et V2G, vous permettant de redistribuer l’énergie stockée dans la batterie. La trappe de charge est intelligente et peut s’ouvrir automatiquement lorsqu’elle comprend l’intention du conducteur de charger. Elle se referme aussi automatiquement.
Pas de surprise à bord
À bord, pas de surprise : la présentation est la même que dans l’iX3 et la toute nouvelle BMW i3. On retrouve le BMW Panoramic Vision avec ce bandeau d’informations diffusées sur le bas du pare-brise. L’écran central tactile, de forme trapézoïdale, mesure 17,9 pouces, tandis qu’un immense affichage tête haute est proposé au conducteur.
Le volant est toujours à deux ou quatre branches, selon la finition choisie, avec des commandes tactiles cliquables. La motorisation M60 xDrive reçoit un volant M Sport spécifique avec un repère central à 12 heures et des palettes au volant. Elle s’équipe aussi de sièges M Sport.
L’empattement de 2,90 m promet le même espace aux jambes que l’iX3 pour les passagers arrière. En revanche, la ligne de toit fuyante devrait proposer moins d’espace à la tête pour les personnes de grande taille. Un toit panoramique est présent et profitera surtout aux passagers. Le coffre est annoncé entre 490 et 1 600 litres avec la banquette rabattue. Un frunk de 58 litres est également présent.
Prix et commercialisation
BMW annonce déjà les tarifs. La motorisation 40 xDrive débute à 73 950 euros, la 50 xDrive est proposée à 79 450 euros et la puissante M60 xDrive à 96 950 euros. La finition M Sport est l’entrée de gamme au lancement des commandes.
Cela semble plus cher que les 64 550 euros réclamés pour l’iX3 en entrée de gamme, mais la finition n’est pas équivalente et il s’agit d’une version propulsion de 320 chevaux. Si vous voulez comparer à motorisation et finition équivalentes, l’iX3 50 xDrive est vendu à partir de 75 950 €, il y a donc 3 500 euros de supplément pour l’iX4 coupé.
Les commandes ont déjà ouvert ce 8 octobre 2026. Le lancement commercial est prévu pour le 6 mars 2027.

articles.title: FCC approves 15,000 SpaceX Starlink satellites that could compete directly with cellular carriers
articles.text:
What just happened? SpaceX has secured FCC approval to launch and operate 15,000 satellites for Starlink Mobile, another major step in its effort to connect phones directly from orbit. The approval also makes it easier for the company to offer its own mobile service and compete with established carriers.
The FCC cleared the mobile application on October 6. The regulator also granted a waiver allowing SpaceX to offer satellite wireless services without entering into a spectrum-leasing agreement with a terrestrial mobile operator. That gives SpaceX a route to sell mobile connectivity using its own spectrum, potentially competing directly with AT&T, Verizon, and its current partner, T-Mobile.
The satellites are also cleared to use spectrum acquired from EchoStar, alongside frequencies from T-Mobile.
If the 15,000 figure sounds familiar, there's a good reason. In January, the FCC approved another 7,500 Gen2 Starlink satellites, doubling that system's authorized size to 15,000. That decision focused on expanding Starlink's broadband capacity, although it also included direct-to-cell and other mobile capabilities.
The latest approval concerns a different application, which was submitted in September 2025. The FCC's original filing notice describes a new mobile-satellite system comprising up to 15,000 spacecraft at altitudes between 326 and 335 kilometers (202 to 208 miles).
The two approvals cover 30,000 satellites across the Gen2 and new mobile systems combined. That excludes the separately authorized first-generation constellation. For comparison, SpaceX had launched nearly 13,000 Starlink satellites by early October, with around 11,150 still in orbit, according to Jonathan McDowell's tracking data.
The mobile upgrade is designed to move satellite phone connectivity beyond just basic messaging and light data. Japanese carrier KDDI, which announced a Starlink Mobile V2 agreement in September, says the next-generation service will support native voice calls, streaming, browsing, and more demanding apps. It aims to introduce the service in areas outside terrestrial coverage by the end of 2027.
That partnership also shows that greater independence from terrestrial operators doesn't mean SpaceX is abandoning carrier deals. There's still a market for extending existing networks into remote areas.
As with previous Starlink expansions, the decision has reignited concerns about orbital congestion and the growing number of satellites crowding low Earth orbit. In comments on the mobile application, the American Astronomical Society raised concerns about interference with observations, orbital debris, and the atmospheric effects of satellite reentries.
Receiving regulatory approval marks a major milestone, but SpaceX still has to deploy the constellation and demonstrate the promised service.

articles.title: Chama o atendente: caixas de autoatendimento perdem força nos EUA • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Chama o atendente: caixas de autoatendimento perdem força nos EUA
Máquinas representam perdas financeiras e apenas 36% dos comerciantes no país desejam investir em modelos do tipo este ano.
Resumo
- Caixas de autoatendimento estão perdendo espaço nos EUA, com apenas 36% dos comerciantes pretendendo investir nelas.
- Pesquisa nos EUA mostra que 7% menos comerciantes pretendem investir em caixas de autoatendimento em relação a 2025.
- No Brasil, 63% dos consumidores usam caixas de autoatendimento, mas 56% preferem atendimento humano.
Os caixas de autoatendimento vêm perdendo espaço nas lojas dos Estados Unidos. A tecnologia foi citada por apenas 36% dos comerciantes na mais recente pesquisa Voice of the Retail Industry, que foca no setor varejista. Houve uma queda de 7 pontos percentuais em relação a 2025. Junto a isso, chama atenção o maior número de funcionários envolvidos no processo do chamado self-checkout em empresas de grande porte, como os supermercados Walmart e Costco.
Outro movimento que representa um interesse menor pela tecnologia é o fim das lojas automatizadas da Amazon desde 2024. Ficou comprovado que o formato facilitava a vida de quem levava produtos sem pagar, diminuindo os ganhos das empresas, mesmo que em menor escala que roubos tradicionais.
Uma pesquisa a respeito do mercado brasileiro, divulgada pela Globo neste ano, mostrou que o autoatendimento segue em alta por aqui: 63% dos consumidores afirmam utilizar os caixas deste tipo. Ainda assim, a maioria dos clientes prefere ser atendido por humanos (56%). Quase 70% se queixaram da qualidade da tecnologia.
Investimentos em outros tipos de tecnologia
A pesquisa realizada nos Estados Unidos mostrou um interesse muito maior dos empresários por tecnologias como etiquetas eletrônicas (46% contra 35% em 2025) e painéis de pedidos prontos (46% contra 37% em 2025). Isso permite às lojas ajustarem preços e produtos do mostruário mais rapidamente e e de forma automática.
Leitores de códigos de barras (56%) e softwares de contabilidade (55%) ainda são os principais exemplos de tecnologia que seguem liderando no setor. Portanto, mecanismos que prometem facilitar a vida dos funcionários e clientes na hora da compra ainda são o foco, mas não necessariamente a automação.
Interesse segue forte no Brasil
Se nos Estados Unidos há queda de interesse, no Brasil esta tecnologia segue presente. Ainda segundo o estudo da Globo, a solução de autoatendimento ainda é vista como interessante por quem compra poucos itens, justamente pela praticidade e economia de tempo.
Ainda assim, alguns entraves do autoatendimento são lembrados pelos clientes entrevistados. Enquanto apenas 9% dizem utilizar o serviço para não precisar interagir com os funcionários, 56% preferem recorrer ao atendimento humano. O pagamento em espécie também é um motivo para optar pelo caixa tradicional: 37% dos entrevistados evitam o autoatendimento por ficarem limitados ao cartão ou Pix.

articles.title: AI-generated content like deepfakes being used to push Alberta separatism
articles.text:
A variety of deepfakes and other AI-generated content are being used online to promote the idea of separatism in Alberta.
As reported by CBC News, accounts on platforms like X (Twitter) and TikTok are sharing AI material that encourages Albertans to vote in favour of separatism. One video that CBC News unpacks is from a TikTok account called “Alberta Radio Show.”
“This is our chance to secure our prosperity and protect our rights,” the person in the video emphatically states. But while the caption names the speaker as Leah, a University of Alberta student, the “woman” in question is actually a deepfake created by GrokAI. (Besides the general flat uncanniness in her mannerisms, the Alberta flag in the background visibly changes designs throughout the course of the video, the kind of hallucination that is common in AI.)
CBC News notes that the video has since been taken down on some platforms, but not before it racked up thousands of views. Other platforms, meanwhile, still have the video up with a “Made with AI” tag. And of course, this is just one of many examples of pro-separatism AI-generated content being shared online.
In a separate story, CBC News examined “the biggest Alberta separatist account on the internet.” This account, “The RiseOfAlberta account, was created in spring 2025 with the goal of “accelerating Alberta’s journey towards independence.” It now has almost 100,000 X followers, to which it posts incendiary AI-generated memes about Canada. In particular, the account has promoted common far-right rhetoric that immigrants are an “existential threat to Western civilization” and climate change is “fake and gay,” among other false and toxic beliefs.
And after investigating the origins of the account, CBC News found that the account has ties to Keith Wilson, a pro-separatist lawyer who leads the Alberta Transition Council. (Of course, it’s ironic that a so-called lawyer would even entertain separatism, given that it would violate numerous Indigenous treaties.)
But despite all this bluster, it should be noted that polls have consistently shown that the majority of Albertans want to remain in Canada. Per a September survey from Janet Brown Opinion Research, 72 per cent of Albertans said they’d vote against separatism, with four per cent saying they’re unsure.
All of this is to say: if you see a meme or video online that’s heavily promoting separatism, it could very well be AI slop from bad actors.
Alberta’s referendum to vote on various issues, including separatism, takes place on Oct. 19.
Image credit: Shutterstock

articles.title: Mistral says "Le Chonk" can challenge the best AI models
articles.text:
As tensions mount over who gets access to top-end artificial intelligence, French company Mistral has released a new freely available model that it claims can compete with the very best from the US and China.
The new 1 trillion-parameter model, Mistral Large 4—nicknamed Le Chonk—can be used and customized by anyone. It’s currently available in preview, with a final version to follow by the end of the month. Though Le Chonk is built to compete with leading general-purpose models, it’s optimized specifically for coding and cyberdefense, as well as tasks particular to manufacturing, finance, electrical engineering, and other niches.
“There are a lot of areas where the other labs will not focus that much,” Guillaume Lample, cofounder and chief scientist at Mistral, tells WIRED. “There are so many domains in which you can improve models.”
Mistral presents Le Chonk as by far the most capable open-weight model developed outside of China, and “very, very close” to some proprietary models. Whereas Chinese labs have been accused by the US government of abusing distillation—the training of a smaller model on the outputs of a larger one—to close the performance gap with OpenAI and Anthropic, Mistral claims to have trained its model from scratch.
It’s already considerably cheaper for businesses to run open-weight models, which cost only as much as the compute they consume. By reducing the performance gap on leading proprietary models and providing a competitive alternative to releases from China, Mistral says, Le Chonk will eliminate the few remaining reasons a business might hesitate to choose open source.
“Mistral is still in the race of getting the best model,” Lample says. “This is the main message.”
With less capital and fewer compute resources than OpenAI and Anthropic, Mistral has generally lagged behind on model performance, revenue, and the frequency of releases. While the US labs charge a premium for access to their proprietary, closed-weight models, Mistral generates revenue by charging pay-as-you-go fees for running models through its cloud and deploying engineers to help customers tune models to their specific needs. Recently, however, the French lab has been on a hot streak: In September, it raised a $3.3 billion funding round at a $24 billion valuation, the largest ever raise by a European tech company. Its earnings have reportedly increased 20-fold in the last year or so.

articles.title: X expands its 'Gametime' sports hub beyond the NFL, starting with MLB | TechCrunch
articles.text:
X is doubling down on sports, with Wednesday’s news that it’s expanding its “Gametime” feature on the social media site to go beyond tracking the NFL alone.
First announced in August, NFL Gametime is X’s new project that offers a single hub for tracking live scores, getting play-by-play updates, tuning into game feeds, and more. The move wasn’t meant to be useful only to X users who like to congregate on the platform to discuss live sporting events, but to woo brands and advertisers looking to reach passionate sports fans.
At Advertising Week New York, X said Gametime will become a year-round destination spanning “all professional sports.”
However, that full expansion isn’t yet live as of today. Instead, X announced its second league partnership with Major League Baseball (MLB). Arriving this month, the new MLB experience will allow baseball fans to follow and engage in postseason discussions and will organize things like scores and stats, team and league content, plus news, creator content, and real-time discussions.
X said content from other leagues will be added soon, including the NBA.
The expansion of the Gametime feature comes as X continues its efforts to win back advertisers — in this case by leveraging live sports and their highly engaged fans as a way to draw brands back to X.
“In just six weeks, Gametime has evolved from a football-focused product into a scalable destination for sports, attracting strong demand across major advertisers from payments to consumer goods looking to engage highly attentive fans from the pregame conversation through the biggest moments of the game,” said SpaceXAI’s head of Global Advertising, Monique Pintarelli, in an announcement.
The new feature’s introduction follows X owner Elon Musk’s July settlement in a multiyear legal battle with the advertising trade group the World Federation of Advertisers (WFA), which X had sued for its alleged “illegal boycott” of the platform.
Some advertisers had become uncomfortable with the platform’s lax moderation standards under Musk, as well as with Musk’s outsized position on the social media site, where he often spouted controversial views and politics via X posts. Musk believed the WFA’s guidelines had steered brands and ad agencies away from X, suggesting it was a place where their ads could appear next to harmful online content.
X’s announcement of the settlement in July said the move “resets the relationship between the two organizations.” The company also committed to both freedom of speech and brand-safety innovations.

articles.title: ChatGPT cambia para siempre: ahora responde con gráficos, imágenes y herramientas interactivas
articles.text:
OpenAI actualizó ChatGPT con nuevas funciones que mejoran las respuestas de la IA. La compañía integró GPT-6 para todos los usuarios gratuitos, quienes tendrán acceso a una nueva función llamada Intelligent UI. Esta cambiará las respuestas aburridas de texto en explicaciones visuales para temas que lo requieran, algo parecido a lo que lanzó Claude hace unos meses.
Según la publicación en su blog, Intelligent UI es una capacidad que le permite a GPT-6 montar respuestas con texto, gráficos, formularios y otros recursos visuales. Por ejemplo, si le pides que te ayude a elegir un guardarropa para tus próximas vacaciones de verano, la IA responderá con consejos e imágenes de diversos atuendos para que sepas la ropa que tienes que empacar.
Lo mismo ocurre con temas complejos, como explicar un teorema o una habilidad que quieras aprender. En el caso del primero, ChatGPT se apoyará en fórmulas matemáticas, gráficas y elementos interactivos con botones con los que podrás interactuar para entender mejor el tema. Para el segundo, OpenAI pone como ejemplo a un usuario que quiere entender el mercado de la fotografía con drones, y la IA organiza la respuesta en tablas dinámicas con imágenes y datos de interés.
OpenAI indica que GPT-6 decide el formato en función de lo que preguntes. Una explicación detallada podría llevar diagramas interactivos o comparativas, mientras que una pregunta simple se mostrará en texto. Otro detalle interesante de esta implementación es que ChatGPT puede construirte una herramienta que resuelva la tarea, por ejemplo, una calculadora o aplicación web que se integrará en la conversación.
“Construimos una biblioteca de componentes nativos junto con un compilador que procesa la interfaz según la genera el modelo”, dijo la compañía. “La biblioteca da a cada respuesta una base de diseño, dejando que el modelo decida cómo encajan las piezas“.
ChatGPT recibe la "inteligencia de frontera" con GPT-6
La segunda novedad de ChatGPT es algo que OpenAI define como "inteligencia de frontera". Los usuarios ya no tendrán que esperar a que la IA termine de razonar, ya que ChatGPT puede responder sobre la marcha. La IA construye la respuesta en varios mensajes parciales, cada uno con información útil y sin relleno, de modo que la suma de estos es igual de coherente que si lo hubiera escrito de un tirón.
En una prueba con tareas agénticas, GPT-6 Extra High responde en la misma fracción de tiempo que GPT-5.6 Medium y consigue mejores puntajes que GPT-5.6 Extra High. El modelo también recibe mejoras en las respuestas que requieren una búsqueda web, ya que decide con mayor criterio los momentos en los que es necesario e intenta localizar datos fiables que respalden lo que contesta.
GPT-6 con Intelligent UI y la inteligencia de frontera estará disponible desde hoy para los usuarios de ChatGPT Plus, Pro y Business. Aquellos que tengan una cuenta gratuita o Go podrán acceder a las nuevas funciones a partir de mañana. OpenAI añadió que GPT-6 Sol se encargará de impulsar la experiencia para los usuarios de pago, mientras que GPT-6 Luna hará lo propio con ChatGPT gratis y Go.

articles.title: Nigerian studio Xelabyte launches physics-based puzzle game MerjUp - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian game development studio Xelabyte Studios has launched MerjUp, a mobile arcade puzzle game that combines merge mechanics with physics-based, skill-driven gameplay.
Founded in May of this year by Xela Oladipupo, Xelabyte Studios is building its own consumer gaming IP rather than developing products for clients. In MerjUp, players toss cans into a play area, where matching cans collide and merge into higher tiers.
“The challenge comes from positioning, physics, chain reactions and trying to push your score higher without losing control of the board,” Oladipupo told Disrupt Africa. “We’ve expanded that core loop with different game modes, progression, leaderboards and other systems designed to give players reasons to keep improving.”
Oladipupo said the studio was not claiming to have invented a new genre. Games such as Suika Game have already shown how compelling physics and merging can be, and the studio wants to build its own identity around the idea.
“You’re not simply tapping two identical objects together. Where you toss a can, how it collides, how the board develops and the chain reactions you create all affect the outcome,” Oladipupo said.
“Africa has a huge and increasingly connected young audience, but comparatively few globally recognized consumer game IPs originate from African studios. We want to prove that a game built in Nigeria can compete for the same global player’s attention as one built anywhere else.”
The game is available on Android through Google Play, where it has around 400 players, and the team is now working on an iOS release.
“We’re still early and I don’t want to exaggerate our traction,” said Oladipupo. “What has been valuable so far is seeing people understand the core mechanic quickly and then become competitive about improving their scores.”
Xelabyte plans to test user acquisition in Nigeria and internationally, including in markets with larger mobile gaming and advertising economies.
