articles.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 : 10 fois moins cher pour faire plier GPT-6 Luna sur son terrain — Frandroid
articles.text:
Anthropic décline ses modèles Claude en plusieurs tailles. Haiku est la plus petite, celle qu’on garde pour les tâches simples répétées des milliers de fois. Après Opus 5.5 le 22 septembre puis Sonnet 5.5 le 28 septembre, la famille 5.5 s’agrandit ce mercredi 7 octobre avec Claude Haiku 5.5.
Pour les développeurs qui paient l’IA à la consommation, c’est surtout la grille tarifaire qui change. Haiku 5.5 coûte 0,10 dollar (environ 0,09 euro HT) par million de tokens envoyés au modèle et 0,50 dollar (environ 0,45 euro HT) par million de tokens générés. Haiku 4.5, sorti en octobre 2025, était facturé 1 et 5 dollars.
Cette baisse inverse la tendance de la génération précédente. À sa sortie, Haiku 4.5 avait au contraire coûté 25 % plus cher que Haiku 3.5, facturé 0,80 dollar en entrée et 4 dollars en sortie (environ 0,72 et 3,58 euros HT). Haiku 5.5 repasse donc nettement sous le prix de ses deux prédécesseurs.
Un token est un fragment de mot. C’est l’unité que les fournisseurs d’IA comptent pour facturer. Une application qui confie des résumés de documents à Haiku 5.5 paie chaque token dix fois moins cher qu’avec Haiku 4.5, du moins sur les requêtes de moins de 100 000 tokens.
Anthropic présente Haiku 5.5 comme son modèle le plus rapide à ce jour. Une note de bas de page apporte quand même une nuance : Opus reste plus rapide quand on active son mode Fast, une version jusqu’à 2,5 fois plus rapide du grand modèle, facturée le double du tarif standard d’Opus 5.5.
Haiku 5.5 est aussi le premier Haiku qui propose un réglage d’effort. Le développeur peut donc choisir entre une réponse plus réfléchie et une réponse moins chère.
Anthropic cible les tâches courtes et nombreuses : résumés, tri de demandes, requêtes dans une base de données. Il y a aussi la compaction, qui consiste à condenser l’historique d’une longue conversation pour qu’un agent puisse continuer à travailler sans saturer sa mémoire. Haiku 5.5 est également pensé comme sous-agent, c’est-à-dire un assistant à qui Opus 5.5 ou Sonnet 5.5 confient les petites tâches d’un projet de code.
Dix fois moins cher par token, quatre fois moins par tâche
La baisse de 90 % ne vaut que pour les requêtes de moins de 100 000 tokens. Au-delà, Haiku 5.5 passe à 0,50 dollar en entrée et 2,50 dollars en sortie (environ 0,45 et 2,24 euros HT). Ça fait cinq fois son tarif de base, et la remise par rapport à Haiku 4.5 tombe alors à 50 %. Anthropic précise tout de même que 90 % des requêtes envoyées à Haiku 4.5 restaient sous ce seuil.
Autre nuance, Haiku 5.5 utilise un nouveau tokenizer, l’outil qui découpe le texte en tokens, et ce découpage consomme un peu plus de tokens pour le même travail. Une fois tout compté, Anthropic annonce donc une facture environ 75 % plus basse qu’avec Haiku 4.5. La baisse reste très nette, mais le « dix fois moins cher » ne vaut que par token et sous le seuil des 100 000 tokens ; à la tâche, la facture est plutôt divisée par quatre.
OpenAI facture GPT-6 Luna exactement le même prix, 0,10 dollar en entrée et 0,50 dollar en sortie. Luna est le plus petit modèle d’OpenAI, lancé avec GPT-6 Sol quelques minutes après Opus 5.5, le 22 septembre. OpenAI avait alors divisé par deux le prix de son petit modèle, puisque GPT-5.6 Luna était facturé 0,20 dollar en entrée et 1,20 dollar en sortie (environ 0,18 et 1,07 euro HT). Anthropic s’aligne donc au centime près sur son concurrent direct, qui misait déjà sur le prix face à Opus 5.5 sur le haut de gamme.
Pour la qualité, Anthropic publie un tableau où Haiku 5.5 devance Luna sur chacun des tests où le modèle d’OpenAI figure. Sur OSWorld 2.1, où l’IA doit utiliser un vrai ordinateur pour finir des tâches en plusieurs étapes, il obtient 72,4 % contre 48,9 % pour Luna et 15,7 % pour Haiku 4.5. Il s’agit d’un score partiel, qui donne aussi des points pour les tâches à moitié terminées. Sur Terminal-Bench 4.0, qui mesure des tâches de code en ligne de commande, il obtient 39,2 % contre 16,4 %. Pour comparer, Haiku 4.5 restait à 0 % sur ce test et Sonnet 5.5 atteint 70,6 %.
Ces chiffres viennent d’Anthropic, qui a choisi ses propres réglages, et aucune mesure indépendante n’est encore disponible. Or les benchmarks d’un constructeur demandent de la prudence. Anthropic reconnaît d’ailleurs que pour du code complexe en mode agent, Sonnet 5.5 et Opus 5.5 restent de meilleurs choix. Sur le papier, Haiku 5.5 tient la route, mais il faudra des tests indépendants pour le confirmer.
À quoi peut servir Haiku 5.5 pour un développeur ?
Anthropic vise d’abord les chatbots qui doivent répondre vite, comme un support client en direct. Asana, qui édite un logiciel de gestion de projets, a mesuré dans ses tests internes un temps de réalisation des tâches réduit de plus de 30 % pour ses agents, par rapport au modèle qu’il utilise aujourd’hui. Attention, ces retours de clients sont choisis et publiés par Anthropic.
Le traitement en masse est l’autre cible. AlphaSense, une plateforme de recherche financière, envoie environ 8 millions de requêtes par semaine à son outil de questions-réponses sur documents. Sur 400 requêtes de test, son score est passé de 0,76 avec Haiku 4.5 à 0,84 avec Haiku 5.5. Box, spécialiste du stockage en ligne pour les entreprises, annonce 11 points de mieux que Haiku 4.5, sans préciser l’échelle utilisée, et un temps de réponse environ deux fois plus court. La baisse de prix pèse le plus sur ce genre de volume.
Pour une application mobile, gardez en tête que Haiku 5.5 tourne sur les serveurs d’Anthropic. Il ne s’installe pas sur le téléphone. L’application l’interroge par Internet via l’API, l’interface qui permet à un programme de dialoguer avec le modèle. La vitesse du modèle se ressent donc directement dans le temps d’attente à l’écran.
Anthropic met aussi à jour, en version bêta, ses kits de développement Python et TypeScript. Ils permettent désormais de faire piloter un navigateur ou un ordinateur par le modèle. D’après Anthropic, Haiku 5.5 est particulièrement adapté à ces deux usages grâce à sa vitesse et son prix.
Haiku 5.5 est disponible dès ce mercredi via l’API sous l’identifiant claude-haiku-5-5, ainsi que chez Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud et Microsoft Azure.
Haiku 4.5, lui, passe dans la liste des anciens modèles sur la grille tarifaire d’Anthropic. Sa fiche technique ne garantit son maintien que jusqu’au 15 octobre 2026, la semaine prochaine, et aucune date de retrait n’est encore fixée. Les développeurs qui l’utilisent ont donc intérêt à préparer la migration, pour laquelle Anthropic publie un guide.
Anthropic divise aussi par deux le prix des lectures en cache de Sonnet 5.5, qui passe de 0,20 à 0,10 dollar (environ 0,09 euro HT) le million de tokens. Comme ces lectures pèsent lourd dans la consommation, Sonnet 5.5 devient environ 20 % moins cher sur la plupart des tâches d’agent.
Enfin, les abonnés Max et Team recevront à partir de cette semaine un crédit API mensuel, utilisable sur tous les modèles. Le montant va de 100 dollars (environ 89 euros) pour Max 5x à 200 dollars (environ 179 euros) pour Max 20x, soit le prix mensuel de chacun de ces deux abonnements. Les comptes Team auront jusqu’à 500 dollars (environ 447 euros), à partager entre leurs membres.
Pour rappel, les abonnements Claude sont jugés environ cinq fois plus généreux que ceux d’OpenAI par le cabinet SemiAnalysis, sur les modèles de milieu de gamme.

articles.title: Georgia Power, Alabama Power Data Breach Hits 400,000 Accounts
articles.text:
Southern Company is notifying roughly 400,000 customers that their utility account information was accessed by an unauthorized third party through its online customer portal.
The Atlanta-based energy holding company serves more than 9 million customers through electric utilities in three states and natural gas distribution businesses in four. Its electric subsidiaries are Georgia Power, Alabama Power and Mississippi Power.
Roughly 300,000 of the affected accounts belong to Georgia Power customers. According to Southern Company, the incident also impacted roughly 100,000 of Alabama Power’s 1.6 million accounts.
Mississippi Power is named as affected in the company’s public notice, but no figure has been released for its customers.
“An unauthorized third party accessed certain, limited information about the accounts of approximately 400K customers. Upon detection, we took immediate steps to stop the activity and have engaged law enforcement,” the company said in a statement sent to the media.
Southern Company’s public notice specifies the type of data involved. “Based on our investigation to date, the limited customer account information that the unauthorized party gained access to includes the customer’s name, mailing address, phone number, email, or the last 4 digits of their Social Security Number, and other basic account details,” the notice reads.
The utility says the attacker did not access bank account numbers, payment card numbers or driver’s license numbers.
Southern Company has not said when the intrusion took place or how the attacker gained access to the portal.
Impacted customers are being notified by mail and email and offered a year of free credit monitoring.

articles.title: Moins cher qu'un iPhone 16 chez Apple : l'iPhone 16 Plus de 6,7 pouces tombe à 849€ chez Amazon
articles.text:
Apple ne vend plus l’iPhone 16 Plus, dernier iPhone au format Plus, mais Amazon le propose à 849 € pendant ses Jours Flash Prime. Écran de 6,7 pouces, deux jours d’autonomie dans notre test, dalle limitée à 60 Hz : voici ce que vaut ce modèle face à la gamme actuelle.
L’iPhone 16 Plus a quitté la boutique en ligne d’Apple, qui ne vend plus aucun iPhone au format Plus. On le trouve encore neuf chez les revendeurs, et Amazon en baisse le prix pour ses Jours Flash Prime, organisés les 6 et 7 octobre.
La version 128 Go de l’iPhone 16 Plus est affichée à 849 € au lieu de 969 €, vendue et expédiée par Amazon, à un tarif réservé aux abonnés Prime. C’est 100 € de moins que son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours. L’offre vise ceux qui veulent un grand écran chez Apple sans passer par un modèle Pro.
Pendant les Jours Flash Prime, Amazon vend l’iPhone 16 Plus 128 Go à 849 € au lieu de 969 €, un tarif réservé aux membres Prime.
Pour profiter du Prime Day, n'oubliez pas de devenir membre Amazon Prime. Vous bénéficiez d'un essai gratuit de 30 jours, c'est donc le bon moment pour tester.
Pourquoi choisir l’iPhone 16 Plus ?
- Un grand écran qui reste léger : Son écran OLED de 6,7 pouces donne un vrai confort pour lire, regarder une série ou jouer. Avec 199 g pour 7,8 mm d’épaisseur, il pèse presque 30 g de moins qu’un iPhone 16 Pro Max.
- Deux jours loin de la prise : Dans notre test, il a tenu deux jours d’affilée sur une seule charge. Apple annonce jusqu’à 27 heures de lecture vidéo, de quoi ne plus recharger chaque soir.
- La puce A18 et Apple Intelligence : La puce A18 encaisse les jeux gourmands et reste très à l’aise au quotidien. Le modèle est compatible avec Apple Intelligence en français, qui manquait encore lors de notre test en 2024.
Un iPhone taillé pour l’écran et l’endurance
La puce A18 a fait gagner deux générations aux iPhone standards, et cela se voit surtout en jeu. Dans notre test de l’iPhone 16 et de l’iPhone 16 Plus, Genshin Impact tournait en qualité élevée à 60 images par seconde, sans écart de performances entre les deux modèles. En photo, le capteur principal de 48 Mpx ouvrant à ƒ/1,6 fait l’essentiel, épaulé par un ultra grand-angle de 12 Mpx qui gère la macro. La vidéo monte en 4K à 60 images par seconde en Dolby Vision.
Ce modèle s’adresse à ceux qui lisent, regardent des vidéos ou jouent beaucoup sur leur téléphone, et à ceux qui veulent tenir deux jours sans recharger. Il convient aussi à qui quitte un iPhone ancien sans viser un Pro. Il est moins pertinent si vous tenez à la fluidité : la dalle reste bloquée à 60 Hz, un écart qui se perçoit en venant d’un écran 120 Hz, même si nous nous y étions réhabitués en un quart d’heure. Les 128 Go demanderont aussi de la rigueur si vous filmez souvent en 4K.
Face à l’iPhone 17 et à l’iPhone Air, un grand format moins cher
À 849 €, l’iPhone 16 Plus coûte 170 € de moins que l’iPhone 16 de 6,1 pouces, vendu 1 019 € par Apple, et 20 € de moins que l’iPhone 17e. L’iPhone 17, à 1 119 €, apporte un écran ProMotion à 120 Hz, la puce A19 et 256 Go d’entrée, sur une diagonale de 6,3 pouces. L’iPhone Air, qui a pris la place des modèles Plus, démarre à 1 329 €. Si vous hésitez avec un modèle Android, notre comparatif des meilleurs smartphones situe ces options face au reste du marché.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran OLED de 6,7 pouces très lumineux, confortable en vidéo comme en jeu
- Autonomie de deux jours relevée dans notre test
- Puce A18 encore très performante, compatible Apple Intelligence

articles.title: Microsoft Outlook to block MSIX attachments starting November
articles.text:
Microsoft announced that it will add .msix and .msixbundle attachments to the list of blocked attachments in Outlook Web and the new Outlook Windows client starting next month.
.msix files are modern Windows installation packages tailored for specific computer architectures or configurations, while .msixbundle is a container that groups multiple .msix packages into a single file compatible with multiple computer architectures.
The change will begin rolling out to Exchange Online users in early November, when the new file types will be added to the BlockedFileTypes list in all OWA Mailbox policies, and is expected to reach general availability by mid-November.
After the policies are updated, .msix or .msixbundle attachments will be blocked by default, and users of Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows will no longer be able to send, receive, open, or download them.
"To enhance security in Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, we are updating the default list of blocked file types in OwaMailboxPolicy," Microsoft said in a Microsoft 365 message center update.
"As part of this update, the .msix and .msixbundle file types will be added to the BlockedFileTypes list in the default OWA Mailbox policy and any custom policies created in your tenant."
Admins don't need to take action if .msix or .msixbundle file types aren't used in their organization, but they can whitelist them by adding them to the AllowedFileTypes property of their users' OwaMailboxPolicy objects if needed.
"Most organizations are not expected to be affected by this update because these file types are infrequently used," Microsoft added. "This update is part of our ongoing efforts to strengthen security and help protect organizations from potentially unsafe file attachments."
This move is part of a broader effort to disable and remove Office and Windows features that attackers have abused in attacks targeting Microsoft customers in recent years.
In June 2025, Outlook began blocking .library-ms and .search-ms file types that have been exploited in phishing and malware attacks since at least June 2022, including attacks targeting government entities.
More recently, in October 2025, Microsoft also announced that Outlook for Web and the new Outlook Windows client would no longer display risky inline SVG images that were also being used in attacks.
The complete list of attachments that can't be saved or viewed from Outlook on the web by Exchange Server and Exchange Online users is available on Microsoft's documentation website.

articles.title: BMW’s iX4 SUV is a 428-mile defensive weapon against China’s EV takeover
articles.text:
While much of the automotive world sits dumbfounded as China gobbles up all its customers, BMW continues to roll out extremely well-crafted, technologically advanced electric vehicles that impress in both drive quality and price. The latest is the BMW iX4, a coupe-shaped SUV that puts a sportier spin on the automaker’s iX3.
BMW’s iX4 SUV is a 428-mile defensive weapon against China’s EV takeover
The iX4 is a sportier spin on the iX3, with the same powerful Gen6 battery providing class-leading range.
The iX4 is the third vehicle to be released on BMW’s next-generation Neue Klasse platform, following the iX3 and i3 models. The iX4 50 xDrive will come first in March 2027, followed by an even more high-performance M60 xDrive version later in the year. The automaker is positioning this new lineup as its bulwark against the flood of Chinese imports that is currently decimating other European brands. But while the iX4 can certainly compete on range and tech, it’s unclear whether BMW can rival China in terms of sheer affordability.
In that respect, the BMW iX4 50 xDrive starts at $66,200 (excluding fees for destination and handling). And it bears all the hallmarks of BMW’s other Neue Klasse models, such as the “Gen6” high-voltage battery with 112.2kWh of usable energy, an 800-volt architecture for lightning-quick charging top-ups, and up to 428 miles of range based on EPA estimates.
That’s more range than the Tesla Model Y, the best-selling electric vehicle in the world. BMW has been blowing away expectations on range to such a degree that even the experts at InsideEVs are left wondering whether it’s overkill. After all, Tesla and others have done plenty well with EVs in the mid-300s, while Lucid continues to struggle despite exceeding 500 miles in range.
But BMW wants to go the distance, believing that range and efficiency are two of its biggest selling points. The third would be performance, and thanks to a dual-motor setup in both the 50 xDrive and M60 xDrive, the iX4 is sure to delivery plenty of giddy up. The 50 xDrive’s motors put out 463 horsepower and 475lb-ft of torque, for a 0–60mph acceleration of 4.7 seconds. Meanwhile, the M60 xDrive’s motors produce 603hp and 645lb-ft of torque, for a 0–60 time a whole second less than the 50 xDrive.
Like other Neue Klasse vehicles, the electrically excited synchronous motor (EESM) in the rear axle serves as the primary drive axle, using electricity instead of permanent magnets to power both its stator outer frame and interior spinning rotor. An inverter acts as the brain of the system, converting direct current from the battery into alternating current for the motor, regulating the electromagnets, and monitoring performance to keep the motor running as efficiently as possible. BMW says this combination helps slash drive-system energy losses by 40 percent and weight by 10 percent.
The Gen6 batteries are built with cylindrical lithium-ion cells measuring 46mm in diameter and 95mm in height that provide a 20 percent increase in energy density compared to the prismatic cells used in BMW’s Gen5 batteries. BMW has eliminated the traditional modules in favor of a “pack-to-open-body” construction where the battery housing serves as the vehicle’s underbody, lowering weight and increasing torsional rigidity.
Like Hyundai and Kia, BMW is building its Neue Klasse EVs to take fast charging to the next level. With its 800V architecture, the iX4 can accept up to 400kWs of DC fast charging, replenishing up to 184 miles of range in 10 minutes, and 10–80 percent charge in just 21 minutes. With a NACS charging port, the iX4 will be compatible with over 80,000 Tesla Supercharger connectors around the world.
The Panoramic iDrive infotainment system is BMW’s redesigned digital dashboard that replaces traditional gauge clusters with a heads-up-style projection along the full width of the lower windshield. The 17.9-inch central touchscreen presents as a free-cut display where you can drag and drop up to six widgets like media, weather, or navigation from the screen directly onto the windshield display.
And like the i3 and iX3, the iX4 can do all sorts of extra stuff, including bidirectional charging with vehicle-to-load and vehicle-to-home capabilities, an intelligent charging flap that opens when a driver approaches a known charging point, and Plug & Charge for automatic charging at 10 different charging providers.
If you look at the whole package, there’s a lot to like. Sure, the Model Y beats the iX4 in a few categories, most importantly price. It’s a bit quicker off the line, and of course, the Model Y comes with the option for Full Self-Driving (Supervised). BMW has something it calls “Symbiotic Drive,” which it describes as a Level 2 system designed for “fluid, intuitive interaction.” In other words, drivers can adjust the steering or even brake without canceling the automated functions. The iX4 also allows for hands-free driving on the highway — but no point-to-point assisted driving. Not until 2027 at the earliest.
Where BMW still bests Tesla is variety. You can get the iX4 50 xDrive, or if you want something sportier, try the M60 xDrive. If you’re rather have a sedan, there’s the i3. Or if you want something a bit more affordable, there’s the iX3. And don’t forget the flagship 7 series. Yep, those are getting Neue Klasse makeovers as well.
Tesla has the Model 3 and Model Y — and that’s about it. (Yes, there’s the Cybertruck, but clearly most people aren’t interested in that. And there’s the Cybercab, but it won’t be on sale anytime soon.) BMW knows its customers want options. And it’s doing it’s best to deliver.

articles.title: M-KOPA acquires Finnish device-locking company for $8 million
articles.text:
M-KOPA, the Kenyan pay-as-you-go startup, has acquired Finnish software company KilpiTek Oy for $8 million, bringing in-house the technology central to its smartphone financing model.
The company acquired 100% of KilpiTek’s voting shares on March 26 in a cash-and-stock transaction, according to M-KOPA’s financial disclosures. M-KOPA paid $2.67 million in cash, with the remaining $5.33 million comprising equity and other consideration, including M-KOPA ordinary shares, deferred consideration, and remuneration.
The acquisition gives M-KOPA direct control of KilpiTek’s device-locking technology, which allows financed smartphones to be remotely restricted or shut down when customers fall behind on repayments.
M-KOPA said the transaction was intended to “bring in-house a critical device-locking capability” and strengthen its control over a key part of its technology platform. It is also expected to support the company’s phone sourcing strategy.
“On 26 March 2026, the Group completed the acquisition of KilpiTek Oy, a Finnish-based software business that provides device-locking and related technology services,” the company said in its financial statement. “The transaction is intended to strengthen the Group’s control over a critical component of its technology stack and support ongoing product and sourcing strategy.”
The deal highlights the strategic importance of device-control software for companies that use pay-as-you-go financing to sell smartphones to consumers who would otherwise struggle to afford them upfront.
M-KOPA’s business model allows customers to acquire smartphones and other products through an initial deposit followed by daily or periodic repayments. The ability to remotely restrict a device is a form of security for loans that banks typically require collateral for.
Owning the technology could give M-KOPA control over how the locking system is integrated with devices sourced from different manufacturers, while reducing its dependence on a third party for a component critical to managing credit risk.
The KilpiTek acquisition also points to M-KOPA’s growing focus on controlling more of the infrastructure underpinning its smartphone financing business as it expands its customer base and works with handset manufacturers.
Finland-based KilpiTek develops software for device locking and related technology services. M-KOPA did not disclose KilpiTek’s revenues, profitability, or number of employees in the financial statements.
The transaction was completed after M-KOPA’s December 31, 2025, reporting date and has been classified as a non-adjusting subsequent event. It did not affect the group’s reported financial position or results for 2025.

articles.title: XUPER TV cómo descargar última actualización: un click que puede hacer vender todos los datos bancarios
articles.text:
Una supuesta actualización de XUPER TV puede convertirse en una puerta de entrada para programas maliciosos capaces de comprometer información personal y financiera. Las plataformas de televisión no oficiales, que ofrecen acceso gratuito a canales, películas o eventos deportivos, suelen requerir la instalación de archivos fuera de las tiendas oficiales, una práctica que aumenta la exposición a aplicaciones modificadas y software malicioso.
El riesgo aparece especialmente cuando el usuario recibe una advertencia para instalar una “última actualización” y acepta sin comprobar el origen del archivo. Lo que parece un procedimiento necesario para continuar viendo contenido puede terminar concediendo permisos que permiten acceder a información almacenada en el dispositivo.
El peligro detrás de una falsa actualización
XUPER TV, conocida anteriormente en algunos mercados informales como Magis TV, opera fuera de los controles habituales de plataformas como Google Play Store o App Store. Por ello, quienes buscan instalarla o actualizarla pueden encontrarse con archivos APK disponibles en páginas web, enlaces compartidos en redes sociales o sitios que imitan servicios legítimos.
Los ciberdelincuentes pueden aprovechar esta situación para distribuir versiones modificadas de las aplicaciones. El archivo puede mantener una apariencia similar a la original, pero incorporar troyanos, programas espía u otro tipo de malware.
Uno de los principales métodos consiste en mostrar mensajes que presionan al usuario para realizar una actualización inmediata. Al descargar el archivo e instalarlo, el usuario puede estar introduciendo un programa malicioso en su teléfono, TV Box u otro dispositivo conectado.
Los permisos pueden abrir la puerta a la información bancaria
El problema se vuelve más grave cuando la aplicación solicita permisos especiales. Entre ellos pueden encontrarse el acceso a los servicios de accesibilidad, las notificaciones o el almacenamiento del dispositivo.
Con determinados permisos, un malware puede intentar observar la actividad que se realiza en el equipo y recopilar información sensible. En un teléfono utilizado para operaciones financieras, esto puede incluir credenciales de acceso, datos introducidos en aplicaciones y códigos enviados mediante mensajes de texto.
Una de las técnicas utilizadas por este tipo de amenazas consiste en superponer pantallas falsas sobre aplicaciones legítimas. De esta manera, el usuario puede creer que está frente a su aplicación bancaria cuando, en realidad, está introduciendo sus datos en una interfaz controlada por los atacantes.
También existe el riesgo de que los delincuentes intenten interceptar códigos de autenticación enviados por SMS. Si consiguen acceder a esas comunicaciones, podrían tratar de utilizarlas junto con otras credenciales robadas para realizar operaciones no autorizadas.
El riesgo también alcanza a televisores y redes domésticas
El peligro no necesariamente termina en el teléfono. Una aplicación maliciosa instalada en un TV Box o dispositivo conectado a una Smart TV puede convertirse en otro punto vulnerable dentro de la red doméstica.
Una vez dentro de la misma conexión WiFi, un equipo comprometido puede ser utilizado para intentar identificar otros dispositivos conectados. Esto aumenta la superficie de ataque y puede poner en riesgo ordenadores, teléfonos y otros aparatos que compartan la red.
Por esa razón, una supuesta actualización que aparece fuera de una tienda oficial debe considerarse una señal de alerta, especialmente si exige permisos que no guardan relación con la función que debería cumplir la aplicación.
Qué hacer si se instaló una versión sospechosa
La principal recomendación es evitar la instalación de APK procedentes de sitios desconocidos y no aceptar actualizaciones que lleguen mediante ventanas emergentes, enlaces o mensajes cuya procedencia no pueda verificarse.
Si ya se instaló una versión sospechosa, conviene desconectar inmediatamente el dispositivo de internet y evitar utilizarlo para acceder a servicios financieros. Las contraseñas deben cambiarse desde otro equipo que sea confiable y, ante cualquier operación extraña, es importante contactar cuanto antes con el banco para bloquear tarjetas o cuentas comprometidas.
También puede ser necesario restablecer el dispositivo a los valores de fábrica para eliminar el software malicioso. Antes de hacerlo, debe conservarse únicamente la información imprescindible y evitar restaurar aplicaciones o archivos provenientes de fuentes desconocidas.
El atractivo de acceder gratuitamente a contenido televisivo no debería llevar a ignorar las advertencias de seguridad. Una actualización aparentemente rutinaria puede convertirse en el punto de entrada para una amenaza que comprometa mucho más que la posibilidad de ver televisión.

articles.title: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5 on AWS | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5 on AWS
Today, we’re excited to announce the availability of Claude Haiku 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. According to Anthropic, Claude Haiku 5.5 is the fastest and most efficient model in the Claude 5.5 family, built for subagents and high-volume, cost-sensitive work. It also costs around 75 percent less than Claude Haiku 4.5 for most tasks.
Amazon Bedrock gives you Haiku 5.5 capabilities while keeping your data within AWS infrastructure with Regional data residency. It works with the AWS controls your team already uses, including AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) for access, AWS CloudTrail for audit, Amazon CloudWatch for monitoring, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. Usage appears on your AWS bill.
Claude Platform on AWS gives you direct access to Anthropic’s native platform experience and capabilities through the AWS Management Console. Build, test, and deploy with the same APIs, features, and console experience you’d get working with Anthropic directly, unified with AWS billing and authentication.
This post covers Claude Haiku 5.5’s improvements, practical guidance on when to choose Haiku 5.5, and how to get started on Amazon Bedrock.
What makes Claude Haiku 5.5 different
Claude Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic’s most capable Haiku model, across coding, tool use, computer use, and agentic tasks. It’s also the first Haiku model with effort controls, so you can tune cost against intelligence for each task instead of picking one setting for an entire workload.
The improvements stand out on quick and repeatable work at scale. For coding tasks, it acts as a subagent routing requests, reviewing code and classifying long documents. For knowledge work, Haiku 5.5 pulls key information from small-to-medium documents, does initial scans, and answers quick questions over a knowledge base. For interactive applications, it responds fast enough for simple conversations to have quick and helpful answers. It also handles traditional natural language processing (NLP) tasks such as classification, summarization, and text generation at the volume and cost that production features require.
Haiku 5.5 handles agentic coding and multi-step tool use, and supports high-resolution images. Haiku 5.5 can be used as a strong computer use subagent for repetitive browser and desktop tasks, at a cost that holds up at scale. In development workflows, it’s a good fit for iterating quickly on UI and UX changes and for small, specific code base changes across multiple files.
Pairing Claude Haiku 5.5 with Opus 5.5
Haiku 5.5 pairs with the recently announced Claude Opus 5.5. Together, they make a strong team: Opus 5.5 plans and makes the judgment calls, and Haiku 5.5 carries out well-defined tasks quickly and at scale. You get careful reasoning where it counts and lower cost and latency everywhere.
- Claude Opus 5.5 plans the work and makes the judgment calls. It breaks down complex problems, decides the approach, and takes on the hardest reasoning, such as release debugging, security review of large pull requests, and long analyses that end in a finished report.
- Claude Haiku 5.5 takes on the fast layer of subagents. It handles quick, high-volume tasks, such as routing requests, classifying and summarizing, rewriting long documents, and applying small, specific changes across many files. As a review subagent, it can quickly check the order of operations and high-level direction, so Opus 5.5 can spend its tokens on the hardest reasoning. Because it is fast and cost efficient, you can run many Haiku subagents in parallel.
Getting started with Claude Haiku 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock
To try Haiku 5.5, open the Amazon Bedrock console, choose Test, then Playground, and select Haiku 5.5 as the model. From there, you can run a prompt directly against it.
Programmatically, you can call the model with the Anthropic Messages API against bedrock-runtime through the Anthropic SDK. You can also use the Invoke and Converse APIs on bedrock-runtime through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDK.
Prerequisites
You must have the following prerequisites:
- Active AWS account with Amazon Bedrock access.
- AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) installed and configured.
- Python 3.10+.
- Boto3 installed: pip install boto3.
- Anthropic SDK installed: pip install anthropic.
- The Amazon Bedrock Token Generator for Amazon Bedrock authentication installed: pip install aws_bedrock_token_generator.
- AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions: bedrock:InvokeModel, bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream.
Here’s a quick example using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) with the InvokeModel API:
You can also use the Amazon Bedrock Converse API for a unified multi-model experience:
You can also use the Anthropic Messages API through the anthropic SDK package for a streamlined experience:
You can explore the Getting Started notebook for more examples. You can monitor usage, performance, and costs through Amazon CloudWatch and AWS Cost Explorer to scale your applications as demand grows.
Availability
Claude Haiku 5.5 is available today on Amazon Bedrock through the US Geo CRIS (us.), EU Geo CRIS (eu.), AU Geo CRIS (au.), JP Geo CRIS (jp.) and Global CRIS (global.) inference profiles on bedrock-runtime. In AWS GovCloud (US), it’s available on both the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints.
See the Amazon Bedrock documentation for the full list of supported AWS Regions. For pricing information, see Amazon Bedrock pricing. It’s also available through Claude Platform on AWS in North America

articles.title: Lo nuevo de Google te permite crear juegos con IA sin saber programar
articles.text:
Crear un videojuego nunca ha sido una tarea sencilla. Aunque existen herramientas que facilitan el trabajo, los interesados necesitan saber de programación, diseño, arte, sonido y otros elementos que conforman el flujo de desarrollo. Google ha querido simplificar todo el proceso con Playground, una herramienta a la que le cuentas tu idea y la IA se encarga de generar el juego.
De acuerdo con una publicación en su blog, Playground es una plataforma experimental donde puedes crear, jugar y compartir juegos. Los usuarios pueden desarrollar un juego con solo describir lo que quieren en unos cuantos mensajes. La interfaz ofrece partir de un lienzo en blanco, adaptar indicaciones de ejemplo o apoyarte en una guía que te ayuda a dar forma a la idea y probar los resultados casi al instante.
En caso de que necesites modificar la física o reescribir las reglas del juego, podrás hacerlo sobre la marcha. Playground también permite modificar el diseño de los personajes y escenarios, incluso rehacerlos a través de un prompt. Google señala que el control creativo, desde el boceto hasta la versión final, siempre estará en manos del usuario.
Debido a que Playground funciona en el navegador, los juegos se pueden abrir en cualquier dispositivo, incluyendo tu móvil. Una vez que realizas las pruebas para ver que todo funcione como esperas, la herramienta te ofrece mantenerlo en privado y compartir un enlace a tus amigos o conocidos para que lo jueguen o encuentren algún error que hayas pasado por alto. Al final, solo basta con publicarlo y aparecerá en la galería Explorar, junto con el resto de títulos creados por otros usuarios.
Según Google, los juegos de Playground son compatibles con multijugador y puedes usar tu perfil de Play Games para valorar otros juegos y seguir a sus creadores.
Google Playground te permitirá crear juegos con IA
En caso de que quieras llevar el proyecto más lejos, Playground ofrecerá una integración con Unity Spark, la herramienta creada por Unity y Google para desarrollar juegos con ayuda de la IA. Esta utiliza el motor de Unity para mecánicas avanzadas y gráficos en 3D para los personajes y escenarios. El objetivo de Google es que empieces con un simple prompt y termines construyendo experiencias inmersivas más complejas sin necesidad de aprender a programar.
A juzgar por el tráiler, Playground ofrece juegos en 2D y 3D con mecánicas básicas, como plataformas, defensa de torres, disparos y más. Los ejemplos nos recuerdan a esos títulos que jugábamos en el iPhone o Android hace 15 años.
Playground se encuentra en una fase temprana de desarrollo, por lo que solo estará disponible para los usuarios de Estados Unidos. Google confirmó que seguirán evolucionando la herramienta con ayuda de la comunidad. La tecnológica dijo que el acceso será escalonado, según la suscripción a Google AI que tengas, lo que nos hace preguntarnos si existirá una opción gratuita.
A diferencia de otras herramientas de desarrollo, crear juegos con IA requerirá mayor poder de cómputo. Es probable que Google limite el número de creaciones disponibles a los usuarios sin suscripción de pago. En el caso de Unity Spark, el acceso también se encuentra en fase de pruebas y la beta cerrada se lanzará muy pronto.

articles.title: Greenairy is building smart plant towers to clean the air in your office | TechCrunch
articles.text:
How clean is the air in your workplace? That’s the question Tanvi Thombre and Lakshya Saraf began investigating when they were engineering students who worked in their university makerspace.
In fact, Thombre said via email that, while working in the space, they were “unknowingly exposed to toxic fumes from laser cutters, 3D printers, and soldering irons,” but they didn’t realize it until Thombre’s best friend fainted and had to go to the hospital.
After that, Thombre said, “We began investigating indoor air pollution and realized it was an invisible but dangerous health risk — especially in schools, offices, hotels, salons, and any commercial buildings where air-conditioning prevents windows from being opened.”
Those issues persist even when a building is equipped with air purifiers, as their makerspace was. The problem, according to Saraf, is that although purifiers are good at cleaning out particulate matter like dust and pollen, they are less effective at removing toxic gases such as carbon dioxide, formaldehyde, and benzine (many of which are classified as volatile organic compounds, or VOCs — chemicals that evaporate easily into the air).
Thombre said that VOCs are linked to chronic disease and “sick building syndrome,” a condition in which occupants experience health effects and discomfort after spending time in a building, even though no specific cause or illness has been identified. She also pointed to Harvard research showing that improving indoor air quality improved cognitive function and productivity as well.
That’s why the pair is targeting toxic gases in the workplace with their startup Greenairy, which will be part of Startup Battlefield 200 at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt.
Greenairy’s approach centers on building plant towers that are supposed to draw in air, break down toxic gases, and then release the purified air. As Saraf put it, “A plant in a pot cleans air slowly. But, when we change the conditions around the plant, it cleans air much faster and better than these conventional methods.”
Saraf also said that while some air purifier filters can remove “a narrow range of VOCs,” those filters need to be changed frequently to be effective. In contrast, plants are “a natural solution, no harmful by-products are formed, and no filter replacement is required.”
Greenairy has already conducted short-term pilots at locations around Singapore. Saraf said that in the startup’s own testing using RESET-certified air monitors, it compared three offices: one with Greenairy plant towers, one that had a medical-grade ionizer (a device that uses an electrical charge to make dust and other particles clump together and fall out of the air), and a third with a HEPA air purifier that traps very small particles.
“Our tower had the lowest VOC levels and removed VOCs the fastest,” she said. “The office staff also grew fond of the natural ‘fresh’ aroma of the tower and the natural vibe it brought.”
Thombre added that they saw an “immediate” improvement within regular office hours, with a 50% reduction in both the daily VOC average and peak levels. She said the results improved even more “as the plants and microbes mature and the gases are prevented from accumulating.”
Greenairy has also had its results validated by the German testing and certification firm TÜV SÜD and will be publishing them soon. (Results are available upon request in the meantime.) The pair plans to begin large-scale manufacturing after the results are certified.
The startup’s founders are currently based on opposite sides of the world, with Saraf in Berkeley, California, and Thombre in Singapore. It’s an arrangement that Saraf said “works well at this stage,” allowing one founder to focus on testing in Singapore while the other can fundraise in the Bay Area.
“If things go to plan, both of us will be in Singapore by the first half of 2027,” she added. “That’s when we expect to launch our first mass-produced towers and install them for our first customers” in Singapore.

articles.title: AI/ML is becoming a performance factor in motorsport
articles.text:
There’s been something of a change in the world of motorsport over the past few years. It has to do with where the money comes from. In the old days, it was tobacco and, to a lesser extent, booze. Today such things are mostly banned, and when you look at a racecar covered in sponsor logos, you’re likely to see something crypto-, cyber-, or AI-related.
This makes sense—an ever-larger share of our GDP is wrapped up in those segments. They’re the ones with all the money, and it takes money to go racing. So at the amateur level, we’ve seen tech CEOs replace dentists as the privateer of choice: This past weekend’s Petit Le Mans included co-founders of GitHub, CrowdStrike, Shopify, and the creator of Ruby on Rails, to name a few.
But this is an instance where a sponsor can provide tangible benefits to their motorsports partner beyond a bank transfer, as Chip Ganassi Racing (CGR) and OpenAI have been showing in IndyCar this year.
Ganassi’s might not be the most well-resourced team on the grid, but it is the most dominant; its drivers have won the championship 13 times in the past two decades. First that was Dario Franchitti, then Scott Dixon. But today the man bringing home the big trophies is Álex Palou, who this year sealed his fifth title in six seasons. And at some races, it’s his car that has worn OpenAI’s colors.
The 2026 season was a harder one for Palou than some, winning a mere third of the 18 races IndyCar held. But that was still twice as many as anyone else. Eight poles were far better than anyone else could achieve, either. And it turns out that OpenAI and one of its researchers have been working with CGR and Palou on optimizing car setups. That collaboration is the subject of a documentary series on YouTube, and the second episode just went live this morning. (The longer Part One is here.)

articles.title: VPN threat protection vs. dedicated antivirus: Are VPNs really enough?
articles.text:
VPN threat protection vs. dedicated antivirus: Are VPNs really enough?
Chances are that your VPN does more than just encrypt your traffic. An increasing number of providers now bundle malware detection, malicious link checkers, and ad blockers into their packages.
This recent trend raises an interesting question: Are a VPN’s built-in security tools enough to replace standalone antivirus products? Or do we still need dedicated antivirus protection layered underneath our VPN?
VPN security tools
Modern VPNs have evolved far beyond simple tunneling tools. The best VPNs like NordVPN and Surfshark now include real-time malware protection that checks URLs against malicious databases and scans files during downloads.
In 2024, NordVPN became the first VPN to earn certification as a reliable anti-phishing tool. Its Threat Protection feature blocks websites, web trackers, and ads while scanning downloads on the spot.
Surfshark takes this further with Surfshark One. It offers real-time protection from viruses and malware, with scheduled scans as part of regular security maintenance.
That said, VPN-based solutions often skip features common in standalone antivirus such as full system scans and behavioral threat analysis.
Here’s where it gets interesting: some VPNs’ antivirus tools are essentially rebadged versions of the same underlying technology. Surfshark’s antivirus is directly powered by Avira’s anti-malware SDK, while CyberGhost Security Suite uses Intego’s frontend – which, for Windows, relies on Avira’s engine and definitions.
This shared infrastructure means they depend on the same detection databases. When Avira pushes an update, VPN partners may take time to integrate it, creating potential gaps in protection compared to native Avira users.
Beyond timing delays, platform support can be inconsistent. Some VPN antivirus features only work on Windows and Android, leaving macOS and iOS users with partial coverage. For threat actors targeting Apple devices specifically, this gap becomes exploitable.
OS-level protection
Having evolved significantly since the days of basic protection, built-in security deserves more credit. Microsoft Defender, once considered a bare-minimum option by many, has improved considerably.
In AV-Comparatives’ July-August 2026 real-world protection test, Defender blocked 95.5% of live threats with just one false positive recorded.
What stands out is its consistency. Across multiple testing rounds, Defender has consistently earned Advanced+ awards and solid protection scores that often rival paid solutions, including Bitdefender and Sophos.
Critically, it recorded fewer false positives than many commercial competitors – meaning fewer instances of legitimate files being incorrectly flagged as threats.
Apple’s approach is equally sophisticated, deploying a trio of defenses rather than traditional signature-based scanning. Gatekeeper verifies authenticity, Notarization scans for known malware before distribution, and XProtect handles background detection with automatic updates. XProtect Remediator, added in recent macOS versions, periodically scans for active infections that slip through.
Between these systems, Apple prevents a substantial share of opportunistic attacks, though zero-day threats remain a vulnerability.
The free options and when to pay
If you prefer not to pay for antivirus software, Avast Free Antivirus remains a solid baseline. In recent testing from AV-Comparatives, it was one of only three products out of 20 tested to achieve a 100% block rate.
Free tiers typically come with trade-offs such as limited cross-platform coverage and reduced toolsets. For casual browsing, these rarely matter, but for managing sensitive files across multiple devices, they start to add up.
However, the value proposition shifts with paid suites. Norton 360 Deluxe and Bitdefender Total Security offer numerous valuable extras beyond antivirus protection that justify their cost for many users.
Features include password managers, cloud backup, parental controls, and identity monitoring. Having all these utilities in one package means less to juggle, and often works out cheaper than buying each tool separately.
The Verdict
Rather than choosing between them, a combination works best. A VPN, free antivirus, and built-in OS-level security creates a solid protection foundation. Relying on any single layer leaves gaps.
A VPN alone won’t catch malware already on your device or protect offline activity. Free antivirus lacks the behavioral analysis and premium support of paid suites. OS-level security can’t stop every zero-day exploit or advanced persistent threat.
That said, for the average user practicing sensible browsing habits, this layered approach provides adequate protection for everyday use. If you manage sensitive data, handle financial transactions regularly, or use older hardware that might delay security updates, investing in a premium suite adds meaningful insurance.
Practically speaking, most users can stay secure without overspending. The key is to stay sharp by keeping software updated and avoiding clicking on unexpected pop-ups or unsolicited links without thinking twice.

He graduated with a degree in English and Journalism from the University of Lincoln and spent several years teaching English as a foreign language in Spain. articles.title: Xreal Aura release date is 'just weeks away,' and coming to Canada
articles.text:
Xreal has revealed more details about the Aura tethered smart glasses. The official release hasn’t been scheduled yet, but we’re now “just weeks away,” according to Xreal.
The smart glasses will launch in the U.S., Canada, Japan and South Korea to start and cost $1,829 for the 12GB+256GB variant and $2,149 for the 16GB+512GB variant. Xreal says that only those who reserved the Aura before October 7 will be eligible to pre-order and complete their purchases on release.
Aura uses split-compute architecture with comfortable optical see-through glasses with a tethered compute puck. It can download any Google Play apps and runs Android XR. It also has Sound by Bose, hand tracking, and a 70-degree field of view. The battery puck can also be used for trackpad navigation and can be carried by a lanyard or a pocket clip.
At Qualcomm Summit 2026, I got the opportunity to go hands-on with Xreal Aura for the second time. This time, I got to spend even more time with the smart glasses.
Again, I really like this Xreal Aura experience. At one point, I was looking at GarageBand on a MacBook, and I was able to ask the Aura questions about what was on the screen and how to get started on the Apple app. It was doing this just by using the Xreal Aura’s cameras and Gemini.
I also got to try out this very cool brain mapping app that’s not aimed at consumer use, but more for health professionals. This app let me split open the human head, look into the brain, blow up the brain huge and with object permanence, you’re able to walk around the brain and see it from different angles. I loved this; it felt so surreal, like out of an episode of Grey’s Anatomy. If I knew anything about medicine or biology, this would probably be even more interesting, and I can see how this could be very useful for learning, especially if you’re looking at a tumour in the brain and trying to figure out a good angle to dissect it. It’s worth noting that running this app made the puck crazy hot, but that makes sense given how much computing it takes.
I was also able to explore the Brooklyn Bridge using immersive view, and it felt like I was right there on the bridge. I was able to look and move around the area, which was quite cool. This wasn’t the first time I’ve used the Xreal Aura or Android XR platform, so the gestures and using the platform were incredibly easy, and I’ve always called it intuitive. Sticking out your palm and pinching opens a familiar Android-like menu. You can pinch to select apps. You can expand a window by pinching on the sides and pulling apart. I thought it was pretty intuitive and made sense.
I’m looking forward to Xreal Aura’s release date. Though they aren’t completely wireless, I like that they’re lightweight and that the puck can attach to a belt clip. Xreal Aura isn’t the answer to standalone smart glasses, but it’s a step in the right direction.

articles.title: Aaron Sorkin's new film The Social Reckoning exposes the inner workings of Facebook - Tech Guide
articles.text:
There’s a saying that you should never see how the sausage is made. In the new film The Social Reckoning it shows the tech version of this saying and exposes the inner machinations of social media giant Facebook in its efforts to keep people engaged on its platform.
Artfully written and directed by Aaron Sorkin, The Social Reckoning tells the true story of Facebook whistleblower Francis Haugan and Wall Street Journal investigative reporter Jeff Horwitz.
The resulting series of stories and investigations became known as The Facebook Files.
Sorkin has already plumbed the social media landscape with his earlier film The Social Network which focused on the formation of Facebook from a Harvard dorm room and its subsequent legal challenges.
This time it’s all about what went down between 2020 and 2021 as the world faced the COVID pandemic and while Facebook was frantically trying to supercharge its algorithm to improve engagement to avoid a substantial loss of revenue.
The subject is topical given the Australian social media ban and talk of creating more restrictions around the algorithm to avoid adverse effects for users.
In the film, it alarmingly exposes Facebook’s approach, which was to create more engagement which ends up stoking the flames of hate speech and anger and all with the goal of keeping people on the platform even longer.
Francis Haugan, played by Academy Award-winning actress Mikey Madison, is a data scientist employed at Facebook in the Civic Integrity Team who responds to a message from Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz, play capably by Jeremy Allen White of “The Bear” fame, who is digging for information around how Facebook is allegedly manipulating data and comments.
Haugen has her own concerns about the data she has found but she is unable to express them to her superiors and is basically told to keep her head down and toe the line.
She has skin in the game after seeing a video shared by former level-headed colleague who has been radicalised by platform’s extreme algorithm. This episode is dramatized in the opening scene of the film.
Jeremy Strong plays Mark Zuckerberg with remarkable accuracy both in terms of his look and mannerisms.
His portrayal shows Zuckerberg as someone who wants to be efficient and get straight to the point on any discussion or presentation while advocating for freedom of speech on the platform.
His foil in The Social Reckoning is played by Bill Burr – a former investor named Charlie who is in Zuckerberg’s ear during a practise session ahead of a Senate hearing about his and the platform’s responsibilities and ethics.
“You’re like a crossing guard standing out front of a school and you’re not doing anything with your arms so the cars are just ploughing down the children – because it’s a democracy,” Charlie tells Zuckerberg.
Charlie’s other gripe is that Facebook doesn’t fact-check political ads.
All this comes together in an absorbing Aaron Sorkin screenplay, which features his trademark razor-sharp rat-a-tat-tat dialogue.
Sorkin has turned a story about leaked documents and statistics into an entertaining and human story.
The story’s timeline also happens to coincide with the January 6 2021 attack at the US Capitol which resulted in the removal of a video posted by Donald Trump.
The Social Reckoning is a compelling portrayal of the power and influence of social media and the modern challenges society is facing.
It lays bare Facebook’s shortcomings, blinkered views and lack of action over misinformation and false advertising.
Meanwhile Facebook and Instagram (now part of the same Meta company) will keep honing its algorithm to keep us engaged on the platforms for as long as possible and harvest our data at the same time.
The Social Reckoning opens in theatres today.

articles.title: SynthID Detector : Google lance un outil pour repérer les contenus générés par IA - Numerama
articles.text:
En mai 2026, Google avait annoncé son intention de faire de SynthID, son filigrane invisible dans les contenus générés par IA, un standard. Gemini, la recherche Google et Chrome peuvent déjà dire si une image contient le filigrane SynthID, avec pour objectif final d’avoir un filigrane unique pour tous les services.
Le 7 octobre 2026, Google annonce le lancement d’un site dédié à la reconnaissance d’images IA : SynthID Detector, accessible à l’adresse synthid.com. Présenté l’an dernier, l’outil était jusqu’ici réservé aux professionnels et aux médias.
Comment fonctionne SynthID Detector ?
SynthID permet d’importer une image, une vidéo ou un fichier audio. L’outil cherche ensuite la présence d’un filigrane SynthID, une signature invisible insérée dans le contenu au moment de sa génération. Selon Google, le filigrane résiste aux recadrages, aux changements de couleur et aux compressions : il est impossible de le supprimer.
En plus des images générées par Nano Banana, SynthID reconnaît les créations OpenAI (dont ChatGPT Images 2.0), NVIDIA et Kakao. Google ajoute qu’Apple rejoindra « bientôt » la liste, sans donner de date. Les rivaux de Google sont plusieurs à avoir accepté la proposition de l’entreprise pour que SynthID devienne la norme.
Un outil utile, mais pas un détecteur universel
Depuis 2023, Google dit que plus de 180 milliards d’images et de vidéos ont été marquées avec un SynthID. Le problème est que SynthID Detector ne peut pas « reconnaître » un contenu IA, mais seulement détecter le filigrane. Par ailleurs, d’autres plateformes comme Midjourney, Meta ou xAI ne figurent pas parmi les partenaires, et d’autres outils plus méconnus peuvent aussi s’en passer. Une personne qui veut tricher pourra donc continuer de tricher. Mais les outils les plus populaires, eux, laisseront une trace.

articles.title: Chemie-Nobelpreis für Forschung zur Chiralität: Warum Moleküle eine „Lieblingsseite“ haben
articles.text:
Chemie-Nobelpreis 2026: Von der Händigkeit der Moleküle
Es gehe um „Chiralität“, um sogenannte Spiegelmoleküle: So wurde der diesjährige Nobelpreis für Chemie vor der Namensbekanntgabe durch die Königlich-Schwedische Akademie der Wissenschaften in Stockholm angeteasert. Ausgezeichnet wurden kurz darauf der Franzose Henri Kagan von der Université Paris-Sud und der Japaner Kenso Soai von der Tokyo University of Science. Die Forschung der beiden Nobelpreisträger habe das Verständnis der Spiegelmoleküle revolutioniert und zur Produktion bestimmter Arzneimittel, Aromen, Duftstoffe und neuer Materialien beigetragen, hieß es.
Der Forschungsgegenstand der Ausgezeichneten übt von jeher Faszination aus. Denn es ist nur ein winziges Detail, das darüber entscheidet, ob zum Beispiel die chemische Substanz Calvon nach Kümmel oder grüner Minze duftet, und ein Stoff namens Limonen nach Zitrone oder Orange. Die Moleküle sind zwar jeweils aus den gleichen Zutaten aufgebaut, aber spiegelbildlich – im Grunde wie unsere rechte und linke Hand.
Fachleute aus der Chemie nennen das Phänomen deshalb nach dem griechischen Wort für Händigkeit „Chiralität“. Die spiegelbildlichen Formen heißen Enantiomere. Auch die sogenannte rechtsdrehende Milchsäure, mit der manche Joghurthersteller für eine besondere Verdauungsverträglichkeit ihrer Produkte werben, ist so ein Enantiomer.
Spiegelmoleküle: kleiner Unterschied, große Wirkung
In der Natur kommen Moleküle meistens in nur einer ihrer Spiegelbildformen vor. Zum Beispiel findet man fast ausschließlich sogenannte linkshändige Aminosäuren und rechtshändige Zuckermoleküle. Die Chemie-Nobelpreisträger konnten helfen, das Phänomen zu erklären. „Henri Kagan und Kenso Soai haben eine Lösung für ein über ein Jahrhundert altes chemisches Rätsel geliefert: Wie kann Homochiralität spontan entstehen?“, sagte Heiner Linke, der Vorsitzende des Nobelkomitees für Chemie, bei der Preisverleihung.
Henri Kagan fand eine Methode, mit der chemische Reaktionen so gesteuert werden können, dass das gewünschte Spiegelbildmolekül in größeren Anteilen entsteht. Ein Katalysator sorgt dabei für die anvisierte räumliche Anordnung der Ausgangsmoleküle bei deren Reaktion. Kenso Soai wiederum konnte erstmals eine chemische Reaktion im Labor nachstellen, bei der lediglich eines der möglichen Spiegelbilder gebildet wurde. Auch in diesem Prozess spielt eine smarte Katalyse die Hauptrolle.
Eine zielgenaue Steuerung des Prozesses ist auch in der Chemie- oder Pharmaindustrie wichtig. Denn eine Verunreinigung mit der unerwünschten Molekülvariante könnte fatale Folgen haben. Das Antibiotikum Ethambutol zum Beispiel hat in der linkshändigen Form eine hohe Schlagkraft gegen Tuberkulosebakterien. Das spiegelbildliche Molekül hingegen ist giftig und kann blind machen.
Zweiter Nobelpreis zu Spiegelmolekülen
Das Thema Chiralität konnte erst vor ein paar Jahren schon einmal beim Nobelkomitee punkten. Im Jahr 2021 ging er an den Deutschen Benjamin List und den Amerikaner David MacMillan für die Entwicklung der asymmetrischen Organokatalyse. Die Forscher hatten potente Werkzeuge für den gezielten Aufbau von Spiegelmolekülen entwickelt, um etwa neue Arzneimittel oder nachhaltige Werkstoffe herzustellen.

articles.title: Google dévoile Nano Banana 2.1, son nouveau générateur d’images le plus performant
articles.text:
En février dernier, Google a dévoilé Nano Banana 2. La firme de Mountain View est aujourd’hui de retour avec une mise à jour de son générateur d’images : Nano Banana 2.1, basé sur Gemini 3.6 Flash. L’entreprise l’assure : Nano Banana 2.1 « surpasse nos modèles précédents à tous égards ». Étant donné que nous disposons de peu d’informations à son sujet, il faudra l’utiliser pour vérifier si c’est effectivement le cas.
Google promet de meilleures performances, mais sans donner de détails
Il faut dire que Google a partagé peu d’informations concernant son générateur d’images mis à jour. L’entreprise américaine promet un meilleur design visuel, une cohérence des sujets, des images d’apparence plus naturelle et une édition basée sur des masques (ce qui permet de retoucher une zone spécifique de l’image tout en préservant le reste de la scène). La fiche technique de Nano Banana 2.1 nous apprend par ailleurs que le modèle peut générer des images en 1K, 2K ou 4K, accepter jusqu’à 14 images de référence dans une même requête et partir d’une simple vidéo.
Mais ce sont à peu près les seules informations dont nous disposons. Google n’a effectué ni comparaisons ni fourni de benchmarks. Seules quatre images générées par le modèle ont été présentées. Il faudra donc utiliser Nano Banana 2.1 pour juger ses performances, et voir surtout si elles sont meilleures que celles de ChatGPT Images 2.5, le générateur d’images d’OpenAI déployé en septembre dernier.
Comment accéder à Nano Banana 2.1 ?
Il reste également à connaître avec précision la disponibilité de Nano Banana 2.1. Ce dernier est bel et bien intégré à Google AI Studio. Mais quid de l’application Gemini ? Google précise qu’il y sera également disponible. À l’heure actuelle, dans le générateur d’images intégré à Gemini, il est possible de choisir le modèle 3.6 Flash, mais rien ne nous assure que Nano Banana 2.1 soit bien le modèle utilisé derrière.
Nano Banana 2.1 vient d’être présenté et il est encore en cours de déploiement. Il faudra donc peut-être se montrer un peu patient.

articles.title: PoeLLM malware infects exposed AI servers in cryptomining attacks
articles.text:
A cryptomining campaign targeting exposed AI services is using PoeLLM malware to turn compromised servers into scanners and exploit launchpads.
The malware features an uncommon method to retrieve command-and-control (C2) addresses by extracting keywords in a poem hosted on GitHub.
Researchers at Lumen's Black Lotus Labs (BLL) tracking the botnet malware say it has compromised more than 3,400 servers, with peak activity reaching as many as 800 infected systems active on a single day.
PoeLLM has been active since at least April, but its activity has increased significantly since then, with at least 11 C2 servers spun up to date.
According to the research, the operation targeted systems across the United States and Western Europe.
Many of those victims run exposed AI tools such as LiteLLM and Ollama, the Gotenberg PDF converter, and the Gitea development toolkit, while signs of Ivanti Sentry targeting were also uncovered.
BLL notes that AI/LLM implementations are attractive targets for threat actors because they are often poorly configured, exposed online, and typically run on powerful GPU clusters that are suitable for cryptomining.
Poetry and malware
In a report today, BLL researchers say that PoeLLM, an ELF file named libgcrypt, retrieves four words or phrases from a poem titled “On the Nature of Connection” in a ‘dash.css’ file hosted in a GitHub repository that appears to fork Node.js.
It then maps these words to numbers using a hard-coded dictionary, generating a IPv4 address corresponding to the C2.
To change the C2 address, the operator changes the poem. Until now, they have modified the poem 11 times, but researchers suspect that there may be at least another update.
The malware incorporates remote-shell functionality, XMRig and Iron cryptocurrency miners, HTTP/S scanning, and exploit deployment capabilities.
BLL researchers found that victims communicate with a Russian crypto-mining service called Kryptex.
Once a server is compromised, it becomes a springboard to spread the malware further, using scanning on ports 3000 and 4000, associated with Gotenberg and LiteLLM, and attempting to exploit CVE-2026-42271.
The CVE-2026-42271 vulnerability impacts LiteLLM’s MCP server test endpoints. It was originally disclosed as requiring authentication and received a high-severity score.
Horizon.ai researchers confirmed that it could be chained with another security issue, CVE-2026-48710, for unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE).
By analyzing the infrastructure, BLL found that several C2 servers featured vulnerable router administration interfaces, suggesting that the attacker reused compromised routers in the attacks.
The researchers could not make a confident attribution but assess with moderate confidence that the operator is Italian, based on comments in the malware and an Italy-based server hosting the administrative interface.
To protect against PoeLLM attacks, system administrators should apply the latest security updates, reduce public internet exposure for critical assets, and restrict external access only to trusted IPs.
Administrators are recommended to inspect network monitoring logs and look for connections to the indicators of compromise (IoCs) shared by Black Lotus Labs.
Update [11:40 EST]: Corrected the number of compromised servers. Original report received by BleepingComputer stated that 2,100 servers were compromised but the researchers updated the number to 3,400 in the live report.

articles.title: Qilin Ransomware Suspect Arrested in Japan, Extradited to Germany
articles.text:
An alleged member of the Qilin ransomware group was arrested in Japan and subsequently extradited to Germany.
The suspect, a 28-year-old Russian national, was detained in Osaka in May and was reportedly handed over to the German authorities on October 2.
Believed to be a core member of the ransomware gang, the individual was wanted in Germany for hacking into a logistics company in September 2024, encrypting data on its systems, and extorting it of over $160,000 in cryptocurrency.
Also known as Agenda, Qilin has been active since August 2022 and has become one of the most prolific ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operations, hitting hundreds of organizations worldwide and causing millions of dollars in damages.
In 2024, the group was blamed for hacking into pathology lab services provider Synnovis and causing disruptions at multiple London hospitals run by the National Health Service.
Last year, Qilin claimed responsibility for hacking beer giant Asahi Group. The incident caused operational disruptions and resulted in the personal information of roughly 2 million people being compromised.
Throughout 2025, the group listed 400 victims on its Tor-based leak site, including Lee Enterprises and pharma company Inotiv.
In June this year, Qilin was exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Check Point VPN and firewall products, tracked as CVE-2026-50751.
In August, the US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) confirmed it had fallen victim to a cyberattack after Qilin added it to its leak site.

articles.title: « Je n’avais jamais vu un PC auparavant » : la confession folle du patron de Nvidia
articles.text:
Jensen Huang, cofondateur et CEO de Nvidia, est monté ce mercredi 7 octobre sur la scène de la keynote Windows et Surface de Microsoft, aux côtés de Satya Nadella, CEO de Microsoft.
Invité à raconter un souvenir commun, le patron de Nvidia a expliqué que son entreprise avait été créée « grâce à Windows », puis il a résumé : « sans Windows, Nvidia n’aurait pas été fondée ». J’y ai surtout entendu un argument commercial, parce que ce récit arrive au moment précis où les deux groupes poussent ensemble le Surface Laptop Ultra et des stations de travail pensées pour l’IA.
Sur le fond, l’histoire tient la route, ce qui la rend d’autant plus efficace. Pour autant, Jensen Huang la raconte en vainqueur, devant le partenaire qui l’a aidé à gagner et juste après une série de démonstrations produits. Bref, un récit d’entreprise qui sent bon le marketing et passe sous silence quelques faits historiques.
Jensen Huang situe le point de départ fin 1992, à l’époque de Windows 3.1, quand on commençait à voir ce que pouvait devenir un ordinateur personnel. Lui travaillait surtout sur des stations de travail, des serveurs de fichiers et des superordinateurs qui servaient à concevoir des puces, et il assure n’avoir jamais vu de PC avant cette période.
Avec ses cofondateurs, il imaginait un PC capable d’afficher de la 3D, à la fois pour jouer et pour concevoir des objets, comme une station de travail. Nvidia démarre en 1993. Pourtant, Jensen Huang désigne Windows 95 comme le vrai tournant : d’après lui, c’est cette version qui a permis de brancher un GPU, la puce graphique, sur un ordinateur personnel (le terme GPU n’apparaîtra pourtant qu’en 1999, quand Nvidia l’utilise pour lancer sa GeForce 256).
Arrive ensuite DirectX, l’ensemble d’outils de Microsoft qui permet aux jeux de dialoguer avec la carte graphique, et plus précisément Direct3D, sa partie consacrée à la 3D. Avec DirectX 8, sorti fin 2000, et la GeForce 3 qui suit en 2001, Nvidia dit avoir « co-inventé » avec Microsoft le premier GPU programmable, grâce aux shaders programmables (de petits programmes qui calculent l’éclairage et l’aspect de chaque pixel à l’écran).
En 2006, ces shaders sont devenus CUDA, la plateforme qui permet d’utiliser les cartes graphiques Nvidia pour du calcul bien au-delà du jeu vidéo. Jensen Huang déroule ensuite sa logique jusqu’au bout. Windows a rendu GeForce possible, et GeForce a rendu CUDA possible. Sans CUDA, enfin, des chercheurs comme Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Yann LeCun ou Andrew Ng n’auraient pas trouvé d’ordinateur pour faire de l’apprentissage profond, la technique sur laquelle reposent les IA actuelles.
Une histoire vraie, racontée par le gagnant
Franchement, je n’ai pas grand-chose à redire sur la chronologie. Le PC sous Windows a bien créé le marché sur lequel Nvidia a grandi, avec des joueurs prêts à payer pour une carte graphique. L’animateur l’a d’ailleurs rappelé à sa façon : son premier salaire chez Microsoft lui a servi à acheter une GeForce FX pour jouer à Half-Life 2.
En revanche, Jensen Huang laisse de côté un point gênant pour sa version : DirectX est une interface de Microsoft, conçue pour fonctionner avec les puces graphiques de tous les fabricants. Windows a ouvert le PC aux cartes graphiques, mais il n’a pas choisi laquelle passerait en tête. Sur scène, personne n’a cité 3dfx ou ATI (racheté depuis par AMD), qui profitaient des mêmes outils à la même époque. Nvidia s’est distingué plus tard, en passant de la GeForce à CUDA, puis à l’IA : un pari propre à l’entreprise, que Windows a seulement rendu possible.
Qui dépend de qui en 2026 ?
Satya Nadella a enchaîné avec son propre souvenir, qui renverse un peu les rôles. Le premier accord dont il se souvient portait sur Azure, le cloud de Microsoft, et sur une question : comment développer le calcul haute performance, ces grappes de serveurs réservées aux très gros calculs. Jensen Huang en a profité pour attribuer à Satya Nadella le premier usage d’InfiniBand, une technologie de réseau très rapide entre serveurs, à l’intérieur d’un cloud.
Le supercalculateur Azure que Microsoft a ensuite construit pour OpenAI, présenté en mai 2020 avec 10 000 GPU, a servi à entraîner ses modèles GPT. Satya Nadella le reconnaît lui-même, « la vie est pleine d’accidents » : sans ce travail sur le calcul haute performance, Microsoft n’aurait pas eu de supercalculateur à proposer. Il félicite aussi Jensen Huang pour une vision du calcul accéléré restée la même depuis le début, « comme une tendance de fond ».
En 1993, Nvidia avait besoin de Windows pour exister. Vingt-sept ans plus tard, en 2020, l’aventure IA de Microsoft a démarré sur un supercalculateur que Jensen Huang présente comme le fruit de leur collaboration. Les deux patrons ont même plaisanté sur un petit « transfert de capitalisation boursière » entre les deux groupes.
Côté Surface, les deux groupes ont d’ailleurs déjà travaillé ensemble : en 2013, la Surface 2, une tablette sous Windows RT, tournait sur une puce Tegra 4 de Nvidia.
Côté PC, Jensen Huang évoque une conversation vieille de quatre ans avec Satya Nadella sur une question simple : à quoi doit ressembler le PC parfait à l’ère de l’IA. Selon lui, la réponse passe par les agents, ces assistants capables d’agir à notre place sur l’ordinateur, et qui ont besoin d’accéder aux logiciels déjà installés.
Il cite les outils de Dassault, Siemens, Autodesk et Adobe, puis Blender, Unreal, Omniverse et Catia, qu’il veut voir réunis sur le même PC que l’IA. Ces logiciels sont aujourd’hui répartis dans l’écosystème Nvidia, entre PC de jeu et stations de travail. Les réunir sur une même machine a pris quatre ans, d’après Jensen Huang. Au même moment, Microsoft veut faire tourner des modèles d’IA en local sur les PC Windows, dont un Nemotron signé Nvidia.
Cette vision profite d’abord à ceux qui la racontent, puisque Nvidia fournit les puces et Microsoft le système comme l’assistant. Côté utilisateur, on a déjà vu l’agent de Perplexity tourner en local sous Windows 11, à condition d’avoir une configuration costaude. Surtout, Microsoft n’a pas encore convaincu tout le monde avec Copilot, que certains cherchent toujours à désactiver de Windows 11.

articles.title: Cowrywise crosses 1m stock trades as retail investing grows
articles.text:
Cowrywise, a Nigerian investment fintech, has processed more than 1 million stock trades one year after launching its Stocks product, as retail investors increasingly use digital platforms to buy Nigerian equities.
The fintech is now launching a curated stocks feature that lets users choose from selected companies backed by analyst research and rated “buy,” “sell,” or “hold.” The feature moves the investment app closer to the point where users decide what to invest in.
The move comes as retail participation in Nigeria’s stock market grows. As younger investors use apps to buy equities more frequently, investment fintechs are competing not only on access and ease of trading, but on how they help users decide where to put their money.
“We have been observing a gradual shift in how younger Nigerians think about investing. There is increasing interest in participating directly in the growth of Nigerian businesses, but historically, accessing the stock market felt complicated for a first-time investor,” Yarmirama Ashama, Associate Vice President of Product at Cowrywise, told TechCabal in an interview.
“Our view was that the opportunity wasn’t simply to give people access to stocks, but to make that access significantly simpler and more intuitive.”
Retail participation on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) has been climbing amid stronger market returns, driving engagement with fintech apps that provide easier access to equities. In the first eight months of 2026, local stock investors traded ₦4.53 trillion ($3.42 billion) worth of equities on the NGX, almost double the ₦2.33 trillion ($1.76 billion) they traded over the same period last year.
The NGX All-Share (ASI) Index, which tracks market performance of listed equities on the exchange, had gained 56.93% by the end of August 2026, giving retail investors more reason to participate as digital platforms made it easier to buy stocks.
In July, TechCabal spoke with young professionals investing fixed amounts monthly, often through mobile apps. Some put in as little as ₦5,000 ($3.77), while others committed between ₦20,000 ($15.07) and ₦200,000 ($150.72) monthly, underscoring how stock investing is becoming a more regular habit for a younger class of retail investors.
Digital investment fintech apps such as Cowrywise and Bamboo are at the centre of that push. Cowrywise told TechCabal that the average age of retail investors for stocks on its platform is 28.
The ongoing Dangote Refinery public offer has given that retail demand another outlet. The ₦2.15 trillion ($1.6 billion) offer, which allows investors to subscribe with as little as ₦5,250 ($3.96), sent a rush of retail investors to digital investment platforms, including Cowrywise.
“We have observed periods of increased activity around major corporate and market events like the extension of trading hours, including significant earnings announcements, dividend declarations, corporate actions, broader market movements, and public offers, just like the ongoing IPO event by the Dangote Petroleum Refinery,” Ashama said.
Founded in 2017, Cowrywise built its business around savings, mutual funds, and managed investments before adding self-directed stock trading. Through Stocks, the fintech earns revenue from brokerage commissions on retail trades it processes on the NGX.
Bamboo, which began by offering self-directed stock investing, launched Managed Portfolio in 2025, allowing customers to invest in a curated portfolio of US stocks with a minimum investment of $100.
Before Managed Portfolio, Bamboo launched access to NGX stocks in 2024—more than a year earlier than Cowrywise. Since then, retail participation on its app has grown. In June, the company told TechCabal it processed 542,582 NGX trades in April alone, surpassing stockbrokers like CardinalStone to become the NGX’s largest broker by weighted market share.
