articles.title: Exvicegobernador de Nueva Jersey usó IA 59 veces para negar un caso de acoso
articles.text:
Dale Caldwell, quien renunció el 25 de septiembre como vicegobernador de Nueva Jersey tras una investigación que determinó que acosó sexualmente a una empleada y violó reglas éticas en reiteradas ocasiones, dijo que consultó chatbots de inteligencia artificial 59 veces para intentar demostrar su inocencia.
En una entrevista con la cadena pública NJ PBS, Caldwell relató que hizo pasar el informe de 61 páginas que motivó su salida por distintas plataformas de inteligencia artificial y les repitió siempre la misma pregunta: ¿cuáles serían tus conclusiones? Según su versión, ninguna encontró una conducta de acoso sexual.
“Todos deberían hacer esa prueba”, le dijo al periodista Rob Nelson. “Y creo que podemos usar la IA para frenar los abusos legales”, agregó Caldwell, de 66 años, sobre su experimento con los chatbots.
Según su relato, repitió la misma consulta en cada plataforma y fue anotando las respuestas, a modo de sondeo propio sobre el expediente que terminó con su carrera política en el estado. La oficina de la gobernadora no comentó puntualmente ese experimento.
Los chatbots de uso masivo no tienen capacidad legal para establecer responsabilidades ni acceso a las pruebas que sustentaron la investigación original, un punto que ninguno de los voceros mencionó al difundir las declaraciones de Caldwell.
Antecedentes de la salida de su cargo
La gobernadora Mikie Sherrill le había dado plazo hasta ese viernes para dejar el cargo, después de que una investigación externa, a cargo de una exfiscal general del estado, confirmara el acoso y una serie de violaciones éticas. Caldwell no mostró señales de que fuera a irse por voluntad propia.
En Nueva Jersey, la gobernadora no puede destituir por sí sola al vicegobernador: solo la legislatura puede hacerlo mediante un juicio político. Por eso la salida de Caldwell dependió de una negociación política y no de una orden directa de Sherrill.
Pastor metodista y expresidente de la Universidad Centenary, Caldwell había llegado al cargo tras ganar las elecciones de noviembre pasado junto a Sherrill, en una fórmula que se impuso con amplio margen. Asumió en enero y también ejerció como secretario de Estado, a cargo de la supervisión electoral.
Fue investigado durante 133 de los 245 días que estuvo en funciones, según su propio relato a NJ PBS. Caldwell es el cuarto vicegobernador desde que el cargo se creó en 2009 y el primero en renunciar.
Nueva Jersey acumula renuncias resonantes en las últimas dos décadas: el senador Bob Menendez dejó su banca en 2024 tras ser condenado por soborno, y el entonces gobernador Jim McGreevey renunció en 2004 después de revelar que era gay en medio de un escándalo por haber designado a su pareja como asesor de seguridad interior.
Cuál fue la respuesta del gobierno
El vocero de Sherrill, Sean Higgins, salió a responderle. Según dijo, la investigación “determinó violaciones graves de las normas éticas estatales y concluyó que su conducta constituyó acoso sexual”.
Higgins agregó que la declaración previa de la gobernadora y lo que llamó un patrón de conducta documentado en el informe “hablan por sí solos”. Sherrill había dicho ante la prensa que este tipo de denuncias “no es la clase de gobierno que dirijo”.
La gobernadora contó además que había hablado y enviado mensajes con Caldwell en los días previos a su salida, aunque evitó precisar si él había mostrado algún tipo de arrepentimiento por su conducta.
Caldwell multiplicó las entrevistas en los días posteriores a su salida. Le dijo a CBS News que “la gente quería que me fuera” y sostuvo ante el programa On New Jersey que la conclusión del informe “minimiza las preocupaciones legítimas” de las mujeres.
En otra aparición, en el programa Hold That Thought, calificó la pesquisa de “trabajo sucio” y dijo que llevó meses completarla, una duración que atribuyó a una intención de perjudicarlo políticamente. Fue en la entrevista con NJ PBS, y no en sus otras apariciones mediáticas, donde reveló por primera vez el número exacto de consultas que hizo a los chatbots.

articles.title: Banjo-Kazooie port developer blasts AI vibe coding as retro gaming fills with low-quality ports
articles.text:
A hot potato: Over the past few months, it seems as if fan-made PC ports of console-exclusive retro games have been emerging almost daily. This is because most of them are built either partially or entirely with AI coding tools such as Claude. Amid the wave, the debate over vibe coding has divided retro gaming enthusiasts.
Developer Dario, a major figure in the emerging PC fan port community, recently published a lengthy, harsh critique of the emerging practice of using LLMs to decompile, recompile, and create new ports for retro video games. His thread on Bluesky provides a detailed explanation of the practice and its pitfalls.
Growing numbers of retro enthusiasts have decompiled the source code of classic video games over the past few years to study their inner workings and reverse-engineer them. Using this knowledge, other developers have ported the games to modern platforms, often by recompiling the reverse-engineered code.
I still see a lot of confusion about what decompilation, recompilation and ports are and what level of effort is involved in each type of project. It's important that people understand the difference, as recompilation took a drastically different meaning that when it was originally introduced.
– Darío (@dariosamo.bsky.social) October 4, 2026 at 9:15 PM
The resulting ports can support higher resolutions, higher frame rates, mods, and many other features not possible with emulation. Ports of games such as Star Fox 64 and Mario Kart 64 have inspired an explosion of attempts to revive and convert beloved titles like Daytona USA, GoldenEye 007, and Bloodborne.
However, many of these projects use AI tools. HarbourMasters, the team behind famous ports of Super Mario 64, Mario Kart 64, Star Fox 64, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Majora's Mask, was revealed to have been using LLMs for years. Besides the usual controversies around LLM use, including its environmental impact and the ethics of training AI on human work without permission, many developers also claim LLM-based coding produces verbose code that is indecipherable to humans.
Dario, a lead contributor to a Banjo-Kazooie port released earlier this year, also explains that many vibe-coded projects come from amateur developers with little to no knowledge of the games they are porting. He also disputes the claim that using AI saves time.
Appreciate the gesture, but for what it's worth, the damage done by AI in this port is far bigger than I could ever imagine. Its entire organization and development is an unsalvageable train wreck. You may not have issues with its usage, but I have major gripes with it for technical reasons too.
[image or embed]
– Darío (@dariosamo.bsky.social) October 1, 2026 at 8:55 PM
According to Dario, LLMs might let inexperienced coders get a game up and running, but that was already the easy part before tools like Claude emerged. Some of these developers have faced criticism for seemingly abandoning bug-ridden projects that offer no advantages over emulation, and it remains to be seen how many AI coders will remain dedicated to fixing and optimizing their work.
For example, Dario compares two identically named Donkey Kong 64 ports, one of which used AI. The developer claims the non-AI recompilation progressed quickly, while the other stalled because of a gap in knowledge about the original game and N64 recompilation tools.
In response to the controversy, some projects have varying policies and disclaimers regarding LLMs. Some teams, for example, require developers to explain what their code does, while others only allow AI for non-coding tasks.

articles.title: Teenage Engineering’s CEO says it’ll stop making synths
articles.text:
Teenage Engineering founder and CEO Jesper Kouthoofd told Highsnobiety that it plans to stop making synths. And yes, that includes the iconic OP-1, which put the company on the map. TE isn’t just a music gear maker; it’s also a sought-after design firm. It’s collaborated with Ikea, Nothing, and Playdate, among others. But almost everything the company makes itself — the OP-1, the OP-XY, EP-133, TP-7, et cetera — is music or audio-focused. Which makes the supposed decision to abandon the market all the more confusing.
Teenage Engineering’s CEO says it’ll stop making synths
The end could be nigh for the iconic OP-1 according to a Highsnobiety interview.
Here’s the relevant quote from Highsnobiety:
Kouthoofd tells me that, as part of a reorganization last fall, he announced to his team he is planning to stop making synthesizers altogether. The OP-1 is no exception. Launched in 2011, it put Teenage Engineering on the map and has been central to its success ever since.
“Everyone was like, ‘What are you talking about?’ But I’ve come to the conclusion that, for us, the products aren’t the business,” Kouthoofd says. “We can be so much more than that.”
Teenage Engineering did not immediately return a request for comment.

articles.title: Elon Musk dobla las manos y confirma que usará la IA de sus rivales en Grok
articles.text:
Elon Musk confirmó que Grok Bot usará modelos de IA rivales para ayudarlo a responder. A unos meses de haber catalogado a Anthropic como "malvada", Musk ahora dependerá de Claude en algunas de las respuestas que se le hagan al asistente de X. El jefe de SpaceX se aprovechará del acuerdo millonario que cerró con Anthropic para ofrecerles capacidad de cómputo para impulsar sus diversos modelos.
De acuerdo con una publicación de Elon Musk, Grok Bot, la aplicación de agentes de SpaceXAI, comenzará a apoyarse en tecnología de otras compañías para responder a los usuarios. El magnate confirmó que su IA usará Claude Opus 5.5 y otros modelos de primer nivel.
“Nota importante sobre Grok @Bot: De ahora en adelante, @SpaceX utilizará el mejor modelo de backend para cualquier tarea dada, incluyendo Claude Opus 5.5, MidJourney, Suno y otras APIs líderes.
Grok @Bot utilizará lo que sea que logre el mejor resultado para los usuarios. Las preguntas simples se dirigirán a modelos pequeños y rápidos. Las preguntas con respuestas complejas se dirigirán a modelos grande. Lo que sea más probable que te dé el mejor resultado”.
Grok Bot funcionaría como un front-end que enruta las solicitudes de los usuarios. Por ejemplo, el agente podría apoyarse en Claude para tareas de razonamiento y programación. Opus 5.5 es uno de los modelos más potentes y eficientes del mercado, sobre todo en tareas de automatización. Hace unas semanas, Anthropic reveló que su nueva IA está diseñada para trabajar en proyectos completos sin perder el hilo y puede coordinar múltiples herramientas.
Musk también mencionó a Midjourney, que serviría para generar imágenes, mientras que Suno estará a cargo de las piezas musicales y efectos de sonido.
Elon Musk pasó del odio al amor con Claude en Grok Bot
Uno de los detalles más curiosos de este anuncio es que Elon Musk nunca ha sido fanático de Claude. Hace unos meses, el magnate respondió a Anthropic en X diciendo que Claude odia a los hombres blancos, a los heterosexuales y a los chinos.
“Esto es misantrópico y malvado. Arréglalo”, mencionó Musk. “Francamente, no creo que haya nada que puedas hacer para escapar de la ironía inevitable de que Anthropic termine siendo misantrópico. Estabas condenado a este destino cuando elegiste tu nombre”.
Meses después, Anthropic cerró un acuerdo multimillonario con SpaceX para obtener el poder de cómputo necesario para impulsar a Claude. Un reporte de mayo confirmó que la empresa de IA se comprometió a pagar 1.250 millones de dólares hasta 2029 por acceder a unas 325.000 GPU de NVIDIA y usar el superordenador Colossus 1 de SpaceX, que ofrece una potencia superior a los 300 megavatios.
Anthropic planea invertir, al menos, 518.000 millones de dólares en infraestructura durante la próxima década, de los cuales un porcentaje irá a los bolsillos de Elon Musk.

articles.title: CIA officer admits to creating fake top secret government program to steal over $190M, including gold bars | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A now-former officer with the Central Intelligence Agency has pleaded guilty to stealing almost $200 million, including hundreds of gold bars, as part of a fraudulent scheme masquerading as a top secret government program.
The U.S. Department of Justice on Tuesday confirmed that David J. Rush, a Virginia resident, admitted to one count of wire fraud linked to running the fabricated operation and defrauding the government while he was a CIA officer. In a statement, prosecutors said that Rush lied about his education and military experience to gain a position at the CIA, and used his access as an employee to set up the top secret and highly compartmentalized program with the intention of using it to funnel U.S. government funds into his possession.
During his arrest, law enforcement found more than $46 million worth of gold bars in Rush’s house linked to the long-running fraud scheme, along with cars, watches, and over $2 million in cash.
The plea deal means that Rush escapes trial, as much as the U.S. government likely avoids having to explain in open court how Rush evaded vetting scrutiny to join the U.S. intelligence agency, and how actions went undetected for more than a year.
Rush was until recently a senior CIA officer who, according to earlier reports, worked for a division of the CIA since 2010 that develops hacking tools and techniques for carrying out espionage. Per court filings, Rush had significant authority over government intelligence programs and spending.
Over the course of 2025, Rush used his position to fabricate a so-called special access program, which are surveillance or intelligence-gathering operations so sensitive that only a few people are read into them. Special access programs, or SAPs, require special clearance that not even the most cleared individuals in government are granted access to. According to The Washington Post, Rush constructed the compartmentalized program under the guise of a fake “continuity of government” plan, aimed at keeping the government functioning in the event of a war, natural disaster, or some other destructive catastrophe. As part of the scheme, Rush used the program and fake government contract to trick an unnamed defense contractor into buying large amounts of gold that Rush then pocketed.
According to The Post, the case astounded officials as Rush’s duties at the CIA involved work with one of the government’s “most sensitive intelligence-gathering programs,” with details so sensitive that only a few senior U.S. intelligence officials and lawmakers know of its existence. The Post withheld details of that program from publication as its disclosure could “jeopardize ongoing intelligence-gathering operations.”
Court filings said that by virtue of his position, Rush “effectively acted as his own approving official, enabling him to expend substantial amounts of United States government money without meaningful scrutiny.”
Rush is scheduled to be sentenced in late January 2027 and faces up to 20 years in prison.

articles.title: Google Messages pourrait bientôt intégrer des jeux dans vos conversations
articles.text:
Google Messages va-t-il bientôt devenir plus divertissant ? L’équipe de Google travaille sur plusieurs jeux, intégrés au sein de la messagerie.
Si les appels vidéos sont actuellement dans les tuyaux, il ne s’agit pas de la seule évolution majeure prévue par l'équipe : la messagerie pourrait bientôt vous permettre de jouer à des jeux. On vous explique.
Google prépare des jeux pour Google Messages
C’est sur X.com que l’information a pointé le bout de son nez : l’utilisateur @yabishekhd a partagé sur son profil une capture d’écran révélant que des jeux pourraient bientôt être intégrés dans Google Messages. Le projet, dont le nom de code semble être « Midnight », n’a pas manqué d’attirer l’attention de nos confrères d’Android Authority qui se sont empressés d’analyser la dernière version bêta de l’application. Ils y ont trouvé des lignes de code très intéressantes.
- L'application est gratuite à télécharger.
- On peut écrire des messages dans des groupes.
- Elle s'intègre parfaitement dans l'écosystème logiciel de Google.
La version messages.android_20261002_00_RC00.phone.openbeta_dynamic de la messagerie montre, en effet, que les développeurs de Google travaillent sur une nouvelle section « Jeux ». Plusieurs jeux y sont d’ores et déjà listés : échecs, billard, fléchettes, Cup Pong, dames, Crazy 8, basket-ball, Puissance 4 et mots mêlés. Comme le souligne @yabishekhd dans sa publication, « en gros, c’est GamePigeon (les jeux iMessage) pour Android. »
De nombreuses questions en suspens
Si Google ne fait pas preuve de beaucoup d’inventivité en copiant l’appli de mini-jeux qui fait le bonheur des utilisateurs d’iMessage, l’ajout d’une telle fonctionnalité à la messagerie est plutôt une bonne nouvelle.
Hélas, on n’en sait pas plus sur ce que prévoit en pratique le géant de Mountain View. Les parties seront-elles disponibles au sein des conversations ou uniquement dans un menu dédié ? Impossible de le savoir. Un mode multijoueur sera-t-il vraiment disponible ? Si cela semble logique au sein d’une messagerie, rien dans les lignes de code ne le confirme noir sur blanc.
Il faudra donc attendre un peu pour être fixé sur toutes ces questions. En espérant, bien sûr, que Google ne renonce pas en cours de route à son mystérieux projet.

articles.title: RBI raises interest rate for first time in nearly four years, signals more hikes
articles.text:
RBI hikes interest rate for the first time in nearly four years, signals more to come
The six-member Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously to raise the repo rate, the first such increase since Governor Sanjay Malhotra took office in December 2024.
The Reserve Bank of India raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on Wednesday, its first increase in nearly four years, and signalled that further hikes could follow as rising inflation and a weakening currency prompt a policy pivot.
The six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted unanimously to raise the repo rate, the first such increase since Governor Sanjay Malhotra took office in December 2024. While the move was widely expected, the central bank sprang a surprise in shifting its stance towards "calibrated tightening", effectively ruling out a rate cut in the near term.
"Rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook," Malhotra said announcing the MPC decisions.
The governor, however, cautioned that the timing and extent of any further tightening would depend on the evolution of inflation and growth, particularly underlying price pressures and the extent to which supply shocks become embedded in the broader economy.
With the decision, India has joined major central banks in raising rates as higher oil prices triggered by the Iran war fuel inflation, squeeze purchasing power and weigh on currencies. Compounding the price pressures is weak rains linked to El Nino.
Inflation pressures have broadened even as economic activity remains resilient. Consumer-price inflation rose to 4.82% in August, above the RBI's 4% medium-term target for a third consecutive month, while core inflation accelerated to 4.2%.
The central bank said inflation risks were no longer as benign as they had been a year earlier, pointing to higher food and fuel prices, deficient monsoon rainfall, El Nino conditions, and renewed volatility in international oil prices.
The RBI now expects headline inflation to average 5.2% in the 2026-27 financial year, with inflation projected to rise to 6.0% in the third quarter and 5.7% in the fourth quarter.
"There are also early signs of inflation becoming generalised," he said, citing a rise in core inflation and a larger share of the consumer price index basket recording elevated price increases.
Oil prices have emerged as a particular risk following the renewed escalation of the West Asia conflict. The Indian crude basket averaged $116.1 a barrel in September, up sharply from $82 in July, according to the RBI.
Food-price pressures have also broadened, with the central bank flagging sharp increases in sugar and onion prices and warning of early signs that inflation is becoming more widespread.
At the same time, the RBI raised its economic growth forecast for 2026-27 by 40 basis points to 7.1%, after the economy expanded 7.8% in the first quarter.
The RBI said activity remained resilient in the second quarter, although momentum had moderated. Manufacturing and services continued to expand, while indicators such as capital-goods production, credit growth and consumer spending remained supportive.
"The Indian economy has been strong, and the economic momentum remains broad-based," Malhotra said, adding that the economy was expected to remain resilient despite global headwinds.
The central bank nevertheless warned that weaker monsoon rainfall, geopolitical tensions, elevated commodity prices, trade frictions and tighter global financial conditions could weigh on growth.
The RBI said monetary policy could not directly address supply shocks but could prevent them from becoming entrenched through inflation expectations and corporate pricing behaviour.
"While there is some evidence of elevated inflation expectations and generalisation of inflation, there are limited signs of supply side pressures getting embedded in pricing behaviour," he said.
The central bank's policy shift marks a balancing act between containing an increasingly broad inflation shock and preserving strong domestic growth. It said the duration and extent of the rate-hike cycle would depend on actual growth and inflation outcomes, particularly the persistence of underlying inflation and second-round effects from supply shocks.
Global risks have also intensified, with the RBI citing the West Asia conflict, elevated bond yields, trade uncertainty and risks of a sharp correction in AI-stock valuations as threats to the outlook.
"We shall strive for price and financial stability as both are essential for sustainable growth in the long run," Malhotra said.
The rate decision comes as financial-system liquidity remains abundant and credit growth has accelerated.
Average daily surplus liquidity under the RBI’s liquidity adjustment framework reached Rs 5.9 lakh crore since the previous policy meeting, while bank credit growth accelerated to 18.1% year-on-year as of September 15, compared with 10.4% a year earlier.
The RBI said strong growth in monetary and credit aggregates represented an additional risk even though evidence of demand-side inflation pressures remained limited.
The central bank said it would use an appropriate mix of liquidity-management tools to align the weighted average call rate with the repo rate.
The RBI's guidance effectively narrows the range of likely policy moves at upcoming meetings to either a pause or another rate increase.
"We continue to see 25-50 basis point of additional rate hikes going ahead, with further upside if global risks persist," said Upasna Bhardwaj, Chief Economist, Kotak Mahindra Bank.

articles.title: Ransomware has a new target. Is your backup ready?
articles.text:
Ransomware is far less frightening when you know you can recover.
That’s why threat actors are turning their attention to encrypting backups. They wipe recovery points and disrupt the infrastructure needed to restore the encrypted data. Once that recovery path disappears, the pressure to pay rises sharply.
For IT leaders, the lesson is uncomfortable but simple. A backup is only a safety net if the attacker cannot reach it.
What attacks on backup infrastructure look like
Ransomware groups have found several ways to neutralize backups, and the methods keep getting more deliberate.
ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware group
In February 2024, the ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware group encrypted Change Healthcare’s systems after breaking through a remote access portal with no multi-factor authentication. The backups were not isolated or robust enough to restore operations quickly.
UnitedHealth paid $22 million in ransom and still did not get its data back. Total recovery costs hit an estimated $1.6 billion.
BlackMatter ransomware
The BlackMatter group made backup destruction their standard operating procedure. When they hit NEW Cooperative, an Iowa-based farm services provider, and Crystal Valley, a Minnesota farm cooperative, in 2021, they used compromised admin credentials to locate every backup data store and appliance on the network — then wiped or reformatted them before encrypting everything else. Since the backups were on the same network, they were easy targets.
CISA, the FBI, and the NSA jointly documented this tactic, noting the group has demanded ransom payments ranging from $80,000 to $15 million in Bitcoin and Monero.
Gunra ransomware
Gunra ransomware, documented in a joint CISA and FBI advisory in August 2026, pushed that logic further. In one confirmed case, attackers deleted backup and archived data at both the organization's primary data center and its disaster recovery site.
A single set of stolen credentials was all it took to reach both. Having two copies in two locations meant nothing, because both locations trusted the same key.
Protecting the way back
The attacks above point to a simple shift in how backup strategy needs to be thought about. Do not only ask how many copies you have or where they are stored. Ask what connects those copies, who can administer them and whether a compromised account could reach them all.
Your recovery strategy should assume attackers will try to destroy the way out. Separate critical backups from production, limit administrative access, and ensure there is no single compromised identity or pathway that can wipe every recovery copy.
Your Backup Is Only as Safe as What Connects to It
Ransomware groups are now targeting backup infrastructure first — wiping recovery points before encrypting everything else.
Our report, Building Security That Survives Human Error, reveals what's stalling organizations from closing the gap and where leading IT teams are focusing first.
Download the Report
The financial reality of losing your backup
The cost difference between recovering with intact backups versus without them is the difference between a manageable disruption and a business-threatening event.
IBM's 2025 Cost of a Data Breach Report puts the average cost of a ransomware incident at $5.08 million. But the financial damage is only part of the picture.
IBM’s 2026 research found that 41% of ransomware incidents also involved threats to damage the victim’s brand reputation, showing how quickly the impact can spread from disrupted systems to lost customer trust.
If attackers destroy the backups, they take away the leverage that lets organizations refuse the ransom.
Why this keeps happening
These attacks tend to expose the same weaknesses. The recovery environment may exist, but the security around it is often less mature than those protecting production systems.
- Backups share the same network and credentials: If the same administrator accounts can access both production systems and backups, an attacker who compromises one of those accounts may be able to reach both. True isolation requires deliberate architecture.
- Backup software gets patched last: The Akira airline attack exploited a vulnerability that had a patch available for over a year. Backup servers are frequently treated as appliances rather than software systems, which means they get updated last, or not at all. Attackers keep careful track of what remains unpatched.
- Monitoring rarely extends to backup infrastructure: Security teams concentrate detection and alerting on production environments. Backup servers often carry minimal logging, weaker access controls and slower response processes. They are watched less carefully, which makes them quieter to work in.
- The deeper barrier is resources: Knowing what good backup security looks like and having the budget, trained staff and operational bandwidth to implement it are separate problems. Many IT teams and MSPs operate with all three in short supply. They understand the exposure but simply cannot close it fast enough.
What closing the gap requires
It requires treating the recovery environment as critical infrastructure.
- Immutable storage as a baseline: Write-once backup copies that cannot be altered or deleted — even by someone with admin credentials — fundamentally change the attacker's calculation. Most modern cloud storage platforms support object lock features that achieve this. It is a minimum requirement now, not an advanced measure.
- True network and credential isolation: A backup environment sharing network access and credentials with production is not meaningfully separate. Proper isolation keeps backup data out of reach even after a network compromise. Multi-factor authentication and role-based access controls for backup infrastructure add another layer of friction that slows attackers down significantly.
- Patch backup software with the same urgency as production systems: This requires discipline, not new tooling. Backup platforms need to be built explicitly into the patch cycle rather than treated as exceptions.
- Test restores, not just backups: An untested backup is an assumption. Regular restore testing — ideally including attack scenario simulations — surfaces gaps before attackers do. Organizations that discover restoration failures during an actual incident have no time to fix them.
The gap between awareness and action
The challenge of protecting backups points to a broader problem in cybersecurity. Most organizations understand the risk of an attack. They may know they need stronger isolation, better monitoring or more resilient recovery, but lack the budget, staff or operational capacity to put those protections in place.
Almost 77% of IT organizations surveyed for our cybersecurity report, Building Security That Survives Human Error, say their cybersecurity investment is not keeping pace with the threats they face. Among MSPs, 65% say their clients are underinvesting in cybersecurity.
The result is a familiar tension. Security teams know what needs attention, but limited resources force them to make difficult choices about where to focus first.
Drawing on responses from more than 1,100 IT and cybersecurity professionals, the report looks at the pressures behind those choices, from human error and underinvestment to staffing shortages and operational friction.
If your team knows where it needs to improve but struggles to make those improvements happen, our report offers a closer look at what is getting in the way and where organizations are focusing their efforts.

articles.title: Lecornu incommodé : son numéro de téléphone fuite à cause du Slip Français
articles.text:
Lecornu incommodé : son numéro de téléphone fuite à cause du Slip Français
Déjà empêtré dans bien des dossiers liés à sa fonction, le premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu peut en ajouter un autre à sa pile : son numéro de téléphone a fuité à cause d'un ancien vol de données.
Ce n'est pas tous les jours que nous avons l'occasion d'écrire un article tout à fait légitime, qui pourrait pourtant passer pour un papier du Gorafi. Ce mercredi 7 octobre, Le Canard Enchaîné nous apprend que le numéro de téléphone de Sébastien Lecornu, ainsi que des informations personnelles du premier ministre, “sont parties dans les méandres d’internet”.
Fuite de données chez Le Slip Français : les dessous de l'affaire Lecornu
Tout commence en 2024 lorsque le site de vente de sous-vêtements Le Slip Français est victime d'un piratage ayant laissé fuiter les données de 1,5 million de ses clients. Aujourd'hui, grâce à un moteur de recherche pirate regroupant un très grand nombre de données issues des multiples cyberattaques ayant eu lieu en France depuis des mois, il est possible de retrouver les personnes concernées, ainsi que leurs informations personnelles.
C'est ainsi que, selon Le Canard Enchaîné, des données de 25 des 36 membres du gouvernement Lecornu circulent. Le premier ministre, alors ministre des Armées, se retrouve donc aujourd'hui exposé à cause d'un achat réalisé sur le site. Il n'est cependant pas le seul, puisque par exemple la ministre déléguée au Numérique, Anne Le Hénanff, est concernée par son numéro de Sécurité sociale et son RIB à la Caisse d'Épargne.
Si Sébastien Lecornu peut assez aisément changer de numéro de téléphone pour ne pas être importuné, peut-être que cette affaire permettra au pays, deuxième le plus touché par des fuites de données en 2026, de muscler son jeu en matière de cybersécurité. En mai dernier, la Cnil annonçait des mesures renforcées, mais il n'est pas certain que cela suffise à étoffer une cybersécurité française au point de rupture.

articles.title: Google Wallet change complètement l'affichage de vos cartes de paiement, voici à quoi ça ressemble
articles.text:
Après avoir retouché le design de toutes les cartes plus tôt cette année, l’interface de Google Wallet abandonne aujourd’hui le défilement horizontal des cartes de paiement pour adopter un affichage vertical plus épuré, dans l’esprit de ce que l’on trouve sur iOS. La mise à jour est diffusée progressivement via les serveurs de l’entreprise et commence à arriver en nombre sur les smartphones Android.
Un défilement plus intuitif pour les cartes de paiement
L’écran d’accueil affiche désormais une seule carte principale en grand format, surmontée par un petit morceau de la carte suivante. Pour accéder à l’ensemble de la pile, il faut appuyer dessus ou faire un glissement vers le bas. On ne peut que saluer ce choix tant l’ergonomie à une main est bien meilleure avec un défilement vertical, surtout lorsque les cartes les plus utilisées se trouvent en bas de la pile.
© Google Wallet / Capture 01net
Il est d’ailleurs possible de réorganiser vos moyens de paiement et/ou de modifier la carte par défaut en faisant un appui prolongé dessus et en la faisant glisser où vous voulez. Vous pouvez aussi utiliser le menu de gestion dédié situé tout en bas de l’écran. Les autres éléments de l’application, comme les cartes de transport ou les programmes de fidélité, restent accessibles directement depuis l’écran principal sans encombrer cette nouvelle vue dédiée aux cartes de paiement.
Une étape supplémentaire pour afficher les transactions
Rien ne change pour le paiement sans contact, il suffit de taper sur la carte que vous voulez utiliser. En revanche, consulter l’historique des transactions ou afficher les informations détaillées d’une carte demande désormais une étape supplémentaire. Une nouvelle icône en forme de roue crantée fait son apparition dans le coin supérieur droit pour ouvrir ces paramètres.
© Google Wallet / Capture 01net
À lire : Google Wallet débarque dans Gemini : voici ce que ça change
Auparavant, il fallait taper directement sur la carte pour obtenir ces informations. Un petit changement avec lequel on devrait réussir à s’accommoder. Tous les smartphones Android qui utilisent Google Wallet devraient prochainement recevoir ces changements (si ce n’est pas déjà fait), via une mise à jour du côté des serveurs de Google.

articles.title: Surface Laptop Ultra : Microsoft invente le port USB-C magnétique : la sécurité du MagSafe, la liberté en plus — Frandroid
articles.text:
Microsoft n’avait pas organisé de conférence Windows et Surface depuis plus de deux ans. Ce mercredi 7 octobre à San Francisco, entre deux démonstrations d’IA, l’entreprise a présenté Magnetic Connect, qu’elle décrit comme « le premier chargeur USB-C magnétique intégré au monde ».
L’idée reprend celle du MagSafe d’Apple : si on se prend les pieds dans le câble, la prise se détache au lieu d’emporter l’ordinateur portable avec elle. La différence se trouve côté PC, où l’on garde un port USB-C standard, sans connecteur maison.
Microsoft promet un branchement sans viser : « Approchez le connecteur et il s’enclenche immédiatement en place. » Le port équipe le Surface Laptop Ultra, le PC portable de 15 pouces dévoilé en juin et construit autour de la puce RTX Spark de Nvidia.
Protégez votre vie numérique avec Bitdefender, la protection européenne de confiance. Bitdefender vous protège contre les arnaques et les fraudes du web. Profitez de vos activités en ligne en toute tranquillité.
Le PC est en précommande depuis ce mercredi aux États-Unis, et les premières livraisons sont prévues le 16 octobre. L’un de ses trois ports USB-C est magnétique, et il accepte n’importe quel périphérique USB-C, comme les deux autres.
Pour 2 599 dollars, Microsoft livre la configuration d’entrée : une puce RTX Spark à 18 cœurs avec 5 120 cœurs graphiques, 24 Go de mémoire vive et un écran mini-LED de 15 pouces. Le Surface Laptop Ultra devient au passage la Surface la plus chère jamais vendue par Microsoft. Les configurations les plus musclées visent le développement d’IA en local.
Un MagSafe sans connecteur propriétaire
Apple a fait un autre choix sur ses MacBook. Le MagSafe 3, revenu sur les MacBook Pro en 2021, est un connecteur à part, avec son propre câble, qui s’ajoute aux ports USB-C. Microsoft avait suivi la même logique avec le Surface Connect, sa prise magnétique propriétaire qui ne servait qu’à brancher le chargeur ou un dock Surface.
Microsoft avait pourtant l’idée depuis un moment. En mai 2018, l’entreprise a déposé un brevet intitulé « Magnetically activated latch mechanism », repéré fin 2018 par Digital Trends : des aimants placés de part et d’autre d’un port USB-C attirent la prise, et les câbles USB-C classiques continuent de fonctionner.
Des adaptateurs tiers proposent aussi le principe depuis des années, avec un petit embout magnétique qu’on laisse en permanence dans le port. Le « premier au monde » tient donc au mot « intégré ». Aucun fabricant n’avait encore mis l’aimant directement dans un port standard.
Le port se repérait d’ailleurs dès la présentation de juin. XDA Developers avait remarqué qu’un des trois ports USB-C du Surface Laptop Ultra était plus large que les deux autres. Microsoft confirmait alors qu’il s’agissait d’un vrai port USB, sans en dire plus.
Sur le papier, la formule tient la route : on garde l’universalité de l’USB-C et un câble qui lâche au bon moment, sans transporter de chargeur propriétaire. Pour autant, les premières annonces ne précisent ni la puissance de charge de ce port, ni la force des aimants.

articles.title: Hadrian Raises $40 Million to Expand Autonomous Offensive Security Platform
articles.text:
Attackers use AI to locate and exploit vulnerabilities at machine speed; Hadrian offers an agentic offensive security platform that allows defenders to operate at the same speed.
Amsterdam-based Hadrian has raised an additional $40 million in a Series B round, to bring its total funding to $65 million. The new funding was co-led by Forgepoint Capital International and SmartFin, with participation from existing investors HV Capital, Motive Partners, Picus Capital and Oetker Ventures.
This new capital will be used to fund expansion across EMEA and the US, and deepen investment in the firm’s engineering and research teams.
Hadrian provides an AI native offensive security platform offering discovery (via Atlas), validation (via Nova), prioritization and remediation. The firm was founded in 2021 by former ethical hackers Rogier Fischer (CEO) and Olivier Beg (chief hacking officer), together with entrepreneur Maurice Clin (head of business development). It develops AI-driven offensive security technology designed to continuously discover, validate, and prioritize externally exposed cyber risks, combining continuous exposure management and agentic penetration testing.
Atlas continuously maps the organization’s external attack surface and uses AI agents to validate which exposures are exploitable. Nova provides on-demand agentic pentesting.
The purpose is to resolve the imbalance in manual pentesting and adversarial probing caused by the increased use of AI by attackers. “Attackers now move at machine speed, but many security teams are years behind, with data showing that 87% of organizations still run manual pentests,” says Hadrian. Manual pentesting struggles to separate importance from noise when only 0.47% of vulnerability scanner findings are genuinely exploitable. That means 99.5% of the alerts teams focus on need no action.
“Everyone can see that AI is changing the threat landscape. It might also hold the answer, but most people are focused on automating the wrong bits,” says Fischer. “We have been working with LLMs since before they went mainstream, and we know that AI can work much faster than any human offensive security team. So, we built a platform that emulates hackers’ attack paths, helping our customers to understand their key risks and prioritize their security resources appropriately.”
By using AI to automate and improve the process, Hadrian claims its customers have seen 10 times greater visibility into critical risks, five times improved ROI over manual pentests, and an 80% faster time to resolution. “Humans set the mission and make the decisions that matter, while AI does the work in between, providing the coverage, repetition and speed that no team can sustain around the clock,” says Hadrian.
Built by former hackers, Hadrian understands how hackers attack. Its agentic system will probe for exploitable pathways with the same machine speed harnessed by today’s AI-assisted attackers. It provides always-on discovery, validation and mobilization of an organization’s most critical cyber risks, autonomously verifying remediation.

articles.title: Unos economistas han analizado si compensa construir estadios con fondos públicos. Tenemos malas noticias para los clubs
articles.text:
Semana sí, semana también, el fútbol obra un milagro: llena estadios con miles de aficionados que quieren apoyar a su equipo. Durante la temporada 2025/26, los campos en los que se disputan los partidos de la máxima categoría del fútbol español recibieron 11,7 millones de espectadores. Con semejantes datos los clubs suelen reivindicar que son motores económicos que benefician a las ciudades, atraen visitantes, dinamizan el comercio, llenan bares y hoteles… Un argumento valioso cuando se pide a un organismo público que financie obras en estadios o facilite los terrenos y accesos.
La pregunta es… ¿De verdad sale rentable dedicar recursos públicos a los estadios? En EEUU un grupo de economistas ha hecho cuentas y sus conclusiones resultan demoledoras.
Sacando la calculadora. Abigail Hall y Aaron D. Wood tienen tres cosas en común: ambos son profesores de Economía en la Universidad de Tampa, ambos pagan sus impuestos religiosamente y ambos son aficionados al deporte. Hace poco decidieron unir esas tres facetas y hacerse una pregunta espinosa: ¿Sale a cuenta que los organismos públicos pongan dinero para estadios? Cada vez que un club profesional llama a la puerta de un ayuntamiento pidiendo fondos para mejorar sus campos, ¿está justificado que se abran las arcas alimentadas con impuestos? ¿Se recupera esa inversión?
Tras echar cuentas y repasar algunos papers recientes sobre el tema, Hall y Wood plasmaron sus conclusiones en un artículo publicado en The Conversation. Su titular (desafiante) es casi un espóiler: "Las ciudades siguen destinando dinero de los contribuyentes a los estadios deportivos, aunque económicamente casi nunca es sensato".
Un porcentaje para reflexionar: 73%. El trabajo de Hall y Wood parte de una premisa que sorprenderá a pocos: construir estadios no es barato. El SoFi Stadium de Los Ángeles costó unos 6.750 millones de dólares y se calcula que la nueva catedral de los Washington Commanders requerirá unos 4.000 millones. Lo que sí resulta llamativo es que, al menos en EEUU, gran parte de ese dinero sale de los impuestos. A pesar de que la NFL, la MLB y NBA ingresan miles de millones de dólares cada año, los economistas calculan que el Estado ha sido el gran mecenas de los campos desde los años 70.
"Es raro que las ligas o franquicias que obtienen grandes ganancias de sus equipos cubran el coste total de la construcción de nuevas instalaciones. De hecho, la mayoría de los nuevos estadios deportivos reciben financiación de los gobiernos estatales o locales […]. Entre 1970 y 2020, los contribuyentes de EEUU y Canadá aportaron unos 33.000 millones de dólares para la construcción de estadios deportivos, aproximadamente el 73% del coste total".
Es mucho dinero, ¿no? Depende de cómo se mire. Cuando buscan respaldo de las instituciones, clubs, franquicias y ligas suelen alegar que los estadios son motores económicos: atraen visitantes de otros lugares, dinamizan el comercio y la hostelería, aumentan los ingresos fiscales y revalorizan las propiedades que están en los alrededores. Tan rotundos suenan esos argumentos que no es extraño que las franquicias amenacen con mudarse de ciudad si no reciben la respuesta que buscan, algo que hemos visto también en España.
El peso social y cultural del deporte y sus valores son incuestionables, pero a la vista de lo anterior vale la pena hacerse una pregunta: ¿Realmente se rentabilizan las inversiones públicas en estadios, sobre todo cuando hablamos de ligas profesionales que mueven millones de dólares y en casos en los que la administración asume el coste de las obras? Es la pregunta que se han planteado Hall y Wood.
UN VISTAZO A...
"Casi nunca se recupera". Esa es la conclusión que dejan botando ambos profesores. Más allá de los beneficios económicos prometidos por los clubs, "la historia demuestra que el sector público casi nunca recupera la subvención inicial". Para afirmarlo se apoyan en un estudio de 2023 que, tras analizar el impacto económico de los estadios durante cuatro décadas, determina que los beneficios económicos para los contribuyentes son "escasos o nulos".
"El auge económico prometido nunca parece materializarse. Los estadios no han tenido un impacto sistemático en la apertura de nuevos negocios. Y, en cuanto al valor de las propiedades, las evidencias son, como mucho, dispares. Algunos investigadores no han encontrado ningún efecto en absoluto, mientras que otros han concluido que el valor de las propiedades alrededor de los estadios aumentó, pero solo después de que los equipos se marcharan", subrayan.
Pero… ¿Y los visitantes y el comercio? Un buen partido puede atraer aficionados de otras ciudades o incluso países, pero Hall y Wood relativizan su impacto a nivel económico. Para empezar porque las personas que habitualmente vemos gastarse dinero en los estadios, razonan, no suelen ser visitantes de fuera que inyectan capital en la economía local, sino residentes que "redistribuyen su presupuesto de ocio".
¿Se gastan dinero antes, durante y después del partido? Sí, pero no son euros extra inyectados en la hostelería, sino bebidas o comida que probablemente dejarán de comprar en otro momento. Hoy vas al estadio a ver un partido; mañana lo compensas comiendo en casa en vez de ir a un restaurante.
A eso se añaden otros hándicaps. Durante los días de partido, los vecinos y negocios situados cerca de los estadios sufren congestiones de tráfico, mayor contaminación e incluso un aumento de la delincuencia. En cuanto a si se revalorizan o no las propiedades situadas cerca de los campos, Hall y Wood recuerdan que las investigaciones sobre el tema están lejos de ser concluyentes: algunas no perciben efecto alguno, otras muestran que sí hay un aumento de valor, pero irónicamente solo cuando los clubs hacen las maletas y se marchan.
Ni más empleo ni más impuestos. En su artículo los profesores de la Universidad de Tampa citan otros papers que cuestionan que los estadios deportivos tengan un impacto significativo en la creación de empleo, la apertura de nuevos negocios o que a la larga aumenten el flujo de ingresos fiscales en las ciudades en las que se edifican. "La experiencia muestra que los nuevos recintos no han proporcionado a los responsables políticos presupuestos más amplios", zanjan los economistas antes de citar un caso concreto: el Truist Park de Atlanta y el traslado de los Atlanta Braves hace nueve años.
"Si bien el condado donde se ubica el estadio de béisbol experimentó un pequeño aumento en los ingresos fiscales el año posterior a su inauguración, también se registró un incremento similar en los condados circundantes". Antes de concluir, Hall y Wood dejan un mensaje más: la vida útil de un estadio profesional ronda los 30 años, así que no es descabellado pensar que EEUU se encamine a "una oleada de construcciones" en los próximos años para renovar o jubilar las instalaciones levantadas en la década de los 90.
¿Es aplicable a España? En España la foto es compleja. Hay estadios renovados con presupuestos millonarios que se financian gracias a inversores privados, otros en los que se utiliza una fórmula mixta, que combina fondos públicos y privados, y casos en los que casi todo el dinero que se destina a las instalaciones es público. Esto último es frecuente en el caso de los estadios municipales, como Balaídos. En cualquier caso, más allá del dinero dedicado a reformas u obras, no es extraño que las administraciones se vean afectadas por otros aspectos que sí requieren implicación pública, como los accesos o los terrenos.

articles.title: TikTok sued over alleged access restrictions in northern Nigeria
articles.text:
TikTok users in four northern Nigerian states have reportedly struggled to watch videos, upload content, and use the app since mid-September.
A digital-rights group has sued the company over the disruption, but its case hinges on an unresolved issue: whether TikTok restricted access or the problem originated elsewhere.
The Foundation for Digital Justice and Sustainable Development filed the fundamental-rights action at the Federal High Court in Abuja, Nigeria’s capital, on October 5, asking the court to determine whether the alleged regional restriction violates users’ rights to freedom of expression and freedom from discrimination.
Access disruptions began around September 11, 2026, in Kaduna, Kano, Kebbi and Sokoto states. By September 14, the platform was heavily restricted or completely inaccessible in those states.
The case will test whether Nigerian courts can hold a global technology company accountable for allegedly restricting access to its platform—but first, the foundation must establish that TikTok caused the disruption.
Unlike recent cases involving Meta and Truecaller, which centred on personal data, this suit concerns access to a major channel for communication and commerce, and whether a platform-imposed regional restriction would violate users’ rights.
The foundation wants the court to find that the alleged regional restriction violates users’ rights to freedom of expression and freedom from discrimination. Before those claims can be resolved, however, the case must establish what caused the disruption and whether TikTok was responsible.
TikTok did not respond to requests for comment and has not publicly explained the reported access problems.
According to the lawsuit seen by TechCabal, videos freeze or fail to load on regular mobile data connections, uploads stall, and other functions do not work.
The foundation says affected users can restore access through virtual private networks, or VPNs. It argues that its investigation and interviews with users point to a regional restriction rather than a local technical glitch.
But reports of disrupted access—and the ability to reconnect through a VPN—do not, by themselves, establish that TikTok deliberately blocked users in those states.
The foundation’s case attributes the disruption to TikTok, while the possibility of a network, routing, or infrastructure problem remains unresolved. The company has not offered an explanation that would clarify the source of the failure.
“TikTok owes its users the duty to offer an explanation concerning the restriction and the discrimination,” Festus Ogun, counsel representing the foundation, told TechCabal. “We maintain that the continuous exclusion and restriction is a violation of digital rights.”
TikTok’s Terms of Service reserve the right to suspend or restrict all or part of its platform for “business and operational reasons,” without prior notice. However, the clause does not specify criteria for restricting access across an entire region. It also does not establish that TikTok exercised that power in northern Nigeria.
The contractual provision and the foundation’s allegations therefore raise separate issues: whether TikTok imposed a restriction and, if it did, whether that restriction was lawful.
The foundation argues that the disruption cannot be treated as ordinary content moderation. Ogun distinguishes enforcement against particular posts or accounts from preventing users across a region from accessing the application.
“This has nothing to do with content moderation,” he said. “Content moderation relates more to the ability to post or make comments and not the ability to access or use the application entirely.”
TikTok’s published enforcement policies describe content removals, temporary feature restrictions, and account bans for repeated or severe violations. They also provide notification and appeal procedures for affected users. Those account-level processes do not explain the reported disruption across the four states.
The foundation says the consequences extend beyond an inability to upload videos. Its suit describes posting, viewing, replying, liking, and reposting as forms of “expressive conduct” that affected users are being denied.
For creators and small businesses that use TikTok to reach audiences or customers, the disruption may also affect income. But the lawsuit’s central claim concerns access to a platform used for communication, public debate and commerce.
The suit relies on Sections 39, 42, 45 and 46 of Nigeria’s Constitution, alongside Articles 2 and 9 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights. The foundation invokes protections for expression and against discrimination to challenge the alleged exclusion of users in particular states.
It argues that TikTok should explain why users in Kaduna, Kano, Kebbi and Sokoto face access problems while users elsewhere in Nigeria can continue using the platform.
“What is good for the goose is also good for the gander,” Ogun said. “They should come to court to explain why some Northern States are excluded while the rest of Nigerian states are not subjected to the same restrictive measure.”
The foundation argues that selective restrictions without an objective and lawful justification could amount to unequal treatment based on place of origin, ethnicity, religion or another constitutionally protected ground. That remains an allegation for the court to assess, rather than an established explanation for the disruption.
The group is asking the court to declare the alleged geoblocking wrongful, unconstitutional and arbitrary. It also seeks a public apology in three newspapers with nationwide circulation within seven days of judgment.
If the foundation establishes TikTok’s responsibility, the case would raise a further question: how constitutional protections for expression apply to a private platform that controls access to a widely used digital space.
Ogun rejects the suggestion that those protections apply only to government conduct.
“The section protects freedom of expression from the whims and caprices of big techs, private persons and authorities,” he said.
