articles.title: Microsoft lança novo notebook Surface com foco em IA e alto desempenho
articles.text:
A Microsoft anunciou a data de lançamento e o preço do Surface Laptop Ultra, seu notebook Surface mais potente até agora. Equipado com o chip Nvidia RTX Spark, o aparelho chega ao mercado em 16 de outubro, com preço inicial de US$ 2.599 (cerca de R$ 14,1 mil).
A configuração de entrada inclui processador de 18 núcleos, 24 GB de RAM e 512 GB de armazenamento. O modelo já está disponível para pré-venda.
O Surface Laptop Ultra foi desenvolvido para disputar espaço no segmento premium de notebooks, com foco em tarefas que exigem alto desempenho, incluindo softwares criativos, jogos e execução de modelos de inteligência artificial (IA) diretamente no dispositivo.
O aparelho utiliza o novo RTX Spark, plataforma baseada em arquitetura Arm que pode oferecer até 128 GB de memória unificada. Microsoft e Nvidia posicionam os notebooks equipados com o chip na faixa mais alta do mercado, especialmente para cargas de trabalho de IA local.
Tela e construção
- O notebook tem tela sensível ao toque HDR de 15 polegadas, com brilho máximo de até dois mil nits. O trackpad também foi ampliado e oferece resposta tátil;
- O computador adota um chassi de alumínio com visual que lembra o MacBook Pro, justamente um dos produtos que a Microsoft pretende enfrentar com o novo Surface;
- Na parte de conexões, o Surface Laptop Ultra traz três portas USB-C, uma HDMI, uma USB-A, leitor de cartões SD de tamanho completo e entrada para fones de 3,5 mm;
- A Microsoft oferece diferentes configurações do notebook. No topo da linha está uma versão de US$ 5.899,99 (cerca de R$ 32 mil), equipada com 128 GB de RAM, processador de 20 núcleos e 1 TB de armazenamento.
Surface Laptop Ultra ganha carregamento magnético via USB-C
Uma das características mais curiosas do novo notebook está na forma de carregá-lo. A Microsoft criou o Magnetic Connect, sistema que utiliza uma conexão magnética acoplada a uma porta USB-C.
O cabo se prende magneticamente à porta localizada no lado direito do computador. Segundo Pavan Davuluri, chefe de Windows e Surface, basta aproximar o conector para que ele se encaixe automaticamente.
A solução lembra o antigo Surface Connect, carregador magnético proprietário que a Microsoft abandonou nos modelos menores da linha Surface no ano passado. A diferença é que, no Surface Laptop Ultra, o sistema magnético utiliza uma porta USB-C.
Apesar de a conexão magnética ser proprietária, a porta continua podendo ser usada normalmente para vídeo, transferência de dados e outros acessórios USB-C quando o carregador não está conectado.
RTX Spark coloca IA local no centro do Surface
O RTX Spark é uma das principais apostas do Surface Laptop Ultra. O chip foi desenvolvido para lidar com jogos, cargas de trabalho criativas e modelos de IA executados diretamente no dispositivo.
A combinação do processador com até 128 GB de memória unificada coloca o notebook em categoria voltada a usuários que precisam de bastante capacidade computacional sem depender exclusivamente de processamento na nuvem.
O Surface Laptop Ultra começa a ser enviado em 16 de outubro, enquanto as pré-vendas já estão abertas.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Edmonton Unlimited announces Deep Tech Foundry program at Startup Week | BetaKit
articles.text:
Edmonton Unlimited is turning its focus to deep tech commercialization with a new program slated to start in 2027.
The news: Announced at Edmonton Startup Week on Wednesday morning, the Deep Tech Foundry program is designed to help founders with highly technical startups commercialize their innovation. Shaheel Hooda of Sprout Fund and Eecomobility president Amit Monga both partnered with Edmonton Unlimited to shape the design of the program, which has been in development for several months.
From the source: “The Deep Tech Foundry will be a highly focused, bespoke, and hands-on program designed to help technical founders move from promising technology toward companies with customers, partners, and investors that they can believe in,” Edmonton Unlimited CEO Tom Viinikka said.
The context: The program’s first cohort of eight to 12 founders will launch in early 2027, with participating founders working through six core areas: problem and technology calibration; customer pain and market demand; technical milestones and decision criteria; IP strategy and freedom to operate; go-to-market and pilot conversion; and capital strategy and funding narrative.
Organizers said they are targeting science- and engineering-driven companies that have shown early momentum but continue to experience commercialization questions. The first iteration of the program will include areas of focus like AI, energy, health, robotics, industrial innovation, and advanced materials. According to its website, the program is looking for companies to participate that are “moving beyond the pure idea or early research” with a working prototype or minimal viable product.
Final thought: Edmonton Unlimited’s decision to focus new programming specifically on deep tech reflects the growth of, and interest in, Edmonton’s deep tech ecosystem. The city boasts a strong post-secondary research and development ecosystem, a robust talent pool of technical workers, and a level of affordability that breakout companies like Zero Point Cryogenics have praised as key to its decision to build there. Despite those benefits, deep tech startups still face distinct challenges around commercialization that are characterized by longer development cycles and higher capital requirements. Programs like this aim to remedy that and help cement the sector as a primary component of Edmonton’s broader tech scene.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.
Feature image courtesy Jesse Cole for BetaKit.

articles.title: Spotify acaba de mejorar muchísimo en España: Amazon se va a enfadar
articles.text:
Amazon no está muy contenta con el nuevo movimiento de Spotify en España. La app de música en streaming acaba de lanzar una de las novedades más esperadas del año para quienes pagan alguna de las suscripciones premium: los audiolibros. A partir de este momento, en España ya se puede acceder a esta función que lleva un tiempo disponible en países como Estados Unidos y buena parte de Latinoamérica, permitiendo acceder a más de 350.000 libros a nivel internacional y unos 45.000 títulos en español.
¿Qué es un audiolibro? Pues, como su propio nombre indica, un libro que no es necesario leer: la app integra el título original y te lo dicta como si estuvieses escuchando un podcast o cualquier historia narrada en audio. Es un complemento que compañías como Amazon llevan explotando bastante tiempo y que se ha puesto muy de moda para poder "leer" entregas en cualquier parte sin tener que llevar un libro electrónico a cuestas o el propio ejemplar en formato físico. Todo desde el móvil.
Spotify, además, colabora con más de 300 editoriales de todo el mundo, entre las que se incluyen Planeta o Mondadori, por lo que la implementación de estos audiolibros es perfecta y está pensada para narrar la historia de la forma más natural posible. No es una IA que lee documentos de forma robótica: hay mucho más trabajo detrás para que la experiencia sea similar a la de otras compañías.
Otra de las ventajas es que la función lleva meses puliéndose en otros idiomas, por lo que la plataforma ya está perfectamente adaptada, ha corregido los errores iniciales y ahora que ha activado el formato en España está lista para disfrutarla sin problemas ni fallos.
Hasta ahora, algunos usuarios estaban aprovechando la función de podcast de Spotify para subir audios leyendo algunos de los libros más populares, pero esto ya no será necesario con la nueva opción de audiolibros.
¿Cuánto cuestan los audiolibros de Spotify?
Nada. Spotify ya permite en España explorar la categoría de audiolibros y comenzar a escucharlos de forma gratuita. Cualquiera de los disponibles. Ahora bien, solo durante 12 horas al mes. Si quieres extender este tiempo, la compañía ha lanzado Audiolibros+, una suscripción adicional al plan que ya tienes contratado.
Cuesta 8,99 euros al mes y permite extender la escucha durante 15 horas más. Es decir, un total de 27 horas al mes. Si este tiempo se te queda corto, puedes ampliarlo aún más comprando paquetes de horas adicionales cuando quieras. Y no, las horas que no utilizas caducan y no se pueden acumular para utilizarlas los meses siguientes.
Por último, Spotify también ha incluido una función sumamente interesante en esta categoría. Se llama 'Encuentra la página', y permite escanear una página de un libro físico con la cámara del móvil para encontrar su homólogo en audiolibro. De esta forma, puedes alternar entre la lectura tradicional y la escucha cuando vas en el metro y no quieres marearte.
La función debería aparecer en tu app de Spotify durante los próximos días si resides en España, aunque es posible que debas actualizar la app desde la Play Store o la App Store.

articles.title: Weniger Lohn für weibliche Chatbots? Was eine Studie über Vorurteile gegenüber KI verrät
articles.text:
Weniger Lohn für weibliche Chatbots? Was eine Studie über Vorurteile gegenüber KI verrät
Der Gender Pay Gap betrifft nicht nur Frauen, die wegen Teilzeitarbeit oder schlechter bezahlter Berufe am Monatsende weniger auf dem Konto haben als Männer. Laut einer neuen Studie zeigt sich dasselbe Prinzip auch bei der Vergütung von KI-Modellen. Geschlechterstereotype können demnach dazu führen, dass auch Chatbots und KI-Assistenten, die als weiblich wahrgenommen werden, weniger Geld erhalten. Entscheidend sei dabei nicht, was ein KI-System tatsächlich leistet. Was bedeuten diese Erkenntnisse für den Einsatz von KI-Agenten im Unternehmenskontext?
Gender Pay Gap macht auch vor KI nicht Halt
Der Gender Pay Gap gilt als zentraler Indikator für die Verdienstungleichheit zwischen Frauen und Männern und beschreibt die Differenz des durchschnittlichen Stundenlohnes. Trotz einiger Verbesserungen gehen die Einkommen weiterhin auseinander: Laut Statistischem Bundesamt liegt der bereinigte Unterschied aktuell bei sechs Prozent. Der Gender-Gap-Arbeitsmarkt zeigt allerdings, dass die Ungleichheit in der Praxis deutlich höher ausfallen kann. Er berücksichtigt neben der Lohnlücke auch Unterschiede in der bezahlten Arbeitszeit und in der Erwerbstätigenquote und erweitert so die Perspektive auf die Verdienstsituation von Frauen und Männern. Hier klafft die Lücke zwischen den Geschlechtern noch um 37 Prozent auseinander.
Eine neue Studie der University of Limerick, die in Zusammenarbeit mit der Universität Zürich und der SKEMA Business School durchgeführt wurde, hat jetzt herausgefunden, dass sich die ungleiche Bezahlung nicht auf Menschen beschränkt. In einer Zeit, in der Chatbots und KI-Assistenten zunehmend als digitale Kolleg:innen fungieren, haben die Forscher:innen untersucht, wie die Darstellung der Systeme als weiblich oder männlich die Wahrnehmung beeinflusst. Insgesamt nahmen 189 Testpersonen an der Studie teil und erledigten arbeitsbezogene Aufgaben mit verschiedenen KI-Assistenten. Das Ergebnis: Der weiblich präsentierte Assistent wurde als weniger menschlich wahrgenommen und geringer vergütet als sein männliches Gegenstück.
Weibliche KI-Systeme wurden niedriger entlohnt
In der Studie kamen KI-Systeme in vier verschiedenen Varianten zum Einsatz. Neben einem textbasierten Chatbot und einem Schreibtischroboter gab es zwei menschenähnliche virtuelle Agenten, die entweder männlich oder weiblich präsentiert wurden. Nach Abschluss der Aufgaben entlohnte jede Testperson ihre KI mit echtem Geld. Sie teilten dazu einen festen Betrag zwischen sich und dem Assistenten auf. So bildeten die Forscher:innen eine reale Transaktion nach und untersuchten, wie viel die Menschen der KI für ihre Arbeit zahlen wollten. Da die Assistenten technisch gleich leistungsfähig waren, standen bei der Studie allein Gestaltung und persönliche Wahrnehmung im Mittelpunkt.
„Das Bemerkenswerte an unseren Ergebnissen ist, dass die Technologie hinter diesen KI-Agenten genau dieselbe war, die Menschen sie allerdings nicht auf dieselbe Weise behandelten“, sagte Co-Autorin Mary Hausfeld gegenüber der wissenschaftlichen Presseplattform Eurekalert. „Wir halten KI oft für neutral, aber die Art und Weise, wie wir diese Systeme gestalten und präsentieren, kann genau jene Annahmen und Vorurteile aktivieren, die auch in unseren Interaktionen mit anderen Menschen bestehen.“ Dieser Aspekt verdiene mehr Beachtung, da immer mehr KI-Agenten am Arbeitsplatz zum Einsatz kommen. „Wir wollen nicht versehentlich bestehende Ungleichheiten in einem neuen technologischen Umfeld reproduzieren“, so die Forscherin.
Die Ungleichbehandlung passiert unbewusst
Viele Teilnehmer:innen hätten angegeben, dass ihnen das Geschlecht des Assistenten egal sei. Ihre Bewertungen und Belohnungsentscheidungen zeigten allerdings, dass die unterschiedlichen Designmerkmale ihr Verhalten messbar beeinflussten. Hausfeld argumentiert, das Aussehen und die Darstellung von KI-Agenten seien daher nicht bloß ästhetische Designentscheidungen. Sie sagt: „Solche Entscheidungen können beeinflussen, wie sehr Menschen der KI vertrauen, wie sie deren Beitrag bewerten und sogar, wie sie sie finanziell belohnen.“

articles.title: SpaceX alumni nab $100M to rethink shipping with autonomous freight trains | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The railroad industry was one of the first to disrupt how the world worked with technology, but lately, innovation in freight railroading has amounted to little more than longer and longer trains.
That has led many railroads to abandon shorter routes, ceding a chunk of the $1 trillion surface freight market to trucking companies. But as diesel prices reach record highs, some of those very trucking companies are going bust, leaving a hole in the market. Recently, at least 16 trucking companies went bankrupt over only a few weeks.
Parallel Systems might have a way to keep freight moving while allowing railroads to recapture market share. The startup has developed a rail vehicle capable of moving over several tons of freight as far as 500 miles without an operator. If the company can scale production of its Panther vehicles, it stands to make railroads profitable over short hauls once again.
“Less than 500 miles is hard for railroads to do competitively,” Matt Soule, co-founder and CEO of Parallel Systems, told TechCrunch. “Our technology allows them to take some of that trucking, and it’s for the public’s benefit.”
Because it runs on railroads, Parallel’s vehicle doesn’t contribute to traffic congestion, and because it’s battery powered, it doesn’t pollute. To scale manufacturing of its third-generation vehicle and speed the commercial rollout, Parallel Systems has raised a $100 million Series C led by AVP, with participation from Hillspire, Agility Global, Cobalt Capital, Anthos Capital, Congruent Ventures, Riot Ventures, and Collaborative Fund.
Soule and his co-founders started Parallel Systems in 2020 after years at SpaceX, where they designed rocket avionics systems.
Parallel’s vehicles can travel either independently or in platoons, which tend to be shorter than typical trains. It’s an approach that bucks the prevailing strategy used by railroads, known as precision railroading: As the railroad industry has matured, investor pressure has driven companies to build longer trains and operate them on fixed schedules, which helps spread some costs like labor across more freight.
As railroads have pulled back from smaller routes, trucking companies have stepped in. Today, some 60% of freight trips in the U.S. are under 500 miles, and trucking companies handle a majority of those.
But more trucks on the road means more congestion, and nowhere is that more apparent than at ports. “If you ever go to the Port of Savannah, you see the truck lines coming in and out of the port — it’s insanity,” Soule said.
Unlike traditional train cars, Parallel’s vehicles don’t have couplers, instead forming uncoupled platoons that move down the rails. The coupler-free design means that, once a platoon reaches a train yard, the vehicles can split up without needing human intervention. And after the Panther is cleared to operate on a section of track, its sensors monitor the rails to ensure the track ahead is clear of obstacles.
Trucking companies have been intrigued by Parallel, despite the fact that the startup is claiming part of a business they currently own. Drayage companies, which move freight short distances, make money for each load they deliver, but they don’t get to charge more when a truck gets stuck in a traffic jam, even at a port where such congestion is common. By moving freight closer to a customer’s door, Parallel allows trucking companies to make more deliveries per day. “They want certainty, they want to be able to move,” Soule said.
Parallel obtained approval a year and a half ago from the Federal Railroad Administration to operate near the Port of Savannah in Georgia, where it has been operating on 160 miles of track to prove the safety of its system.
“We’ve been verifying all the safety controls and operating practices that are best evaluated in a real-world setting with a path toward our first commercial payload coming up very soon,” Soule said.

articles.title: Thermal Complexity Grows With AI Chips And Photonics
articles.text:
Increasing power density makes heat, stress, and aging harder to predict, and more critical to address earlier in the design flow.
Key Takeaways:
Experts at the Table: Semiconductor Engineering sat down to discuss the impact of heat on photonics, transient behavior, and system reliability, with Lang Lin, director of product management at Synopsys; Jack Berg, vice president of business development at Silvaco; Satish Radhakrishnan, head of semiconductor and electronics at Vinci; Chris Mueth, director of new markets management at Keysight EDA; and John Ferguson, senior director of product management at Siemens EDA. What follows are excerpts of that conversation, which was held behind closed doors at the recent Design Automation Conference. This is the second of a three-part series. Part one is here.
L-R: Silvaco’s Berg; Synopsys’ Lin; Vinci’s Radhakrishnan; Keysight’s Mueth; Siemens’ Ferguson.
SE: Moving data takes power, which generates heat. So how do we keep data moving while still remaining within the power budget? Is the solution photonics? Even there, heat can cause issues.
Mueth: Photonics has a lot of promise for reducing data center bottlenecks, but it can’t be scaled right now. Building a large mesh switch requires many components, and you have high losses. So you have to revisit the whole architecture for how things are done in photonics and do them differently, probably in a modular style that’s scalable. Another issue is heat sensitivity. You have to stabilize that. But even then, your photonic structure is going to have heaters in it because these have to be controlled. And if you have a large mesh switch, the amount of control you need is significant. So how do you calibrate your structures through that chip to get enough performance when you may have thousands of heaters that you have to control? If we can solve that problem, it will open things up a bit. But that still doesn’t get rid of the losses in the |photonics chips. That has to be solved with a modular, scalable architecture.
SE: This leads to another issue, which is that you’re no longer dealing with just one type of processing element. What happens when you go from a GPU to a CPU? Do they both generate the same amount of heat? And is that, in turn, different when you have a high-intensity workload that’s short-lived? How do you cool everything down to keep temperatures consistent?
Radhakrishnan: Co-packaged optics is trying to solve that problem, to some extent, bringing the silicon photonics into the package, keeping it small for EICs/PICs. They are trying to thermally isolate it. But if you try to simulate the whole thing, the part that will be missing is the transient nature, and that’s what’s really needed. If you try to keep something far off, then the heat is going to take more time to get there, and by the time the next wave comes on an ASIC, the heat will still be there. Even a very small change in temperature can shift the ring oscillator. What’s needed is the ability to simulate the whole thing together in a transient domain to make sure it’s going to function reliably and optically. Being able to simulate one part of a system in a transient domain is key to making sure co-packaged optics is viable and that we can push it forward.
Mueth: That’s a good point. The difference in time constants really messes things up. And if you’re doing co-packaged optics, the EIC driver typically would be mounted near or on top of your PIC, so you have heat pollution, which steers your photonics. You’re introducing new stresses, and those stresses have a very big impact on the optical signals — maybe bigger than thermal. You have to know what those trade-offs are, and make sure you’re taking them into consideration so that you’re combining the best of both. Just by moving something, you can make things worse instead of better.
SE: And how do you know your thermal sensors are functioning properly all the time?
Mueth: You can do that in the calibration process. You can put a sniffing loop inside the photonic PIC, but it makes that incredibly complicated.
Ferguson: We can try to move things to reduce some of the thermal that’s built up. But when you’re moving big elements, particularly like what we have in photonics, you’re introducing new stresses. Those have a very big impact on optical signals — maybe bigger than the thermal. So you have to know what those trade-offs are and make sure you’re taking them into consideration so that you’re combining the best of both.
Lin: For silicon photonics, you can think about it as a type of analog circuit. When we deal with analog versus digital, the thermal behavior is very different. Digital transistors involve switching current. The current will supply the transistor’s on and off, so the Joule heating effect is not that bad. But for silicon photonics and analog devices, the DC current is always there, and there’s a big swing of signals. That creates current flowing through the interconnects, like a waveguide. It generates a lot of heat, and we need this heat for the CPO to work. That heat is needed to operate the EIC. But what if there are so many heaters together? How do you place them far enough away so that everything can operate, but not create hot spots within the heater area? Stress is another problem that has to be considered for silicon photonics to operate well.
SE: Heat can cause warpage. If you put two warped chips together and they’re very thin, you may be able to flatten them, but at the same time you’ve probably lost some ability to dissipate heat due to thinner dies, right?
Berg: Thermal variation on a PIC chip generally results in a mismatch of features — much more so than in EIC circuits. If you’re talking about multi-physics and digital twins and surrogate models affiliated with EICs, you essentially can triple that need in photonics ICs because they’re much more sensitive to warpage and thermal gradients. A laser is a heat source that potentially creates a reliability problem. To that end, photonics needs a thermal understanding and a multi-physics confirmation of not only the electrical, mechanical, and thermal, but optical as well. So now you’ve got four solvers that you potentially have to do. It’s a bit more complicated than the electronics, and that’s the reason why photonics has been the next big thing in the semiconductor world for the past 30 years. It’s much more complicated from a physics perspective than anybody thought it would be.
Mueth: Traditionally we were worried about thermal in semiconductors. We ignored the passives. Now, with photonics, you have thermal effects on the passives.
SE: Within a chip you may have multiple dies, because you cannot get the performance you need out of a single die, especially in AI data centers. How do we coordinate the different dies within a package so you aren’t just running everything flat-out all the time?
Berg: You need to be very careful.
SE: This is a complex orchestration problem, right? And it needs to be hierarchical.
Mueth: Yes, and when you’re doing the architecture, you’re going to have to model your thermals. One of the corners would be, ‘What are your high-performance use cases?’ You have to model those thermally, electrically, and mechanically, so when you are farther down the design path you have a higher chance of success. But that modeling has to be done up front.
Ferguson: You can do each of those standalone variables, but then you’re not getting the full story. You have to do them all consecutively, which means that what you’re doing is running each one many, many times, one after another, until you get to a steady state. And then you hope that is the correct steady state. That depends on what you’re building.
Radhakrishnan: If you look at the direction AI chips are going, they’re trying to get from training to inference. They are trying to increase the bandwidth. That’s what is driving all the chips to be stacked on top of each other, and that affects their behavior. They want to understand the inference behavior. But it’s not just about peak performance. How much higher is the temperature going to be in transient? If I have much more headroom, because it’s only going to last for a nanosecond, maybe I can go to extra power. But is that nanosecond going to come every millisecond or microsecond? How often am I going to allow peak power? And how much of the thermal budget can I push and let the data center people create a design rule that says, ‘For inference, I can allow a millisecond pulse every 100 milliseconds.’ This is a huge new paradigm that people can exploit when they go to different use cases. It’s all driven by what the end user wants and how they want to achieve the maximum performance they need.
Lin: Going back to the question about hierarchical models, those are important not only to deal with the capacity to simulate thermal for an AI chip, but also to enable an ecosystem with different vendors providing their model hierarchically. For example, HBM vendors have to provide some kind of model for an HBM chip. Then they send that to a system integration house, which will combine different models, build a whole multi-die stack, and run thermal. First, they need to consider the impact of the vendor’s model on thermal. Second, they need to finalize the whole system. They’re the final product delivery hub. They have to make sure all the models are connected, assembled, and then simulate the whole system. So the hierarchical model is a must, and not only for capacity. The industry is working on this. We need the ecosystem to deliver a model, and we have to agree on standards so that everybody can share their models and the integrators can assemble them.
SE: One of the big concerns in data centers is aging of data paths due to electromigration, which is accelerated by heat. How does that impact the overall design process?
Radhakrishnan: I’m seeing a lot of thermal sensors being embedded into the die for aging. Those have to be on-chip to determine degradation over time. Then, you can throttle parts of the chip. But everything is packaged up, so it has to be done by software getting some sensing information back, and then you see what changes you can make. This is even more of an issue with automotive, where chips have to last 10 to 15 years. That’s where you need to do simulation to determine if you’re putting the sensors in the right location. Can I get the right sensing back so a chip can function over time as things change? You need to be able to capture all that, and this is the direction companies are heading.
SE: This can vary by ambient temperature, right?
Berg: Yes, particularly places like Saudi Arabia. The simple rule of thumb is the Arrhenius equation. Every 10 degrees results in a substantial reduction in reliability. This is really important to get right.
Lin: But I don’t see a lot of tools in the industry for accurately predicting thermally induced aging. There’s a gap. We need tools to pair the correct equation so we can predict aging effects, and how to resolve them. Sensors are a way to monitor the aging effects, but what’s happening on the design optimization side? No one has done that for aging-aware design optimization.
Radhakrishnan: It’s an under-design/over-design kind of problem. That’s why, ideally, it has to be dynamic over time. And that is a huge problem.

articles.title: Edtech firm byteXL raises $9M as investors back college-linked AI skilling model
articles.text:
Edtech firm byteXL raises $9M as investors back college-linked AI skilling model
Hyderabad-based byteXL said the fresh capital will help expand its college network, strengthen AI-led learning tools, and reach 500,000 engineering students across 15 states.
Edtech company byteXL has raised $9 million in its latest funding round, led by Elevar Equity, an impact investor, with participation from existing investors Kalaari Capital, an early-stage VC, and The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation, a philanthropic foundation.
The Hyderabad-based startup’s latest round follows a $5.9 million Series A raised in July 2024.
byteXL, founded by brothers Karun and Sricharan Tadepalli, works with engineering colleges, particularly in Tier II and Tier III cities, to bring industry-oriented technology and artificial intelligence learning into students’ regular degree programmes.
Its business-to-business model (B2B) works through institutions instead of selling courses directly to individual learners. The company combines curriculum, practical projects, technology platforms and trained educators with existing college programmes.
byteXL claims that 7,600 of its graduates were placed in IT and engineering roles last year.
The new capital is intended to expand byteXL’s institutional network, strengthen its technology and AI capabilities, increase academic and delivery capacity and develop new industry-aligned programmes.
The company plans to increase its presence from 40 institutions to 120 over the next two years, while expanding its reach from about 200,000 students to 500,000 across 15 states. Planned product investments include AI-enabled learning and assessment, student analytics and personalised learning tools.
CEO Karun Tadepalli said the next phase will focus on “expanding our institutional footprint” and deepening its technology and AI capabilities.
For byteXL, the proposition is less about adding another online course and more about embedding employability-focused training inside the four-year engineering journey.
Kalaari partner Sampath P said this allows byteXL to work within the existing college ecosystem and not “re-invent the wheel,” while noting the company’s growth and ability to reach profitability.
The funding comes as the country’s edtech market becomes more selective. Tracxn data showed sector equity funding at $214 million in the first eight months of 2026, down sharply from the 2021 peak, even as median round sizes increased.
Yet capital is still reaching differentiated AI and education businesses. Arivihan raised $10 million from Accel and Prosus in September to expand its AI tutoring platform, while ProLearn raised Rs 30 crore in June for an AI-focused learning platform.
The policy environment is also moving towards AI and employment-linked learning, with the government’s Skill India Digital Hub bringing training, assessment, certification and employment services onto one platform, while its SOAR programme has expanded from foundational AI courses to 50 AI-related qualifications.
Separately, SWAYAM Plus is expanding industry-aligned, credit-eligible learning through higher education.
For companies like byteXL, the opportunity is increasingly tied to whether they can sustainably turn this emphasis on AI skills into measurable learning and employment outcomes.
Elevate Education, a Gurugram-based higher education platform formerly known as Sunstone, which also operates in a similar space, secured Rs 170 crore in funding in July, highlighting investor interest in the segment.
(Disclaimer: Kalaari Capital is an investor in YourStory.)
Edited by Megha Reddy

articles.title: 129 000 failles débusquées : Anthropic dévoile le bilan impressionnant de Claude Mythos
articles.text:
Claude Mythos tient ses promesses. Ce mardi 6 octobre, Anthropic a donc annoncé l’élargissement de son Cyber Verification Program, le programme qui ouvre ses IA les plus puissantes à des spécialistes de la cybersécurité. Davantage d’entités pourront désormais se servir de Claude Mythos pour chercher des vulnérabilités dans du code informatique. Lors de la sortie de Mythos en avril dernier, Anthropic avait choisi de réserver l’IA à une poignée de partenaires triés sur le volet, dans le cadre d’une initiative baptisée Project Glasswing. Cette approche prudente devait éviter que des individus malveillants exploitent l’IA générative pour mener des cyberattaques.
 We’re expanding our Cyber Verification Program to give security professionals broader access to our most capable models.
Through this program, verified security professionals can access Claude Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, and Sonnet 5.5 with safeguards designed for defensive work.
We’re also opening up new tiers to allow for authorized offensive work, like penetration testing and red-teaming.
https://t.co/blaJtvxhJh
— Anthropic (@AnthropicAI) October 6, 2026
À lire aussi : Claude a trouvé 2 failles dans des algorithmes jugés indestructibles, c’est une première… et ça change tout
Plus de 130 000 failles
Six mois plus tard, il s’avère que Claude Mythos a nettement tenu ses promesses. Selon Anthropic, les partenaires de Project Glasswing ont identifié au moins 129 000 vulnérabilités logicielles vérifiées entre avril et juillet 2026. Les analyses de logiciels open source, menées par Anthropic, ont ajouté 5 500 failles entre avril et octobre. En mai, un mois après le déploiement, Anthropic ne revendiquait encore que 10 000 failles débusquées par son IA. Plus de 33 000 de ces failles sont classées « critiques » ou considérées de gravité « élevées ».
Anthropic juge que ce premier bilan est très prudent. Il repose en effet sur un sondage mené auprès d’une partie seulement des partenaires de Glasswing. De facto, il est probable que davantage de failles aient été repérées sur la période. L’entreprise estime que le nombre de défaillances est « au moins cinq fois » supérieur. Plusieurs des partenaires d’Antropic affirment que Mythos a accéléré la chasse aux failles de plusieurs mois, voire de plusieurs années. Ces derniers mois, Claude a notamment déniché une faille de sécurité vieille de près de 30 ans.
À lire aussi : 16 millions d’ordinateurs touchés – Claude lève le voile sur une faille Linux vieille de 9 ans
Trois niveaux d’accès à Claude Mythos
Fort du succès de Mythos, Anthropic ouvre un peu plus les vannes. Le nouveau Cyber Verification Program fusionne en effet deux dispositifs lancés il y a six mois, dont Glasswing et le premier Cyber Verification Program. Désormais, trois niveaux d’accès vont être mis en place. Tous les niveaux disposent d’un accès à Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 et Mythos 5.1.
Baptisé Defense, le premier niveau couvre l’analyse de malwares, la réponse aux incidents et la validation de failles. Il est ouvert aux équipes de sécurité, aux opérateurs d’infrastructures critiques, comme les hôpitaux régionaux ou les services municipaux, aux mainteneurs de projets open source et aux chercheurs ayant déjà signalé des failles par le passé.
Le niveau Red Team ajoute des tests d’intrusion, à savoir des simulations destinées à tester les défenses d’un système. Il est réservé aux organisations. Enfin, le niveau Specialized se distingue par des restrictions plus souples. Ce niveau est réservé à un petit groupe d’organisations qui sont autorisées à tester des systèmes critiques, comme les réseaux électriques, les systèmes d’aviation, les télécoms ou les virements interbancaires. Chaque membre fait l’objet d’un examen par le gouvernement américain.
Ce n’est pas tout. Les organisations inscrites au Cyber Verification Program doivent accepter que leurs données sont conservées par Anthropic. La start-up américaine veut pouvoir piocher dans les données pour détecter d’éventuels usages malveillants. Pour rassurer ses partenaires, Anthropic va déployer une solution intitulée Enterprise Frontier Safeguards dans le courant de l’automne, qui permettra aux clients de stocker leurs données sur une infrastructure sous leur contrôle.
« La cybersécurité est par nature à double usage : les mêmes outils qui permettent à une équipe de sécurité de détecter et de corriger une vulnérabilité peuvent également servir à un acteur malveillant pour l’exploiter », fait valoir Anthropic pour justifier ses précautions.

articles.title: Beyond the Chatbot: The AI Technologies Quietly Reshaping How Machines Think - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Chatbots may be the most visible face of AI, but the truth is that they are only the ‘front door’. Sure, when you ask a tool to write an email, explain a topic or brainstorm ideas, it can feel like the whole AI story is just about having a clever conversation.
But in reality, bigger changes are happening behind your screen. Today’s AI systems are starting to recognise images, understand speech, work with documents, use software tools, and complete multi-step tasks. They’re moving from simply replying to prompts towards helping us plan, decide and act.
No need for alarm: this doesn’t mean machines are suddenly thinking like humans. They’re not. But it does mean the software you use at work, at home and online is becoming more capable, connected and useful. The shift is from AI that talks to an AI that helps you get things done.
Machine Learning Is Getting Smarter, Faster, and More Adaptable
At the heart of the shift is machine learning, the process that helps software spot patterns in data. Instead of being given a rigid list of rules for every situation, though, a machine learning model learns from examples. Show it enough invoice pictures, for example, and it can begin to identify totals, dates, and supplier details.
This is why AI is becoming more flexible. Older software usually followed a fixed path: if this happens, do that.
Modern AI models, on the other hand, can work with text, images, audio, video and computer code. This is known as ‘multimodal AI’, meaning a system doesn’t have to treat every type of information as a separate problem.
Multimodal AI takes things further by combining different kinds of information. You might upload a photo of a broken part, describe the problem in plain English and receive troubleshooting steps. Or a system could review a sales call, read the follow-up notes and suggest the next action. They find connections that would take a person much longer to uncover.
Generative AI has also pushed this capability into everyday life. These systems can create text, images, code, music and other content by predicting what should come next based on patterns learned from huge amounts of material.
For people looking to build practical skills in this fast-moving area, a Graduate Certificate in Artificial Intelligence online can offer a useful way to understand both the technology and its real-world applications.
AI Agents, Automation and Algorithms Are Changing What Software Can Actually Do
The next big change? It begins when AI offers advice.
An AI agent is a system designed to work towards a goal by breaking it into smaller steps. Instead of only answering, “How should this report be prepared?”, it helps gather data, sort information, create a draft and flag anything that needs human approval.
This is called an agentic workflow. The AI is not left entirely on its own, and it shouldn’t be. Instead, it works through a guided process with built-in limits, instructions, and checkpoints.
A useful agent might be able to:
- Search an internal knowledge base.
- Read and summarise customer feedback.
- Update a project board.
- Prepare a meeting brief.
- Send a draft response for approval.
Yes, algorithms still matter. They’re the behind-the-scenes decision systems that rank, recommend, match and predict. From routing deliveries to filtering spam, algorithms quietly shape countless digital experiences.
But tool use is what turns an AI model into something entirely more practical. When an AI can safely connect with calendars, databases, spreadsheets, email platforms or customer systems, it can move information between tools and support real work.
Why Understanding AI’s Foundations Matters in the Next Tech Cycle
With AI, the temptation is to focus on the latest product. A new chatbot appears, a new model launches, and everyone starts talking about what it can do.
You don’t need to become a machine-learning engineer. But it does help to understand a few basic ideas:
- Models learn patterns from data and use those patterns to produce outputs.
- Algorithms provide methods for processing information and solving problems.
- AI agents can combine models, tools and instructions to complete multi-step tasks.
- Automation allows software to perform processes with less manual intervention.
- Multimodal systems can work across different forms of information, such as text, images and audio.
These concepts make it easier to understand what AI can and cannot do. It’s important to recognise that a system may produce an impressive answer while still making basic mistakes. It may also complete one complicated task successfully, but struggle with another.
The future of AI is not limited to a chat window.
Behind today’s conversational tools sits a growing mix of machine learning, multimodal models, algorithms, automation and agents that can support more complex work.
The change will be gradual, not magic. Still, it will reshape how software operates and how people spend their time. Understanding the basics now puts you in a stronger position to use AI wisely.

articles.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 met tout le monde d'accord avec son nouveau trailer
articles.text:
L’attente touche enfin à sa fin pour les fans de l’univers de CD Projekt Red : l’annonce du retour de la série animée Cyberpunk: Edgerunners pour une saison 2 vient d’allumer une véritable poudrière au sein de la communauté.
Après le choc émotionnel et le succès retentissant de la première saison, chaque seconde de la bande-annonce de Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Saison 2, qui vient d’être publiée ce 7 octobre par Netflix sur YouTube, est disséquée avec une précision d’orfèvre.
L’objectif d’un enfant comme miroir de Night City dans Cyberpunk: Edgerunners saison 2
La véritable surprise de cette séquence de Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Saison 2 tient au choix de sa mise en scène. Plutôt que d’adopter une caméra omnisciente, la vidéo épouse le point de vue d’un jeune garçon armé de sa propre caméra, filmant la violence ordinaire de la rue.
Ce parti pris visuel, qui filtre l’animation à travers le grain rétro des bandes VHS des années 80 et 90, rappelle immédiatement les grandes heures d’animes cultes comme Ghost in the Shell. Mais au-delà de l’hommage esthétique, ce cadrage intrigue et inquiète. Les spectateurs n’ont pas tardé à s’interroger sur le sort réservé à cet enfant. Beaucoup y voient déjà le catalyseur d’un traumatisme majeur qui guidera l’intrigue des dix nouveaux épisodes de Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Saison 2. Tout le monde est totuefois d’accord sur le fait que cette suite devrait être pleine d’émotions.
La précision du lore et l’angoisse des fans
Pour les habitués du jeu vidéo Cyberpunk 2077, l’extrait regorge également de clins d’œil techniques qui témoignent du soin apporté par le Studio Trigger. Du design extrême des prothèses cybernétiques du personnage de Talia, arborant le fameux cyberware « Vampyres » jusqu’au bruitage très reconnaissable des implants de double saut, la bande-son et le visuel s’alignent parfaitement avec l’univers établi.
Pourtant, sous les éloges concernant la direction artistique, c’est surtout la prudence qui domine les échanges. Échaudés par le destin tragique de David Martinez dans la première partie, les fans refusent de trop s’attacher à cette nouvelle distribution composée de King, Roman ou Talia. L’ambiance mélancolique du teaser confirme que cette suite ne fera aucun cadeau à ses protagonistes, poussant déjà les spectateurs à se préparer au pire avant le grand lancement de Cyberpunk: Edgerunners saison 2 sur Netflix le 20 octobre 2026.

articles.title: Un géant est né : Paramount boucle sa fusion avec Warner, et beaucoup de choses vont changer
articles.text:
C’est fait : Paramount a finalisé le rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery, pour 110 milliards de dollars. De Harry Potter à CNN, David Ellison dirige désormais un empire rebaptisé Skydance.
Le feuilleton aura duré presque un an. Car initialement, c’est bien Netflix qui convoitait Warner Bros. Discovery, mais Paramount Skydance a rapidement surenchéri et a fini par l'emporter. Mais il fallait encore convaincre les autorités, alors que 12 États américains, menés par la Californie, ont tenté de bloquer l’opération devant la justice. Les deux parties ont finalement conclu un accord à l'amiable, ouvrant la voie à la création d’un nouveau géant des médias.
HBO Max et Paramount+ vont fusionner
Le nouveau groupe, coté depuis ce 6 octobre à la Bourse de New York, réunit deux grands studios, deux plateformes de streaming (Paramount+ et HBO Max), CBS, HBO, ainsi que deux chaînes d’information, CBS News et CNN. Il dispose aussi d’actifs dans le sport avec CBS Sports et TNT Sports.
C’est simple, Skydance revendique « le plus important volume de sorties en salles du secteur « et plus de 200 millions d’abonnés. David Ellison, P-D.G du géant, a salué « un jour historique, non seulement pour Skydance, mais pour toute notre industrie ».
Et il va évidemment falloir s’attendre à du changement. Si Skydance assure que rien ne va changer côté média, les deux plateformes de streaming, elles, sont appelées à être unifiés « en un seul service au fil du temps », précise le communiqué. De même, la direction prévient que l’intégration entraînera forcément « des décisions difficiles » qui toucheront, entre autres, les effectifs.
- moodRemboursement sous 30 jours
- devices2 connexions simultanées
- live_tvQualité vidéo : Full HD
- downloadLecture hors ligne disponible
- escalator_warningEspace enfant disponible
Les réticences persistent malgré les engagements de Skydance
Skydance a multiplié les promesses pour obtenir ce feu vert. Le groupe s’engage à sortir » au moins 30 films par an en salles », chacun avec « une fenêtre d’exclusivité minimale de 45 jours ». Il promet aussi plus de 180 séries et un soutien aux producteurs indépendants. Ellison aurait en plus accepté de consacrer 1,5 milliard de dollars supplémentaires au cinéma sur cinq ans.
Le groupe garantit en outre la mise en place d’un « conseil d’indépendance éditoriale » pour CBS News et CNN, bien que ses membres soient choisis par Skydance. Le patron, lui, s’engage à ne pas intervenir dans la couverture des chaînes d’information phares. Car on le rappelle, la proximité d’Ellison avec Donald Trump a nourri de nombreuses critiques, tout comme l’arrivée au capital des fonds souverains saoudien, émirati et qatari.
Dans ce contexte, ces gages n’ont pas dissipé tous les doutes. Des associations de défense de la liberté d’expression jugent ces efforts insuffisants, tandis que des centaines de professionnels à Hollywood redoutent une concentration du pouvoir et des pertes d’emplois.

articles.title: ASOS Confirms Cyberattack, Data Breach
articles.text:
British online retailer ASOS has confirmed that hackers compromised a third-party communication platform after users received rogue notifications on their phones.
Over the past couple of days, numerous ASOS users in the UK complained about receiving a pop-up notification on their mobile apps, titled “ASOS hacked”.
“Dear ASOS DPO [data protection officer] and IT, we have fully compromised the Snowflake instance. Engage with us, or we will leak it,” the notification read.
In a Tuesday filing with the London Stock Exchange, the clothing and cosmetics retailer confirmed that its users received unauthorized notifications after a third-party platform used for customer communication was hacked.
“We took immediate action to restrict access to the notification platforms and are working with our internal and external specialist advisers, as well as all relevant authorities,” ASOS said.
According to the company, the hackers might have accessed basic user information, including names and contact details.
“We do not believe that payment-card information or account passwords were impacted,” the company said.
ASOS pointed out that its website and application have not been affected, and that its operations have not been disrupted.
The company has not shared details on which platform was compromised and who was behind it, and made no mention of its Snowflake instance being hacked.
“Snowflake is a data analysis and AI platform used by several organizations. In 2024, ShinyHunters hacked Snowflake instances of over 160 organizations and stole sensitive data that was used for extortion. They used credentials obtained from infostealers for initial access. This recent hack may be similar, although it is not confirmed what the initial access was,” said Forescout Research – Vedere Labs VP of research Daniel dos Santos.
The incident was claimed by a hacking group calling itself Xuanye Group, on a newly created Telegram channel. The name points to a Chinese-speaking threat actor, but could also be a false flag, dos Santos said.
“If the attackers have successfully compromised ASOS via a Snowflake vulnerability, hopefully this will be investigated as a priority to understand whether this could impact further organizations utilizing the online data platform,” Talion Cyber Security head of threat intelligence Natalie Page said.
“Directly messaging customers via the ASOS app is an interesting move which highlights that the attackers want to gain publicity around the breach. This is a typical tactic of extortion groups, who often leverage media attention and publicity to apply further pressure to victim organizations,” Page added.

articles.title: Musician sent to prison for $10 million streaming fraud using AI bots
articles.text:
A North Carolina musician was sentenced to 18 months in prison for collecting more than $10 million in royalties from Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, and YouTube Music in a massive streaming royalty fraud scheme.
54-year-old Michael Smith pleaded guilty in March after being indicted in September 2024 for fraudulently inflating his songs' listening stats between 2017 and 2024.
According to court documents, with help from the Chief Executive Officer of an AI music company and an unnamed music promoter, Smith uploaded hundreds of thousands of AI-generated songs bought from an accomplice to streaming platforms and used automated AI bots to stream the tracks billions of times.
To avoid detection by anti-fraud systems, he had the bots connect to the streaming platforms using virtual private networks (VPNs).
At the scheme's peak, Smith used more than 1,000 bot accounts to boost streams artificially. On October 20, 2017, he emailed himself a financial breakdown highlighting how he operated 52 cloud service accounts, each with 20 bot accounts.
Based on his estimates at the time, each bot could stream around 636 songs per day, for a total of roughly 661,440 streams per day. At an average royalty rate of half a cent per stream, the scheme's daily earnings reached $3,307.20, monthly earnings reached $99,216, and annual earnings exceeded $1.2 million.
One year later, on October 4, 2018, Smith emailed accomplices to say that "we need to get a TON of songs fast to make this work around the anti fraud policies these guys are all using now." and added that they needed "a TON of content with small amounts of Streams" to not raise issues "with the powers that be."
"By flooding music streaming platforms with automated bots in the place of consumers, and fake songs in the place of creativity, Smith robbed millions in royalty payments from genuine artists and their fans," said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald.
"For example, in April 2023, the entire catalogue of Taylor Swift received 9.3 million streams on YouTube Music from family plan streams, while in the same month, Smith's Bot Accounts used family plans to fraudulently stream his AI-generated music 80.9 million times," the Department of Justice added.
In a February 2024 email, Smith also confirmed these claims, boasting to accomplices that the songs had generated "over 4 billion streams and $12 million in royalties since 2019."
In addition to the 18 months in federal prison, Smith was also ordered to pay $8,091,843.64 in forfeiture and was sentenced to an additional two years of supervised release.

articles.title: Cuáles son los salarios de Elon Musk en Tesla y de Jeff Bezos en Amazon: el secreto detrás de los millonarios con tecnología
articles.text:
Los paquetes de compensación de los principales ejecutivos tecnológicos de Estados Unidos muestran una brecha extrema entre sí. Mientras Elon Musk, director ejecutivo de Tesla, recibió 158.300 millones de dólares en 2025, Jeff Bezos, fundador y presidente ejecutivo de Amazon, mantiene desde 1998 un salario fijo de apenas 81.400 dólares anuales.
Ambos casos, documentados por la organización sindical AFL-CIO y por el informe anual (proxy) de Amazon ante la Comisión de Bolsa y Valores (SEC), ilustran modelos opuestos de remuneración ejecutiva dentro del sector tecnológico estadounidense.
Musk ganó 2,5 millones de veces más que el empleado medio de Tesla
La compensación de Musk en 2025 equivale a 2.522.203 veces el salario medio de un trabajador de Tesla, fijado en 57.243 dólares anuales. En términos prácticos, el magnate acumula el equivalente al ingreso anual de uno de sus empleados cada 4,23 segundos. Durante un trayecto habitual de media hora de viaje al trabajo, ya habría sumado 24,36 millones de dólares en compensación.
La cifra total surge del valor razonable, calculado en la fecha de otorgamiento, de las acciones restringidas de Tesla que se le asignaron ese año, las cuales podrían llegar a valer hasta 1 billón de dólares si la compañía cumple con determinados objetivos de desempeño.
En declaraciones a Fortune, Brandon Rees, investigador principal del área de paywatch ejecutivo de la AFL-CIO, describió el paquete de Musk como “algo nunca antes visto” en los casi treinta años que la organización lleva midiendo los niveles de pago a directivos.
Rees añadió que “nuestra economía está cada vez más desequilibrada porque multimillonarios como Elon Musk están tomando una porción mayor de la torta económica mientras los trabajadores luchan para llegar a fin de mes”.
El monto recibido por Musk en 2025 fue 14 veces mayor que la compensación total combinada de todos los demás directores ejecutivos de las empresas que integran el índice S&P 500.
Si se incluye a Musk en el cálculo, los líderes de las firmas del S&P 500 ganaron en conjunto alrededor de 340 millones de dólares el año pasado, un incremento de aproximadamente 1.700% respecto de 2024. Al excluir su caso particular, el salario promedio de los directores ejecutivos del índice aumentó 21%, hasta 22,8 millones de dólares.
Para dimensionar la brecha, el director ejecutivo promedio del S&P 500 gana 312 veces más que sus empleados, muy por debajo de la relación que presenta Musk frente a la mediana salarial de Tesla.
Bezos cobra el mismo sueldo desde 1998
Bezos, cuyo patrimonio se estima en 375.000 millones de dólares, mantiene un salario de 81.400 dólares anuales desde 1998, cuando lo incrementó desde los 79.197 dólares que percibía el año anterior, según confirmó el proxy de Amazon presentado el jueves ante la SEC. El documento señala textualmente que “el señor Bezos solicitó no recibir compensación adicional y nunca ha recibido una compensación en efectivo anual superior a su monto actual”.
Ese salario, que en 1998 duplicaba el ingreso medio de los hombres en Estados Unidos (31.096 dólares), apenas superaba en 16% la mediana salarial masculina del último año, fijada en 68.952 dólares, lo que evidencia que no se actualizó junto con la inflación. Bezos explicó en una entrevista para el DealBook Summit de The New York Times los motivos detrás de esta decisión: “Ya poseía una cantidad significativa de la compañía, y simplemente no me sentía bien tomando más. Sentía que me habría parecido incómodo”.
Bezos, reemplazado como director ejecutivo por Andy Jassy en 2021, posee actualmente alrededor del 8% de Amazon y es su principal accionista individual. Al valor de la acción del viernes, esa participación equivalía a unos 225.000 millones de dólares, la mayor parte de su patrimonio total.
El actual director ejecutivo de la compañía, Jassy, percibió un salario base de 365.000 dólares el año pasado, monto equivalente al que reciben todos los funcionarios ejecutivos nombrados de Amazon, incluidos el director ejecutivo de Amazon Web Services, Matt Garman, y el director ejecutivo de la división de tiendas globales, Doug Herrington. La compensación de Jassy en acciones aumentó casi 473.000 dólares entre 2024 y 2025.
Amazon justificó en su presentación ante la SEC que estos salarios bajos, “significativamente menores a los que se pagan a altos directivos en compañías de similar magnitud”, buscan “vincular estrechamente la compensación total con el valor a largo plazo para los accionistas”.
Bezos recibe además algunos beneficios asociados a su cargo de presidente ejecutivo: la compañía destinó el año pasado 1,6 millones de dólares para cubrir sus gastos de seguridad y viajes de negocios, un monto que la empresa calificó de “especialmente razonable a la luz de su bajo salario y del hecho de que nunca ha recibido compensación en acciones”.

articles.title: En vidéo : la Xpeng L03 peut-il faire trembler la Tesla Model Y ?
articles.text:
Le constructeur chinois Xpeng continue son offensive sur le marché européen avec une nouvelle voiture électrique particulièrement attendue, la Xpeng L03. Lancée ce mercredi 7 octobre 2026 à partir de 34 990 euros, cette nouveauté s’attaque frontalement au segment très disputé des SUV familiaux électriques.
Si la voiture est affichée à 16 000 euros en Chine, les taxes et frais d’importation doublent son tarif chez nous. Produite là-bas, elle se prive en plus du bonus écologique en France.
Un design travaillé mais un coffre étonnamment exigu
Esthétiquement, ce SUV coupé de 4,65 mètres de long ne manque pas d’allure. Dessiné par Ranma Lopez – un ancien designer de chez Ferrari – , il affiche des lignes fluides, des poignées affleurantes et des portières sans montant très élégantes. En revanche, le bât blesse dès que l’on ouvre le coffre arrière. Avec seulement 367 litres de volume utile, l’espace de stockage se montre particulièrement restreint pour un véhicule de ce gabarit.
Pour compenser cette faiblesse, Xpeng a heureusement intégré un coffre de 69 litres à l’avant sur cette version à quatre roues motrices, ainsi qu’un espace généreux pour les passagers à l’arrière. L’empattement profite directement aux jambes, au détriment du coffre. C’est un choix d’aménagement très typique des productions chinoises.
Trois écrans à bord et une conduite tout en souplesse
À l’intérieur, la planche de bord se démarque par une profusion d’écrans. Contrairement à Tesla qui mise sur le côté dépouillé, la Xpeng L03 propose un combiné d’instrumentation solidaire de la colonne de direction, un grand écran central et un affichage tête haute – même si ce dernier a la fâcheuse tendance à disparaître si vous portez des lunettes de soleil polarisantes.
Côté technique, le modèle essayé dans sa version Performance Ultra développe 388 chevaux. Les accélérations se montrent franches (le 0 à 100 km/h est abattu en 4,5 secondes) pour une autonomie annoncée de 440 kilomètres. Sur la route, le comportement se révèle plus souple et mieux amorti qu’à bord d’une Tesla Model Y.
Le volant, très plat sur ses parties haute et basse, s’avère toutefois un poil déroutant lors des manœuvres. On regrettera aussi l’absence de mode de conduite à une seule pédale (one-pedal), pourtant bien pratique au quotidien. Reste à voir si ses qualités routières et son tarif agressif suffiront à compenser l’absence de bonus écologique de ce côté-ci de l’Europe.

articles.title: South Africa tech scale-ups need to create their own exits
articles.text:
South Africa tech scale-ups face a structural challenge: moving from early-stage venture funding to the governance, predictable unit economics and audit-ready financial structures required to attract institutional capital and scale. It has no shortage of technology companies solving real problems.
The core challenge is the structural commercialisation gap between early-stage venture capital funding and institutional governance readiness. While seed capital can prove product-market fit, local tech SMEs frequently stall when transitioning to scalable corporate governance, predictable unit economics, and audit-ready financial structures required by growth-stage investors.
That makes the partnership between the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), Africa’s largest stock exchange, and the Technology Innovation Agency (TIA), a government agency that supports technology commercialisation, more significant than a 16-week programme for 10 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
The pilot targets one of the weakest points in South Africa’s innovation pipeline: the gap between building something that works and building a company that can attract serious capital, enter new markets and scale.
The JSE and TIA selected 10 businesses in health, agriculture, and fintech for support, covering investment readiness, pitch development, market access, and connections to potential sources of capital. Some could eventually become eligible for AltX screening or private placements.
But the programme is not really about getting 10 companies onto the stock exchange. Its bigger test is whether South Africa can get better at turning innovation into scalable businesses.
“One of the key challenges in the innovation value chain is ensuring that new technologies and innovations are commercialised and access the markets,” said Patrick Krappie, executive for innovation enabling at TIA, in a September 30 statement.
South Africa does not simply have a startup funding problem. It has commercialisation, market access, and scale challenges that often present themselves as funding problems.
A company can develop good technology and raise early-stage capital without becoming investment-ready for the next stage. Institutional investors want predictable revenue, sound governance, financial controls, credible management teams and a market large enough to support a much bigger business.
Traditionally, an exchange enters the picture once a company has built a product, found customers, generated revenue and established the governance structures required by public investors. The JSE’s intervention suggests that preparing companies for capital markets may need to start much earlier.
The question is whether that preparation can help more companies make the journey from innovation to scale to exit.
South Africa already has evidence that its technology companies can produce meaningful exits.
In 2025, Nedbank, a pan-African banking giant, acquired Durban-based fintech iKhokha for R1.65 billion ($99.5 million), providing an exit for investors including Apis Partners and the International Finance Corporation.
Lesaka, a fintech and payments group, completed its R1.67 billion ($100.7 million) acquisition of Adumo in 2024, making it South Africa’s largest independent payments processor at the time. The deal created a larger Southern African fintech platform spanning consumers and merchants.
These acquisitions highlight an essential strategic pattern: South African fintech and software ventures achieve liquidity primarily by being absorbed into larger corporate balance sheets. While trade sales to established institutions like Nedbank or Lesaka validate local innovation, they also expose a dilemma of independence. Promising tech firms are frequently acquired before reaching the scale of public markets, limiting the local ecosystem’s ability to produce self-sustaining, independent tech conglomerates that can act as acquirers themselves.
Strategic mergers and acquisitions (M&A) are an important exit route, but can South Africa produce more technology companies that become large enough to remain independent, list publicly or eventually become acquirers themselves?
There are encouraging examples.
Johannesburg-founded financial analytics software company Syft Analytics was acquired by Xero, a global cloud accounting software company, for $70 million in 2025, giving its founders and investors an international exit. DocFox, another South African software company, was bought by US banking technology company nCino for about $75 million in 2024.
The pattern shows that South Africa can build globally relevant technology businesses. But when those companies reach a certain level of maturity, the most obvious sources of liquidity may lie outside the local public market or within a much larger corporate buyer.
That is where the JSE’s experiment becomes important.
The exchange is not merely trying to create more listings. It seeks to build a stronger pipeline of companies ready for capital.
Vuyo Lee, the JSE’s chief marketing and corporate affairs officer, believes the programme is intended to equip technology SMEs with the capabilities and opportunities to compete regionally and globally.
That “regionally and globally” part may ultimately matter more than whether any of the 10 companies ever ring the JSE’s opening bell.
The real prize is building companies that can keep attracting capital as they grow, expand beyond the domestic market and create liquidity for early investors without having to sell to the first strategic buyer that comes along.
The JSE has already shown that public markets can support technology businesses. Optasia, a digital credit infrastructure company, listed on the Main Board in 2025 at an implied market capitalisation of R23.5 billion ($1.4 billion), while 4Sight, an enterprise AI solutions provider, moved from AltX to the Main Board earlier that year.
The challenge is producing more companies capable of following that trajectory.
TIA’s Krappie described the agency as a connector for commercialising local innovation. Egypt offers a useful regional comparison: fintech company ValU has floated shares on the Egyptian Exchange, demonstrating how public markets can provide technology businesses with another route to liquidity.
South Africa’s challenge is to build a repeatable pipeline that prepares more growth-stage tech companies for institutional investment, credible valuations and eventual listings or private placements. If the JSE–TIA pilot succeeds, it could help more local startups scale into substantial businesses before they are acquired by strategic buyers.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution.
